08/Apr/08 10:34 PM;557058:c714f0f0-b42d-45c7-be2f-d002135599e4;This is a modification of the acts_as_authentable plugin. It handles password
encryption, authentication, identification of current users and admins, login status,
and remember_me. 

Key features:

To enable authentication, puts "acts_as_authentable" in the model; to disable extra
features (remember_me, for example), use "acts_as_authentable(false)". (There's
probably a more intuitive way to set that up.) Then run "script/generate authentable
yourmodelname" to create a migration to add columns to the model. For regular models,
those are: login, email, salt, crypted_password, remember_token,
remember_token_expires_at, activation_code, and activated_at. If the model name
contains the word "admin", it leaves off the last four, and just gives you: login,
email, salt, and crypted_password. 

Validations and authentication/encryption methods are in authentable_entity.rb. 

Methods related to the current session (current_user, logged_in?, etc.) are in
user_authentication.rb and admin_authentication.rb. 

Remember me/forget me methods are in session_persistence.rb. 

You should be able to access current_user, current_admin, logged_in?, and
logged_in_as_admin? from other controllers and views. You can also use login_required
and admin_only as filters. The user_logout_required and admin_logout_required filters
are to prevent people with multiple accounts from having overlapping logins; those
should include a redirect to a logical place. 

Activation emails and methods live outside the plugin right now.

31/Aug/08 12:22 PM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;As of revision 511:

Via acts_as_authentable we now have validation for:
- login length (3-40 characters)
- password length (6-40 characters)
- email length (3-100 characters)
- uniqueness of login and email

We also have validation for: 
Users:
- login format: begin and end with a letter or number, may contain only letters,
numbers, and underscores. 
- validity of email address (should match requirements and also check for valid mail
server at domain)
- acceptance of Terms of Service
- confirmation of age over 13

Pseuds:
- pseuds must have a name
- name must have at least one letter or number in it
- name may contain only letters, numbers, spaces, underscores, and dashes
- name cannot be more than 40 characters long

Works:
- title, summary, and notes must be between the min/max values specified in the
config (currently 255, 1250, and 2500 characters respectively). 
- title must be present.

Chapter: 
- title, summary, and notes must be between the min/max values specified in the
config (same as for Works)
- content must be present and at least 10 letters and no more than 500,000 letters.

External Work: 
- title and summary must be between min/max values specified in config, and title
must be present.

Bookmark: 
- notes must be no more than max value specified in config. 

Comment validation is not presently working, but this is a separate problem, see
issue 290. - **Status changed**: `FixedAndVerified`

Summary: Improvements to translation interface
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 28
Alas, click-to-globalize has some issues we've uncovered now we've used it
for a while. It stores strings in the session, making it too large to use
cookie storage, and storing session info in the db is not great. 

So instead, we will be using just the single-page translation mechanism.
However, we want to get some of the advantages of click-to-globalize into
this page instead. 

Goals: 
* Strings should have a link to the page they come from.
* Strings that have to be "broken up" because they contain links in context
should be kept together and ideally presented as a single string for
translation. 
* Strings should be nicely sorted and stay in order. 
* If possible, a bit of before/after context would be included around the
strings to translate. 
* When strings are input, they should be sanitized to strip all HTML tags.
Translations should only contain text.
* We should have in-place-editing enabled for those translators with
Javascript.

This may require expanding the ViewTranslations object that is part of
Globalize.

constant is getting set from the database every time the language_menu

21/Apr/24 3:49 AM;557058:baa5f297-c116-4036-bbf1-109f8a7e50a7;I looked into the Phrase In-Context Editor (ICE). There is a [Ruby gem|https://rubygems.org/gems/phraseapp-in-context-editor-ruby] available. In fact, an older version of the gem is already installed and configured for the archive. However, it most likely wasn’t activated or used in a while: It’s broken on the homepage of the archive since at least Ruby 3.0.

I would target the new ICE (linked below by Sarken), so the gem needs to be updated to at least version 2.0.0 and newly configured. There are a few roadblocks for this:

* -Version 2.0.0 of the gem requires Ruby 3.2. The archive currently uses Ruby 3.1. I opened a PR for the gem to- [-support Ruby 3.1-|https://github.com/phrase/phraseapp-in-context-editor-ruby/pull/74]-.- Merged and released as gem version 2.1.1.
* Parts of the gem are not or only improperly updated to handle the [Ruby 3.0 change to positional and keyword arguments|https://www.ruby-lang.org/en/news/2019/12/12/separation-of-positional-and-keyword-arguments-in-ruby-3-0/]. This was already [monkeypatched once by us|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4439], and there is another instance of this issue [here|https://github.com/phrase/phraseapp-in-context-editor-ruby/blob/8f87ed8a5a97512431b6c478ece4703c3bc5588c/lib/phraseapp-in-context-editor-ruby/delegate/i18n_delegate.rb#L27]. This causes the crash on the archive homepage in the currently installed version of the gem. This crash is in [number_with_delimiter|https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActionView/Helpers/NumberHelper.html#method-i-number_with_delimiter], which suggest to me that Phrase may be overeager in inserting itself into translation functions, but I did not investigate further.
* Phrase inserts itself into Faker generators. This is not a problem for the usual website translations because Faker is not used during normal operation. However, the mailer previews use Faker to generate email addresses and text used in the emails. Phrase replaces these with its placeholder strings, which leads to issues similar to [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6386|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6386|smart-link] . So Phrase should be prevented from inserting itself into the generators, because they shouldn’t show up in the ICE either.
* [The docs|https://support.phrase.com/hc/en-us/articles/5784095916188-In-Context-Editor-Strings] recommend a separate staging environment. I would also recommend it because enabling the ICE appears to interfere with normal site function.

* I manually patched/worked around the issues above and got the ICE to work locally.
* Because I am not AD&T nor Translation, I couldn’t log into Phrase to activate the editor. However, even without logging in, it was clear that the gem was working, because the placeholders for the ICE were used everywhere the translation method was used and showed the correct keys.
* The ICE also works inside mailer previews.

work.tags << Label.create

of self-referential relationships and models that the roadmap called for.

you can create a definition tag  (meta == 'parent') which can be applied to a label.

instead of 
TagCategory model: id, name, description, is_official
you create a tag with meta == 'official' - the name of the tag is the category name

the "flash" warnings that appear at the top of the page

live validations -- errors that appear as you type

Related to Issue 158

Having the Fandom tags (on story entry pages) be a free form field could be
problematic - both for the database and the users.  Freeform allows for
spelling errors to create multiples of a fandom, or differences in entry of
the fandom (ie: Supernatural/Stargate Atlantis vs. Stargate
Atlantis/Supernatural - this would be 2 entries by fandom, but they're the
same 'fandom').

If there were a dropdown box with a list with 'multiple selection'
available, this would eliminate a lot of these types of errors.  There may
need to be some preliminary selection criteria to make the list more
managable -> TV, Film, Music, Literature, etc., then subcategories,
perhaps?  This dropdown should also be searchable by typing in the letters
for the fandom name, instead of 'scroll only' for ease of use.

There would also need to be an 'other' option to allow for manual entry of
a fandom name that isn't already in the list.  However, this should have a
built in delay and need to be entered manually to the story by an
administrator to avoid duplicating existing fandoms with incorrect
spellings of the fandom name, etc.

Feedback:

Thoughts on the recs section.

As the archive grows, one of the most important features will be the recs
section. Recs help us winnow fanfic. 

Outsiders visiting the archive will likely go to the recs page once they're
daunted by the sheer volume of fic. The recs section is our second gateway.
It is especially important to have a carefully designed recs section
on-site because some authors will mark their stories private. 

1) The recs page must sort by the reccer's name, else it will be useless. 

Readers go to a recs page because of the reputation of the reccer.
Delicious assumes the subject (i.e., tag) is more important than who
bookmarks it. As Isiscolo put it, we look for recs based on those who have
similar tastes to our own. Who recc'd the story is the first thing we look for.

2) Several of the current recs don't have reccers' names at all. 

This makes it seem as though tagging and reccing are separate functions
(since we can't join yet, I can't test it). If that's so, it will quickly
create chaos.

3) We need a separate page that lists only a member's recs.

Listing the recs at the bottom of a user's profile will only work for those
don't write. 90% of reccers also write (a lot). Their recs will be buried.
In some cases, under 100+ fics.

4) We need a count of the number of stories recced next to the reccer's name.

Readers need to easily find the active reccers who put a lot of time into
reccing. We can't qualify how good the recs are, but we can quantify them. 

5) I would like to be able to sort the reccer list by number of recs.

If the listing by reccer looks just like the author listing (only with the
number of recs next to the name), it will still be hard to find the active
reccers. Perhaps we can have something similar to delicious's "popular
bookmarks" feature.

6) We need a very long comment field to describe our recs. 

The best reccers (Seperis, for example, or Regan_v here:
http://regan-v.livejournal.com/60719.html#cutid1) write a paragraph (or
more!) about a story. The primary flaw of delicious is that the comment
field is never designed for recs and is waaaaay too small. I can't test
this feature yet, but all the examples seem short.

Finally:

7) What do we do with Meta Recs? 

Is there a place on the archive for long meta-commentaries that involve
more than one fic? There's my SGA Flavor of the Year:
http://icarusancalion.livejournal.com/583242.html, and I know Regan_v does
them as well, usually on a theme. 

Finally, I'm very impressed you guys are on time and the site is functional
and effective. Good work.

The A-Z sort is preceded with numbers written in figures as usual, but
these are preceded by titles that have leading punctuation (a single

order. The alphabetical ordering restarts after each new punctuation mark.
The numbers are ordered digit by digit, resulting in the sequence 20, 33,
48, 6.
After the Z's at the end, a title commencing with a square bracket followed
by an O appears

scrolled down and realised what had happened, but as the archive grows the
number of misplaced works could end up going on for pages. (Currently,
after less than a month of story posting there is a total of nine works
involved, in a 1152 work total.) Even with a search function available,
scanning the list for a title you remember more or less will no doubt also
occur, and the misplaced ones would not be found.

Putting the numbers in the correct order may be quite complicated, but it
should be relatively easy to coax the punctuated titles, which cause the
worse confusion, out of their misleading locations.

rev 907

We need to add new fields to works (and bookmarks?) for user-facing dates,
perhaps published_at and revised_at, and allow the user to customize these
dates (eg to set published_at to the date when the story was originally put
up when posting an older story) and also to auto-update revised_at (rather
than updated_at) when we change the version of the story. 

We can't use the built-in created_at and updated_at for this because we
want these fields to accurately reflect what they are meant to, which is
when the database entry for the work (or bookmark) has been
created/altered, which is not necessarily going to correspond to when the
content encapsulated in the work has been *meaningfully* created or
altered. EG, any migration on the content of work objects (eg to change
titles to strip out spaces as we had to do pre-rev 907) will change the
updated_at data even though this is strictly for data-cleaning and not the
real content.

23/Jan/11 7:29 PM;557058:6f5727a4-d47a-45b6-8132-04378f742448;Comments from a security analyst I met at work :)

The recommended blocking time is a little long. If someone’s trying to log in and fails
( it happens ) then 2 hours will stop them participating. 5 minutes is short enough
to wait around for while the password blocking system resets and will avoid upsetting
members. It’s also sufficient to block most brute-force attacks, since you could have
a 24 hour timeout after three consecutive 5-minute blockouts. 2 hours will push someone
away from their keyboard though. 

As for point 4, the “Username or Password Incorrect.” is good – since it helps to avoid
enumerating the usernames. However you probably want to be told “Warning, your account
will be blocked with X more incorrect attempts” so they don’t just blindly enter the
wrong password five times.  

Keep in mind that as long as permanent damage can’t occur (eg, Deletes can be undone
later) and logging of attempt and accesses are turned on, that security can be fairly
minimal. It’s not like people are storing secret documents in the server. 
 
A bigger issue is that someone might give an account to a friend and the friend will
log in and lock them out. So perhaps having a link to block an account and have an
access evaluated by someone is good to include as well. For dealing with emergency
situations.

Keep in mind that if a friend knows the password, they might also know the email password,
so using email to verify such requests isn’t always possible

Summary: Users and People have unnecessary duplication
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 792
What archive revision are you testing on? (See the revision number next to
"An Archive Of Our Own: Extreme Alpha (rev. #)" in the header).

r1531

This is a code design issue rather than a front-end issue but involves some
design input. 

Currently, people is very nearly just a duplicate of the users index which
is a problem because it violates "Don't Repeat Yourself" principles and
will inevitably lead to inconsistency. 

Solutions:


1) Have users index just redirect to people index and get rid of the users
index views. This still splits off people controller/views without an
underlying principle and doesn't feel intuitive, but on the upside it is
quick and easy and keeps the "people" url. We shouldn't really have the
people url if we're keeping to a clean RESTful design -- that is,
("people/[name]" should be the person you look at going from the "people/"
index, not "people/" => "users/[name]"). However, because people/ includes
pseuds also, there's a case to be made for stepping outside this for the
index. 

-- OR --

1) Get rid of the duplicate people controller/views and just keep users
including pseuds (as it already does). 

2) If necessary, rename users to people --> this is a huge amount of work
for a fairly tiny reward IMO, just having "people" versus "users" in the
urls, but if we are going to do it, we should do it now before too many
users have shared the URLs to their archive home pages. The downside is
this would break any existing users' links to their archive home pages.

Summary: Matching data across external bookmarks to the same link
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 811
As per issue 707 : when an external bookmark is posted with a link already
in the archive, data from the previous bookmark is automatically fetched. 
If the information is left untouched, then the bookmark will post as a
second bookmark on the link (with a "2" beside it).

Adding or changing any of this top-level info (title, author, summary,
tags) makes a new bookmark.  However, the top-level info is always fetched
from the first external bookmark made.  If you alter that info, then it
saves as a new bookmark (even if you change it to the same info as another
bookmark.) So if one user made a bookmark with only a little top-level
info, then any other user who bookmarks that link who adds any top-level
info, will be making a new bookmark, even if other users have made
bookmarks with the identical info.  Somehow bookmarks for the same links
will need to be synched or organized.

(https://otw.16bugs.com/projects/4911/bugs/121540).

External works created via bookmarks before the bookmarks upgrade have no
fandom tag. We've now made fandom a required tag. An unfortunate
side-effect is that bookmarks on external works created before the upgrade
can no longer be edited. Because the tag should be on the external work
rather than the bookmark, the user can't add it; at the same time, they
can't save the bookmark because the tag is missing. :(

allow admins to edit external works (I think that would be good for other
reasons too). Then we would have to go through and add the correct fandoms
to the external works without them. I realise that's not ideal, but there
shouldn't be too many, external works were a bit hidden.

18/Nov/09 3:40 PM;557058:56c6aaf0-abec-4140-88a3-59aa2f24c990;Hi, ars.arboreous!

Thought I'd jump in here and try to make sense of this - it's a tag wrangling issue,
and kind of complicated.  Basically, the associations between a pairing and
characters doesn't happen automatically - the system doesn't automatically tie
together "Bob Bryar" with "Bob Bryar/Frank Iero"; instead, one of us tag wranglers
goes to the pairing and manually adds in the two characters.  So with Bob/Gerard, the
system doesn't tie that pairing to any or all "Bob"s in the archive; instead a
wrangler decides which Bob the pairing applies to, and ties it to that Bob ("Bob
Bryar", in this case).

Once the character is tied to the pairing, then only the pairing, not the character,
is displayed on the "works" page (since Bob Bryar/Gerard Way, Bob Bryar, Gerard Way
looks redundant).  The fic is still tagged with that character - if you filter by
character: "Bob Bryar", your Bob/Gerard fic should still come up, even if the
character isn't showing; and if you go read the fic itself, "Bob Bryar" should be
listed in the character tags at the top of the page. (Whatever wranglers do, we
shouldn't be altering any of your actual tags, just how they're organized.)

If you have other fics where the pairing and characters are both listed on the works
page, then that's probably because the tag wranglers haven't gotten around to hooking
up those pairings with those characters - with the archive newly opened and all the

Summary: Prioritizing of duplicate tags
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 945
r1742

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Post a new work with new duplicate tags in more than one field: E.g.
"Testing Taggy" in both the Fandom and the Freeform tag field.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

Because the system cannot handle having duplicate tags, the tag in "Fandom"
is renamed "Testing Taggy - Fandom". See:
http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/works/15976

This then causes trouble for the tag wranglers, who have to get an admin to
rename the fandom Testing Taggy to "Testing Taggy" and name the freeform
tag to "Testing Taggy - Freeform"

Ideally, when the system is presented with two new duplicate tags
simultaneously, it would prioritize the non-freeform tag.  So, given a
conflicting identical tag in the Fandom, Pairing, or Character field, the
freeform would be renamed "- Freeform" and the Fandom/Pairing/Char tag
would be left as-is.  Basically, we want the posting interface to process
the Fandom/Pairing/Char tag fields before it processes the Freeform field.

(Actually ideally users wouldn't be entering duplicate tags, but at present
it's pretty easy to get confused - renaming the Tags field will hopefully
help with that, but until then, it would be really helpful for us wranglers
if we didn't have to be renaming all the duplicates.)

(Um, and I'm not a coder, so if what we're requesting doesn't make sense,
please ask me to clarify!)

that users get made into tag wranglers or translators).

- An archivist who looks at the import form can import more works at once
and can import works for other users. 

- When works for other users are imported, we try and work out the identity
of the user from the source (as noted above, right now this is only working
for livejournal, if the user has their email displayed on their profile). 

- If we can do so, we go down one of two paths:

PATH ONE: Either there is a user in the archive who is already using this
email address as the address on their profile, or there is a user in the
archive who has already claimed this email address previously. 

* The user will automatically be given ownership of the stories in question.
* The user will be sent an email notification that the stories were added
to her account. 


PATH TWO: There is no user in the archive who has claimed this email address. 

* The user will receive an invitation email explaining about the import
process, with a link to claim their works. 

* If the user already has an account, they can log in and claim the stories
into their existing account. 

* The user can also create a new account, and when it is activated, the
stories will be added to their new account.

* If the user claims the stories, she will be sent an email notification
that the stories were added to her account. 

* The user can also instead orphan or delete the works if they wish.

- Collections should only be nestable one deep -- ie, you should NOT be
able to make a subcollection the parent of another one. 
- You should be able to create a subcollection from the parent collection's
page.

Summary: Tags retain synonym relationship even after being unhooked
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 1233
r2050

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Take a new tag (with at least 1 work) and make it a canonical. (e.g.
make new work with "Circuses")
2. Take an already-existing canonical tag (with works), un-canonicalize it,
and make it a synonym of the new canonical tag.  Check the "works" listing
for either the canonical or the synonym - it should list all works tagged
with either tag. (e.g. take existing canonical "Circus", de-canonicalize
it, and make it a synonym of "Circuses" - the Works page for either will
show works tagged with either.)
3. On the canonical tag's page, unhook the synonym from the canonical, then
make the synonym into a canonical again. (e.g. make 2 separate canonicals -
"Circus" and "Circuses".)
4. Check the "works" page for the former canonical. It will show some works
for both the canonical and the former synonym-canonical, even though the
tags themselves show no relationship. (e.g. "Circus" only brings up works
tagged "Circus"; but "Circuses" brings up works tagged with "Circus" or
with "Circuses")

This bug is tricky to duplicate, as it seems to depend on the order in
which it's done. Unhooking the canonical from the synonym tag's page
doesn't seem to cause problems.  However, if I unhook the synonym from the
canonical, then I get this effect.

It's happening on the archive now - we had a canonical tag "Pre-Slash",
which was then made a synonym of a new tag "Pre-Relationship". However that
proved confusing for some users, so we made Pre-Slash into its own
canonical again. However, the filter for "Pre-Relationship" still brings up
many works only tagged "Pre-Slash":

http://archiveofourown.org/tags/Pre-Relationship/works

even though if you look at the tags themselves, they are not synonyms and
there is no visible relationship between the tags:
http://archiveofourown.org/tags/Pre-Relationship/edit
http://archiveofourown.org/tags/Pre-Slash/edit

25/Jul/10 11:57 PM;557058:33aa6c27-2fd0-479b-b291-1f8e13db0fe4;More info for AD&T!

We currently serve our XHTML 1.0 as text/html, which limits our ability to use any
of the supported XML functions because the browsers on the other end believe text/html
== HTML 4.0. We do this to have maximum compatibility with IE, which is XML-incompetent.
See http://www.colincochrane.com/post/2007/11/10/Internet-Explorer-7-Did-Not-Kill-XHTML.aspx
and the Wikipedia article on IE 8. Note no support for XHTML as application/xml, which
is what XHTML 1.1 demands.

So, what does this mean for ARIA support & validation? It means we can't validate as
we stand, even though our ARIA roles are working, but we also can't move up, because
moving to XHTML 1.1. would break our pages in IE.

I'll leave this issue open because the situation may change in the future.

Summary: Gift Exchange challenge functionality
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 1332
revision 2264

**********************

NOTE: for this issue, please create NEW ISSUES for any bugs (under
Roadmap-Challenge), and mark this issue as verified after everything has
been tested and either it works or a new issue has been created for any
problems!

**********************


It should now be possible to:

- Make a collection (or a subcollection) into a Gift Exchange in the
collection settings

- Create signup settings for the Gift Exchange including instructions,
specific tags, limits on number of tags of various kinds, and required
descriptions or urls. 

- This should create a signup form link which users should see if:
-- The collection is unmoderated
-- The collection is moderated and the user is a member
(If the collection is moderated and the user is NOT a member, they should
see a "Join" link instead. Once they have been made a member by the
moderator, they should then see the Sign Up link.) 

- In the signup form, users should see:
-- if the moderator put in specific tags for a given type of tag,
checkboxes for those tags
-- text input fields for other types of tags that the moderator allowed
-- a textarea for optional tags if the moderator allowed that (not if the
moderator didn't)
-- a text input field/textarea for url/description if the moderator allowed
that (not if the moderator didn't) 

- When signing up, users should get error messages if they:
-- use non-canonical tags
-- use the wrong number of tags 

- If a user has signed up, they should then see "edit/cancel signup" links
in the collection and be able to edit the signup without having to re-enter
everything from scratch.

- If a user goes to the new signup url after signing up the first time,
they should be redirected to their existing signup.

- The owners/maintainers of the collection should be able to see a list of
all the signed-up users.

16/Jul/11 2:47 PM;557058:327d6059-0150-4fe5-8791-0d5e6025a597;This is a very complex problem, not so much because of what causes the issue but because

E.g. here are two related bugs I've found:
- Deleting tags on work will not (always) properly delete filters on work
- Adding tags that are meta tags to tags that already exist on the work will not be
properly set to be direct filters (they are still set to be inherited)

The main issue here is that properly removing a tag and all metatags without removing
those metatags that are still needed cannot be done the way it's implemented now. At
the moment we loop over the metatags and check if some of their subtags are still in
the filters list. However that will of course be the case if those subtags also happen
to be metatags of the original tag that should be removed. And we can't just ignore
all metatags of the original tag to remove because there might still be remaining tags
on the work that also have those metatags.

The rather simple solution is to get an up-to-date list of all meta tags from the current
list of tags minus the one to be removed. Then all filters/meta tags not in that list
can safely be removed.

http://archiveofourown.org/admin/settings (You can only actually see the
problem in action if you are an admin on Beta Archive, but you don't need
those powers to make the fix.)

1. Look at where it says '30 people are scheduled to be sent invitations on
$DATE'.
2. Feel perplexed, because $DATE is some time in the past, but the
invitations queue is running happily. 

$DATE is calculated from the last time the invitations queue sent out
invitations, but if the job is interrupted and then resumed, this throws
the date out. The date should be calcuated from time.now + frequency, not
the old time + frequency. 

The fix needs to be applied in the rake task for invitations, on the line:

new_date = AdminSetting.invite_from_queue_at +
(AdminSetting.invite_from_queue_frequency).days


Please also add some logging so that when the job issues invitations, it
records having done so.

I’ve established that a couple of major ebook readers can’t parse epubs with internal
files bigger than 300kb. (This is a known issue of those ebook readers.) (Sonys and
Jinke-derivatives; haven’t had the chance to try a Nook.)

(To understand what I’m talking about, grab any chaptered fic, download as epub, change
the .epub extension to .zip, and unzip. Inside the OEBPS folder will be several HTML
files. If those are bigger than 300kb, the ebook won’t work on some ebook readers.)

This is roughly 45,000 words. While ebook readers can handle (pretty much) any size
of file, if any one chapter is bigger than ~45k words, it’ll freeze up or have other
problems. (IIRC, a Sony won’t open the file; my PEZ opens & reads until it hits the
300kb mark and then stops mid-word.)

The epub export function automatically splits chapters into separate sections. Single-chaptered
works don’t get split. I’m not sure there’s an easy solution to this (Calibre splits
into separate HTML files that have no connection to chapter breaks, which is annoying),
but it’s worth knowing what causes the “my ebook reader can’t read those files” problem.

If it matters, the work I discovered/tested this on is archiveofourown.org/works/156093

.mobi files don’t have this problem, because the way .mobi is read by the software
is different.

a problem with the overall size of the work, just with the chapter size.

08/Nov/10 10:34 AM;557058:be6d5da9-c318-4a37-90a3-f06f5f84c0eb;I've taken care of the first one. epub files (and mobi's)  have separate pages for summary
and meta only when they are chaptered. For single chaptered works, this looks much
better, but it still allows you to have a table of contents on multi-chaptered works.

As for making it look pretty, a front-end coder can take this issue now! :)

Some constraints:

no per-person customizing (no "if current_user" logic). If someone wants a personalized
skin, they can download the html and fix it up themselves before converting it.

the styles are in the file /app/views/layouts/barebones.html.erb. All styles must be
in the header element, you can't link to stylesheets.

remember, some readers will ignore styles altogether, and typically the font and text
size will be overridden on the device as well.

the views are in /app/views/works/

download.html.erb is for any html and pdf download, and for single chaptered mobi and
epub downloads. In these cases, the same rendered html is created, and then the non-html
formats are converted. This means if someone else comes back later and wants a different
format for the same work, much of the work has already been done.

download.html.erb calls the following partials, which are also used directly in the
mobi and epub formats for chaptered works.
 
_download_preface.html.erb
_download_chapter.html.erb  (once per chapter)
_download_afterword.html.erb

for chaptered works only, you can customize the formatting for mobi files with the
@mobi instance variable (I found putting chapter titles in mobi chapters caused duplication.)

22/Jan/20 1:06 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;The reason this is happening: if you call {{redirect_back_or_default}} in an action that doesn't have {{skip_before_action :store_location}}, then {{redirect_back_or_default}} will try to redirect to the _current_ URL, because that was the location most recently stored.

When deleting a related work, the URL is the same as the URL for showing that related work (just with a different HTTP method). Which means that the call to {{redirect_back_or_default}} in {{RelatedWorksController#destroy}} always tries to redirect to the related work that was just deleted.

I think this can be addressed by adding {{skip_before_action :store_location, only: [:destroy]}} to the header of the {{RelatedWorksController}}. Or by using {{redirect_back}}, so that it relies on the {{Referer}} header instead of the location stored in the session cookies.

* Add a task to find all chapter kudos and transfer them to works. If the transfer failed (because the same user/IP address has also left kudos on the work), simply remove the chapter kudos.
* Remove kudos validation code that loads chapters ([creator check|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/6f987a7665d309c6f4e749a34787bcab632d864b/app/models/kudo.rb#L57-L67], [guests on restricted works check|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/6f987a7665d309c6f4e749a34787bcab632d864b/app/models/kudo.rb#L76-L85]).
* Add kudos validation for the presence and the type of the commentable, similar to [what we did with subscribables|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/6f987a7665d309c6f4e749a34787bcab632d864b/app/models/subscription.rb#L11-L15] ([https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5008#icft=AO3-5008|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5008#icft=AO3-5008|smart-link]).

How to test:

* (Server admin) Test the rake task.
** Get the number of chapter kudos on staging.
** Find one work with a chapter kudo (from user A).
** Run the task.
** Check that there are no chapter kudos on staging.
** Check that the example work still has kudos from user A.
* (Anyone)
** Check that you cannot leave kudos on your own work. You can do this by logging in as someone else, opening your own work, and then logging in as yourself in a new tab and attempting to kudos the work in the original tab
** Check that as a guest, you cannot leave kudos on a restricted work. You can do this by opening the work in a private tab, then change the work to restricted in another tab, then return to the first tab to leave guest kudos. You’ll get a generic error message this way, not a specific one about the work being restricted, but it’s fine. (Alternately, you can use inspect element to change the commentable ID of an arbitrary kudos form to get the more specific error message, e.g. “You can't leave guest kudos on a restricted work.“)

{{bundle exec rake After:clean_up_chapter_kudos}}

Summary: Prompt meme challenge type
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2218
New feature: prompt meme challenges

A new challenge type, instead of being a gift exchange, a challenge can be a prompt
meme. This will allow things like fic_promptly or comment_fic to run on the AO3, or
various other memes.

Basic workflow:
Mod creates a new prompt meme challenge
Users sign up with one or several prompts, which can be public or anonymous
Users can then claim prompts, to indicate they are intending to fill them
Several users can claim the same prompt, and it will show if this has happened
Users can then post to fulfil their claims, and it will fill in the request details
automatically
This will then show on the list of claims as fulfilled.
Mod can make challenge unrevealed or anonymous-writers just as for a gift exchange.

When an admin removes wrangling permissions from a user, the wrangler's fandoms still
remain assigned to that wrangler, but the wrangler doesn't turn up on the Wrangler
drop-down list anymore (making it difficult to remove those fandoms from the wrangler.)

appears in the "Filter by Wrangler" dropdown on http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/tag_wranglers

accidentally get removed, they'll still retain their fandoms) but the de-commissioned
wranglers should still be listed in the drop-down, so their fandoms can be removed.

(Low-priority fix since there's an easy workaround, to simply restore permissions long
enough to unassigned the wrangler's fandoms.)

Summary: Works incorrectly counted as WIPs
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2225
Latest release: 0.8.5

The is_wip method for works currently checks the position column for the work's chapters
and evaluates the maximum value against the expected number of chapters. Right now,
the position values are unreliable due to a separate bug, so we're getting works marked
as wips that are actually complete. We probably eventually want to use the complete?
boolean flag to determine the status, but for now, we should just count the number
of posted chapters so as to minimize the inconvenience to users. And fix chapter positioning,
but that's another issue. :(

  def generate

Summary: Reusing invitation can expose original invitee's email
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2269
What archive revision are you testing on?
Release 0.8.6

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Use the Send invite function from the interface to send an invite to an email address.
2. Invitation is never used.
3. Decide to give it to someone else by copy-pasting the link, and not by updating
the invite to another email address.
4. The invite is redeemed by the new invitee.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

In my Invitations management page, I see the invitation as sent to [old email] and
redeemed by [new invitee], and I can no longer edit/update it.

More importantly, the invitee has seen the old email when they were on the new user
creation page, because we set the form to fill in the email with the email associated
with the invitation.

This is, I grant it, user error - I (the user) should have updated the invite to resend
it by email.

But there are cases when you don't know the email, and people find it easier to follow
links given directly to them rather than dig for emails in the Spam bin where they
often end up. Also, the average user will have no idea that the original invitee's
email would be exposed, because they don't know our code inside out (or at all...)

So I'm just logging this so we don't forget it entirely.

27/May/11 2:56 PM;557058:8eb04462-c6aa-4b1b-b7b4-259ed44d3c0b;- **Labels added**: Milestone-Internal0.8 27/May/11 2:59 PM;557058:8eb04462-c6aa-4b1b-b7b4-259ed44d3c0b;- **Labels added**: Component-BackEnd 03/Oct/11 9:17 PM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;The broad strokes of what happens throughout this code. The heart of the changes are centered around the new OwnedTagSet model, which represents a managed and curated tag set, the kind used in a challenge. The old TagSet model remains -- this is as before a very basic model which is just a bag of tags. TagSets are still the "guts" of prompts and requests, and there's one that acts as the guts in each OwnedTagSet model. However, OwnedTagSet adds a layer of complexity atop this model for management and nomination purposes. The requirement for canonical tags in the TagSet model has been removed. Tags must still exist, however, before being added to a TagSet, EXCEPT if the TagSet belongs to an OwnedTagSet, in which case new tags can be created. (There is some refactoring work to do here, btw, to improve the encapsulation of the inner tag set, which is currently exposed in some places where tags are being added/removed from the set. Ideally we should instead be passing through those commands to the internal tag set transparently via method missing.) Because the basic tag set is just an internal guts thing, I've used tag_sets for the routing and name, to keep that inner tag set invisible to users for more clarity. The road to the happy land of OwnedTagSets branches off on the "tags" tab, but most users will probably come to tag sets from the challenge setup page, which links to them where the former paste-in box was. OwnedTagSets can have owners (who can do whatever with them) and moderators (who can approve and reject nominations), on the theory that what someone really needs less-authorized help with is managing a bunch of user input. OwnedTagSets have three key prefs: whether they are visible (whether anyone can see the tags in the set), whether they are usable (whether people other than the mods can use it in a challenge), and whether they are taking nominations. If a tag set is taking noms, the owner can specify the number of nominations of each type of tag. Without nominations, the OwnedTagSet can just have tags specified manually the way they used to be in the challenge settings form. For clarity, tags currently in the set are listed in checkbox fields (scrolling if the number is really big) to remove. With nominations, individual users can submit nominations for a set number of tags. These create TagNomination objects rather than actual tags, in order to avoid polluting our db with piles of unused tags. TagNominations try and track the state of corresponding tags (eg, to determine whether they're canonical or not and if they have the desired parent tag or not) and store their approved/rejected state. (It's not super-critical if this gets out of sync as it's mainly to give the tag set mods some extra info when deciding whether to approve/reject, so I haven't hammered on this a ton.) Mods can then review noms and approve, reject, edit, or leave them hanging out for a while. :) For performance reasons, a limited number of noms of any one type are shown to users at a time. As nominations are reviewed, they clear out and new noms are displayed. The front end will not be working until after lim's css/html revisions are merged, but the general principles of the display and forms are: - char/rel tags are organized under fandoms for display, and also for review if the set includes fandom nominations - if a set doesn't allow fandom nominations, only char/rel nominations, these will be shown flat for review on the assumption that such a tag set is going to be for a single-fandom (or small group of fandom) challenge. Finally, OwnedTagSets can also include TagSetAssociations. These allow a moderator to hook up chars/rels with fandoms in their tag set the way that wranglers do with canonical tags, for autocomplete purposes in signup forms. There are tools for batch loading associations and for picking through nominations to find potential associations. The key change to challenges (aside from just the technicality of how they get hooked up to tag sets -- prompt restrictions can now have multiple tag sets attached and pull their tags from all of them) is in how characters and relationships are collected for autocomplete when being done via autocomplete. When the user picks a fandom, chars and relationships for that fandom are pulled (from redis) from both canonical tag associations AND tag set associations. The mod can then choose whether to show ALL of these options, or to limit the options to only the chars and rels that are in the tag set. *What is the expected output? What happens instead?*

If I type “AO,” it should suggest both “ÂO3-2380” and “AO3-0000,” but it only suggests “AO3-0000.”

If I type “ÂO,” it should suggest both “ÂO3-2380” and “AO3-0000,” but it only suggests “ÂO3-2380”

*Notes*

The solution may involve normalizing the user input and keeping normalized copies of the tags in Redis for searching. The[ code that allows wranglers to change the diacritics on a tag|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/b63fce67a3975ec0614bb535c75d76c8dafbda71/app/models/tag.rb#L193] handles it like so:

{code:ruby}# ordinary wranglers can change case and accents but not punctuation or the actual letters in the name
# admins can change tags with no restriction
unless User.current_user.is_a?(Admin) || (self.name.downcase == self.name_was.downcase) || (self.name.mb_chars.normalize(:kd).gsub(/[^\x00-\x7F]/u,'').downcase.to_s == self.name_was.mb_chars.normalize(:kd).gsub(/[^\x00-\x7F]/u,'').downcase.to_s)
  self.errors.add(:name, "can only be changed by an admin.")
end{code}

*Deploy notes*

This functionality is accomplished by storing in redis autocomplete strings stripped of diacritics (in addition to the lower casing that was already happening to make it case insensitive) via {{ActiveSupport::Inflector.transliterate(string)}} and then similarly stripping diacritics from input when invoking the autocomplete. 

You will need to run the rake task {{autocomplete:reload_tag_data}} in order to get this functionality for existing tags.

For each tag, we store it under all the possible prefixes. EG, "Edgar" is stored under e, ed, edg, edga, edgar. If you want to show accented-character tags, and you have Édgar, it has to be stored under e, ed, edg, edga, edgar AS WELL AS é, éd, édg, édga, édgar. If you have a string with more than one accented character in it, the permutations get bigger if you want to support typing one accented character but not another. On top of that, lots of characters don't have an ASCII equivalent, and there's no programmatic way that I know of to do this. key to exit the autocomplete menu. The only way to properly exit the menu is the Escape
key.

again (AC options will come up but down arrowkey will not access them, though they
still can be selected by mouse.)

Note: Hitting the Escape key *does* close the autocomplete menu properly (and allow
it to be accessed again), so this isn't a major concern, but it'd be helpful if mouse-clicking
back to the field also worked.

Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.

Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2433
1. Claim several different prompts from the same user on a prompt meme
2. Post to fulfill for one of these prompts.
3. Notice that under "Fulfill a Claim: " on the Post New Work page, that multiple prompts
are checked - any prompts by the same user (including any anonymously-submitted prompts)

Even if you uncheck all but the correct prompt, if you go back and edit the work after
posting you will see all the prompts re-checked. The only way to get it to stop checking
the prompts is to uncheck all of the prompts for the meme, post, and then edit to recheck
the correct one.  The only prompt acknowledged will be the first one checked; however,
this may *not* be the prompt you are actually trying to fill.

This is especially problematic because if a user happens to have submitted some anon
prompts and some public prompts, responses for the anon prompts can show as belonging
to that user.

(Oddly, the Fulfilled Claims at /collections/*/claims only shows the correctly filled
prompt, and the work will only show one "In response to a prompt by:" line in notes;
the problem is only really evident if you happen to have claimed an anon prompt and
a public prompt by the same user.)

(A work with the anon author problem here:
http://testarchive.transformativeworks.org/works/214430
I posted this as a fill for the last (anon) prompt on the list; it treats it as a fill
for the first prompt.)

Summary: Putting a wrong category tag in the fandom/media field can end up with impossible/impossible to remove parents
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
*Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2455*
otwarchive v0.8.7.4

*If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:*
[http://archiveofourown.org/tags/Movies|http://archiveofourown.org/tags/Movies] | [http://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Movies|http://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Movies]

All the fandoms under "Parent tags" should be under children tags (and in fact appear there as well) - Media category tags shouldn't even be able to have parent tags. All the media tags have a few of these false parent tags, and there's no way to remove them (removing the media from the fandom tag does not remove it from the parent tag list.) While they aren't causing any apparent trouble, they're a confusing artifact.

*Description of code changes:*

Currently, it's possible for wranglers to add invalid relationships (e.g. a Character tag that's the parent of another Character tag, or a Freeform that's the parent of a Relationship tag, or a non-canonical Character that's the parent of a canonical Relationship tag, or a tag that is its own parent). This pull request does several things to fix this:

# It adds two validation checks to the CommonTagging class: one to make sure that the parent tag is canonical, and one to make sure that the type combination of parent and child is allowed. This prevents the creation of new invalid relationships.
# It modifies the tag associations code so that new CommonTaggings are handled more like new MetaTaggings, but with error messages passed on to the user to make it clear why the CommonTagging/MetaTagging is invalid. It also uses Tag.parent_types in order to make sure that it handles all of the different types correctly (rather than having each tag type have its own version of add_association).
# It modifies the fandom_string/character_string/etc. code so that when you enter a tag of the wrong type, it will prevent the Tag from being saved and show an error message.
# It hides the mass "Wrangle to Fandom(s)" option on the fandom-specific Mergers page and the fandom-specific SubTags page, since that option isn't needed (and would always cause the creation of invalid wrangling relationships in the old system).
# It adds a task to destroy all invalid CommonTaggings, and a task to destroy all invalid MetaTaggings.
# It adds some rspec tests to make sure that the new code will add the associations it should, and show errors for the associations it shouldn't.

*Testing:*

It would be good to have several Tag Wranglers run the code through its paces -- go through their standard routine, and make sure that they don't get any unexpected errors. There are a lot more validity checks now than there were before, and it'd be good to make sure that none of them breaks any useful tricks currently used by the Tag Wrangling team.

lead to issues it would be good to have them gone. The only way we've found to remove
them is to de-canonize the tags and unhook all relationships, but for many tags (especially

ArgumentError: unknown encoding name - macintosh

app/models/story_parser.rb:524:in parse_story_from_unknown'
app/models/story_parser.rb:514:in `parse_common'
app/models/story_parser.rb:180:in `parse_story'
app/models/story_parser.rb:152:in `download_and_parse_story'
app/controllers/works_controller.rb:554:in `import_single'
app/controllers/works_controller.rb:541:in `import'

That's with the site's own content encoding, "macintosh." We should catch that error

naturally mess up the special characters.) My theory: "MacRoman" isn't known to Nokogiri,
thus it falls back to the "macintosh" declared in the document, which it fails on,
too.

We are getting the encodings list to choose from from the Encoding module, not from
Nokogiri. Seems that Nokogiri hast a slightly different list, we'll have to find out
if there's a way to get a list of encodings directly from Nokogiri.

1. Post a work with some unevenly capitalised italics tags, like the file attached.

2. Preview and find that the italics are spread over paragraphs where they shouldn't
be

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

As far as I can see, when the parser encounters [i] it doesn't recognise [/I] as a
closing tag. So, it looks for the next [/i] - if this is several paragraphs away it
helpfully puts italics round all the intervening paragraphs. THEN the parser downcases
the offending [/I] (for extra confusion when you go back to edit mode). So, the original
italicised text looks normal, but several subsequent paragrphs are a mess. 

(Testing this with the attached will make this a lot easier to understand!)

In theory, this should be fixable by downcasing all HTML tags BEFORE the parser does
anything else. In practice, IDK if that will be possible.

Revisions to the tokeninput-based autocomplete based on fb from wranglers et al! This
is fixed as part of the tag sets update and will be pullreq'ed shortly. 


1) Arrow keys should now work intuitively. Here is my concept of intuitively :) 
* If there is something typed in the input box, the right and left arrow keys will
move you around in the input. If you edit/delete, the autocomplete search should fire
again & the results should reflect the changes. 

* If the dropdown menu is open, the up and down arrow keys will move you around in
the menu. If you are at the top and you press the up arrow, the topmost item should
be deselected (so that return will instead enter whatever you have typed in the input
box as a new tag), but the dropdown menu should remain open. (Escape key should continue
to close the dropdown.)

* If there is nothing typed in the input box, but there are tags added, the arrow keys
will move you among the added tags. Each arrow key should make the neighboring tag
selected. The input box should NOT move and the tags should remain displayed inline.
You should be able to delete tags via keyboard only without clicking with the mouse.

2) When you click out of the autocomplete field with text entered into it, the search
should NOT stop, and the text should NOT be added as a tag automatically. Instead,
the search should continue. When the results come back, you should be able to select
one. You should also be able to enter a new tag not on the list by hitting tab/enter/return/comma
at the end of the tag. 

3) It should be possible to paste in comma-separated items and each item should be
added as a separate tag, but unfortunately there isn't a good way to allow going in
mid-string and typing a comma as an edit without the comma triggering the adding of
the tag.

Summary: Allow anonymous posting
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2562
Users should be able to post works (and series and prompts) anonymously, at a more fundamental
level than the current challenge anonymity system allows.

Proposed plan:
1) When posting or editing a work, the user can choose to make it anonymous.
2) Anonymous works are associated with an anon user account, not with the current user's
account, preventing the authorship from ever being revealed due to bugs.
3) Every anonymous work has an access key, and the original poster can use that key
to edit or delete the anonymous work or to de-anon and list the work under their own
name.
4) Anon works don't appear on the author's works list, but users should have a separate
area where they can view their keys and edit their works.
5) The user can choose to throw away the key, which is to say, delete the association
between their account and the work, losing their ability to edit/delete/claim but ensuring
that the work is permanently anonymous. Needs a workflow that will make it difficult
for people to do this accidentally. (See: many many support requests re: accidental
orphaning.)

Things to consider:
1) How this impacts our current orphaning feature.
2) How anonymous works will be handled by the abuse team. My instinct is that keys
should not be visible to site admins and should not be used when dealing with abuse
cases - otherwise they're not truly anonymous, and users should be made aware of that
- but we'll have to discuss it with Abuse and Content.

(then click download, then EPUB)

What browser / OS has this been witnessed on? N/A

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Download the EPUB from that page
2. Get EPUB Checker from http://www.rainwater-soft.com/epubchecker/
3. Validate the downloaded EPUB using the "preflight" tab.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

There should be no errors or warnings, but there are lots. The first one is the one
I'm talking about here:

ERROR: C:\Documents and Settings\Keith\My Documents\Downloads\Blue Skies over Bad Lands.epub:
mimetype contains wrong type (application/epub+zip expected)

Please provide any additional information below.

When an EPUB is created, the mimetype must be the first file in the archive. That's
correct in the AO3 Epubs. But it also has to be uncompressed.

Fortunately the fix for this should be trivial. The EPUB download code in app/controllers/downloads_controller.rb
has this as line 102:

    cmd = %Q{cd "#{@work.download_dir}/epub"; zip "#{@work.download_basename}.epub"
mimetype; zip -r "#{@work.download_basename}.epub" META-INF OEBPS}

..separating the zipping of mimetype from the other files to ensure that it's first.
All that needs to be done to fix this is to add a -0 to it to specify compression level
zero for that file.

    cmd = %Q{cd "#{@work.download_dir}/epub"; zip -0 "#{@work.download_basename}.epub"
mimetype; zip -r "#{@work.download_basename}.epub" META-INF OEBPS}

By default, dl, dt, and dd all display as block elements, meaning they stack on top of each other instead of lining up side by side. There are two ways to view the symbols key and other help pages. Summary: Allow collection owners/mods to add/invite works to their collections
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2668
What archive revision are you testing on? Beta 0.8.9.12

Currently there's no way for mods or owners to add works they haven't created to their
collections, short of waiting for authors to submit them, making the process of curating
collections more complicated.

The ideal feature would allow mods/owners to invite a work into their collection in
some manner, and then send the author a notice so that they can approve of it or not.


There's already a preference for authors to “Automatically agree to your work being
collected by others in the archive.” so if the author of the work has clicked it, the
mod's invitation would simply cause the work to be added to the collection.

Hey, there.

I was reading an article about using overflow: hidden and floated content and it made
me remember the funky bug with the user fandoms list disappearing if you take off the
border. I see there’s a second one about that being the case in One Point Faux.

The issue is a known hazard of setting overflow:hidden (which .listbox has) and people
always used to set a width on elements to make it work correctly in older browsers.
This practice has fallen off as browsers have improved.

I tested One Point Faux and the default skin with #user-fandoms {border: 0; width:
100%} and there was no disappearing content. So setting width: 100% on either .listbox
if that won’t screw anything else up or on #user-fandoms alone will let anyone do what
they want with borders on that element.

(List all that apply, but at miminum give the system you are testing on) Safari, Firefox, Chrome, Opera What steps will reproduce the problem? 1. View the footer stylesheet: http://archiveofourown.org/stylesheets/site/2.0/06-region-footer.css 2. Notice the #footer a:hover has the style { background:#500; box-shadow:none } 3. Go to a page on AO3 and hover on a link in the footer What is the expected output? What do you see instead? You would expect to see a red background when you hover over links in the footer. Instead the link goes unchanged. Please provide any additional information below. This happens because only footer links are within ul.navigation, which has its links styled separately and more specifically with #footer ul.navigation a and#footer .secondary li a, thus overriding#footer a:hover style. This can be fixed in one of two ways, assuming we want the links to change on hover (see screen capture for preview): 1. By making #footer a:hover into #footer ul.navigation a:hover. 2. By making #footer ul.navigation a into #footer a. Either of these changes will require the secondary step of adding #footer .secondary li a:hover to make the skin chooser links (i.e. the names of the skins) readable in hover mode. If we don't want the red background, #footer a:hover can be deleted.

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Log in
2. Go to create new skin: http://archiveofourown.org/skins/new
3. Notice size of CSS textarea is on the small side

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?
The CSS area only displays about ten lines of text at a time, which is especially frustrating
given its tendency to display every element on its own line. The CSS textarea should
be bigger, like the same size as the Work Text textarea: http://archiveofourown.org/works/new

Please use labels and text to provide additional information.
The size of the story textarea is currently defined in 07-interactions.css with .post
.text textarea { height: 36em; clear:right} in the section called "INTERACTION: POST."

The CSS textarea can be targeted through textarea #skin_css or .edit_skin textarea,
but it does not need clear: right, nor does it belong in the same section as .post
.text textarea. To implement this, we would need something like .edit_skin textarea
{ height: 36em; }. In the spirit of DRY, I'm thinking it would be better to set { height:
36em; } up as its own class, since we will probably want other large textareas elsewhere
in the future -- something like textarea .large { height: 36em;}. The large class can
be added to the relevant textareas as needed, and height: 36em can be removed from
.post .text textarea in 07-interactions.css.

h1. Original issue

*Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2780*
otwarchive test-0.8.10.12

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*

1. Have a story posted on the archive
2. Have another version of the story archived on AO3 from a different site (e.g. the Yuletide archive gets imported, after you have already uploaded your previous Yuletide stories to AO3.)

*What is the expected output? What do you see instead?*

I would expect some way to combine the different copies, or at least a warning message and explanation of what to do.  Ideally there would be a way to move comments/hitcounts/community associations from one version to the other - but since we don't have a way to do that (yet?) at least explain that the copy of the story can be claimed and deleted. (Mention it in the email invitation and claims page?)

It also might be useful to provide a link for adding the existing AO3 story to the archivist's collection, or some other way to replace an imported story with an existing AO3 copy?

(Considering the number of authors who have uploaded their past Yuletide stories to AO3, there are going to be a lot of people contacting Support about this unless it's clearly explained.  Not to mention the Smallville Slash Archive - I've got a dozen stories posted there myself that are already up on AO3, would like to have some way to manage this.)

h1. Spec from Open Doors:

*Feature request:* A tool that can be used to combine the stats and additional attributes of two AO3 works into a chosen body of work (W-original), by inputting two work URLs.

*Essential*
1. The user of the tool selects the work they want to keep (W-original), and the one they want to merge into it (W-dupe). All the components from W-dupe that are not editable (comments, kudos, and hit counts) will be added to W-original (on top of any comments, kudos, and hits it has already). 

2. Any co-author on either one of the works will be added to the final work.

*Desirable:*
1. This will be a self-service tool that checks to see if the logged-in account owns the works in question. 

2. The URL of the merged work should be the URL of the W-original.

3. The tool should keep the merged work in any collection or series either copy was part of. 
For example, if W-original is part of the collection "Clark/Lex Funtimes" and W-dupe is part of "Smallville Slash Archive", the combined work (W-original-merged) should appear in both collections.

4. Any bookmarks made on W-dupe will be transferred and link to W-original. 

5. Any redirects pointing to W-dupe will automatically point to W-original. 
For example, redirects were set up for the Smallville Slash Archive. If "[http://smallville.slashdom.net/w-dupe|http://smallville.slashdom.net/w-dupe]" redirects to W-dupe on AO3, it will redirect to W-original on AO3 after the merge.

6. The URL for W-dupe should automatically redirect to W-original.

7. The merge tool page should include a reminder that if the user of the tool wants to keep any editable attributes (like ratings or tags on the work, and inclusion in any collections if this is not part of the tool) of W-dupe, they should add it themselves to W-original before merging the works.

8. After combining the works, W-dupe is deleted.

Summary: Wrangler page allows you to assign non-canonical fandoms to yourself (but not remove them)
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
*Originally reported on Google Code with ID 2785*
otwarchive test-0.8.10.12

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*

# Log in as a tag wrangler
# Go to the edit page for a non-canonical fandom tag, e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/The%20100/edit|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/The%20100/edit]
# Follow the “Sign Up” link to go to the Tag Wrangling Assignments page ([https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglers|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglers]) with the fandom listed under “Assign fandoms to yourself”
# Press “Assign” to create the assignment

*What actually happens?*

The assignment is created and the fandom appears on your wrangler assignment page.

However, if on the /tag_wranglers page you filter for yourself using the "Show Only Wrangler" option, the non-canonical fandom tag will not appear, so there is no way to unassign it from yourself. (You can work around this by canonizing the tag, unassigning it, and de-canonizing the tag again).

*What should happen?* 

You should not be able to assign non-canonical fandoms to yourself. This means: 

* There should not be a “Sign Up” link on the edit page for non-canonical fandoms.
* Entering a non-canonical fandom directly in the “Assign fandoms to yourself” field and pressing “Assign” should not create the assignment. (If you enter a nonexistent or non-fandom tag in this field, it fails silently while giving a success message. There’s no need to fix that as part of this issue – we can live with the misleading success message and silent failure for this as well.)

Please also include a rake task to destroy any existing wrangling assignments for non-canonical fandoms.

16/Nov/12 7:13 AM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;So unfortunately, this is wrong. :( 

PromptMeme maintainers should NOT be able to edit prompts. 

The only reason GiftExchange maintainers are allowed to edit is in order to allow them
to successfully create matches. What often happens in a GE is that after signup is
closed, it's discovered that a participant can't be matched; they have to be asked
for changes. 

However, opening signup to allow them to make those changes would also allow other
people to come in and make changes and sign up even after it's supposed to be closed,
thereby potentially introducing NEW issues with matching. 

In practice, therefore, it is necessary to allow this editing, and the participants
also get a check on this because they then in fact end up assigned, so if the maintainer
has changed their signup to something weird, they will find out when they get their
gift! :P 

In a PromptMeme, this consideration doesn't arise. If a prompt is inappropriate, the
maintainer should be able to delete it, but not edit it.

29/Oct/13 8:19 PM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;More detail on this issue: 

The underlying problem is that potential matches were being generated by exhaustively
comparing every signup against every other signup in the challenge, even if that was
not necessary (because the two signups didn't share any tags) and even if the signup
already had a massive list of potential matches. 

Instead, we now only compare signups that share at least one tag of a type required
for matching by the challenge (that is, if you have to match on fandom, signups are
only compared if they share at least one fandom tag), and potential matches are cut
off after a top limit (currently 50). 

This drastically speeds up matching. For instance, Yuletide with 1800 participants
was taking ~3 days for matching to run under the old system; under the new process,
it takes ~15 hours instead. 

IN ADDITION, if people turned up who had no potential matches, after getting more offers/requests
from those people, potential matches had to be regenerated for the ENTIRE challenge.
The new process now allows a mod to regenerate potential matches just for a single
person without throwing out all the old matches. 

Testing this sadly requires: 
- creating a collection and gift exchange challenge 
- in the gift exchange settings it would be great to try a variety of "required" settings
-- note that the "yuletide" option of 1 fandom and all characters is really well exercised
in the automated tests, and I have done a lot of testing with a challenge of 1 character
and 1 freeform required, so other combinations would be great to try. 
- having multiple people sign up with various options, some matching and some not
- have at least one person sign up who doesn't match anyone else
- close signup and generate potential matches from the "Matching" page in the collection
sidebar

You should see: 
- potential match generation progress should show correctly (you should see a name
listed and a % of the way through the challenge when you refresh the page)
- after potential matches are generated you should see the person who didn't match
anyone else listed separately
- you should be able to edit their signup, make them match, and then regenerate potential
matches for them
- after their potential matches are generated, you should be able to regenerate assignments

I have also tried to clean up the page, break out a lot of the (ugly) view code into
partials, and move the too-wordy and confusing instructions into a single help file
with more context and explanation. Any suggestions for further improving the help very
welcome!

if you type in "Norse" in the fandom field, you will see both "Norse Mythology" (the
canonical) and "Norse Mythology - Fandom", despite there being no tag on the Archive
"Norse Mythology - Fandom".  (see: http://archiveofourown.org/tags/search?utf8=%E2%9C%93&query%5Bname%5D=Norse+Mythology+-+Fandom&query%5Btype%5D=Fandom

It seems like this happens when an admin edits a tag - the autocomplete continues to
list the old tag wording, not the new one.

to "Supernatural - Fandom", it will still be listed as "Supernatural" on the autocomplete.
If a user then selects "Supernatural" from the autocomplete, it will create a new,
unwrangled tag.

This is not that big a problem for the works and bookmark autocompletes, which don't
care whether or not a tag is canonical, but it is an issue with the tag wrangling interface
and challenges, which sometimes require users to select canonical tags - the tag will
appear as a canonical in the autocomplete, but will be unusable when the user attempts
to save. It also can create duplicate fandoms - if the new unwrangled tag is canonized,
a new entry will be added to the autocomplete for it, ignoring the old entry.  (e.g.
if after changing the Supernatural tag to "Supernatural - Fandom", you then create
a new tag "Supernatural" and canonize it,  "Supernatural" will appear twice in the
autocomplete, though either one will link to the same tag.)

 * The padding might look better if it was set on all four sides, so longer content
doesn't run directly up against the footer and scroll bar

NOTES ON WHERE SCROLLTO JAVASCRIPT WORKS:

The function that takes you to the top of paginated comments http://code.google.com/p/otwarchive/issues/detail?id=2812
only works in some instances.

In theory, clicking the bottom pagination should be taking you to #comments_placeholder,
which is beneath the comment form. If this were successful, the comments' top pagination
would be at the top of your screen. 

In reality, try the following. This uses a general audiences-rated work to avoid any
problems that might come from the adult content warning. We're using beta to observe
the existing behavior.

==

1.  Follow this link to a work with paginated comments: http://archiveofourown.org/works/215867

Now, click the Comments (#) link on the bottom of the work to reveal the comments and
the comments pagination. Use either the top or bottom pagination links to travel to
the second page of comments. Notice that the top pagination is the topmost item in
your browser window. 

This is the desired effect. We use jQuery to make the pagination scroll to #comments_placeholder,
a container whose first visible item is the top pagination. It works because we're
loading the next page of comments with Ajax.

Close that window or tab.


2. Now, follow this same link to the same work with the same paginated comments: http://archiveofourown.org/works/215867

This time, click the Comments link on the top of the work. This causes the page to
reload with both the comment parameters and the comment anchor appended to the URL.
Your address bar will say http://archiveofourown.org/works/215867?show_comments=true#comments
and the kudos will be the topmost item in your browser window. This is because #comments
refers to an invisible page anchor in the invisible h3 element above the kudos section.

Now use either the top or the bottom pagination to travel to the second page of comments.
Notice that you are at the top of the work. 

This is the desired effect. This is the same behavior that users with Javascript disabled
will always see, regardless of which comment link they use. This behavior is not broken,
although we may wish to modify the pagination links to include the #comments anchor
in this instance.

It is not possible to reproduce the effect from (1) here because we are loading a new
page rather than using Ajax.

<% if @skin.ie_condition.present? %><abbr title="internet explorer">IE</abbr><%= @skin.ie_condition

<% if @skin.ie_condition.present? %><dd><abbr title="Internet Explorer"><%= @skin.ie_condition

of IE, since the above abbr would encompass "IE6" or "IE7" and so on -- which are abbreviations

plain ol' "IE" is what displays under "Condition:" when you select the version-less
"Internet Explorer" option from "IE Only").

06/Sep/13 7:07 AM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;This is more complicated than it might seem alas!

1) Once a tag is approved and in the set, the nominations become extraneous -- they're
ephemeral, and we want to be able to trash them once the set is finalized, so we can't
use information in those nominations. Basically, the nominations are purely a tool
to help the moderator populate a tag set. If the moderator puts a tag in the set, it's
in the set. Tag set code doesn't "know" about nominations, in other words -- the tag
set code stands alone. I don't think it's a good idea to change this. 

2) Once tags are added to a set, we rely on the canonical information from the AO3
tag universe in order to establish the relationships between those tags -- this is
how characters get slotted into fandoms in the list by and large. We only use manual
tag associations for characters and fandoms that aren't already hooked up. 

As a result, the only way to NOT have a character tag appear in every fandom tag where
that character "lives" in the tag universe is if we allowed tagset moderators to turn
off using the canonical relationships entirely. But if they did that, they would have
to manually associate EVERY character they approved in EVERY fandom they wanted the
character to appear in. 

3) I am pretty sure (haven't actually tried this) that there is a workaround for particular
tags which would be to nominate and approve a new, non-canonical version of a tag that
specified the tag -- eg, "Captain Jack Harkness (Dr. Who Only)" -- and then set up
a tag set association for that non-canonical tag. 

Anyway, offering option #2 would be a substantial amount of work on our end, and it
would entail tons of work on the tagset moderator's end that I'm skeptical any actual
tagset moderator would really want to choose to do, given the existence of the workaround
in #3. 

I would lean towards just adding an explanation to the FAQ to clear up confusion, and
marking this WontFix.
