Summary: Add chapter number to comment notifications for multi-chaptered works
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
*Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3076*

*Site revision:*
Originally created for version 0.8.13.8, updated for version 0.9.252

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*

1. Receive a comment notification for a multi-chaptered work
2. Want to know what chapter it was on

*What is the expected output?*

The subject line should say, “[AO3] Comment on [Chapter #] of [Work Title]”.

The first line of the comment should say, “[Commenter] left the following comment on [Chapter #: Chapter Title] of [Work Title]:” and the chapter info should link to the relevant chapter.

The link to all comments should say, “Read all comments on [Chapter #] of [Work Title]”.

*What do you see instead?*

Instead, there is no chapter information mentioned.

*Notes*

Similar changes will be needed in the edited comment notification, sent comment notification, and comment reply notifications.

h2. Testing instructions

You need two users whose emails you can access.

# Log in as a user whose email you can access
# Set your preferences to receive copies of your own comments
## Hi, username! > My Preferences
## Uncheck “Turn off copies of your own comments”
## Press “Update”
# Post a work with a single chapter. Note its URL
# Post a work with multiple chapters. Do not give the first chapter a custom title. Give the second chapter a custom title. Note the work URL
# Log in as a different user whose email you can access
# Set your preferences to receive copies of your own comments
## Hi, username! > My Preferences
## Uncheck “Turn off copies of your own comments”
## Press “Update”
# Go to the work from step 3 and leave a comment on it
# Edit the comment
# Go to the work from step 4 and leave a comment on each chapter
# Edit the two comments
# Log in as the user from step 1
# Reply to the comments you left in step 7 and 9
# Edit the three comment replies

h3. Expected behaviour

* At step 7
** work creator receives comment_notification for a comment on work title. It should not mention a chapter
** commenter receives comment_notification for a comment on work title. It should not mention a chapter
* At step 8
** work creator receives edited_comment_notification for a comment on work title. It should not mention a chapter
* At step 9
** work creator and commenter each receive two comment_notifications, one per comment on the specific chapter. The comment on the untitled chapter should only mention the chapter number, the comment on the titled chapter should include the chapter title in the mailer body (but not the subject) 
* At step 10
** work creator receives two edited_comment_notifications, one per comment on the specific chapter. The edited comment on the untitled chapter should only mention the chapter number, the edited comment on the titled chapter should include the chapter title in the mailer body (but not the subject)
* At step 12
** work creator and original  commenter each receive a total of 3 reply notifications. As above, the notification for the single chapter work should not mention a chapter and the other two notifications should mention the chapter number in both subject and email body, while only the comment notification for the titled chapter should include the chapter title in the mailer body
* At step 13
** original commenter receive a total of 3 reply edited notifications. As above, the notification for the single chapter work should not mention a chapter and the other two notifications should mention the chapter number in both subject and email body, while only the comment notification for the titled chapter should include the chapter title in the mailer body

h1. Deploy notes

Mailer workers need to be restarted.

Summary: squid caching: guests should correctly see the adult warning and be able to skip it in future
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3132
Squid caching problem: if one guest goes to an adult work with the view_adult preference
already set in their session, they will load the squid cache with the work WITHOUT
the adult page meaning that any subsequent guests will see the work with no warning
even if they do NOT have the preference set.

Solution: we are now setting a cookie the first time a guest chooses the preference;
if this cookie is set, then the webserver will rewrite the URL to include ?view_adult=true
at the end automatically. Otherwise, guests will always get the "adult" page, meaning
that for guests, the cached version at .../works/123 will be the adult warning, and
the cached version at .../works/123?view_adult=true will be the actual work, and they
will be redirected to the second if they have the cookie set. 

This should not change behavior for logged-in users/admins. 

To test: 

1) Visit an adult work as a guest (you should get the "adult" warning) and choose "proceed"
2) Visit a SECOND adult work as a guest (you should NOT get the "adult" warning but
be sent directly to the work)
3) Clear your cookies and go back to the SECOND adult work. You should once again see
the adult warning. 
4) Have another guest who has already chosen not to see adult warnings also go to the
SECOND adult work. They should NOT see the adult warning.

Looking at the schema we have:

CREATE TABLE `kudos` (
  `id` int(11) NOT NULL AUTO_INCREMENT,
  `pseud_id` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `commentable_id` int(11) DEFAULT NULL,
  `commentable_type` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  `created_at` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `updated_at` datetime DEFAULT NULL,
  `ip_address` varchar(255) DEFAULT NULL,
  PRIMARY KEY (`id`),
  KEY `index_kudos_on_commentable_id_and_commentable_type` (`commentable_id`,`commentable_type`),
  KEY `index_kudos_on_ip_address` (`ip_address`),
  KEY `index_kudos_on_pseud_id` (`pseud_id`)

IP address should be a 32bit int :)

From the performance book.

Another example is an IPv4 address. People often use VARCHAR(15) columns to store IP
addresses. However, they are really unsigned 32-bit integers, not strings. The dotted-
quad notation is just a way of writing it out so that humans can read it more easily.
You should store IP addresses as unsigned integers. MySQL provides the INET_ATON()
and INET_NTOA() functions to convert between the two representations.

Summary: Setting expires headers appropriately
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3160
Expiry headers are used by a web application to tell a client how long a page is valid
for so it doesn't need to be re-feteched. Both simple web clients and web caches can
use this information to speed up displaying pages.

Currently squid lives between nginx and the unicorns. Currently the application sets
a big do not cache set of headers on all requests.

This is an example of the headers my I get when I am logged in.

HTTP/1.1 304 Not Modified
Server: nginx/0.8.54
Date: Tue, 26 Jun 2012 21:54:11 GMT
Connection: keep-alive
Status: 304 Not Modified
Etag: "900ef6255cfb05774b55fae27f2f1b16"
Cache-Control: max-age=0, private, must-revalidate

There is a relatively simple document at http://www.howtoforge.com/how-to-set-up-a-caching-reverse-proxy-with-squid-2.6-on-debian-etch-p2

And the following page explains how we tell squid to ignore what the application is
saying.

http://www.squid-cache.org/Doc/config/refresh_pattern/

So these are the policies we currently have:
refresh_pattern http://archiveofourown.org/admin/.* 1 1% 2
refresh_pattern http://archiveofourown.org/users/.* 1 1% 2
refresh_pattern http://archiveofourown.org/user_sessions.* 1 1% 2
refresh_pattern http://archiveofourown.org/admin_posts/.* 1 1% 2
refresh_pattern http://archiveofourown.org/passwords.* 1 1% 2
refresh_pattern http://archiveofourown.org/abuse_reports/new.* 1 1% 2
refresh_pattern http://archiveofourown.org/support.* 1 1% 2
refresh_pattern http://archiveofourown.org/downloads/.* 1 1% 2
refresh_pattern http://archiveofourown.org/signup/.* 1 1% 2
refresh_pattern http://archiveofourown.org/works/.* 1 1% 2
refresh_pattern http:// 25 90% 30 ignore-no-cache override-expire ignore-private	ignore-reload
override-lastmod ignore-no-store ignore-must-revalidate 

So we don't currently cache a large number of urls, and anything for a user we believe
is logged in.

I think to test this it will need to be on test ( where we would set up another nginx
instance so we could test the new features ) or we will need to work together to get
squid working for a webdev.

Looking at setting the expiry header in ruby the following pages look reasonable.

http://stackoverflow.com/questions/3117361/how-do-i-set-expires-header-when-using-send-data

If we are generating expires headers I would hope that it would be possible to change
the amount of time we set the expiry for without a redeploy. ( if you did use mysql
please make the query identical so it get answered by the query cahce but I would expect
one of the redis to be a better place to store the config. Unless we can have it in
a file and a restart of the unicorns to reload it ?

View a help box that instructs users to input text in hopes of achieving a specified result (eg help boxes on search page) What is the expected output? What do you see instead? The help boxes currently use em tags, which are used to place emphasis on text, to set off text that the user should input and text that should be returned. HTML has better tags for this: kbd should be used anywhere we're showing text a user should/has/can/etc input and samp should be used where we're showing likely/desired/example/etc output. Please use labels and text to provide additional information. For instance, we currently have:
Harry Potter will find Harry Potter and Harry James Potter but not Harry.
We would instead want:
Harry Potter will find Harry Potter and Harry James Potter but not Harry.
(You might also need to add samp to the CSS for styling -- I don't see it on a quick glance. I'd expect it to be in with kbd, tt, code, var, pre.)

The feed_sweeper is only invoked from works_controller:
  cache_sweeper :feed_sweeper

The feed sweeper only observes works (observe Work) and only does expire_tag_feeds
when the update action of the works controller is invoked. Not when the work *object*
has been updated. It is not like a model observer.

at all.

The only things that trigger it are posting a new work, or changing the global revised_at

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1.  Create a work, Preview, then choose "Save Without Posting" to send that work to
your "Drafts" page.
2.  Go to the "Drafts" page and click the "Edit Tags" button on the work.
3.  Edit your tags, then look around for an option that will let you save these edits
without posting the draft.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

Expect to find a way to save your tag edits to the draft.  Instead find only choices
to cancel or to save the tag edits to the draft _while also posting it_.

Please use labels and text to provide additional information.

The Edit Work Tags form that comes up when clicking "Edit Tags" on a draft has three
buttons--Preview, Update, and Cancel.  Cancel cancels your changes.  Update keeps the
changes but causes the work to be posted.

Clicking Preview takes one to a preview of the work blurb with the choices Post, Edit,
and Cancel.  Cancel cancels your changes.  Edit takes you back to the editing form,
with the three buttons described above.  Post keeps the changes but causes the work
to be posted.

Thus, there is no way to edit the tags from the "Edit Tags" button without posting
the work.

Tags _can_ be edited without posting the draft by using the "Edit" button, previewing,
and then choosing "Save Without Posting".

The x for deleting isn’t a link, so you can’t tab to it, ergo it doesn’t work with
screen readers. The easiest thing to do would be to just add an a href=“#” around the
x, but that would just be a stopgap and not totally accessible (because you could delete
a tag, sure, but which tag are you deleting? and you’d have to know “x” meant “delete”).

field for typing your tags on of course, but instead of just tossing the tags up above
the text field, display them in a field set below the text field, and with checkboxes
instead of an x. The checkboxes could be pre-checked, and unchecking the boxes would
remove the tags on save (rather than making them vanish as soon as you unchecked the
box).

Titled Checkboxes similar to the "Check to Remove" buttons on the Tag Wrangling pages

Comment:
12/Aug/12 7:18 AM;557058:8eb04462-c6aa-4b1b-b7b4-259ed44d3c0b;Aha! This really is lupus-er, caching. Memcaching, to be precise.

In the _commentable partial, commentable can be a work or a chapter.

If looking at a chapter, this will load the kudos partial with the chapter as the commentable:

<%= render "kudos/kudos", :kudos => @kudos, :guest_kudos_count => @work.guest_kudos_count,
:commentable => commentable %>

The kudos partial uses the commentable's cache key:

  <% cache "#{commentable.cache_key}/kudos" do %>

which will be a chapter, in this case.

But the kudos sweeper only expires the fragment corresponding to the newly created
kudos' own commentable - which will always be a work, not a chapter.

expire_fragment "#{kudo.commentable.cache_key}/kudos"

The result is that fragments corresponding to chapters live forever - or for however
long unexpired memcache fragments live, anyway.

This will be fixed in AO3-5880.

However, user anonymity is still broken if we have a series with both anonymous and non-anonymous works. The bylines of the series and its anonymous works will show "Anonymous", but the byline of non-anonymous works will show the actual creators. To fix this, we have these options:

1. Add a warning after a work is edited to add a series: "Because this anonymous work is part of a series, others may be able to guess your identity." Allow the edit to succeed anyway.
2. Change the series byline to "anonymous, creator_name". We decided against this because (1) you still have a pretty good guess who "anonymous" can be and (2) this will contradict how bookmarked series search works (where a series is [indexed with creator "Anonymous"|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/e699d746172468ad819432753f72a41c6d99ff33/app/models/series.rb#L289-L291] if any work inside is anonymous).
3. Change all works in an anonymous series to be anonymous. This is unpredictable and we don't want to retroactively hide any works users never intend to hide.

We're going with option 1.

AM;557058:acee4fce-21cc-4291-8fa0-d813e774e099;Instructions for use: Before you start, you will need: - archivist's username (or new user, email and password) - collection name and display title (or new ones) - the name of the .pl database (probably ARCHIVE_DB.pl) - the relative path to where the archive files are stored (relative to otwarchive/) Run the rake task using "bundle exec rake massimport852:prospect[true]" (where true=send email notifications and false=don't send email notifications) *Notes:* - Relatively few of the author email addresses are in the .pl file, so most are collected from the HTML story files. Furthermore, the code only grabs the *very first* email address in the story and assigns that as the author. (Some of the stories have dummy emails embedded in the story, or list the email addresses of people who betaed etc, so this was safer than harvesting all the email addresses and making them authors, but may obviously lead to issues with stories that have multiple authors) - If the harvested email address matches that of an AO3 user, the story is added automatically to their works and a notification email is sent to say the story has been imported. - If the harvested email address doesn't match that of an AO3 user, the story stays assigned to the archivist (who is rather confusingly listed as the author in some views), but the email address is used to create a new External Author. 14/Nov/12 10:54 AM;557058:1804058f-89f5-4734-8604-8bb294f3deef;OK, update: this was not in fact related to the async code or to the number of works
on a tag, but to the search engine reindexing, which wasn't being fired off for subtagged
works. 

The search engine should now be told to reindex results for all works and bookmarks
tagged even in subtags and subtag synonyms. A bunch of the code in the tag model had
to be touched for this so sadly it needs a really good banging. :/ 

The reindexing of works and bookmarks will also now have a batched delay (firing off
every 7 minutes and every 13 minutes respectively) for performance. 

To test: 

- find some tags that have a bunch of subtags and synonyms, ideally where the subtags
themselves have subtags and synonyms
- with each of those tags, try one of the following: 
* give one a new synonym and make sure all the syns and subtags move over (on the edit
page) and all the works move over (on the works page)
* give one a new meta tag and make sure it and all its subtags and works move over
* remove the subtags and make sure all the subtagged works go away
* remove a synonym and make sure the synonym-tagged works go away

Remember that the works pages will NOT update right away -- it will only happen once
the reindexing completes. To be safe give it 10 minutes and if it hasn't happened,
it's not working. 

BACK END NOTES FOR DEBUGGING:

*** If the synonyms/subtags don't appear on the edit page, Resque may not be running.


*** If the syns/subtags appear on the edit page, but the works don't refresh, check
in console to see if the work ids have been put into redis: 

> $redis.smembers("search_index_work")

in which case the rake task rake search:reindex_works may not be getting run by cron,
try running it manually and see if it works.

When you enter the field, VoiceOver will give you a lot of information about the field, and the information will end with some instructions: “Type text, or to display a list of options, press Control - Option - Space.”

After you press Control - Option - Space and enter some text, you _should_ be able to press the down arrow on your keyboard to make VoiceOver read through the suggestions. This does not happen. In fact, nothing happens other than your text being entered.

The default instructions are a bit confusing because they suggest you can get a list of options before you type, but it’s _probably_ familiar to people—the search box on the Google homepage behaves the same way. 14/Dec/13 6:42 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;*nods*

In the majority of instances, word-wrap and word-break both work, just a little differently:
word-wrap lets the word get as long as it can be within the container, even if it means
pushing it onto another line, while word-break only lets the word get as long as it
can on the line, effectively letting us choose between adhering a bit closer to the
users' input or prettying up the input to preserve the layout a bit more. For example,
if the user puts in a 12-character word and line 1 can fit 10 characters, but line
2 can fit 20 characters, word-wrap will put that word on the second line, while word-break
will spilt it across two lines.

The problem in the inbox isn't with wrapping the text, but with the default display
of the fieldset element. While it's possible to make the text in the inbox wrap with
a combination of break-word, pre-wrap, and an explicit width on the container, the
fieldset element won't shrink accordingly, so you're still left with horizontal scrolling
for the entire window. There are a variety of workarounds, all of which have down sides.
I opted for horizontal scrolling for the inbox form's content because it'll do something
to improve the experience for Firefox users who are viewing an inbox page with an overly
long word (they'll be able to use the filters on that page), but it won't have a negative
affect on that page for anyone else (or, worse, a negative affect on all inbox pages).

v0.9.2.21

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1.  When creating or editing the Challenge Settings for a prompt meme, set "Number
of prompts per signup" Required to a number greater than that for Allowed
2.  Hit "Update"
3.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

The blue-backgrounded message at the top of the form says:

If you set the "Required" value higher than the corresponding "Allowed" value, we will
automatically assume that you want the allowed value to be the same as the required
value. You only need to manually set the "Allowed" number if you want more allowed
than required.

So, I'd expect to get a prompt meme with Required and Allowed both set to the number
I entered for Required.  Instead I get a prompt meme with the settings as I entered
them.

Please use labels and text to provide additional information.

A prompt meme set up with Required > Allowed is impossible to sign up for.  The Signup
form has only the number of prompts allowed available, so filling it out completely
and then submitting it always gives the error:

Sorry! We couldn't save this ChallengeSignup because:

You must submit between <Required> and <Allowed> requests to sign up for this challenge.
You currently have <Allowed>.

If you set Allowed to zero (regardless of what you set for Required), this issue http://code.google.com/p/otwarchive/issues/detail?id=2476
makes it so you get an error message.  However, for any non-zero Required number, it
would make more sense to simply set Allowed=Required, as the form text implies will
happen.

Note that leaving Allowed blank causes it to be set to zero rather than to the value
of Required (on Beta).

Summary: works index pages cache needs to be invalidated whenever work on the page is orphaned/deleted
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3426
Currently when a work is deleted or orphaned, the works index page cache is not invalidated

We were trying to do this manually with a cache sweeper but it has a lot of problems.


Instead, I've now reworked so the cache key itself will change (and thereby invalidate
the cached stuff) automatically whenever the contents of the page should change. 

The cache index key is now made up of:
+ The @owner type and id -- @owner is eg the tag  in .../tag/TAGNAME/works, or the
user in /users/USERNAME/works, or the collection in /collections/COLLECTIONNAME/works

+ The count of works belonging to that @owner

+ The updated_at timestamp of the most recently updated work belonging to that @owner


How this invalidates: 

* The count will capture a change in any works that were orphaned/deleted
* The most recently updated-at value will capture new works or edited works
* Can't orphan/delete and keep the count the same except by posting a new work with
new updated_at

In addition, the redis queue will touch now works when they get reindexed because of
wrangling changes, which will un-stale their filters; that will be on the 7min delay
but that seems reasonable. 

See the revised index_cache_key method in works_controller.

not been approved.

This issue seems to also be present for moderated anonymous and/or unrevealed collections,
although for unrevealed ones it is less obvious because the work shows up as a "Mystery
Work" on the Works page.

Summary: Revamp em scale, increase line height, make skin of old values
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
*Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3462*

*What archive revision are you testing on? (See the version label in the footer, for example v0.8.13.8.)*

0.9.4.2

*If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:*

Any

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*

# Set your browser font size 
# Expect the main text of the Archive to respect that

*What is the expected output? What do you see instead?*

If I set my browser font size to 12px, I expect the majority of the Archive's text to be 12px. Instead, it is in 10.5px because our main text is set to 0.875em (0.875 x 12 = 10.5). Work text is 11.3px instead of 12px because the work font size is set to 1.08em (0.875 x 1.08 x 12 = 11.3). The default font size setting of most browsers is 16px, so most users see the majority of our text at 14px (0.875 x 16 = 14).

While some browsers will let me set a minimum font size, this is less than ideal if I want the font to be larger: just because I want to see most text in 24px doesn't mean I want to force the date on work blurbs to be 24px as well.

Additionally, 0.875em is not a pleasant number for coders to work with. Check out our
front end documentation and compare the numbers from [The Scale in Ems to the numbers from Our Em Scale|http://otwcode.github.com/docs/front_end_coding/em-scale.html ].

We end up using awkward numbers that we have to round to the nearest thousandth, and sometimes browsers differ in the way they round numbers. For instance, we frequently use 0.25em.

0.25 x 14 = 3.5. 

Opera rounds this down to 3px while Safari rounds it up to 4px.

We currently use 1.286 to set our line height to 18px for most users (1.286 x 14 = 18). We use unitless line height, not ems, but it is the same principle and needs to be adjusted along with the rest of the scale. However, instead of just changing it to 1.125 to keep lines at roughly 18px, we will increase it to 1.5 in order to meet the [Web Content Accessibility Guidelines|http://www.w3.org/TR/2008/WD-WCAG20-TECHS-20080430/C21.html].

I'm also copying the old numbers into a skin so Support can direct any unhappy users that way. (Alternatively, they could decrease their browser's default font size and rarely have to see size 16 body text anywhere on the web...)

NOTE: Please do mention if you notice issues with:

* inconsistency with other things on the archive
* how this might work for screenreader/mobile/other devices or users with other accessibility issues
* overlap with other features or gap left between features
* the clarity and conciseness of the text
* how well one action flows to another
* how intuitive you find the correct actions
* if not intuitive, how badly things go wrong if you do what you find intuitive

Summary: Duplicate and invalid Collections can be created by submitting the form twice very fast
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3475
What archive revision are you testing on? otwarchive v0.9.4.2

What steps will reproduce the problem?
Fill a New Collection form, and submit it twice very fast.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

The second submitting should be rejected. Instead, duplicate collections are created.
Because they're duplicate, they are invalid. Uniqueness needs to be enforced at the
database level.

Reported here: [https://otw.16bugs.com/projects/4911/bugs/248568|https://otw.16bugs.com/projects/4911/bugs/248568]

Note that in order to add a uniqueness constraint at the database level, we first need to handle any pre-existing collections with duplicate names. Otherwise the migration won’t run (if it’s a standard migration) or it will remove duplicates (if it’s a {{pt-osc}} migration).

As in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5923|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5923|smart-link], a PR for this issue should probably include the following:

* A rake task to rename duplicate collections (e.g. “Collection” => “Collection_2”).
* A migration to add the uniqueness constraint. 

h2. Deploy notes

For the Staging deploy please follow the testing instructions.

For the production deploy:

After deploying, run the rake task: {{bundle exec rake After:rename_duplicate_collections}} 

*After* that task has been run successfully, run the migration (with departure): {{rails db:migrate:up VERSION=20260728014110}}

h2. Testing instructions

This needs to be tested by a database admin and can only be tested once as part of the deploy to Staging

# On the linked user collections page, there should now be only one collection named {{TestingPromptMemesAgain2}} and one collection named {{TestingPromptMemesAgain2_7867}}
# Run the migration (with departure)
# As a smoke test, log in as a user and try to create a collection with the same name as another collection. You should get an error as usual

13/Jun/20 11:57 AM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;When you use {{ChaptersController#post}} to post the first chapter of a multichapter draft, the sequence of code is, roughly:

{noformat}@chapter.posted = true
@chapter.save
@work.save
@work.update_attribute(:posted, true) unless @work.posted?{noformat}

After the first two lines, {{@chapter.posted}} is true, and that value has been saved to the database.

The third line is where things get weird. The work model has this callback, intended to post the first chapter when the work changes from unposted to posted:

{noformat}  # If the work is posted, the first chapter should be posted too
  def post_first_chapter
    chapter_one = self.first_chapter
    if self.saved_change_to_posted? || (chapter_one && chapter_one.posted != self.posted)
      chapter_one.published_at = Date.today unless self.backdate
      chapter_one.posted = self.posted
      chapter_one.save
    end
  end{noformat}

[(Source)|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/6ce960255567efa9550046db4c70fc37f5e80992/app/models/work.rb#L641-L649]

At this point, however, the work is still unposted, but the chapter is posted. So {{chapter_one.posted != self.posted}}, and the code inside the {{if}} block will run, setting {{chapter_one.posted}} to false and saving. This means that in an attempt to post the chapter, the work callback ends up _unposting_ the chapter (temporarily).

The last of the four lines fixes this, because the work is unposted. The same {{post_first_chapter}} callback ends up reposting the first chapter again.

However, the {{set_word_count}} callback runs before the {{post_first_chapter}} callback. This means that it correctly calculates the word count the first time the work is saved (because the chapter was set to posted before the callback), but incorrectly calculates the word count the second time the work is saved (because the chapter is still unposted when the callback runs).

The result is a {{nil}} word count. I’m not sure why the word count would spontaneously fix itself after a few minutes, though. (Presumably something else calls {{save}} or {{update}} on the work again?)

Summary: Comment threads squished on narrow displays
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3528
What archive revision are you testing on? 0.95

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:
Any page with threaded comments, like a work chapter or a news post.

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Expand the comments section.
2. Make or find a series of replies 3+ levels deep.  (more levels makes the problem
worse)
3. Shrink your browser window (if you're not already on a phone) to ~300px wide.

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?
Comment boxes should remain wide enough to read the text inside. Instead, the indenting
for replies makes them very narrow, to the point where they can only fit one word per
line.


=== user did some investigation in their ticket, pasting below: ===

There is a comment on the “Meta” news post pointing out that comments, and in particular
long comment threads, are difficult to view on a mobile device. They are so narrow
that you can get one letter of each word stacked vertically when you have a small screen.

This is caused by two things:

The div with the ID of feedback (the one that encloses the comment form and all comments
on news and work pages) has some left and right margin space in ems. This is not overridden
on the mobile stylesheet.

Two, the indentation that visually shows the threaded nature of the comments is a left
margin of 3ems on .thread .thread.

Therefore, on a mobile device, comments on any post or work have a lot of whitespace
on each side, and that whitespace increases with larger fonts, since that’s how ems
work.

My suggestion, which I’m afraid to type out in code since your system strips so many
characters, was to add to the mobile stylesheet some code that would change that indentation
to two percent, rather than 3ems, so that the size of the indent is dependant on screen
width rather than the size of the font. Also, if you remove the right and left margin
from the div “feedback” on that stylesheet, that excess margin space goes away too.
The result is a lot more space for comments and a lot less unnecessary margin allowing
a more subtle indentation that still visually cues threading.

My initial thought was to simply make a skin to do this. The commenter also said that
on a wider screen there is a great deal of white space to the left of the comments
as well, so I thought offering users a full width comment option would be nice.

I made a skin, which has a parent that puts a negative margin on the div “feedback”
for non-mobile view, allowing it to stretch over into the space left for the dashboard
list on the left of the div ID of “main”. I then chained to that a skin that would
make my suggestions above apply on mobile view.

However, your actual mobile style sheet uses a media condition of both screen size
of less than 480 pixels and handheld. Your skin system just uses handheld as a media
type, so I don’t trust any code in it to trigger on all narrow widths and override
the code in the parent skin. Your skin system should produce media conditions that
match your base stylesheet. I could not submit my skin to be made public, or suggest
it to anyone, since any mobile device that didn’t load CSS under handheld, and there
are a bunch, would have a borked view.

Summary: Batch wrangling and general overhaul of tag wrangle pages
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.

Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3531 Note: This feature requires familiarity with the wrangling interface. We want the “Wrangle” page for tags (i.e. the ao3.org/tags/TAGNAME/wrangle, such as http://archiveofourown.org/tags/Homestuck/wrangle ) overhauled to simplify the wrangling process, especially to give us batch-wrangling features so we can wrangle multiple tags at once. Currently many wrangling actions require us to open individual tag edit pages, which is very time consuming, as well as putting more load on the servers. Batch wrangling is essential if wranglers are to keep up with the volume of new tags we are seeing on the Archive now. Detailed feature description (see attached mockup) Please note: every different table should be slightly different, featuring different columns and different batch-wrangle actions. The mockup is an example "All" page for Characters. General changes: 1. "edit tag and parent associations" button text changed to "edit [TAGTYPE] tag & associations" to make use clearer 2. Text change "showing [TYPE] [TAGTYPE]" to "showing [TYPE] [TAGTYPE] tags" to be clearer (e.g. "showing canonical characters" changed to "showing canonical character tags") 3. "Add new characters" removed from page (function is still available from the above-linked page) 4. "Batch-wrangle tags" section added, with various actions listed to be applied to all selected tags: Mark as Canonical, Mark as Unwrangleable, Remove from This [TAGTYPE], and Wrangle to Fandom with a selection box (allowing us to mass-add the tags of one fandom to another fandom, such as moving Marvel chars to new movie fandoms) All of these actions, if applied to a tag that is already canonical or unwrangleable, should just be skipped without an error message 5. "Wrangle" buttons removed (as now superfluous) 6. Changes to mass-wrangle table: * Canonical & Synonym columns merged (saves room and is easier to read & understand; making tags canonical now a batch-wrangling feature) * Batch-wrangling checkbox column added (with all/none selection buttons) * Tag comments column added, showing comment count if >0 linking to comments; or else added "comments" button in "Manage" column * "Remove" button removed from the "Manage" column (moved to batch wrangling) * "wrangle" button removed from "Manage" column(except possibly on the "Mergers" page for fandoms/make the "wrangle" page otherwise accessible?) Batch-wrangling features on specific pages: * Viewing tags: "All" ** Batch-wrangling: Mark as Canonical, Mark as Unwrangleable, Remove from This [TAGTYPE], and Wrangle to Fandom with a selection box * Viewing tags: "Canonical" ** Batch-wrangling: Remove from this fandom, wrangle to another fandom ** "Canonical" column removed (superfluous!) * Viewing tags: "Non-canonical" ** Should be changed to "Synonyms" as per previous request, and show only synonyms ** Batch-wrangling: Remove from this fandom, wrangle to another fandom ** ("Canonical" column renamed to "Synonym to"? Not required; keeping it Canonical/Synonyms is fine) * Viewing tags: "Unfilterable" ** Batch-wrangling: Mark as canonical, Mark as Unwrangleable, Remove from this fandom, Wrangle to another fandom * Viewing tags: "Unfilterable" ** Batch-wrangling: Mark as canonical, Mark as Unwrangleable, Remove from this fandom, Wrangle to another fandom ** "Canonical" column removed (superfluous!) * Viewing tags: "Unwrangled" (moved to last position, as makes more sense???) ** Batch-wrangling: Add to this fandom (will add all checked tags to whatever fandom you are wrangling in, without having to enter the fandom name into the box), Wrangle to another fandom (to easily dispose of No Fandom tags!) ** Canonical/Synonym column should remain, as occasionally canonical tags do end up unwrangled by mistake and it's good to be able to see these! * Viewing tags: "Unwrangleable" ** Batch-wrangling: Mark as wrangleable (the only feature, as unwrangleable tags should be marked as wrangleable before we do anything else with them, else they risk getting lost...) The same features should be available on the Characters and Freeforms lists. Batch-wrangling features are probably not necessary on other tags with children (Characters, Media) other than "remove from this tag" (which can be left as a separate check button if that's easier; training-wise it would be preferable to have them have the batch-wrangling feature as well, but only have "remove from this tag") (copied from https://transformativeworks.basecamphq.com/W5232636 )

There is an assumption that feeds and downloads are stored on shared storage.

This is an issue with the feeds as they are all in a single directory and there are
too many for the nas to have that many directories in a directory.

The right answer is to have a resque or rabbitmq queue so that when a feed needs updating
it will place a task on the queue and the first web server picks up the task an deletes
its copy ( creating another task for any other web server ).


The current work around is to delete all the feeds periodically ( currently every 24
hours ), this task runs every 2 hours from cfengine.

Original name was “Submitting the work post/edit form without a title and/or with too few words of work text makes the choice to Post Without Preview vanish”

*What archive revision are you testing on? (See the version label in the footer, for example v0.8.13.8.)*

v0.9.6.12-ish

*If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:*

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*

1.  Submit the work posting (or edit) form without a title and/or at least 10 words of work text, either by choosing Preview or Post

*What is the expected output? What do you see instead?*

Expect to be able to fill in the missing information and then have the option to either Preview or Post. 

*What do you see instead?*

Instead the Post button has turned into "Please wait....", so the only option for posting is now to Preview first.

*Please use labels and text to provide additional information.*

Having only the fandom and/or warnings missing gives a flash error message and does not cause the Post button to go away.

This issue was introduced as a side-effect of Issue 2757, "Add Javascript to prevent double submission of forms". (AO3-2754)

It apples to any form that uses the aforementioned JavaScript and that has LiveValidation fields that require input (or input of a certain length), including but not limited to:

* logged out comment form, when neglecting to enter a name or email
* support form, when neglecting to enter a summary or comment

[Additional note|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/3982#pullrequestreview-617094477] from Sarken regarding the solution:

{quote}I think we need to make sure the LiveValidation error is resolved before we reenable the submit button. If we don't, it's just going to do the "Please wait..." thing all over again without the user having any idea what's going on. (And if for some reason the button _isn't_ stuck in that state due to a LiveValidation error, but rather because the site or the user's connection is horrendously slow, we definitely don't want to [automatically] reenable the button [after a certain time] and let the user resubmit the form.)

I think the best thing to do is going to be scroll the user to the first field with the error, make sure it and all the other errors are resolved, and then reenable the button.{quote}

*Testing notes*

Please see if this helps with the problem in other locations that disable the submit button when the fields are not all filled in:

* comment form (logged out is the best to test)
* chapter form
* support form

That's the general idea of what we're doing -- locating the hidden class and removing
it -- but we don't have one single function in our application.js that covers all the
instances of hidden classes across the site. We do a lot of showing and hiding things
in a lot of different patterns (e.g. items we always want showing if the user has JavaScript
enabled, items we only want showing after the user has clicked something else) with
more than a few different class names, and were, I suspect, making a lot of stuff up
as we went along, so it got away from us before anyone said, "Hey, we should have one
standard way of doing this."

So now we have a case where we have a bunch of little bits of JavaScript scattered
throughout our partials, and, if I remember correctly, in some helpers, too. Someone
could attempt to clean it up, but I can absolutely guarantee stuff will be missed and
it will be a nasty, unpleasant project for planning, coding, and testing. It would
be lovely to have it fixed, but, well...

Anyway, what's going on here is we used the hidden class to make the Share button on
your own bookmarks hidden when JavaScript is disabled, since the Share buttons do awful
things and aren't even useful if you have JavaScript disabled. That's the $j(".actions
.hidden").removeClass("hidden"); in the bookmarks/_bookmark_owner_navigation partial.
But we also use the hidden class to toggle the Expand Fandoms List and Collapse Fandoms
List button in the user/_contents partial. When you're on your own dashboard, both
of those partials are used at once, so $j(".actions .hidden").removeClass("hidden");
latches onto the hidden class on the Expand/Collapse buttons and removes it. So we
end up with both buttons visible initially. When I click the Expand button, it does
$j("#collapse-fandoms").toggleClass("hidden");$j(this).toggleClass("hidden"); -- and
thus the hidden class is added back to *both* buttons and they go bye-bye. To fix it,
all I have to do is add the bookmarks class to make it $j(".bookmarks .actions .hidden").removeClass("hidden");
-- then it will only target hidden action items within the bookmark blurb.

THIS IS ALL MY FAULT. It was a last-minute fix for a problem with the Share boxes and
the new modals. I also added it to the Share portion of works/_work_header_navigation
and am going to tweak the targeting on that, too, just so it never causes a problem
like this there, either. And for double stupidity, I failed to take into account that
the contents of bookmarks/_bookmark_owner_navigation are rendered once per own bookmark,
so now we have pages that have <script type="text/javascript">//<![CDATA[$j(".actions
.hidden").removeClass("hidden");//]]></script> TWENTY FREAKING TIMES.

Oops, fml, etc.

*Steps to reproduce:*

The bookmarks should appear on the default pseud's bookmark page, ideally within a few hours.

The bookmarks continue to exist (e.g. if you go to the work you've bookmarked, you'll see "Edit Bookmark" rather than "Bookmark" at the top), but never show up on the default pseud's bookmark page. h2. What should happen

Due to issues such as [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5696|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5696|smart-link] causing confusion for users, we'd like to resolve this by:

* creating a rake task to remove all current orphan_account user subscriptions
* removing the ability to subscribe to any works/series solely owned by orphan_account (as these will never be updated, it doesn't make sense to allow new subscriptions to them). Users should receive a message saying: {{You cannot subscribe to this [work/series] because it has been orphaned and will not receive new updates. You can bookmark it instead.}}

Orphaning a work/series should not affect existing subscriptions to that work/series. 

It should still be possible to subscribe to works or series that are co-created with another user (who could still update the work/series).

Summary: Admin wrangler tracking sometimes is inaccurate
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.

When logged in as an admin, we can view the last wrangler to make a change to a tag in a "last updated" line at the bottom of the tag edit page.

However, sometimes this report is entirely incorrect. For instance, on the above tag, the wrangler is listed as:

{quote}Last updated by Zebra on 2013-05-30 14:10:22 \-0400

{quote}
Which is impossible, as Zebra is a retired wrangler who has not had wrangling permissions for several months before the date given.

We're not sure what causes this error \- whether the username is correct but the date is wrong, or that the update date is correct but the username is wrong. As we use wrangler tracking to find wranglers who are wrangling incorrectly, it's crucial that we have accurate tracking.

*Notes*

A tag’s last_wrangler is set using a before_save callback on the Tag. However, a tag’s updated_at can be changed without editing the tag – for example, if I wrangle a freeform into a fandom, the CommonTagging model will touch the tags, changing their updated_at date. 

Maybe the way around this is adding a new column, like edited_at, which can have its date set at the same time the last_wrangler is set. 

However, Tag Wrangling note that “we often get last updated dates of weeks or months earlier, for fandoms that are consistently busy,” so there is probably another issue at play that causes a tag’s updated_at not to change when CommonTaggings change.

05/Jul/19 10:38 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;I’ve been poking around, and I doubt I’ve found everything that causes this, but I think I might know one potential cause. Oddly enough, it’s linked to AO3-3631.

When a new {{CommonTagging}} is created – such as when a relationship has a new fandom added – the autocomplete for the child tag needs to be updated, so that e.g. the relationship is listed in its parent’s fandom. This works fine if the new parent is added while editing the child tag, because editing the child causes the child’s autocomplete info to be updated.

This also works if the new parent-child relationship is added while editing the parent, though it initially looks like it shouldn’t. Adding a new {{CommonTagging}} always touches the child tag, but this doesn’t trigger the autocomplete update. However, adding a new {{CommonTagging}} while {{User.current_user}} is set does trigger an update to the autocomplete. This is thanks to a callback in {{CommonTagging}} that tries to keep track of the last wrangler, and updates the autocomplete as a (possibly unintended, but useful) consequence. Hence the connection to AO3-3631.

But there are some cases where {{CommonTaggings}} can be added when {{User.current_user}} is not set, which doesn’t update the autocomplete. For example, the {{Tag#add_merger_associations}} function is called asynchronously, and I believe that Resque doesn’t set {{User.current_user}} for asynchronous wrangling jobs (which causes some of the failures in wrangler tracking). This means that any {{CommonTaggings}} added as a result of synning two tags may not be picked up by the autocomplete.

I think you should be able to replicate this bug with these steps:

# Log in as a tag wrangler.
# Create two canonical fandom tags: Canon X and Canon Y.
# Create two relationship tags: Ship A and Ship B.
# Edit Ship A and add it to Canon X.
# Edit Ship B to make it canonical and add it to Canon Y.
# Check the autocomplete on the New Work form by entering “Canon X” for the fandom, and then try typing a space in the relationships field to trigger the autocomplete. It should say “(No suggestions found)”.
# Edit Ship A and add Ship B as its synonym.
# View Ship B and note that Canon X has been added as one of its parents.
# Check the autocomplete on the New Work form by entering “Canon X” for the fandom, and then typing a space in the relationships field. It ought to list “Ship B” as a suggestion, but it doesn’t. (Make sure you open a new copy of the New Work form, since I think the results can be cached.)
# Edit Ship B and press “Save changes” without making any changes, to fix the autocomplete.
# Notice that Ship B now shows up in the autocomplete for Canon X.

(Unfortunately, I’m not sure this can be replicated in automated tests, because the async calls are performed synchronously in the same thread in the test environment. This means that {{User.current_user}} is always set properly, and so the autocomplete is always updated.)

There might be a similar way to break all relationships in a fandom by synning one canonical fandom (with children) to another. And I’m not sure why the autocomplete might be broken for a fandom that hasn’t had any recent synning. But I think this might contribute to some autocomplete issues.

Description:

otwarchive v0.9.6.16

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:

What steps will reproduce the problem?
0. Be an Open Doors staffer with admin powers
1. Manage the aftermath of a mass import 
2. Need to delete some duplicate works, e.g. by user request

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?
The user gets an email that reads "Your story has been deleted by our Abuse team" and
panics a bit. It should ideally say "by our Open Doors team", in such a case. 

In issue 3455 we introduced a new kind of deletion notification, primarily with Abuse
cases in mind - before that, deletion by Abuse would only deliver the usual "your work
was deleted by you" notification, confusing users. However, now it only checks if the
deleter is logged in as an admin (cf. app/models/work_observer.rb).

We need to expand on the use case of admin deletions and do one of the following: 

- create a general "by an admin" template
- hook it into the admin role architecture started in issue 3064
- make sure it correctly reflects who deleted what in some other way

- Selecting Log Out

Summary: Specify media type for new fandom tags created in the context of tag sets
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3752
Issue: when new fandoms are added to a tag set, they are added as "Uncategorized Fandoms"
and must be wrangled before they get slotted into correct media categories, often under
time pressure given that tag sets are used for challenges. 

The tag set moderator or tag nominator should be able to specify the media category
for a new tag being added so wranglers do not have to wrangle the tags in order to
have them appear in the right category within the challenge. 


*** A design decision is required between the following two options: ***

1) Have the new tag be wrangled into the specified media category. 

2) Have the tag be associated with the specified media category only within the tag
set. Wranglers will still have to wrangle the tag into the given category officially.



The effect for the tag set will be the same. For the wranglers, #1 means less work,
#2 means more oversight. 

I'd lean towards #1 because the category selection is limited (people cannot add new
media types, they have to choose from a pull-down to specify) and the person adding
the tag is presumably as much an authority on it as we could expect to get, especially
since they know better than we do whether they mean the movie or the book version of
whatever fandom they're adding etc. So I don't see a huge advantage to taking on the
extra work. 

But either option can work fine to at least remove the time pressure from the wrangling.
Comment:
22/Sep/13 10:36 AM;557058:56c6aaf0-abec-4140-88a3-59aa2f24c990;Wrangling staff discussed this and would prefer option 2 - Have the tag be associated
with the specified media category only within the tag set. Wranglers will still have
to wrangle the tag into the given category officially.

(The main reasons for preferring option 2 is that fandoms with assigned media "get
lost" in the media bins; they'll get attended to quicker if they appear in the main
fandom bin.  As well, many fandom tags are potentially cross-media or ambiguous, so
would need to have other media added anyway when they're on the archive proper.  Also
we have a ton of problems with overlapping tag set and wrangling code - wranglers "screwing
up" tag sets by wrangling tags while they're in a tag set - so the more separation
between them the better.)

However, if option 1 is substantially easier to code we can work with it!

When a tag is canonically wrangled (typically a fandom added or removed) the changes
are not reflected in any tag sets where that tag appears. This happens because the
tag set view cache isn't expired after wrangling. 

Probably the right fix for this is to add some code to the tag_sweeper to go through
any owned tag sets where the tag appears, and expire the tag set view cache there.
(See tag_set_sweeper for the way to expire the tag set view cache.)

Summary: Race conditions can create duplicate or invalid signups that cause assignments to crash
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3815

otwarchive v0.9.10.7

A signup can be created that is a duplicate or invalid by the rules of the challenge.


This issue is essentially impossible to reproduce because it only occurs if there's
a hiccup in the server, generally due to extremely high volume of signups. It happens
occasionally during Yuletide signups. The most common cause of an invalid signup is
a duplicate of an existing prompt. 

This isn't a case that can be avoided easily because the rules of each challenge are
substantially different and there isn't a SQL condition that can be put in the database
to prevent the insertion of these Rails-invalid records. 

Afterwards, if not cleaned up, the duplicate signup will cause doubled assigning and
the invalid signups will cause assignments to crash (and even worse, silently, because
they are running in the background).

I think probably the best imperfect solution would be to put a check for validity on
the individual signup "show" page. This is the page the user gets redirected to from
signup creation. It could check just that user's signups for a duplicate signup for
the same challenge, or if the new signup is invalid, and possibly clean it up right
then. 

The downside of this is that it violates the RESTful concept where going to a "show"
page should not change anything. But given that this is not something where we can
solve the underlying cause (it's a known and accepted part of Rails that this can happen,
see the Concurrency and Integrity section here http://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActiveRecord/Validations/ClassMethods.html),
I think it's probably the right thing to do.

*Stop saving user agent strings for comments*
Not viable. We save user agents on comments so comments can be marked as spam later. Akismet requires user agents in all spam reports.

*Use a fallback user agent string if the real one is too long*
e.g. {{AO3-hand-spam}}. This is an easy fix. Unknown whether it will make spam detection less accurate.

*Introduce some code the hack down the length of the user agent string so it won't be too big for the column*
This is an easy fix, however, we risk polluting our Akismet dataset and making spam detection less accurate.

*Make the column able to handle longer user agent strings*
This is the lawful good fix, which requires a database migration on the big comments table. However:
- There's no max limit for user agent strings, someone will exceed whatever limit we set.
- "If strict SQL mode is not enabled and you assign a value to a BLOB or TEXT column that exceeds the column's maximum length, the value is truncated to fit and a warning is generated." ([MySQL docs on BLOB/TEXT|https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.0/en/blob.html]).

If you are new to CSS, here are the basics:
A line of CSS code looks pretty much like this: selector {property: value;}

The selector is either the name of an HTML tag (like body or h1), or it can be an id
or class that has been set on a tag. The property is what you want to change in the
contents of that tag (for instance the font size), and the value is what you want to
set it to.

Examples:

Inside the "body" tag, set the font size slightly larger than the baseline: body {font-size:
1.1em;}

15/Jul/19 5:40 AM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;I suspect this might be happening because [the default scope on Bookmarks orders by ID|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/dd6ca1180f875ae8def2b21b7b78adc68c805c1f/app/models/bookmark.rb#L16]:

{code}  default_scope -> { order("bookmarks.id DESC") } # id's stand in for creation date{code}

Further calls to {{order}} don’t override the order set by this scope; they add to it. So calling {{order('RAND()')}} in a bookmark query generates SQL with {{ORDER BY bookmarks.id DESC, RAND()}}. That results in bookmarks being sorted by ID, with any ties broken randomly. (Though I’m not sure how that could show the oldest bookmarks, instead of the newest ones.)

I think the fix is either to delete the default scope (and fix up any queries that rely on that default order), or update any queries that order bookmarks to call {{reorder}} instead of {{order}}.

h2. Purpose
From the [ebook-convert documentation|https://manual.calibre-ebook.com/generated/en/ebook-convert.html#cmdoption-ebook-convert-toc-threshold]:

{quote}\-\-toc-threshold
If fewer than this number of chapters is detected, then links are added to the Table of Contents. Default: 6

{quote}
So basically what was happening was, if the work had fewer than four chapters (because four actual chapters, plus preface and afterword equals six) and it had work or chapter endnotes, you'd end up with "notes" as a TOC entry.

This was weird, since it's not like we were also adding entries for the beginning notes or summary. It was even weirder if you had multiple end notes because only _one_ of the endnotes would be linked because, by default, ebook-convert does not allow you to have two TOC entries with the same name.

So anyway, we're going to stop it from turning "notes" into a TOC entry.

Post a work with at least one endnote and less than four chapters and make sure "notes" does not appear in the download file's table of contents.

23/Feb/16 1:40 AM;557058:85e7b59e-f3ad-4868-81c9-145d4251c741;Unfortunately, the issue Lady Oscar noticed appears to be due to time zones. Although this pull request correctly detects the time on an external work, there is no time zone information, so the Archive interprets the imported time as being its default of EST (GMT-5). So to illustrate, using the equivalent UTC date-time:

1. Manually posted in the HST time zone with a date-time of "2016-02-21 08:20:00" = UTC "2016-02-21 18:20:00"
2. Manually posted in the HST time zone with a date-time of "2016-02-21 08:27:00" = UTC "2016-02-21 18:27:00"
3. Imported with a date-time of "2016-02-21 08:26:00", which is interpreted as EST = UTC "2016-02-21 13:26:00"

Because the Archive can't tell the time on the latter is supposed to be in the HST time zone, the imported work has an earlier date-time than the manually posted ones.

There is no solution to this problem, as we can't detect time zones in external works that don't contain them, so this is likely to cause more confusion than it resolves. The pull request was reverted and this being closed as Won't Fix.

Summary: Remove expensive counts from work index caching check
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3893
Currently, when you hit a works index page for a tag, pseud, user or collection, we
cache the results but do some expensive database counts to check whether or not the
cache should be expired. Instead of doing that, we want to expire the cache keys when
the data is updated.

Testing cheat sheet:

Stuff that should expire the works index cache for a tag:
-a new work is posted with that tag
-a work with that tag is updated
-a work is edited to add the tag
-a chapter is added to a work with that tag
-a work with that tag is deleted
-a work with that tag is edited to remove the tag
-the tag gains or loses a synonym
-the tag gains or loses a subtag

Stuff that should expire the works index cache for a user or pseud:
-the user posts a new work
-the user updates a work
-the user adds a chapter to a work
-the user deletes a work
-the user is added as an author to an existing work
-the user is removed as an author to an existing work
-the user orphans a work
-a work by the user is added to an anonymous or unrevealed collection
-a work by the user is removed from an anonymous or unrevealed collection
-a collection that includes a work by the user is changed to no longer be anonymous
or unrevealed

Stuff that should expire the works index cache for a collection:
-a work is added to the collection
-a work in the collection is updated
-a chapter is added to a work in the collection
-a work is removed from the collection
-a work in the collection is deleted
-the collection stops being anonymous or unrevealed

Summary: Can't reorder tags on a work
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
*Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3945*

*What archive revision are you testing on?* 

v0.9.14.5

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*

# Post a work with some tags
# Edit the work and change the order of some or all of the tags
# Update, with or without previewing first

*What is the expected output?*

Expect to see your tag order changes. 

*What do you see instead?*

Instead, the tags are in their original order.

*Workaround*

Remove all tags, update the work, edit again, then re-add in the order you want.

*Notes*

This bug exists because tags (taggings) are not given a particular assigned order, as they would be if we used acts_as_list (which we use for ordering chapters, for example). Instead, tags are listed on the work in the same order they exist in and are retrieved from the database. Since reordering doesn’t destroy and recreate the taggings, this order doesn’t change.

*We have not yet decided on the proper approach to fix this.* Two possible solutions:

* Destroy and recreate all taggings when reordering. This might be somewhat inefficient (e.g. it might lead to works' filters being unnecessarily recalculated and the work being unnecessarily reindexed).
* Use acts_as_list to make the order explicit. This would require a migration of the taggings table, and we’d also need to determine whether tags should be ordered as one big list, or with each type (fandom, relationship, etc) as its own list (in case we want to change how tags are displayed in the blurb, e.g. make characters come before relationships).

The "Matching" page would not load for many challenges after the potential matches
are generated. This is because the page included a list of all the potential givers
for each participant, sorted by quality of match, which for a challenge where users
can end up with many potential matches caused the page to take way too long to load,
so it timed out. 

In addition, the potential matches page was a hideous mess of inconsistent separate
forms for dealing with various issues, including users without potential matches, users
who didn't have an assignment, etc. 

The fixes: 

- The Matching page now looks like the attached screenshot. Tabs at the top allow the
moderator to see and handle each set of issues separately. (Each tab is paginated as
well, in case of a large challenge.) 

- You should be able to click on the assignment ID link to see the assignment in detail.


- You should be able to X out and change the recipient or the giver. Xing out the giver
will produce an autocomplete of all the potential matches for the recipient, Xing out
the recipient will produce an autocomplete of all the potential matches for the giver.


- Known issue: if you change BOTH, you can create an incompatible assignment -- there
isn't a way to avoid this without making this a live-edit form, which would be the
ideal but not in the cards at this time. 

- You can leave the fields blank to create an assignment with no recipient or no giver.


- The help file and brief instructions should hopefully be fairly clear! Suggestions

tags that they no longer want to have marked unwrangleable.

3531.)

Summary: Get rid of tags in collections links
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3961

*How to reproduce:*

As described in AO3-3345, we have the following problem:

1. Go to a work in a collection from the collection page - make sure that the link
is to ao3.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME/works/####
2. See that the tag links in the header box link to the tags within the collection
(e.g. ao3.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME/tags/TAGNAME/works rather than just ao3.org/tags/TAGNAME/works)
3. Go to the main listing of the work ao3.org/works/###
4. See that the tags still link to ao3.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME/tags/TAGNAME/works
rather than the expected ao3.org/tags/TAGNAME/works

This is because work blurbs are cached and shared between:

- ao3.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME/tags/TAGNAME/works
- ao3.org/tags/TAGNAME/works

We have a similar problem for child tag links, cached and shared between:

- ao3.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME/tags/TAGNAME
- ao3.org/tags/TAGNAME

*How to fix:*

This particular behaviour is due to caching, and is theoretically fixable. However,
after due consideration, we have decided that getting rid of the tags-in-collections
links altogether would be a better use of everyone's time and save Support from dealing
with users bewildered by being trapped in a collection.

Please consult the comments on AO3-3345 concerning the location of the code that
needs to be removed to eradicate the above behaviour. 
(And add tests to replicate the steps above to verify that the problem is forever gone)

Make sure that we don't break the tags-in-collections links on ao3.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME/tags and ao3.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME/fandoms.

Summary: Commas in Chinese and Japanese scripts do not register as tag separators
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 3965
Commas in some scripts do not register as commas, so users inadvertently make tags that
are actually several tags combined into one, for example:

百里屠苏，方兰生
http://archiveofourown.org/tags/%E7%99%BE%E9%87%8C%E5%B1%A0%E8%8B%8F%EF%BC%8C%E6%96%B9%E5%85%B0%E7%94%9F

(this should be two different tags, combined they are unwrangle-able)

This definitely happens with Chinese and Japanese language tags; it may happen with
other non-Roman alphabet scripts as well.

Users can still make separate tags by hitting "enter".

Unicode commas such as ， should either register as commas and cause a new tag to be
created, or else not be allowed in tags at all, to prevent this confusion.

2. Go to a translation for a post

It only has the few last posts. This is reasonable when you're posting translations
in general (because we post translations of relevant, current posts).

loses the connection to the old post, and to mark it as a translation we're forced

attached to a newer, incorrect post.

appear in it.

A way to fix it is to make the drop down keep the older post (avoid it getting unstuck).


Ideally, though, we would prefer to have a field in which we could input, for example,
the post number.

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*
1. Log in
2. Hi, username! > My Dashboard
3. Skins
4. Create Site Skin
5. Fill in a title and some CSS
6. Submit
7. Look for the navigation in hopes of getting back to your skins
8. Edit
9. Look for the navigation in hopes of getting back to your skins

*What is the expected output? What do you see instead?*
On the skin show page:
- The navigation options used to be positioned on the right, like the rest of our navigation,
and the options were Work Skins, Public Skins, Remove Skin, My Skins, Create Skin.
- The options are currently positioned on the left and they are Revert to Default Skin
and Create Site Skin.
- I'd expect them to be Revert to Default Skin, My Site Skins, My Work Skins, and I'd
expect them to be on the right. I'd also expect them to be at the top of the home header
module, since that's where the actions usually are in such modules, and the icon should be directly after the h2. (See screen shot.)

On the skin edit, skin new, and skin new wizard page:
- The navigation options used to be Work Skins, Public Skins, Remove Skin, My Skins,
Create Skin, Use Wizard Instead?
- The options are currently Revert to Default Skin, Create Site Skin, Write Custom
CSS, Use Wizard. 
- I'd expect them to be Revert to Default Skin, Write Custom CSS, Use Wizard, My Site
Skins, My Work Skins.

(Note that Revert to Default only appears if you're using a skin, which is correct.)

- The copy currently says, "A site skin lets you change the way the Archive looks in
your browser, so you can customize your reading experience. You can use work skins
to customize the way your own works are shown to others."
- It's been brought to our attention that this is both fic-centric ("reading experience")
and assumes the user is browsing visually ("looks in your browser" -- work skins cannot
have different media types, so "shown" is probably okay), even though we also allow
users to create stylesheets for any media type: http://www.w3.org/TR/CSS21/media.html#media-types
- If you wanted to get ambitious, the My __ Skins indexes should probably be home zones
with spiffy header modules.

15/Dec/16 8:50 PM;557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0;*Why this happened:*
We take away the input field after you choose a tag, and that confuses browsers. In some (e.g. Safari 10.0), focus would stay on the now-hidden input, so you couldn't _see_ where it was, which was confusing, but at least hitting Tab would put it on the next field. But other browsers would just freak out and lose focus entirely, and you'd start back at the top of the page -- super annoying if you're halfway through filling out a form.

This less-than-desirable behavior would happen in any place we limit how many items you can enter in an autocomplete field. 

*What will happen now:*
After you arrow down or click to select the synonym, focus will be on the × for removing the syn -- then you can hit Enter to remove the tag and type a different one, or hit Tab to move on to the next part of the form.

Another good place to test it would be the URL field on http://test.archiveofourown.org/external_works/new. Type a little something in the URL field, select something from the autocomplete suggestions, and focus should go to the × near the URL you selected.

16/Feb/18 10:38 AM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;Maybe there was an update that decreased the load on the workers? (Or a configuration change?)

The code for removing a meta-tagging through the interface first calls Tag.remove_association asynchronously, and then when the meta-tagging is deleted it triggers an asynchronous call to Tag.remove_meta_filters. So if you have two meta-taggings being deleted with sufficient delay between the deletions, and the Resque utilities workers are very responsive (i.e. very few things on the queue, or a lot of workers), these steps get executed in the following order:

1. In the interface, remove Lowest Tag as a subtag of Middle Tag.
2. "Middle Tag".remove_association("Lowest Tag")
3. "Lowest Tag".remove_meta_filters("Middle Tag")
4. In the interface, remove Middle Tag as a subtag of Highest Tag.
5. "Highest Tag".remove_association("Middle Tag")
6. "Middle Tag".remove_meta_filters("Highest Tag")

That order ensures that when step 3 is executed, "Highest Tag" is still a meta-tag of "Middle Tag." So when dissociating "Lowest Tag" from "Middle Tag," it will correctly dissociate "Lowest Tag" from "Highest Tag" as well (deleting the associated filter-taggings, and updating the appropriate Elasticsearch indexes).

However, if step 3 occurs after step 5 instead, the association between "Middle Tag" and "Highest Tag" will be gone when step 3 is executed, and "Lowest Tag" will never be dissociated from "Highest Tag." This leaves an incorrect, invisible meta-tagging in place, as well as all of the filter-taggings associated with that meta-tagging (and because the Elasticsearch filter_ids are built from the filter-taggings, Elasticsearch also gets it wrong).

I simulated this by suspending the workers while I made the changes in the interface, then re-enabling them. With only one worker, suspending the worker will cause it to fail every time; with more than one worker, there's a slim chance that the sequence of steps would work out, but it's still very likely to fail. In theory, suspending the workers should behave similarly to when all of the workers for the utilities queue are busy with other tasks.

I can also simulate it without suspending the workers by performing the two meta-tagging changes in a single edit (editing the Middle Tag and checking the boxes to remove both "Highest Tag" and "Lowest Tag"), which seems to cause it to fail pretty consistently. But I'm only running two workers, so I don't know if that would work with more.

23/Apr/22 5:34 AM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;Because of a minor error in the way that the cache key is set in {{comments/single_comment}}, comment caches are never expired even though they look like they have {{expires_in: 1.week}} set:

{code:ruby}      <% cache(key: "/v2/single_comment/#{single_comment.id}/#{single_comment.edited_at}/#{single_comment.updated_at}", expires_in: 1.week, skip_digest: true ) do %>{code}

[(source)|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/59bb5ebc3ca4fa86056b410d922152905b8cc179/app/views/comments/_single_comment.html.erb#L17]
Because the cache key is passed as a keyword argument, and the cache function expects at least one non-keyword argument, all of the keywords are converted into a hash and passed as the first argument to {{cache}}, which is then converted into a key that looks something like this:

{noformat}ao3-v2-dev:views/comments/_single_comment:8234591ee9f225dc96ab3129de848d1f/localhost:3000/works/18?expires_in=604800&key=%252Fv2%252Fsingle_comment%252F370%252F%252F2021-06-17+20%253A50%253A44+UTC&skip_digest=true{noformat}

That key is then cached with no expiration. The only way the cache ever gets expired is if someone replies to the comment, someone edits the comment, or memcached runs out of space and starts deleting old caches (which is extremely unlikely, because production has oodles of extra memcached space).

Obviously fixing that wouldn’t completely address this issue, because it’d still be good to have the name update immediately instead of in a week, but if the expiration were working and the problem fixed itself in a week, it might help cut down on the complaints.
