Summary: Potential match progress indication crashes when there are more than 1000 signups
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 4136
What archive revision are you testing on? (See the version label in
the footer, for example v0.8.13.8.)



If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Find a challenge with (substantially -- at least 100-200 or else you'll probably
miss it) more than 1000 signups
2. Run potential matching
3. Reload the potential matching page and watch the progress indicator tick along
4. After the potential matching passes the 1000th signup, try to reload the potential
matching page
5. You get a 500 error

The progress indicator is the only part that's broken -- potential matching is actually
continuing on in the background. The issue is with this code in potential_match.rb:

    unless REDIS_GENERAL.exists(collection_byline_key)
      score = 0
      collection.signups.pseud_only.find_each do |pseud|
        REDIS_GENERAL.zadd collection_byline_key, score, pseud.byline
        score += 1
      end
    end

This code populates the "collection_byline_key" set with the pseuds of every user who
has signed up, which enables a progress indicator to be calculated by finding the rank
of the current user being processed inside the set. 

find_each is supposed to go through all the items in batches of 1000 (to avoid excessive
memory usage), but for some reason it is only doing one batch. As a result, this code
only puts 1000 names into the bylines list, and when we look for the rank of name 1001+,
redis doesn't find it in the list, so it returns nil and nil/1000 causes the 500 error.

The fix for this is to replace "find_each" with just "each". 

A temporary workaround is to just wait for the potential matching to complete (the
collection owners will be emailed when this happens), or if the progress indicator
is really needed, a senior coder can fix the collection bylines list in the production
console by running this small block of code:

collection = Collection.find_by_name(COLLECTION NAME GOES HERE)
collection_byline_key = PotentialMatch.byline_key(collection)
score = 0
collection.signups.pseud_only.each do |pseud|
  REDIS_GENERAL.zadd collection_byline_key, score, pseud.byline
  score += 1
end

http://archiveofourown.org/admin_posts

What steps will reproduce the problem?

2. Instead of creating a new news post for a translation, click on 'Edit' by mistake
3. Replace the English text with the translated text
4. Select the language and mark it as a translation

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

Someone doing this by mistake would expect the translated news post to appear.
What actually happens is the English news post disappears; the existing post gets replaced
with a translation added to the latest news post (regardless of the original post having
been selected in the posting screen—that post disappeared, after all).
Any translations posted previously still remain linked to the original post, and clicking
on the link they show leads to the new translated overwritten version.
The overwritten post disappears from the news and tag listings.

When this happened, we tried to fix by replacing the post with the original English
content. We could select "English" as the language, but as we could not select for
it to be a translation of no post, it became listed as an English translation. The
mistake was finally fixed by using browser developer tools to manually re-add and select
the Please select option: <option value="" selected="selected">Please select</option>.


It would be good if there were a warning when one tried to overwrite a previously published
English post with a translation

Summary: Investigate Dalli
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 4178
https://github.com/mperham/dalli
https://rubygems.org/gems/kgio

I decided to write Dalli after maintaining memcache-client for two years for a few
specific reasons:

The code is mostly old and gross. The bulk of the code is a single 1000 line .rb file.
It has a lot of options that are infrequently used which complicate the codebase.
The implementation has no single point to attach monitoring hooks.
Uses the old text protocol, which hurts raw performance.

So a few notes. Dalli:

uses the exact same algorithm to choose a server so existing memcached clusters with
TBs of data will work identically to memcache-client.
is approximately 20% faster than memcache-client (which itself was heavily optimized)
in Ruby 1.9.2.
contains explicit "chokepoint" methods which handle all requests; these can be hooked
into by monitoring tools (NewRelic, Rack::Bug, etc) to track memcached usage.
supports SASL for use in managed environments, e.g. Heroku.
provides proper failover with recovery and adjustable timeouts

Note to testers, there should be nothing to test.

differently than the button on Tags pages. Yet it uses the same term, possibly leading
users to expect the same behavior. The former buttons result in an Archive action;
the latter's function is browser-dependent.
* Browser support: IE handles feeds natively and automatically. Firefox can natively
support feeds as Live Bookmarks if enabled. Chrome and Opera do _not_ natively support
RSS without an extension. The current wording includes a verb, indicating action, but
at least two browsers don't do anything beyond load a page.
* Translation: "Subscribe" provides issues in translation, and will result in very
long buttons in some languages.

After discussion on Coders mailing list and discussion with Docs and Translators, a
simple label of "RSS Feed" will probably be the best, moving forward. We probably want
the orange icon as well.

Summary: Story parser extracts spurious metadata from story text
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 4267
What archive revision are you testing on? (See the version label in
the footer, for example v0.8.13.8.)

0.9.54

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Import an external work which has a line starting with "Warning: <random ramble>"
in the middle of the story
2. Discover that the random ramble has been imported as a freeform tag because of the
fix for Issue 3732

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

In order to import from a variety of external sites like LiveJournal or people's personal
webpages, the story parser tries to scrape metadata from the raw HTML of the external
page by looking for lines starting with e.g. "Warning:", "Characters:", "Pairings:"
etc. Authors are particularly prone to inserting facetious warnings which will result
in false positives like this. The fix for Issue 3732 guards against actual warning
tags being created but still results in freeform tags being created instead. A similar
issue will occur with notes, which may create unwanted author notes if a story paragraph
begins with "Note:".

In the case where the external site is under our control (for OD mass imports), the
story parser needs to be amended not to parse the text it has identified as the chapter
content for metadata. This problem is not resolvable for other external sites as there
is usually no code-discernible distinction between the metadata and story text.

In a couple cases, we had {{ArchiveWarning}} tags that could not be converted because a {{Freeform}} with the {{ - Freeform}} suffix already existed. This happened with {{ Wincest}} (note the leading space) and it was necessary to use the Rails console to replace the suffix’s dash with an em dash (making the converted tag {{Wincest – Freeform}}), per Tag Wrangling procedure. (If the em dash version already exists, Tag Wrangling’s next resort is an en dash.)

{code:ruby}User.current_user = Admin.find_by_login("admin-sarken")

aw = ArchiveWarning.where(name: " Wincest").first
 => #<ArchiveWarning id: 3751475, name: " Wincest", canonical: false, created_at: "2014-12-24 06:46:30", updated_at: "2014-12-24 06:46:30", taggings_count_cache: 1, adult: false, type: "ArchiveWarning", merger_id: nil, delta: false, last_wrangler_id: 82382, last_wrangler_type: "User", unwrangleable: false, sortable_name: " Wincest">

 => "Wincest — Freeform"

aw.save
 => true{code}

Also in a few cases, we had tags that couldn’t be converted because the {{ArchiveWarning}} had a leading space _and_ there was a {{Freeform}}with the same name and no leading space. In this case, we used the Rails console to add the regular {{- Freeform}} suffix to the warning tag before rerunning the rake task.

{code:ruby}User.current_user = Admin.find_by_login("admin-sarken")

aw.name = "sexual situation - Freeform"
 => "sexual situation - Freeform" 

aw.save
 => true {code}

Summary: Mass import URL checker should only search for exact matches
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: AD&T Chairs
Description:
Originally reported on Google Code with ID 4307
What archive revision are you testing on? (See the version label in
the footer, for example v0.8.13.8.)

0.9.62

If appropriate, enter the URL of a page where the problem can be seen:

What steps will reproduce the problem?
1. Use the mass import API to import story A with the URL http://temporary.site/12345
-- it gets imported as http://ao3.org/789
2. Use the API import checking functionality to see whether story B with the URL http://temporary.site/123
has been imported yet
3. The Archive helpfully responds that story B is at http://ao3.org/789 - which is
actually where story A lives

What is the expected output? What do you see instead?

Expect to be told that story B hasn't been imported yet.

The API's URL checker uses the same method in the Work model as the redirect tool to
match an external URL to an AO3 work. Unfortunately, if it doesn't find an exact match,
the redirect tool performs increasingly fuzzy matching to account for end users importing
with query parameters etc. The final fallback is a partial match for any work whose
original URL *contains* the URL it is searching for. So "http://temporary.site/12345"
becomes a match for "http://temporary.site/123".

Since the API is only used by OpenDoors, we can assume that they will use consistent
URLs when importing and then searching for a URL. The API should only perform exact
matches. The redirect tool should remain as is.

Summary: Live search for fandoms and media pages
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. [The All Fandoms Page|http://test.ao3.org/media]

h2. Behavior With JavaScript Enabled
1. There will be a "Search for fandoms" field with no submit button.
2. Enter two or more characters in the text field.
3. There will be a 500 millisecond delay after you last enter text in the field before the search begins.
4. A list of fandoms containing the text you entered will appear beneath a header specifying X Fandoms Found; the name of a fandom will link to the fandom's works page. If no results are found, no fandoms will be listed, but the 0 Fandoms Found header will appear.
5. The list will update when you add or remove text from the "Search for fandoms" field; when there are less than two characters in the field, the header and list will roll up and disappear.
6. When results have loaded, screen readers should tell you how many results have been found.

Note that the list of fandoms is cached for 4 hours for performance, so newly-canonized fandoms may not appear immediately.

h2. Behavior With JavaScript Disabled
1. There will be a "Search for fandoms" field with a "Search Fandoms" submit button.
2. The search field will behave like a [Tag Search|http://test.ao3.org/tags/search] where "Fandom" has been selected from the dropdown menu and "Canonical" has been checked. The page will reload and then display the results with the same as the JavaScript version ("X Fandoms Found" header, a list of fandom names that link to the fandoms' works pages).

h1. A Fandoms Page (Ex: [Movie Fandoms Page|http://test.ao3.org/media/Movies/fandoms])

h2. Behavior With JavaScript Enabled
1. There will be a "Search for fandoms" field with no submit button.
2. Enter two or more characters in the text field.
3. There will be a 500 millisecond delay after you last enter text in the field before the search begins.
4. A list of fandoms containing the text you entered will appear beneath a header specifying X Fandoms Found; the name of a fandom will link to the fandom's works page. If no results are found, no fandoms will be listed, but the 0 Fandoms Found header will appear.
5. The list will update when you add or remove text from the "Search for fandoms" field; when there are less than two characters in the field, the header and list will roll up and disappear.
6. When results have loaded, screen readers should tell you how many results have been found.

h2. Behavior With JavaScript Disabled
1. The page will be the same as it currently is, with instructions about in-page search but no search field: "You can search this page by pressing CTRL+F or CMD+F and entering what you are looking for." (It doesn't make much sense to build a new search function that will require a page reload when all possible results are already available in a neatly alphabetized list.)

h1. Other Notes

Description:
The "published_at" field in chapters is a Date object instead of a DateTime object. Because this information is used to set the revised_at field for works, we routinely lose time information about when creations were published, which causes them to be (eg) displayed out of order, especially in automated tests where they get published within seconds of each other.

The CSS parser we use retains only one declaration for each property, meaning that rulesets like

Summary: Mass import: Chapter content and metadata overrides work metadata
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Ariana
Description:
*Background*
The StoryParser which imports external works is designed to detect metadata in the external content. This metadata overrides any information provided in the mass import API request, and also processes the API metadata incorrectly in some scenarios.

*What steps will reproduce the problem?*
Scenario 1:
# Use the API to import a work with no metadata in the chapter contents
# Specify both the work's title and the titles of each chapter in the API request
# Discover that the Archive now has a work whose title is the title of the first chapter

Scenario 2:
# Use the API to import a work whose content includes incorrect metadata (or text that looks like metadata, like a paragraph that starts with "Pairing:") 
# Specify the correct metadata in the API request
# The Archive now has a work with a whole paragraph as its pairing

*What is the expected output?*
I would expect the metadata in the API request to override any information the StoryParser thinks it has found in the story itself.

The desired solution is for the content metadata to be used only if the related field isn't provided in the API request.

Summary: Store sortable name on subscription object
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Elz J
Description:
In order to sort subscriptions by title/name, we currently get all subscriptions for a user in the subscriptions controller and then for each one, we go get the subscribed object in order to compare it to the user's other subscriptions. If a user has many subscriptions, then this page will perform very poorly and make a very large number of database calls.

In order to improve this, we could add a "sortable_name" field to subscriptions as we have on works and tags. Then we can do the sorting in the database and only retrieve the subscriptions that we need, as well as eliminating the extra n+1 queries to the subscribed works/series/users.

Challenges: there are a lot of subscriptions in the database, and we'd need to add a column to the table and then run a background rake task to populate it for existing subscriptions. Will probably take a while to run.

For the bug causing the subscriptions page to error if the user is subscribed to a deleted object but the subscription itself fails to delete, see AO3-4728.

Summary: Translation: Make emails translatable and all the locales work
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Cesy Avon
Description:
All the bits and pieces required to make emails translatable. AO3 interface translation will be tackled after emails are translatable.

Emails are the first target for internationalization (i18n) because they have less edge cases than the AO3 interface. This will allow us to develop standards and workflows for i18n within a smaller scope. Once these standards are developed they can be used for the larger project of making the whole interface translatable.

Making an email translatable involves moving all strings to the locale ({{.yml}}) files by converting from {{ts()}} to {{t()}} according to the [i18n standards|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Internationalization-%28i18n%29-Standards] and ensuring that the mails are sent with the locale set in the preferences by the user.

The locale preference for users is behind a rollout that can be enabled with {{$rollout.activate_user(:set_locale_preference, User.find(000))}} in the Rails console.

Ideally, translatable emails should have [mailer previews|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6776] to simplify testing the translated emails.

As the [i18n standards|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Internationalization-%28i18n%29-Standards] have been largely established, the AO3 interface is now made translatable whenever it is touched during other work. However, email i18n is still the priority until the complete i18n workflow is more fleshed out, so tasks specific to the interface i18n (caching, handling of locale in URLs etc) are still under discussion.

Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
First, get thee to the skin wizard:
1. Log in
2. Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Skins
3. Create Site Skin
4. Use Wizard

Or just go to http://test.ao3.org/skins/new?wizard=true

From there? Where to begin, where to begin...

1. The fields are all in one jumbled mess. Let's break them out into sensible chunks, e.g. a section for basic information, another for fonts, and another for colors.

2. Provide more information about the fields on the form instead of making users click the help text... but not by putting in in the label. For instance, instead of the field label saying, "Foreground color (name or hex code)," the label should be "Foreground color" and there should be a footnote-style message beneath the field telling users to format it as a name or hex code. If we use aria-describedby, it'll be read for screenreaders, too.

3. For clarity and accuracy, some labels should be changed. "Foreground color" label should be "Text color", "Font family" should be "Font", "Margin width" should be "Work margin width", and "Percent of base font size" should be "Percent of browser font size". The text on the skin's show page should match.

4. Entering a "Font" should do a better job of changing the font. Right now, for example, it fails to change the font on form buttons, e.g. Subscribe, Favorite Tag, or the font on the header's links. (Note: This can continue to change only the main font. Anything in Georgia, e.g. headings and the site name, should remain in Georgia. In the future, we can give users an ~accent font option for those.)

5. Entering a "Header color" should change the red parts of the header. Right now, it changes the white part. /o\

6. Entering an "Accent color" should change most of the grey parts, e.g. forms and the dropdown menus in the header. Right now it changes the dashboard, meta, and behind the icon in the header.

7. Entering a "Work margin width" should actually adjust the work margins in a fairly predictable way. Right now it really doesn't because of the max-width on the work area.

8. Entering a "Percent of browser font size" should increase or decrease all font sizes on the Archive by that percentage. Right now... idk. (This name is still a little misleading -- as you may know, most, but not all, of the Archive doesn't use your browser's font size, but rather a size that's ~87.5% of the default. Other name suggestions are appreciated.)

9. If a skin was created with the wizard, the edit link should drop you directly in the wizard.

10. If you create a skin with the wizard, you should also be able to add custom CSS to the same skin to override or tweak it, e.g. if you make the "Header color" a light pink and don't change anything else, you can choose "Edit," switch to "Write Custom CSS", and enter 
#header .heading a { color: purple }
to make the site name more readable on the white background. Right now, if you try to add custom CSS to a wizard skin, it completely overrides the wizard skin.

*Before this is deployed to staging,* make and apply a skin with the current incarnation of the wizard. This pull request includes an after task that will let you keep your existing wizard skin(s) as they now look. Why you'd _want_ to, I don't know, but...

Notice there's a fairly dramatic shift in the size of the margins.

We'd like to increase the margins to get rid of or reduce that shift.

*There are a few pages that need their margins adjusted separately, so after confirming that the margins in the midsize and narrow views are generally bigger than they currently are on production, please also check:*
1) the inbox has the same margins as the rest of the site in regular, midsize, and narrow views (in regular view, the best way to check this is to look at your inbox and your works page -- there used to be bigger space between the dashboard & comments and comments & filters than there was between the dashboard & works and the works & filters, but now they should be the same)

4) that work text has slightly bigger margins that the rest of the site in the midsize view (it should be approximately the same as it is on production)


Some math to explain where the new 3.5% margins came from:

Assuming the user is used to browsing at 62em and they are using a default browser font size of 16px, their browser width is 992px. The margins are created by applying 2.5em of padding to the #main area, which has a font size of 0.875em, or 14px, making the margins 35px on either side (2.5 x 14). So in a 992px window, the margins each take up 3.5% of the page width.

But why assume they were used to browsing at 992px instead of, say, 800px, where the 35px margins would make up 4.3% of the page? Mostly because we're trying to keep the margins small, and because it will reduce the amount of jarring changes that happen as we go from normal to midsize to narrow.

Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.

Description:
Note: While it's possible to edit a work to have no fandom on both staging and production, staging does _not_ appear to give a 500 error. 

Here is the work I (as testy) was able to create the error with on production: http://archiveofourown.org/works/6485314

1. Log in
2. Post > New Work
3. Fill in the form
4. Post Without Preview
5. Edit Tags
6. Choose the "x" next to the fandom tag to remove it
7. Post Without Preview

You may or may not receive a 500 error immediately after posting. You will probably need to wait a few minutes for the error. It might not even work! Isn't this fun?

Regardless of whether the 500 error happens, however, you will _not_ be able to add a chapter to the work:

8. Add Chapter
9. Fill in the form
10. Post Without Preview
11. The new chapter form will just keep reloading without an error or success message, and the chapter count may increase to something odd like 2/1 with no new chapters visible on the work, e.g. http://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1061566 (note that if you go to the Edit page for the work, you _can_ see the chapters listed above the form, so they're... sort of there, sort of not)

Ideally, we should make it so accessing a work without a fandom does not give a 500 error _and_ we should make sure you cannot save a work without a fandom by following the steps above. Just stopping the 500 error would be a big improvement, though.

Tracing the error points to trying to call the name method on nil in https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/controllers/works_controller.rb#L223

Much like we did with fandom tags, we want to add a sortable_name column to the languages table so admins can set an optional name to use for alphabetization. If no name is set, it should continue to fall back to the abbreviation (short_name).

That process should go like:

4. Enter an optional name to sort on (e.g. Suomi) in a text field labeled "Name for alphabetical sorting"
5. Update Language
6. Voila ! Suomi is now with the other S-languages on the Language menu and in the list of translations on any news post that uses it

We want to do this via a new sortable_name column rather than using the languages' actual names to avoid having all the languages that begin with non-Latin characters ending up in a jumble at the end.

Summary: Potential match limitations not working leading to loss of mysql connection
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: shalotta
Description:
When potential match and assignment generation go on too long, the process can lose its mysql connection and cause the entire process to fail. In combination with a process that was restarting failed resque jobs automatically, this was leading challenges to restart matching endlessly until manually killed. (See http://wiki.transformativeworks.org/mediawiki/Database_Admin_Things_-_AD%26T#Stopping_runaway_challenge_matching)

Potential matches are supposed to be limited to a max per challenge participant (currently 50), which has the effect of significantly speeding up matching because a great deal of time is spent generating unnecessary matches for participants who are highly flexible and can match many other individuals. These matches are then all compared against each other during assignment generation to select the "best" match, which further slows the process. 

The limit however never made it into cfengine and was therefore not being applied. In addition, while investigating this issue I realized that for a small collection, the absolute cap of 50 does not make much sense. Therefore, the cap has been changed to now be the smaller of 50 or 10% of the participants in a collection, with a floor on the cap of 10, in the case of very tiny collections (like the ones in our test suite). 

This new process has been manually used on a small challenge of 133 participants that was crashing repeatedly due to the lack of limits and produced successful results (3 people unassigned as giver, 3 as recipient, about as good as we expect to get for most challenges) while completing in literally one tenth of the time. 

The values POTENTIAL_MATCHES_MAX and POTENTIAL_MATCHES_PERCENT and POTENTIAL_MATCHES_MIN need to be added to cfengine.

Summary: Inviting a work to an anonymous or unrevealed collection makes it anonymous or unrevealed
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
Short version: invite a work to your anonymous or unrevealed collection and it will be anonymous or unrevealed, regardless of whether the creator has accepted your invitation.

Step-by-step version:
1. Log in as user1
2. Collections > New Collection
3. Fill in required information and check "This collection is unrevealed" or "This collection is anonymous" or both
4. Submit
5. Log out
6. Log in as user2
7. Hi, user2! > My Preferences
8. Uncheck "Automatically agree to your work being collected by others in the Archive."
9. Update
10. Post > New Work
11. Fill in required information
12. Post Without Preview
13. Log out
14. Log in as user1
15. Navigate to the work user2 just posted
16. Choose the "Add To Collections" button at the end of the work
17. Enter the name of your anonymous or unrevealed collection from earlier
18. Add

The work will now be unrevealed or anonymous, even though user2 has not accepted the invitation.

What should happen instead is the work should remain visible unless or until the creator accepts the invitation.

Marking high priority because it essentially allows anyone to hide a work, which has a fairly high potential for abuse. Fortunately, the creator can work around this by going to Hi, username! > My Collections > Manage Collected Works and choose the "Remove" option for the affected works. However, the work can still be re-invited (and thus re-anoned or re-hidden).

Summary: Give certain admins the ability to remove pseud icons and update pseud descriptions
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Matty Lynne
Description:
Policy & Abuse needs the ability to remove pseud icons and update pseud descriptions. 

*Design/Testing*

* On [https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERS/pseuds|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERS/pseuds], admins with the policy_and_abuse or superadmin role should see the “Edit” link on the blurbs. Other admins should not see the link.
* They should be able to follow said “Edit” link to access the pseud edit page, [https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERS/pseuds/PSEUD/edit|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERS/pseuds/PSEUD/edit]. Other admins should not be able to access this page.
* Assuming there is an icon uploaded for the pseud, admins who can access the pseud edit page should be able to check the “Delete your icon and revert to our default” box and press “Update” to remove the icon. 
* Admins should also be able to modify the pseud description field.
* They should not be able to save changes to any other fields; ideally, the fields would be disabled.
* At the bottom of the edit form, there should be an "Ticket ID (required)" field that is only present for admins. It should have a footnote specifying only numbers should be entered, and it should be used to validate the ticket exists in Zoho, a la [AO3-6156|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6156].

When you save changes to the pseud:

If no number is provided, it should not save the change and should give the admin an error saying the field cannot be blank.

If a ticket with the number does not exist, the admin should not be able to save changes and should get an error message saying "Ticket ID must exist."

If a ticket with the number does exist, the change should be saved and a new admin activity log item should be created and displayed on the Activities admin page:

* the target should say "Pseud [name] ([user login])" and should link to the user's pseuds page ({{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/LOGIN/pseuds}}), where you can see the descriptions and icons for each pseud
** if the pseud is deleted after the activity is created, it should say "Pseud [id]" and the link should point to {{/admin/activities}}, as it does for other deleted items
* the summary should say "Ticket #000 for User #000", and it should link to the relevant ticket on Zoho (we don't want to record a summary of the text before the change because pseud descriptions can include personal information subject to privacy laws; however, including the user ID number will give us some info to work with if the pseud is later deleted)
* the time of the change and the name of the admin who made the change should also be recorded

Note for testers: While on the Activities admin page, please also locate an activity for a destroyed work, follow the link, and check the summary. It should be an ugly bit of text like {{#<Work id: 123, expected_number_of_chapters: 2, created_at: "2023-06-15 05:21:55.000000000 +0000", updated_at: "2023-06-15 05:25:49.000000000 +0000", major_version: 2, minor_version: 0, [truncated for length, since you probably get the idea now]>}}.

*Notes*

This should be done using the [ALLOWED_ATTRIBUTES_BY_ROLE|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/b63fce67a3975ec0614bb535c75d76c8dafbda71/app/policies/user_policy.rb#L15-L22] approach we’ve implemented in the user and admin settings policies.

Summary: Can't use keyboard shortcuts to copy text from help pop-ups and other modals
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
http://test.ao3.org/works/search

1. Open a help pop up by clicking a ? near a field name
2. Highlight some text
3. Press Ctrl+C or Cmd+C on your keyboard to copy the text to your clipboard
4. In another window or in a text area, press Ctrl+V or Cmd+V on your keyboard to paste

*What happens...*

The text that gets pasted is _not_ the text you expect to have copied. Instead, it is what was already in your clipboard.

If you highlight some text, right-click (or equivalent) on it, and select Copy from the context menu that pops up, you will be able to successfully paste the expected text. 

You _can_ Ctrl+C/Cmd+C to copy text from a text box in a modal (e.g. the Share code on http://test.ao3.org/works/###).

*What _should_ happen...*

I _expect_ to be able to copy and paste whatever text I darn well please using my keyboard shortcuts.


*What poking the code has led me to believe*

This is related to the killing of events from outside the modal with !targetInModal: https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/public/javascripts/ao3modal.js#L274 

It seems that the highlighted text on which you press Ctrl+C/Cmd+C does _not_ count as an event.target -- rather, the document is the event target, so targetInModal is set to false because the document has no parent element with the id #modal https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/public/javascripts/ao3modal.js#L267
Environment:
I tested and reproduced this in 
* Chrome 51.0.2704.103 (64-bit)
* Safari 9.1.1

There's a slight chance it might work in other browsers, but I doubt it.

29/Sep/16 5:09 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;There's a good chance that this is at least partly caused by caching issues. The updated_at field only has resolution down to the second, not the millisecond, so if two skin (or other) updates are performed within the same second, the cache key used to access the cached version of the data won't change between updates. But in order for caching to work properly (and always serve up the correct version of the data), the cache key has to change whenever the underlying data changes.

Long story short, if the tests run fast enough, the cache won't update properly, most likely leading to the two skin failures.

Summary: Improve API error handling and roll over to v2
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Ariana
Description:
The API was originally designed to mirror the behaviour of the existing StoryParser with minimal changes to the latter. Now that Open Doors are performing more semi-automated imports, the API needs better error-handling:

- the StoryParser currently throws a generic Error when anything goes wrong: it should return different errors depending on what happened
- similarly, the API relies on only a couple of HTTP status-inspired error codes and human-readable text messages to communicate errors - it should define a broader set of possible error codes and use the same ones for work and bookmark imports where appropriate
- it should not use HTTP statuses to communicate information beyond simple success/failure

The purpose of all this will be to allow API clients to take action automatically based on the errors, without breaking existing behaviour for manual imports.

*Testing*
Testing will involve checking that manual imports are unchanged, and API testing will happen using a mass import temporary site.

*ETA*: In order to implement this without breaking existing Open Doors import sites (about half a dozen already lined up), I am taking this opportunity to roll over the API version to v2 to accommodate the improved error codes and messages.

Summary: Download and Chapter Index menu positioning issues
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce/What happens

# Using a desktop browser, go to a multi-chapter work.
# If you're in Entire Work mode, choose "Chapter by Chapter" from the work navigation.
# Choose the Download option at the top of the work to open the menu.
# Choose the Chapter Index option at the top of the work to open the menu.
# Slowly decrease the width of your browser window, observing the behavior of the menus.
## At full width, assuming the navigation is all on the same line, the menus may overlap if they’re both open at the same time.
## As the screen gets narrower and the buttons wrap onto two lines, the menus may obscure the Download button, making it impossible to close the menu.
## Once the narrow stylesheet is triggered, the menus jump very high on the screen, overlapping the main navigation. If you just opened them at this width, you might not notice they opened because they’re so far removed from the buttons.
# Drag your window back to a wider width.
# Disable JavaScript in your browser. (This is no longer possible with Safari. It’s possible in Chrome, but in my experience, the message at the top of the screen sometimes disappears mid-resize, which slightly affects behavior, so Firefox works best.)
# Reload the page.
# Slowly decrease the width of your browser window, observing the behavior of the Download menu as you do. (The Chapter Index menu is not available when JavaScript is disabled.)
## It’s the same as 5a-c, but without JavaScript, it is always open.

h1. What should happen instead

h2. JavaScript enabled

The menus should always be positioned directly below the buttons that trigger them. While they may still overlap other buttons, you’ll always be able to close them to access those buttons.

h2. JavaScript disabled

With JavaScript disabled, the download menu should be displayed in a way that does not obscure other items on the page. (The Chapter Index menu will remain a link to the full page index.)

h3. Limitations

# With Javascript enabled, you will probably briefly see a flash of the non-JavaScript version when the page first loads. This is normal and happens currently, but it will probably be more noticeable with the new menu style.
# The menus may run partially off the edge of the screen if your screen is narrow and your font size is large. In the current version, this happens with the Chapter Index menu, but not the Download menu.
# If we ever want to add a button _after_ Download, it will look a little goofy because the button will move down below the open Download menu. 
# When JavaScript is disabled, the alignment of the Download header and buttons is slightly off, but it didn’t seem worth the code needed to fix a minor cosmetic issue. 

h1. Deploy notes

An admin will need to update the Reversi skin with the [latest Reversi CSS|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/public/stylesheets/masters/reversi/reversi_site_screen_.css]. 

Systems will need to run the recache skins playbook.

h1. Testing notes

Please repeat the “Steps to reproduce” using the Reversi, Low Vision Default, Snow Blue, and Dark Mode skins, which should all be in the footer. Please ensure the menus as well as the Chapter Index and Download buttons themselves have reasonable colors applied.

Additionally, please repeat them with a wizard skin that changes the background and accent colors and ensure they are applied to the menu:

# Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Skins > Create Site Skin > Use Wizard
# Fill in the fields for Title, Background color, and Accent color
# Press “Submit” to save
# Press “Use” to apply 

Note that there is an existing bug in the Low Vision Default skin that makes the skin chooser buttons and true buttons (i.e., not links styled to look like buttons) in the work navigation turn into red text on a red background with a red border on hover or focus. ([AO3-7151|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-7151]) This will apply to the Chapter Index and Download buttons now, since I have switched them from links to buttons.

Summary: Challenges: Speed up gift exchange matching
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
We'd like to explore speeding up challenge matching through the following methods:

(1) Reduce SQL queries in ChallengeSignup.match and Prompt.match. (Challenge signups are bounded in size by limits set in ArchiveConfig, so it should be feasible to load the complete signup into memory, and avoid taxing the database with excessive queries.)

(2) It might be useful to process signups in small batches, to further reduce the load on the database.

(3) The current code reduces the set of signups to examine based on overlapping tags, and then runs ChallengeSignup.match on all candidate pairs of signups. But ChallengeSignup.match compares all of the prompts pairwise. For many exchanges, it might be faster to try to generate potential *prompt* matches through a similar overlapping-tag method, and then group up the potential prompt matches based on the offer signup id and request signup id (cutting down on the number of calls to Prompt.match).

Summary: Mass Import: Add option to turn off metadata detection
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Ariana
Description:
The StoryParser is designed to scrape metadata from the web pages it imports. However, this often results in rubbish tags being imported. Some specific problems have been addressed in AO3-4383 and AO3-3724 among others, but additional tags still scoop up rambling nonsense. In some cases, these are also invalid tags which make the import fail. 

When Open Doors are performing more semi-automated imports where the metadata is provided directly from the external site's database, there is no need to detect the metadata from the content - it's provided in the API call. There should therefore have an option to allow the detection to be turned off.

Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Ariana
Description:
When Open Doors are preparing an external archive import, they must search manually for every work on the Archive to avoid importing duplicates where creators have already imported their own works. Possible fields to match on would be: title, author pseud and fandom (or associated fandom). The full work blurb fields should be returned so the human checkers can decide whether that's the same work.

Summary: Add comment freezing to all comments
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Ariana
Description:
In order to prevent discussions in work and news post comment threads from getting off-topic and becoming distressful to users, we want to introduce LiveJournal-style comment freezing to the Archive.

The broad specifications for the feature are as follows:

* *Works:* the feature should be available only to work owners and policy_and_abuse and superadmin admins
* *News posts:* the feature should only be available to AO3 admins
* *Tags:* the feature should only be available to tag_wrangling and superadmin admins
* When available, it should add a toggle button with initial text *Freeze Thread* and alternate text *Unfreeze Thread* to each comment in a thread
* When a valid user clicks on *Freeze Thread* on a comment, it should:
*# toggle the button to *Unfreeze Thread*
*# NOT hide any of the comments in the thread
*# hide the *Reply* button
*# prevent anyone from adding a reply to that comment and any child comments (i.e.: back-end check - don't rely only on removing the button)
*# display a message or some clear visual and non-visual indicator on the frozen comment to indicate that the comment thread is frozen
*# apply all of the above to each child comment as well
*# still allow people to reply to parents and ancestors of the frozen comment

* Clicking on *Unfreeze Thread* on a comment should:
*# toggle the button to *Freeze Thread*
*# remove any visual indication that the comment thread is frozen
*# display the *Reply* button
*# allow anyone to reply to the comment and all its children

We suggest starting this work by implementing all the above steps as Cucumber tests, and discussing any design questions in Slack.

Summary: Hits to the most recent chapter of a work should increase the hit count
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
*Current behavior:*
A multi-chapter work's hit count only increases when someone visits the first chapter of the work. 

This is undesirable because:
1. Subscription notifications contain a link directly to the newly-posted chapter, and visits from those links don't increase the work's hits.
2. People sometimes share links directly to updates, and visits from those links don't increase the work's hits.
3. People want us to add a link to the most recent chapter on the work blurb (AO3-4750), but if we do that with the current code, visits from that link won't increase the work's hits.

*Desired behavior:*
Going _directly_ to the most recent chapter of a multi-chapter work should increase the work's hits. 

"Directly" here means by following a link that's _not_ on the work. Code-wise, we're defining "on the work" as "any page that has '/works/####' in the URL" (where '####' matches the id of the work the chapter belongs to). 

*Things that should be true when testing:*
1. Following the "Chapter #" link in a subscription notice increases the work's hits.
2. Following a link to a chapter that has been posted anywhere on the web increases the work's hits.
3. Pasting/typing the chapter's URL into your browser (and going there) increases the work's hits.
4. Following the recent chapter link (AO3-4750) in the blurb increases the work's hits.
5. Using the Next Chapter link on the work *does not* increase the work's hits.
6. Using the Chapter Index on the work *does not* increase the work's hits.

Additionally, this uses the existing method of increasing hits, which means:
7. The work's hit count *does not* increase if you're logged in as the work creator.
8. The work's hit count *does not* increase if you access the most recent chapter twice in a row (e.g. if you follow the link in the subscription email and then follow a link on Tumblr).

_Important:_ Hits in the _blurb_ are cached for about an hour. Hits on the _work_ update immediately.
 
*Notes*
Do not merge without AO3-4750. These issues should be deployed together following a news post.

      end
    end
  end

Summary: Collection email receives "Work added" emails when a mod updates a work's accepted, anonymous, or unrevealed status from Manage Items page
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sam Johnsson
Description:
h2. Overview:

If a collection owner supplies a collection email and enables the "Send a message to the collection email when a work is added" option for the collection, that email address will incorrectly receive "Work added" emails when the mods update works using the collection's Manage Items page.

You can use the sub collections here: http://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/AO34854/collections

h2. Steps to reproduce: 

h3. *SCENARIO 1:* Updating a single work's Anonymous or Unrevealed status sends many emails it should not
# Log in
# Browse > Collections > New Collection
# Fill in required information
# Fill in "Collection email" with an email address you have access to
# Check either "This collection is unrevealed" or "This collection is anonymous"
# Check "Send a message to the collection email when a work is added"
# Submit
# Follow "Post to Collection"
# Fill in required information (the collection info will already be included)
# Post Without Preview
# The collection email will receive an email with the subject "[AO3] Work added to COLLECTION DISPLAY TITLE" and a body saying "USER posted a new work to your collection, [COLLECTION NAME]: [WORK TITLE]"
# Return to your collection (you can follow the link on the top of the work)
# Repeat steps 8-10 two more times
# Manage Items > Approved
# Uncheck "Unrevealed" or "Anonymous" on a single work
# Submit


h3. *SCENARIO 2:* Modifying a single work's Approved or Rejected status in a collection sends one email it should not
# Log in
# Browse > Collections > New Collection
# Fill in required information
# Fill in "Collection email" with an email address you have access to
# Check "Send a message to the collection email when a work is added"
# Submit
# Follow "Post to Collection"
# Fill in required information (the collection info will already be included)
# Post Without Preview
# The collection email will receive an email with the subject "[AO3] Work added to COLLECTION DISPLAY TITLE" and a body saying "USER posted a new work to your collection, [COLLECTION NAME]: [WORK TITLE]"
# Return to your collection (you can follow the link on the top of the work)
# Manage Items > Approved
# Change the dropdown menu on the work you added from "Approved" to "Rejected"
# Submit

h2. What happens:

In *SCENARIO 1*, the collection email will receive one "[AO3] Work added to COLLECTION DISPLAY TITLE" email for _each work_ on that page -- so in our example, you will receive three emails.

In *SCENARIO 2*, the collection email will receive exactly one "[AO3] Work added to COLLECTION DISPLAY TITLE" email.

h2. What should happen:

No work is being added to the collection, so no "[AO3] Work added to COLLECTION DISPLAY TITLE" email should be sent when the work's Approved, Rejected, Anonymous, or Unrevealed status is updated.

h2. Notes:

It doesn't matter if you're checking or unchecking Unrevealed or Anonymous. Likewise, it doesn't matter whether you're setting the work to Approved or Rejected. The bug happens no matter what.

Summary: Batch tag count updates to speed up posting
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: james_
Description:
Current when under high load the systems takes a long time to post new works, this is really only apparent when multiple people are posting works which share the same tag.

Currently posting takes a long time as the following query takes around 2 minutes:

UPDATE `tags` SET `taggings_count` = COALESCE(`taggings_count`, 0) + 1 WHERE `tags`.`type` IN ('Rating') AND `tags`.`id` = 11   

So my plan is to remove taggings_count as a field in the db and make it a method with some smart caching.

*Testing notes:*

- Tags with less than 999 uses are small and should not be cached
- Tags with 1,000-39,999 uses are medium and should be cached for a variable period of time (3-40 minutes)
- Tags with 40,000 uses or more are large and should be cached for 30 minutes

You will want to find a tag in each of these categories, and then go to the edit page for that tag (http://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Tag%A/edit) _before_ you post. *Note the number listed in "Taggings Count (#)" in the sidebar.*

Now post the work. 

Then reload the edit page. The "Taggings Count (#)" should change immediately for the small tag, but it should *not* change for the medium and large tags until the caching period (3-40 minutes) is up.

*Also check* that you can access the pages linked in the sidebar on http://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings:

- Fandoms by media (#) http://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings?show=fandoms
- Characters by fandom (#) http://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings?show=characters
- Relationships by fandom (#) http://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings?show=relationships
- Freeforms by fandom (#) http://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings?show=freeforms
- Unsorted Tags (#) http://test.archiveofourown.org/unsorted_tags

On each of those pages, make sure you can sort tags by their taggings count. Click the "↓ Taggings" link at the top of the table (between the Canonical and Manage columns) to sort.

Summary: "Invited" membership level in collections has no purpose
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Former user
Description:
In collections, there are two ways to join:
1) The collection mods can add you, and assign the permission level they want
2) You can select the "Join" button on a moderated collection, which grants you "None" permission level until the moderators change it to "Member"

There is a permission level "Invited" but it doesn't seem to convey any permissions and is essentially the same as "None". It's possible this was intended for collection owners to invite people, they sit at this level until they accept, but this isn't currently coded. Once a person has been added as a member or below, the "Join" button on the collection's page becomes "Leave". If they’re added as a moderator owner, the button becomes “Membership”.

One of the options for resolving this bug is to simply remove the {{invited}} membership level.

Summary: Unapproved/rejected/invited works in an unrevealed/anonymous and moderated collection don't get revealed/de-anoned when the moderator deselects the unrevealed/anonymous collection settings
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
*Steps to reproduce*
1. Log in as USER1, who will be our collection moderator
2. Browse > Collections > New Collection
3. Fill in "Collection name"
4. Fill in "Display title"
5. Check "This collection is moderated"
6. Check "This collection is unrevealed"
7. Press "Submit"
8. Log out as USER1
9. Log in as USER2, who will be our creator
10. If necessary, return to the collection you created as USER1
11. Follow "Post to Collection" link
12. Fill in required information
13. Press "Post Without Preview"
14. Log out as USER2
15. Log in as USER1
16. If necessary, return to the collection you created as USER1
17. Follow "Collection Settings" link in sidebar
18. Uncheck "This collection is unrevealed"
19. Press "Update"

Note: The above is an example. This applies in more cases, as discussed below.

*What should happen*
I'd expect the work to be revealed.

*What happens instead*
The work is not revealed. It still appears under "Awaiting Approval" on the "Manage Items" page and pressing the "Details" button shows a work blurb that says "Part of" without listing the collection name; additionally, the work itself displays a banner that says "This work is part of an ongoing challenge and will be revealed soon\! You can find details here:" without listing the collection name.

Because the "This collection is unrevealed" setting has been de-selected, the "Manage Items" page does not contain an option to reveal the work manually. The good news is if you turn "This collection is unrevealed" on and then off again, the work will be revealed and all will be right in the world.

*Notes*
This issue previously mentioned problems with unchecking the “This collection is moderated” setting; however, they are separate issues and should be handled separately… if the issues with moderated collections were still happening, but they are not. (Previously, if a moderator unchecked “This collection is moderated” while works were awaiting approval, the work count in the sidebar would increase but the works would not appear in the collection. Now the count does not increase.)

*Testing notes*
All works regardless of approval status should be revealed or de-anoned upon unchecking the relevant collection setting. 

*In the case of invited works in an unrevealed collection*, only works that have been approved by the work creator should have gift, prompt fill, or related work notifications sent. (Notifications are only sent for these works because they are the only works that will appear unrevealed. It’s not possible to invite a work to an unrevealed collection, but if a collection moderator invites a work to a collection and _then_ sets the collection to unrevealed while waiting for the creator’s approval‌_,_ the work will not be unrevealed.)

If both the collection moderator and work creator have approved the work’s inclusion in the collection, the gift and prompt fill notifications should include the name of the collection.

*If you’re testing with the anonymous setting* rather than the unrevealed setting, note that de-anoning does not send gift, prompt fill, or related work notifications – it sends subscription notifications if you are subscribed to a creator whose work was de-anoned.

There are a couple of issues that might come up in testing that are existing bugs:

* If a work is in both Regular Collection and Unrevealed Collection, the notification emails that are sent when Unrevealed Collection is revealed _might_ say "A gift work has been posted for you in the Regular Collection collection." That's because the emails only list the work's _first_ collection.
* If the moderator reveals the collection, sets it back to unrevealed, and then reveals it again, a second set of notifications will be sent.

I think the reason it got worse was because the taggings count is displayed on the tag edit page. When the taggings count for a small tag is displayed, it’s recalculated and cached, and queued for writing to the database in batches. This happens even if the taggings count hasn’t changed.

This means that very soon after viewing the tag edit page – that is, soon after visiting the page you need to visit in order to make a tag canonical or add a synonym – the tag is updated in a batch transaction that might cause any other transactions involving that tag to be very slow. I believe that [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3830|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3830|smart-link] is caused by jobs being queued before the end of the transaction. The competition between the batch update and the canonical/synonym update probably caused even longer delays between when the job was queued (in the {{before_update}} callback) and when the data was committed to the database.

Hopefully resolving [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3830|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3830|smart-link] should be sufficient to fix this even without updating the taggings count code to reduce the number of updates.

Summary: Chapter: Make it easier to see and add co-authors who are already on the work
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. The Background

Strong parameters broke the bug that was causing AO3-3752: "Adding a co-author to any chapter of a work will cause them to be an author on all subsequently posted chapters whether you like it or not" \o/

So, yay, co-authors are no longer added to subsequently posted chapters whether you like it or not.

However, now we need to clean up the broken code, add some tests, and implement the design from that issue.


h1. The Issue

!3752.png|thumbnail! 

There should be handy checkboxes so you can add co-creators who are already on the work to a chapter. This is the shiny new "Chapter co-creators" area. It should be available when creating or editing a chapter on a co-authored work.

Once a given co-creator is added to a chapter, their checkbox will be disabled and you will not be able to remove them.

If there are no co-creators already on the work, there should be no "Chapter co-creators" section.

On the chapter form, where it used to say "Current co-creators," it now says "Work co-creators" to distinguish them from chapter co-creators. The work form should say "Current co-creators."

The other change is everything on the form (for chapters and works) now says "creator" instead of "author."

h1. Testing Notes

This might be more confusing than clicking around and checking the page against the description above, but if you want step by step instructions for checking out what's on the chapter form, try this:

1. Log in
2. Post > New Work
3. Fill in the required information

{quote}1) If a comment marked as spam has children, they will become invisible to anyone but admins along with the spam comment. (When viewed as admin, they have a "Spam" button rather than "Not Spam", so they're presumably not being marked as spam.) They are still included in the overall comment count.

2) Deleting the parent marked as spam causes the child comment to re-appear, with "(Previous comment deleted.)" as a placeholder parent. The comment count is now correct for the number of visible comments.

It seems undesirable for someone's non-spam response to be automatically hidden when a comment is hidden as spam; if the response is considered irrelevant or confusing (by the work creator, comment leaver, or admin) with the spam gone, it can always be deleted.{quote}

It’s also important to ensure spam comments without non-spam replies are _not_ counted toward pagination (formerly [AO3-6008|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6088]):

# Log in
# Post a work (but this mainly happens on news posts)
# Leave a comment on the work
# Log out
# Leave 26 more comments on the work (top level, not threaded)
# Reply to the 25th comment (i.e., not the last comment, but the one before it) 
# Log in as the work creator
# Go to the comment section with all the spam
# Mark all but the first and last +top-level+ comments as spam (i.e., don’t mark the reply from step 6 as spam)

Currently, there are still two pages of comments, but each page only displays one comment.

But there _should_ be one page with three comments and a placeholder, because

* the spam comments should not count toward pagination, and
* the spam comment with the non-spam reply should display as a placeholder with a visible reply

Summary: Prevent maintainers of an anonymous and/or unrevealed collection from adding or inviting works to the collection
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
*How to reproduce:*
As User A, make an anonymous and/or unrevealed collection: 
1. Log in as User A
2. Browse > Collections > New Collection
3. Fill out required information
4. Check either "This collection is unrevealed" or "This collection is anonymous" (or both!)
5. Press "Submit"
6. Log out

As User B, agree to your work automatically being included in collections:
7. Log in as User B
8. Hi, User B! > My Preferences
9. Check "Automatically agree to your work being collected by others in the Archive."
10. Press "Update"

As User B, post a work (if you don't already have one):
11. Post > New Work
12. Fill in required information
13. Press "Post Without Preview"

As User A, invite User B's work to your anonymous or unrevealed collection
14. Go to User B's work
15. Press "Add To Collections" at the bottom of the work
16. Enter the name of your anonymous or unrevealed collection
17. Press "Add"

*Variation:* You can _also_ try this without setting User B's preferences to "Automatically agree to your work being collected by others in the Archive."

*What happens:*
- The page will reload and User A will receive a blue flash message saying, "Added to collection(s): Collection Title." 
- User B's work will be added to the collection and made unrevealed or anonymous, likely freaking out User B because the work is either (a) listed as being by Anonymous or (b) just plain unfindable and inaccessible.

*Variation:* If User B doesn't have the "Automatically agree to your work being collected by others in the Archive" preference set, the blue flash message will say, "This work has been invited to your collection (Collection Title)." User B will receive and email and have to confirm that they want the work added prior to freaking out.

*What should happen instead:*
In either the primary case or the variation:
- The page should reload and User A should receive a red flash message saying, "Sorry, you can't invite works to an anonymous or unrevealed collection."
- The work should not be added to the collection.

*Steps to reproduce*
1. Log in as a tag wrangler
2. Browse > Tags > New Tag
3. Fill in a name for the tag

5. Choose a tag type
6. Press Create Tag

10. Where the page says "0 Works in Steps to reproduce," follow the name of the tag to go to its landing page
11. Follow the Edit link
12. Uncheck the canonical checkbox
13. Press Save changes
14. Wait a few minutes
15. Follow Browse > Tags
16. Click a tag's name to go to its works page
17. Using your browser's developer tools, inspect the Favorite Tag button and replace the value of the tag you're currently looking at with the value of the tag from step 9
18. Press Favorite Tag

(a) get a non-canonical tag's tag_id from the database and follow steps 15-17
(b) open a canonical tag's works page and edit page in separate browser tabs, de-canonize the tag from the edit page, and then press the Favorite Tag button on the work page you already have open

# Fill out the form

*What happens*
I get an email with the subject "[AO3] Your sign-up for COLLECTION NAME has been deleted." It's unformatted and has no text, just attachments of my sign-up in html and txt format.

*What should happen*
While it's somewhat nice to have, this is new behavior introduced in the Rails 5.1 upgrade (it does not happen on production and has not for at least a year). So let's say the email should _not_ be sent and the related code should be removed.

If we decide we want to send it in the future, we can always make a proper email with text and stuff. But for now, the simplest course of action would be keeping the behavior consistent with production.

Summary: Comment validation prevents deletion

Create more than one comment by the same user on the same work (top level comments, not replies). Then add replies to both of them. Fix: skip the uniqueness validation when the comment is being marked deleted. Then both comments should be able to be deleted.

Summary: Excessive calls to Tag.reset_filter_count in Tag.remove_filter_taggings
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
Tag.remove_filter_taggings contains too many calls to Tag.reset_filter_count -- one for each FilterTagging that gets deleted. Since each call to reset_filter_count forces the database to count all visible works in the filter (which requires a join between two tables, and conditions on both), I believe this results in runtime quadratic in the number of works in the tag. It would be better to keep it linear, and only call reset_filter_count once per filter.

This is more of a runtime change than a functionality change, but to verify that the pull request hasn't completely stripped out the ability to fix the filter counts when wrangling, I believe this test will work:

1. Pick two small fandom tags, one canonical, one non-canonical.
2. Count the number of works in both tags.
3. Syn the non-canonical fandom to the canonical fandom.
4. Verify that when you view the canonical fandom on the Fandoms page, the number listed beside the fandom has changed. (You may have to wait a few minutes.)
5. De-syn the non-canonical fandom.
6. Verify that when you view the canonical fandom on the Fandoms page, the number listed beside the fandom has gone back down. (You may have to wait a few minutes.)

(And of course, AO3-3830 and AO3-4965 mean you might have to try a few times to get wrangling to stick.)

Summary: Revisit desired autocomplete behavior
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
There are a couple of questions to consider about autocomplete behavior.

When you enter "A & B" into the tags autocomplete, what are the desired results?
- If there is a tag "A & B", exactly the same as the autocomplete, should that be the only result? Or just the first result? What if there's also a tag "A & B & C"? Or a tag "C & A & B"? Or a tag "B & A & C"?
- If the only tag containing both the token A and the token B is "B & A", should that be the only result? Or just the first result?
- What if the only tag containing both tokens is "A/B", with an incorrect symbol?
- If there are no tags matching both A and B, it seems logical to include results for tags matching A or tags matching B. Should tags matching the "&" also be included?
- Should tags starting with "A &" be prioritized over tags starting with "A/", since they contain the correct symbol?

What about the other symbols? Currently, the ampersand, the hyphen, the tilde, the double quote, the forward slash, and both left and right parentheses are handled one way, while the remaining symbols (e.g. vertical bar, period, colon, square brackets) are handled differently. So you can use autocomplete to get a list of tags containing a vertical bar, but not to get a list of tags containing an ampersand.
- Is this the desired behavior?
- Should it be possible to search for tags with just an ampersand?
- Should it be impossible to search for tags with just a vertical bar?
- Does it depend on the context? e.g. It might be too resource-intensive to do autocomplete for an ampersand in all tags, but not if you're just trying to get a list of all the "&" relationships in a particular fandom.

What about words like "the"? If the user enters "The L" into the autocomplete, it seems like it should include tags like "The L-Word" and "The Last Unicorn".
- Should it also include "The A-Team" because both tags share the word "The"?
- What about "They Live" or "Lost" or even "Thelonious Monk"?
- How should the search results be ranked? Is "They Live" automatically a better match than "Lost", or should it depend on their taggings counts?

Once elasticsearch has been upgraded, it might be good to try reimplementing the autocomplete code using elasticsearch's autocomplete capabilities. Elasticsearch probably already handles many of these questions in a reasonable way.

Description:
All Searchable objects have a successful_reindex function that's supposed to be called whenever some number of items in the class have been reindexed. The Work class uses this to update the works index cache key for its pseuds, filters, and collections, which is used to cache search results on various pages. So without the successful_reindex callback, it could take up to 20 minutes for a new work to show up in the tags.

If both the new indexing code and the old indexing code are enabled, the callbacks in the old indexing code should help ensure that the cache is properly cleared, so it may be difficult to reproduce this issue at the moment. Summary: Gift Exchange test broken by Daylight Savings Time redux
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Ariana
Description:
A few years ago, [the "Change timezone for a gift exchange" scenario|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/features/gift_exchanges/challenge_giftexchange.feature#L55-L58] broke when daylight saving ended in Alaska (AO3-4132). 

This was fixed by setting the expected non-UTC timezone to PGT (Papua New Guinea) as that timezone does not switch to daylight saving time in summer. Unfortunately, during the work to upgrade to Rails 4 in May 2017, someone set the timezone in that test to Pacific Daylight Time (PDT), so it failed in November 2017 when the expected close date for the gift exchange happened to fall in the PST period instead.

The solution is to reapply the original fix and set it to {{(GMT+10:00) Port Moresby}} and {{PGT}} again, maybe with a note why it's like that and not to change it again, thank you very much.

1. Log in as an admin

4. Open another browser or incognito/private window and _don't_ log in as an admin

2. Open another browser or incognito/private window and log in as admin
3. Go to the languages page: http://test.ao3.org/languages

The good news is the non-admin can't actually _do_ anything they're no supposed to, since it appears they're just getting a cached page, but this is still Not Good.

The easiest way to test this is to log in as an admin and then check that you have a cookie called admin_credentials.

Summary: Update Import URL Mappings Rake task to use AO3 ids
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Ariana
Description:
[AO3-5125|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5125] added a rake task to update the {{imported_from_url}} field on works imported using a temporary site. It uses a CSV file and works by matching the import URL from the temporary site and changing it to the story's URL on the original archive.

This script assumes that the works still have the original url from the temp site. However, in a recent case, the script apparently caused the works to have a nil {{imported_from_url}} field (or at least the works had a nil field several weeks later).

In this case, it would be better to use the AO3 id to find the imported work, and then replace the {{imported_from_url}} if it is nil or set to the URL from the temporary site (this will stop it overwriting import URLs in the unlikely event that the CSV contains works that were actually imported from elsewhere than the temporary site)

*Testing*
As this is a rake task, it can only be tested manually from the command line on an installation of the Archive. However, I will write an automated test for it to check basic functionality

*Update March 2019*

This task which is very rarely run anymore - partly because this bug made it undesirable to use and because Open Doors updated their policies to reflect that so they no longer offer individual story redirects. However, in the event that we did want to run this again for whatever reason, it would be better if it worked properly.

There are automated tests for it, but if someone with access to Staging wants to test it from the console:

# Update the imported_from_url on two works to, say, [http://foo1|http://foo1] and [http://foo2|http://foo2]
# Create a CSV with the following columns:

{code:java}AO3 id,URL Imported From,Original URL
<AO3 id of foo1 work>,http://foo1,http://bar1
<AO3 id of foo2 work>,http://foo2,http://bar2{code}

3. Run the rake task: {{bundle exec rake opendoors:import_url_mapping <path to CSV>}}

Once this has run successfully, the imported_from_url field for the two works should be [http://bar1|http://bar1] and [http://bar2|http://bar2] respectively.

TagQuery
* performs a case-insensitive search ('AbC' matches 'abc')
* performs a query string search ('ab OR cd' matches 'ab cd', 'ab/cd' and 'ab “cd” ef')
* performs an exact match with quotes ('xgh OR “abc d”' matches 'abc d')
* lists closest matches at the top of the results ('abc' result lists 'abc' first)
* matches every token in any order ('d abc' matches 'abc d' and 'abc-d', but not 'abc' or 'abc+')
* matches tokens with double quotes ('ab "cd" ef' matches 'ab "cd" ef')
* matches tokens with single quotes ('ab'c d' matches 'ab'c d')
* performs a wildcard search at the end of a term ('abc*' matches 'abcd' and 'abcde')
* performs a wildcard search in the middle of a term ('a*d' matches 'abcd')
* performs a wildcard search at the beginning of a term ('*cd' matches 'abcd')
* preserves plus ( + ) character ('abc+' matches 'abc+' and 'abc', but not 'abccc')
* preserves minus ( - ) character ('abc-d' matches 'abc-d', 'abc -d', 'abc d' but not 'abc' or 'abcd')
* preserves minus ( - ) preceded by a space ('abc -d' matches 'abc -d', 'abc d' and 'abc-d', but not 'abc')
* preserves slashes without quotes ('ab/cd' should match 'ab/cd' and 'ab cd')
* matches tags with canonical punctuation ('yuri\!\!\!' on ice matches 'Yuri\!\!\! On Ice')
* matches tags without canonical punctuation ('yuri on ice' matches 'Yuri\!\!\! On Ice')
* matches unicode tags with unicode character ('Dave ♦ Sawbuck' matches 'Dave ♦ Sawbuck')"
* matches unicode tags without unicode character ('dave sawbuck' matches 'Dave ♦ Sawbuck')

Description:
*The problem:*

Sorting a work list by creator using the "Sort by > Author" dropdown of the filters will not properly sort creator names (default pseuds or otherwise) that start with numbers.

*The cause:*

There is an issue in the "sorted_authors" and "sorted_pseuds" methods in the work class. If the first character of a pseud is a special character we remove it; unfortunately due to an error in the regex we're also removing the first character if it is a range of possible things, including numbers.

2) From the "Sort by" dropdown of the filters, choose "Author" and hit "Sort and Filter"
3) Look at the top of the list to see if the creator names with numbers are sorted correctly in order (for example, "007aardvark" should sort before "221b_wombat", which should sort before 666tasmanian_devil).

Summary: Old Indexing: Tag search by type doesn't work for newer tags.
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
Tag search by type doesn't work for newer tags. The indexing code in IndexSubqueue sets _type equal to Tag.document_type (i.e. "Tag"), while the search code is expecting _type to contain the type of the tag (e.g. "Fandom"). So all tags indexed using IndexSubqueue disappear from the search when you pick a tag type.

*Steps for reproducing:*
# Create or find a new tag with a fairly unique name.
# Search for the tag using tag search with no type specified. See that the tag shows up in the results.
# Restrict the search to only include tags of your new tag's type.
# Notice that the new tag disappears from the search results when it shouldn't.

Even if you don't use a unique name, you can typically see missing tags just by picking a relationship tag from a fairly new fandom and trying to search for it with and without a tag type selected.

Interestingly, it looks like this bug can also cause a tag to show up twice in the search: once from being indexed using Tag.reindex_document, and once from being indexed using IndexSubqueue. This is distinct from the duplicate tag issue in AO3-2349. In fact, when I do [a search for "final fantasy tactics a2"|http://archiveofourown.org/tags/search?utf8=✓&query%5Bname%5D=final+fantasy+tactics+a2&query%5Btype%5D=], I see *three* versions of the tag: one with the unprintable characters at the end of the link, and two with no unprintable characters (resulting from this bug).
