Summary: Use ScheduledReindexJob and IndexQueue in cucumber tests.
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
Currently, all of the automated cucumber tests involving search rely on:
# The code in lib/searchable.rb that performs synchronous indexing with reindex_document when in the test environment.
# The "all search indexes are updated" step, which deletes and recreates each index from scratch.

As a result, indexing/reindexing in the automated tests doesn't necessarily behave the same way as indexing/reindexing on the deployed version, which queues up items using IndexQueue and periodically runs ScheduledReindexJob to perform the actual indexing. It would be good to modify the tests to more accurately simulate this process, to catch more errors that might occur outside of the test environment.

This is a change that should only affect the tests, and shouldn't require manual QA.

Summary: Make updating filter counts asynchronous
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Elz J
Description:
We currently update the filter_counts table (which caches tag uses) in real time when users create new works or edit their tags. These are slow requests, and the counts don't really need up-to-the-minute accuracy, so we should handle this asynchronously instead, ideally adding the tag ids to a set and running a scheduled task hourly or every n hours.

*Testing*
# Pick a medium and go to its page.
# Pick a canonical fandom in that medium.
# Write down the current count associated with that fandom.
# Create a new work in that fandom.
# Wait 1 hour.
# Check the medium's page again and verify that the count has increased by 1.

You can also do similar tests with other actions that should change the count: e.g. deleting a work, adding or removing a canonical tag from an existing work, wrangling a tag, etc.

Summary: ES5 BOT: Pseud index doesn't update when a work is updated.
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
*Steps to reproduce:*
# Log in as a user.
# Pick a canonical fandom that the user has never written in.
# Post a new work in that fandom.
# Wait for the pseud index to update.
# Search for the canonical fandom in people search, and keep refreshing until the people search is updated and you appear in the search results.

You'd expect to show up in the people search eventually. But because Work.update_pseud_index wraps the list of pseud IDs within another list (making the argument malformed), it won't be updated until something else triggers an update to the pseud index.

Even when the correct pseud IDs are passed in Work.update_pseud_index, there are several ways for a work to be updated that won't trigger an update to all of the relevant pseuds:
# Adding a pre-existing canonical fandom after the work is posted.
# Removing a canonical fandom from the work after it's been posted.
# Removing yourself as an author after the work is posted. (The value of authors_to_sort_on will update, which will cause all of the remaining authors on the work to have their pseuds reindexed -- but not the person trying to remove their name from the work.)
# Orphaning a work after it's been posted. (Just as when removing yourself as an author, the orphan_account will be updated, but not the user trying to orphan their work.)

All of these scenarios should cause the people search to update.

On a technical side, the current behavior doesn’t technically add the “http://archiveofourown.org/…” prefix in the HTML at all, the browser will simply interpret urls without a protocol (http(s)://) as if that prefix was present. This is quite useful because users can leave links to other pages on AO3 without adding the prefix at all\!

For the case you describe, it’s hard to say what we could do to fix this issue. Optimistically adding a protocol prefix has several problems:

* It breaks relative links as described above (e.g. a user links to /works/31439690). This isn’t a very commonly known feature of HTML links, but it would probably still break some links for users.
* Adding “http://” or “https://” as protocol prefix is pure guesswork since we can’t tell which of these the URL actually supports. Adding the wrong one would break the link just as adding none at all would.

Overall, I think the current behavior is perhaps the least confusing, if at least because it literally follows what the user instructed it to do (even if that was nonsense).

Summary: ES5 BOT: IndexSweeper fails for bookmarkable items.
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
The BookmarkableIndexer appends "-series" or "-work" or "-external_work" to the IDs of all of the items that it indexes. So when the IndexSweeper retrieves the IDs of any failures, those IDs will have the extra suffixes. When those IDs are passed back to a BookmarkableIndexer class, the batch function will call routing_info(id), which will call document_id(id), which will append the suffix again -- this time incorrectly.

This results in (a) incorrect IDs if a failure is followed by a successful reindex, and (b) the IndexSweeper viewing each iteration of failure as a separate document. So in the event of a permanent failure, the IndexSweeper and the AsyncIndexer will keep calling each other until the ID becomes so long that Elasticsearch throws an error.

*Testing*
This one is very difficult to test manually. I think you'd have to deliberately modify the code to produce an error, and then watch the failure stores. One way to consistently produce errors is to modify the line @batch << document(object) in Indexer.batch to read @batch << document(object).merge("_id" => "asdf"), since Elasticsearch doesn't like it when you try to embed the "_id" in your document.

Summary: Autocomplete keyboard controls assume users are using QWERTY keyboards
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
*Steps to reproduce*
Using a keyboard with a layout that does _not_ have the comma key in the same position as [this diagram of a QWERTY keyboard|https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QWERTY#/media/File:KB_United_States-NoAltGr.svg] 
# Log in
# Post > New Work
# In an autocomplete field like Additional Tags, do one of the following:
## enter some text and press the comma key on your keyboard
## enter some text that uses the key in the same position as the QWERTY keyboard's comma key (e.g. ת on a [Hebrew keyboard|https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hebrew_keyboard#/media/File:Hebrew_keyboard_layout.png])

*What happens*
If you press the comma key on your non-QWERTY keyboard, a comma appears in the field and nothing else happens. You'd expect it to finalize the entry of the tag, making it appear over the field the same way pressing the comma key on a QWERTY keyboard does.

If you press the key that's in the same position as a QWERTY keyboard's comma, it finalizes entry of the tag, making it appear above the field. This effectively prevents you from using whatever letter/character is on that key. You'd expect to be able to use that letter/character normally. (If you're using a QWERTY keyboard, you can also see this behavior by trying to use the < character, which requires you to use the comma key in combination with the Shift key.)

*Notes*
The autocomplete JavaScript [uses the code attribute for all keyboard functionality|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1b70938c17edc6d59b06ba3f1f8ec5d01cabeaf5/public/javascripts/jquery.tokeninput.js#L63]. We probably need to considering using [the key attribute|https://developers.google.com/web/updates/2016/04/keyboardevent-keys-codes] instead, because we care about the character being inputted, not the physical key being pressed. KeyboardEvent.key has [good support on new browsers|https://caniuse.com/#search=keyboardevent.key], but it will likely break things for anyone using an unsupported browser.

Summary: Series bookmarks do not appear on tag's bookmark page when a formerly canonical tag is synned to a new tag
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce
# Log in as a Tag Wrangler
# Post a new work in a new series, with a new tag:
## Post > New Work
## Fill in required information, using a new tag for the Fandom, e.g. "New Fandom Test Tag"
##* Note: It doesn't _have_ to be a new fandom tag, but it's easier/quicker for testing purposes
## Check "This work is part of a series"
## Fill in "Or create and use a new one:" with a name for your series, e.g. "New Test Series"
## Post Without Preview
# Canonize the tag:
## Go to the Edit page for your new tag, e.g. http://test.ao3.org/tags/New%20Fandom%20Tag/edit
## Check "Canonical"
## Press "Save changes"
# Make your work and series bookmarks:
## Hi, username! > My Works
## Follow the linked title of the work you just posted
## Press "Bookmark" to go to the bookmark form
## Press "Create" to save the bookmark
## Follow the link to the work's series
## Press "Bookmark Series" to open the bookmark form
## Press "Create" to save the bookmark
# Wait 10 or 15 minutes -- as long as it takes for the work and the bookmarks to appear on the work (http://test.ao3.org/tags/New%20Fandom%20Tag/works) and bookmark listings (http://test.ao3.org/tags/New%20Fandom%20Tag/bookmarks)
# Make your test tag a synonym of another tag:
## Go to the tag's edit page, e.g. http://test.ao3.org/tags/New%20Fandom%20Tag/edit
## Fill in "Synonym of" with another brand new tag, e.g. "Canonical New Fandom Test Tag"
## Press "Save changes"
# Wait 10, 15, or even 20 minutes while the wrangling change takes place

h1. What happens
The bookmark of the work correctly appears on the bookmark listing (http://test.ao3.org/tags/Canonical%20New%20Fandom%20Tag/bookmarks). The bookmark of the series does not.

h1. What should happen
All bookmarks should appear on the bookmark listing.

h1. Notes
Could be related:
* AO3-4540 (I suspect it's the same cause)
* AO3-5253 (Basically the same problem with external works)

Before I turned the canonical tag into a synonym, these were the filters on the series:

{code:java}
2.3.0 :004 > s_before = Series.find(63418)
 => #<Series id: 63418, created_at: "2018-02-20 00:58:36", updated_at: "2018-02-20 00:58:36", title: "Test Series", summary: nil, notes: nil, hidden_by_admin: false, restricted: false, complete: false, summary_sanitizer_version: 0, notes_sanitizer_version: 0> 
2.3.0 :006 > s_before.filter_ids
 => [10, 1218352, 14] 
{code}

And after I did the synning:

{code:java}
2.3.0 :011 > s_after = Series.find(63418)
 => #<Series id: 63418, created_at: "2018-02-20 00:58:36", updated_at: "2018-02-20 00:58:36", title: "Test Series", summary: nil, notes: nil, hidden_by_admin: false, restricted: false, complete: false, summary_sanitizer_version: 0, notes_sanitizer_version: 0> 
2.3.0 :013 > s_after.filter_ids
 => [10, 1218352, 14, 1218355] 
{code}

So the good news is the new filter_id (1218355) is getting added to the series -- but I suspect it's just trickling down to the series from the work update, since series tags come from the works -- so the series bookmark will indeed show up if the series bookmark gets reindexed. The bad news is the old filter_id (1218352) is still attached.

Part of the issue might be that [the reindex_taggables method|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/e2c284a95ed1feb8d23ad33cad6ee2c4b2ec1174/app/models/tag.rb#L680] only reindexes works and bookmarks that use the tag. If the tag is on the bookmarkable (i.e. the series), the bookmark will not be reindexed.

Creator: coaldustcanary
Description:
A user's Related Works page will include listings of works inspired by works in unrevealed and anonymous collections.

*Example:* 

[https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/coaldustcanary/related_works|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/coaldustcanary/related_works]

"Filth" ([https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1067371)|https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1067371] is currently set as Unrevealed, but on my related works page, "Not at all filthy by testy5 " is listed as a related work. This was also the case when the collection was set to Anonymous.

*To replicate:*

# Log in as User A
# Post a work to an anonymous (or unrevealed) collection
# Log out
# Log in as User B
# Post a work inspired by the work from Step 2
# Go to the related works page for User A, i.e. https://test.archiveofourown.org/UserA/related_works

*What happens:*

The Related Works page for the creator of the anonymous/unrevealed work (User A) will list the work "inspired by" said work. This means everyone now knows that User A wrote the anonymous/unrevealed work.

*What should happen:*

This information should only be included if you are currently logged in _as_ User A. Otherwise, works inspired by User A’s anonymous or unrevealed works should be excluded.

*Notes:*

There’s a similar issue that occurs if User A writes an anonymous or unrevealed work that’s marked as inspired by one of User B’s works. Those works are currently included on User A’s related works page as “A work in an unrevealed or anonymous challenge,” with a link to the inspiring work. This means that if the related work is approved, it’s fairly straightforward to track down User A’s anonymous work. (Just follow the link to the inspiring work, and check the “Works inspired by this one:” section.)

Instead, anonymous/unrevealed works by User A that are inspired by a work by User B should not be included on User A’s related works page for anyone other than User A. (It’s okay if they occur on User B’s related works page, though, as long as they don’t reveal the association with User A.)

This should also apply for translations, as well as remixes.

Summary: Fix intermittent test failure in pseud searches
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: redsummernight
Description:
We have a few tests related to pseud indexing (for AO3-5326 and AO3-5327) [that does this|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/f759e3dab530c9c7fdf3de38d270c32599bba2d2/spec/models/pseud_search_form_spec.rb#L64-L67]:
{code:ruby}
bookmark = create(:bookmark, bookmarkable_id: work.id)
run_all_indexing_jobs
result = PseudSearchForm.new(name: bookmark.pseud.name).search_results.first
expect(result).to eq bookmark.pseud
{code}

The last assertion often fails because:

- fields are faked in factories as random alphanumeric strings, then indexed by PseudIndexer with the "simple" analyzer (e.g. "le5kct26" is actually "le kct")
- PseudQuery [doesn't set the operator on name queries|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/f759e3dab530c9c7fdf3de38d270c32599bba2d2/app/models/search/pseud_query.rb#L55], so "le kct" will match anything with "le" OR "kct"
- the query can return results in the wrong order (because of a small number of results on [multiple shards|https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/6.2/consistent-scoring.html], see the tests for AO3-5265), so the pseud we want is not necessarily the first one

How to fix so the tests should pass more consistently:

- We set the pseud names ourselves instead of letting factories do it, less chance of some random name appearing in the desired results.
- We limit the number of shards to 1.

Since we're not testing search relevance/order, and the test just needs a pseud search result, I'm going with the first fix.

*How to test*: no manual testing required.

Summary: ES6: Pseuds indexing ignores numbers
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Ariana
Description:
As indicated in AO3-5358, pseuds are indexed using the *simple* mapping in Elasticsearch. This means that, for example, numbers and punctuation are ignored, such that {{testy2}} and {{testy3}} are both returned in a search on "testy2", and {{man}} or {{x-file}} will be returned for a query on {{x-man}}.

This is the problem that also occurred with the tag mapping (see AO3-5265). The purpose will be to change the behaviour so the following are true:

- a search for *testy2* should return *testy2* first, followed by the other *testy*s 
- a search for *x_file* should return *x_file* first, followed by any other combination of *x* and *file*

Summary: ES5 BOT: Add separate "Any field" and "Tag" fields for bookmarks and bookmarkables on bookmark search
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: redsummernight
Description:
On the [bookmark search form|https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search], we have the fields "Any field" and "Tag" which can match either bookmarks or bookmarkables. During the ES6 upgrade, we switch to a parent-child indexing model for bookmarkable-bookmark (to avoid reindexing e.g. all bookmarks when a work is updated), which makes querying across bookmarks and bookmarkables complicated (it's unclear what should be AND'ed or OR'ed together), and leads to issues such as AO3-5301, AO3-5320.

We can avoid this problem by making it explicit to users what they want to match on. Add these fields on the bookmark search form, which correspond to new fields on bookmark filters in AO3-5355 :

- Any field on bookmarked item (form) = Search within results (filters)
- Any field on bookmark (form) = Search bookmarker's tags and notes (filters)
- Bookmarked item's tags (form) = Other work tags to include (filters)
- Bookmarker's tags (form) = Other bookmarker's tags to include (filters)

These should only be visible on the ES6-version of the form.

Help pop-ups will be updated separately.

Summary: Bookmarks: Language option missing from search and filter interface
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
*Example URLs*
Bookmark Search page: https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search
Bookmark tag page: https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Suits%20(TV)/bookmarks
User bookmark page: https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/testy/bookmarks
Collection bookmark page: https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/yuletide/bookmarks

*The problem*

We index bookmarks based on the bookmarkable item's language, making it possible to search for bookmarks of works in another language, e.g. Russian: 

* In Elasticsearch 0.90, you can do this by entering bookmarkable_language_id: 30 in "Any field" on the Bookmark Search page, or in "Search within results" on a tag, user, or collection bookmark page
* In Elasticsearch 6, you can do this by entering language_id: 30 in "Any field on work" on the Bookmark Search page, or in "Search within results" on a tag, user, or collection bookmark page

However, there's no way to select a language on either the filters or the search page.

*The solution*
On Elasticsearch 6 -- no need to implement it on 0.90 -- we should add a "Work language" select menu to both the filters and the search page. 

* On the filters, it should be between "Search bookmarker's tags and notes" and "Bookmark types" (to mirror its position of after the search field on work filters)
* On the search page, it should be between "Bookmarker's tags" and the checkbox for "Rec"
** If AO3-5374 is implemented, it can be before or after the field for selecting the type

There should also be automated tests for these fields.

*Notes*
Only works -- not series or external works -- have languages set, so if you specify a language, the results will only be works.

Summary: ES5 BOT: Use whitelist, not blacklist, for indexing fields
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
*Problem:*

When we index a work document, we take a blacklisting approach -- that is, we use "except" to say "index every except these fields": https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/329b7d049861758074749a4b597f9dc681da87d0/app/models/search/work_indexer.rb#L48

This has the potential to go very wrong if we add a new column (say, idk, orphaner_ip_address) to the work table and forget to say "don't index this information."

Indexers for works and bookmarks are affected. Indexers for pseuds, tags, and bookmarkables are already using whitelists.

*Solution:*

Let's instead use "only" to say "index only these fields." 

*Testing note:* 

This is a code issue, not a reproducible bug. To test this, someone with database access to staging will need to get the JSON for a work *before* this code is deployed and things are reindexed. *After* things are reindexed, they should get the JSON for the same work. Summary: Rerunning failed Resque tasks breaks assignments for gift exchanges hit by the stuck-in-a-matching-loop bug
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. The problem

Occasionally, a gift exchange's matching will get stuck in a loop and a database admin will have to ensure that it completes. All the failed runs for this exchange end up in the Resque failures list.

When someone goes to the Failed page on Resque and presses the Retry Failed Jobs button (e.g. because they want to send out failed subscription emails), it retries the failed matching jobs. *EDIT:* This might only happen when rerunning the tasks using `bundle exec rake resque:run_failures`, not when using the Retry Failed Jobs button.

If the exchange has already set assignments, this effectively unsends them by setting the ChallengeAssignment's sent_at to nil. The assignments remain visible on the challenge's assignments page (https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/COLLECTION_NAME/assignments), but they disappear from the participants' assignments pages (https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/assignments). 

The means the challenge mods either have to purge assignments and rerun matching and recreate the assignments themselves or ask a database admin to fix things by setting the sent_at date. (For assignments that were _not_ automatically generated, such as pinch-hits or write-in recipients or givers, request_signup_id and offer_signup_id information is actually lost from the ChallengeAssignment objects and can only be restored if the challenge mods have kept a record.)

h1. The solution

Failed matching jobs should not be rerun, especially not if the challenge has successfully generated potential matches and/or sent assignments.

h1. Testing

Unfortunately, we do not currently know how to reproduce the failed matching loops that cause this issue.

Summary: Backdated work's published_at date does not always override revised_at date, resulting in blurb and meta showing different dates
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.

h1. Steps to reproduce

Note: This can _only_ be reproduced if the time is after 00:00 UTC, but before 00:00 US Eastern. Thanks to daylight saving, this can be between 00:00-04:00 or 00:00-05:00 UTC depending on the time of year.

# Login
# Post > New Work
# Fill in required fields
# Check "Set a different publication date" but *do not change the pre-selected date*
# Post Without Preview
# Edit work
# Change publication date to e.g. 23 July 2015
# Post Without Preview

h1. What happens

The work meta on the top of the work uses the backdated date and says "Published: 2015-07-23." 

The date in the upper right of the blurb (located on the creator's works pages, tag listings, etc) says the day the work was posted, e.g. 23 Apr 2018. 

In work listings sorted by Date Updated, the work is sorted by 23 Apr 2018.

h1. What should happen

The work meta behavior is correct. 

The blurb, however, should use the backdated date. 

The work should be sorted in listings according to the backdated date.

h1. Notes 

This is *not* a caching or indexing issue. A look at a buggy work as it exists in MySQL shows:

{code:ruby}2.3.0 :014 > work_edited.revised_at
 => Sun, 22 Apr 2018 23:51:42 EDT -04:00 
2.3.0 :015 > work_edited.published_at
 => Thu, 23 Jul 2015{code}

For comparison, a backdated work that is *not* buggy looks like:

{code:ruby}2.3.0 :002 > w.revised_at
 => Mon, 22 Sep 2014 08:00:00 EDT -04:00 
2.3.0 :003 > w.published_at
 => Mon, 22 Sep 2014{code}

Summary: Make IndexSweeper send fewer commands to REDIS
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
IndexSweeper is currently rather inefficient: even if a batch of 1000 has no errors, it reads and writes all three failure stores once for each item in the batch, resulting in a total of 6000 REDIS commands per batch.

On top of that, each failure store is an array of all previous errors encoded as a JSON string. If each error takes 200 characters to encode in JSON, and each of the three failure stores has 1000 errors, then each error store is 200KB, and a single successful batch receives over 600MB of data and sends over 600MB of data, for a total of over 1.2GB. This only gets worse as the number of previous errors increases.

When a lot of Elasticsearch errors occur, this causes the REDIS server to be swamped with requests.

Ideally, the number of requests should be independent of the size of the batch. In addition, it would be nice if the amount of data transmitted/received was independent of the number of errors that have previously occurred (so that if the number of errors ever reaches millions, it won't require reading and writing a 200MB string).

*Testing:* Like all modifications to IndexSweeper, this change is not particularly feasible to test manually. (You'd need a consistent way to produce indexing errors, which either means finding a way to consistently produce errors on staging, or deliberately modifying the code to produce Elasticsearch errors.)

Summary: Every time the TOS updates, users must be asked to agree to the new version
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
We need some sort of popup that will appear every time we update the TOS and that will require users to agree to the new TOS before they can continue using the site. 

- It should contain the text in the "UPDATED SITEWIDE BANNER LANGUAGE" section of the OTW Language Additions document

- It should cover enough of the screen in order to prevent anyone from using the site without accepting the new TOS 

- It should not appear on the TOS page, the Report Abuse page, the DMCA page, or the Support page

- To accept the new TOS, a person needs to both a) check a checkbox and b) press a button to close the banner/popup. The checkbox should be labeled "I have read & understood the new Terms of Service and Privacy Policy" and the button should say "I agree/consent to its terms"
 
- The button should be disabled until the checkbox is checked
 
- When a logged out user accepts the new TOS, we should give them a cookie that prevents them from seeing the popup again in that browser unless they clear their cookies

- When a logged in user accepts the new TOS, we should record it in the database so that, as long as they are logged in, they never see the banner again for this version of the TOS

- If you have just created your account and have just logged in, you should not see the popup until the next version of the TOS

- If JavaScript is disabled, you should not see the popup and you should be able to navigate the site as usual

You'll need to use your browser's developer tools to confirm that the accepted_tos cookie is set to expire in 20 years. (In Safari, you can find this information in the Storage tab under Cookies.)

Summary: Users can get a cached version of the wrong type of search, resulting in 500 error
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: james_
Description:
On production, we currently have some users on Elasticsearch 0.90.7 and others on 6.2. Users on 6.2 somewhat frequently encounter [a 500 error|https://rpm.newrelic.com/accounts/115892/applications/190034/traced_errors/2f519296-6ff5-11e8-a5fd-0242ac110009_0_14317?original_error_id=2f519296-6ff5-11e8-a5fd-0242ac110009_0_14317] resulting from the following when attempting to access a tag's works page, e.g. https://archiveofourown.org/tags/Derek%20Hale*s*Stiles%20Stilinski/works:

{code}
Error message
NoMethodError: undefined method `max_search_results_notice' for #<SearchResult:0x0055b2dcb2ce80>
{code}

SearchResult is the old Elasticsearch, while max_search_results_notice is the new, which tells us the user is getting cached results for the wrong version of Elasticsearch. Therefore, we need to use different cache keys for the different Elasticsearch versions.

This may also happen on bookmarks, but so far all reports we've received have been for works pages. Still, the code should be updated to be sure it doesn't start happening.

*Testing*
Unfortunately, this is not reproducible at will and does not appear to have happened on staging. To test, we'll have to deploy to production and keep an eye on New Relic to see if these errors stop, and we'll have to ask our production testers to make sure to let us know if they encounter 500 errors.

Summary: Occasional 500 error when deleting works due to Net::SMTPFatalError: 550
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
Support and Policy & Abuse have encountered several works that give 500 errors during the deletion process, regardless of whether the person deleting the work is an admin or a work creator. Database admins are similarly unable to delete the affected works using the destroy method on the command line -- they receive errors such as

{code}
Net::SMTPFatalError: 550 maximum allowed line length is 998 octets, got 1002

	from app/models/work.rb:211:in `block in before_destroy'
	from app/models/work.rb:203:in `each'
	from app/models/work.rb:203:in `before_destroy'
{code}

Replacing the content of the work or the beginning or end notes (it depends on the work) with new text enables deletion, but means the user does not receive a full copy of their work.

The error does not appear to be related to the length of the content or notes -- this error has even happened when attempting to delete a work that consisted solely of an image. It also does not appear to be related to the _specific_ content; that is, if you recreate a problematic work on staging, it will still delete.

Since this error is not reproducible on demand, any fix for this can't be tested beyond making sure it is possible to delete a work. We will have to deploy the fix and see if we stumble upon the error again. 

*Notes*

james_ discovered that this is due to the plain text part of the email having 7bit encoding. red found that [Mail's documentation on multipart emails|https://github.com/mikel/mail#writing-and-sending-a-multipartalternative-html-and-text-email] says:

bq. Mail assumes that if your text in the body is only us-ascii, that your transfer encoding is 7bit and it is text/plain. You can override this by explicitly declaring it.

*How to test*

- Post a work and delete it
- Post a work and have an admin delete it

In both cases, as the work's author, you should receive emails, with the HTML and plain text versions of the work attached. If you look at the raw email, you should see that the plain text attachment has base64 encoding, like this:

{code}
----==_mimepart_5b2b25fe3d906_773ffab1942599d
Content-Type: text/plain; charset=UTF-8; filename="2k line.txt"
Content-Transfer-Encoding: base64
Content-Disposition: attachment; filename="2k line.txt"
{code}

*More notes*
Sarken has the URL of a work affected by this bug on production. Once this is deployed, we can delete that work to confirm the issue is fixed.

A side effect of having static content in meta tags is that Google ignores it for their search results and displays the first text on the actual page instead. But the first text on every AO3 page is actually the ToS popup text, and so that is what shows up for every single AO3 search result on Google right now. [Here is an example search|https://www.google.de/search?ei=9zA5W9jxI4K26AT817uYBQ&q=Berty+finding+the+words+site%3Aao3.org&oq=Berty+finding+the+words+site%3Aao3.org&gs_l=psy-ab.3...135711.138109.0.138341.18.10.0.0.0.0.337.860.2j1j1j1.5.0], where as of the creation of this issue, this is the case. Attached you’ll also find a screenshot.

If we have page-specific content in our meta tags, Google will hopefully use that to display in their search results. Therefore, this issue is to change the meta tags to the following:

{code:html}<meta name="title" content="[1]">
<meta name="description" content="[2]">{code}

\[1] We’re currently not using this tag. But it should be added and should contain the title of the work. Alternatively we could use the content from the title tag, which is already page specific.
\[2] The work’s summary.

We want to additionally use the twitter and og-specific meta tags (used by facebook and others), to enable link previews on these sites. 

The tags that need to be added are roughly:

{code:html}<!-- Open Graph / Facebook -->
<meta property="og:type" content="website">
<meta property="og:url" content="[url of this page]">
<meta property="og:title" content="">
<meta property="og:description" content="">
<meta property="og:image" content="">

<!-- Twitter -->
<meta property="twitter:card" content="summary_large_image">
<meta property="twitter:url" content="[url of this page]">
<meta property="twitter:title" content="[1]">
<meta property="twitter:description" content="[2]">
<meta property="twitter:image" content="[3]">{code}

\[1] For the title, something like {{author: work title}}, would be the easy solution. {{work title by author}} would read nicer, but you’d have to do some Maths to not go over the max character length, which would cause the author name to be cut off.

\[2] For the description, tags in the order of {{fandoms, relationships, characters}} could work, or {{fandoms. summary}}. Again, some experiments with some example works versus the max length would probably help figure this out.

The pre-generated tweet text for the twitter share button on works pages displays {{title by author - fandoms}}, as further orientation.

\[3] For the preview image, our idea is to generate one image for each possible permutation of blurb icons upfront and then link to the static image matching the work’s blurb. Since our icon blocks are in a 1:1 format and these preview images are cropped/fitted to 16:9, we had the idea of generating these images in 16:9 and do something like \[ logo | icon block ], excuse the ascii design.

Official documentation: 

* [twitter cards docs|https://developer.twitter.com/en/docs/twitter-for-websites/cards/overview/markup]
* [Open Graph Meta Tag Docs|https://developers.facebook.com/docs/sharing/webmasters/]

Description:
Currently, if you enter broad search criteria (e.g. just check "Canonical" and perform a tag search) or look at the works or bookmarks for a large tag (e.g. Teen and Up Audiences), only 100,000 results are available. Comment:
01/Dec/19 9:00 PM;557058:f99670ac-6f0b-469b-bdfb-a9817a67932f;[https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/6.8/search-request-search-after.html|https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/6.8/search-request-search-after.html]

{quote}Pagination of results can be done by using the {{from}} and {{size}} but the cost becomes prohibitive when the deep pagination is reached. The {{index.max_result_window}} which defaults to 10,000 is a safeguard, search requests take heap memory and time proportional to {{from + size}}. The Scroll api is recommended for efficient deep scrolling but scroll contexts are costly and it is not recommended to use it for real time user requests. The {{search_after}} parameter circumvents this problem by providing a live cursor. The idea is to use the results from the previous page to help the retrieval of the next page.{quote}

We use from + size with {{index.max_result_window}} set to 100k. Switching to cursor pagination would remove the limit and also improve ES performance as well.

The downside of {{search_after}} is that you cannot jump to a random page (e.g. you can't just request page 754). A few ways we can deal with random page jumping:

* Just don't allow random page jumping. Any listings will have "Previous" and "Next" buttons only, no more 1, 2, 3, etc. URL parameters like {{page=12}} will cease to have meanings. This is what the Tumblr dashboard does.
** [~accountid:557058:443ab871-4096-403e-bd6f-f3534fe417f0] noted we don't want this approach as it places even more emphasis on page 1 works (with the most kudos/comments/bookmarks, or most frequently updated).
* Allow random page jumping by chaining {{search_after}} queries. So if users ask for page 10, we have to get all of the first 10 pages. This approach would use less memory than from + size but will generate a crap ton of queries we ultimately discard. Not very viable.
* Maybe a mix? For the first 10k results (default {{index.max_result_window}}) just use from + size as usual. Then if users want to go beyond, switch to {{search_after}}. Example: [https://medium.com/@Benoit_Travers/elasticsearch-how-we-paginated-over-10-000-items-11198af5018c|https://medium.com/@Benoit_Travers/elasticsearch-how-we-paginated-over-10-000-items-11198af5018c]. Downside: complicated to implement.
* Why doesn't {{search_after}} let us specify a starting offset? The answer is unfortunately no: [https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/28068|https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/28068].

Summary: Missing inherited MetaTaggings break crossover check
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
In production, some tags, such as [Guardians of the Galaxy (Movies)|https://archiveofourown.org/tags/Guardians%20of%20the%20Galaxy%20(Movies)/works] are missing their inherited meta tags. Until these meta tags are fixed, tags like Guardians of the Galaxy will be treated as having 0 first-class meta tags, resulting in a lot of false negatives for the crossover check. (Because currently, we check whether one fandom's first-class meta tags are a subset of the other's.)

The crossover check should iteratively and/or recursively compute the missing inherited meta-tags to fix the check (at least until the meta-taggings table is fixed).

*Testing Notes:*

1. To create a fandom with a missing inherited meta tag, create four canonical fandom tags. I'll call them Fandom A, Fandom B, Fandom C, and Fandom D.
2. Edit Fandom A and add *sub* tags Fandom B and Fandom C.
3. Edit Fandom D and add *meta* tags Fandom B and Fandom C.
4. Edit Fandom C and remove Fandom A from its meta tags.
5. Keep refreshing the edit page until Fandom A disappears, then remove Fandom D from its sub-tags.
5. At this point, Fandom D should have Fandom B as a direct meta-tag. Because of the meta-tag issue, however, it should be missing the inherited meta tag Fandom A. You can check this by creating a work with Fandom D, and checking whether it shows up when you add Fandom A to "Other tags to include."
6. Try tagging a work with Fandom D and another unrelated fandom. The work should be marked as a crossover, but as a result of this bug it won't be.

Summary: Use a GET parameter and localStorage to determine whether a guest should be shown a TOS/GDPR prompt
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: redsummernight
Description:
We prompt users to agree to the TOS any time they visit a page, unless they have already agreed to it while logged in or with cookies enabled (AO3-5416). There is no way to avoid the TOS popup if accounts are not available (people who browse using incognito/private mode) or cookies don't work.

We would like to use localStorage instead of cookies to determine whether the TOS prompt should be shown to guests.

We will also skip the TOS prompt if the URL has {{?tos=yes}} at the end. (We don't add these parameters to the URL automatically after you press "I agree/consent to its terms" because we don't want people accidentally sharing links with them. We want it to be something a user has to manually add so we can be relatively sure they actually agreed to the TOS and didn't just follow a link that happened to have the {{?tos=yes}} params.)

*Testing instructions*

Part 1:
- Log out.
- Go to https://test.archiveofourown.org and the TOS prompt should appear. Check the box and press the button to accept the TOS. 
- Navigate to another page and make sure it doesn’t reappear.

Part 2:
- Open a private / incognito browser session.
- Go to https://test.archiveofourown.org and the TOS prompt should appear. Don't press the button yet.
- Go to https://test.archiveofourown.org?tos=yes and the TOS prompt should not appear.
- Navigate to another page and make sure it doesn’t reappear.
- Close your private / incognito browser session and open a new one.
- Go to https://test.archiveofourown.org/tos and make sure the TOS prompt does not appear.

Part 3:
- Browse logged out and accept the TOS prompt.
- Have a registered user that has not accepted the TOS (by asking a site admin to reset your account's accepted_tos_version, since accounts have to accept the TOS upon registration).
- Log in as this user. Check that the TOS prompt appears. Don't press the button yet.
- Go to https://test.archiveofourown.org?tos=yes. Check that the TOS prompt still appears.
- Accept the prompt, navigate to another page and make sure it doesn’t reappear.

# Log out

# Hide the work

# Log in as UserA
# Post work, and make note of its URL
# Log out
# Log in as UserB
# Access the work from Step 2 as UserB
# Wait for UserB's reading history to update (or run {{bundle exec rake readings:to_database}} from the command line)

# Refresh your History

The work is listed on your History. You cannot access the work.

h1. What should happen

The work should not be listed on your History.

# While logged in as UserB, attempt to visit the Marked for Later URL of the draft and hidden works you created: {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/####/mark_for_later}}
# You should get redirected to your dashboard with the error, “Sorry, you don't have permission to access the page you were trying to reach.”

Summary: Marvel Is Broken: The Missing FilterTagging Reason
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as a wrangler
# Create a canonical fandom tag "Metatag" (note: it doesn't have to be a fandom, but all tags must be canonical and of the same type)
# Create a canonical fandom tag "Subtag A" and add "Metatag" as its metatag
# Create a canonical fandom tag "Subtag of Subtag A" and add "Subtag A" as its metatag
# Create a canonical fandom tag "Subtag B" and add "Metatag" as its metatag
# Post a work that uses both "Subtag B" and "Subtag of Subtag A"
# Wait for listings to update and confirm the work appears in the listings for "Metatag," "Subtag A," and "Subtag of Subtag A."
# Edit the tag "Subtag of Subtag A" to remove "Subtag A" as a metatag

h1. What happens

The work posted in step 6 should continue to be in the work listings for "Metatag" because it still has "Subtag B."

h1. What happens

It is no longer included in the listings.

h1. Notes

This is affecting a bunch of Marvel Cinematic Universe works. Info from ticking instant:

{quote}ticking instant [17:49]
I was poking around the Avengers tag to try to see how the new crossover code was doing, and I noticed that there's nearly 20,000 works tagged with "The Avengers (Marvel Movies)" that don't seem to have their inherited "Marvel" filter.

This isn't part of the previous bug, since "The Avengers (Marvel Movies)" still seems to have "Marvel" as a meta tag. (I checked a newly-posted work.)

It turns out that there's actually yet another bug related to removing meta tags, this one affecting the FilterTaggings instead of the MetaTaggings.

If you have an overarching meta tag (like "Marvel") with two sub tags (like "Thor - All Media Types" and "The Avengers (Marvel Movies)"), and a subtag of the first sub tag (like "Thor (Movies)"), and you delete the MetaTagging between "Thor - All Media Types" and "Thor (Movies)", then any work tagged with both "Thor (Movies)" and "The Avengers (Marvel Movies)" will have the "Marvel" filter removed.

As far as I can tell, this has happened a bunch of times with Marvel tags, including: "Iron Man (Movies)", "Thor (Movies)", "Guardians of the Galaxy (Movies)", "The Incredible Hulk (2008)", and even a couple of comics tags as well.

Between the two bugs, there are over 40,000 works in the "Marvel Cinematic Universe" tag that are missing the "Marvel" meta tag.{quote}

Note from Tag Wrangling about the structure of the Marvel tags:

{quote}
The tag structure was:

- Marvel
-- Marvel Cinematic Universe
--- Thor (Marvel Movies)
--- The Avengers (Marvel Movies)
-- Thor - All Media Types
--- Thor (Marvel Movies)

and is now:

- Marvel 
-- Marvel Cinematic Universe
--- Thor (Marvel Movies) (with Thor - All Media Types synned to it)
--- The Avengers (Marvel Movies){quote}

This often happens alongside AO3-5508 in production, as seen in Marvel fandoms. The issues can, however, occur separately. (According to ticking, there are over 40,000 works in the "Marvel Cinematic Universe" tag that are missing the "Marvel" metatag, and 5508 accounts for about 13,000 of those.)

This is not super high priority as we are eyeing a rewrite of this code. However, it's good to have these things logged.

* the ID should be visible on work pages only to admins with the superadmin or policy_and_abuse role
* the ID should not be in the search index
* the ID should be scrubbed from orphan works after 72 hours

It can go in the work meta, above the IP Address. Usernames can consist of only numbers, so it’s necessary to emphasize that the ID, _not_ the name, is the main piece of information being presented. It could look like this:

{quote}Original Creator ID: user ID (username){quote}

If the account is deleted and the username is no longer accessible, it should just display the user ID. This would happen if:

* someone posts a work, orphans it, and deletes their account
* someone posts a work, invites a co-creator (who accepts the invitation), and then deletes their account

(Note: This was previously intended to also help with a different sort of abuse of the co-creator feature, but we’ve changed that behavior.)

*Testing*

{color:#bf2600}*Before merging*{color}*, post two works and orphan one of them.*{color:#bf2600} {color}This should be done within the 72-hour window.

Once this is in QA:

# Post a new work, then orphan it.
# View the work as a super- or policy and abuse admin. Make sure there’s a new field in the meta with the original creator’s user ID and username.
# Delete the creator’s account.
# View the work again as one of the correct admins, and make sure the original creator’s user ID is present (without a username this time).
# After 72 hours, view the work as an admin again and make sure the original creator’s information is no longer shown.

Summary: Limit the number of password resets
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: james_
Description:
We want to limit the number of password resets without getting too much in the way. 

We want to implement this in a way similar to [Devise Lockable|https://github.com/heartcombo/devise/blob/5d5636f03ac19e8188d99c044d4b5e90124313af/lib/devise/models/lockable.rb], including making this a concern module. Unlike Lockable, we won’t distinguish between successful and failed attempts.

Add config values for how many resets a user is allowed to request ({{ArchiveConfig.PASSWORD_RESET_LIMIT}}) before they must wait a given period of time ({{ArchiveConfig.PASSWORD_RESET_COOLDOWN_HOURS}}), e.g. 12 hours after 4 resets. 

(Note: You’re welcome to come up with better names for these; it was just easier to write the issue if we had names to reference instead of constantly needing to express the concept.)

Add a {{resets_requested}} integer column to the {{users}} table that records how many resets the user has requested. Ensure this field is indexed. 

We’ll use the existing {{reset_password_sent_at}} [column|https://github.com/heartcombo/devise/blob/5d5636f03ac19e8188d99c044d4b5e90124313af/lib/devise/models/recoverable.rb#L28] when we need to reference when a reset was last sent. 

When someone makes a password reset request for an account, increase {{resets_requested}} by one and inform the person how many reset requests remain. The info on remaining resets can be added to the current flash message, so it reads:

{quote}Check your email for instructions on how to reset your password. You may reset your password {{#{ArchiveConfig.PASSWORD_RESET_LIMIT - user.resets_requested}}} more times. After that, you will need to wait {{#{ArchiveConfig.PASSWORD_RESET_COOLDOWN_HOURS}}} hours before requesting another reset.{quote}

Even unsuccessful attempts should increase {{resets_requested}}.

If {{user.reset_password_sent_at > ArchiveConfig.PASSWORD_RESET_COOLDOWN_HOURS.hours.ago}} or {{user.resets_requested <= ArchiveConfig.PASSWORD_RESET_LIMIT}}, send a password reset.

If the password cannot be reset, an error flash message should be shown.

{quote}You cannot reset your password at this time. More resets will become available at #{(time of last reset + ArchiveConfig.PASSWORD_RESET_PERIOD) in user's time zone}.{quote}

If a reset is requested and {{user.reset_password_sent_at > ArchiveConfig.PASSWORD_RESET_COOLDOWN_HOURS.hours.ago}}, the {{user.resets_requested}} should be set back to 1 and a reset should be sent.

*Testing*

{{PASSWORD_RESET_COOLDOWN_HOURS}} is set to 12 hours and {{PASSWORD_RESET_LIMIT}} is set to 3

* Request a password reset and ensure the success message is correct and you receive the email. 
* Repeat X times, until you have no resets left. Ensure the error message is correct and you do not receive an email.
* When X hours pass, request a password reset and ensure the success message is correct and you receive the email.

Summary: Collections: Occasional 500 error when revealing or de-anoning due to lingering CollectionItem for deleted Work
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Details and steps to reproduce
If you're running an anonymous or unrevealed collection and you reveal or de-anon all the works by unchecking the unrevealed/anonymous option in Collection Settings, it occasionally gives a 500 error. (Some of the works may be revealed or de-anoned upon reloading the collection's works list.)

This happens because someone deleted a work that was in the collection, but for some reason, the {{CollectionItem}} associated with that {{Work}} object still exists. A database admin can delete the {{CollectionItem}} and the challenge owner can then successfully reveal or de-anon the collection.

These steps will not always reproduce the bug, but here is the process:

# Log in
# Browse > Collections > New Collection
# Fill in required information
# Check either “This collection is unrevealed” or “This collection is anonymous” (or both\!)
# Press “Submit”
# Follow the “Post to Collection” link
# Fill in required information (the collection info will already be filled in because you used the “Post to Collection” link)
# Post Without Preview (or Preview and then Post – it doesn’t actually matter)
# Return to the collection via the link at the top of the work
# Repeat steps 6-8
# Follow the “Edit” link on the top of your work
# Follow the “Delete” link on the top of the work
# Choose “OK” to confirm deletion
# Return to your collection
# Follow the “Collection Settings” link in the dashboard
# Uncheck “This collection is unrevealed” and/or “This collection is anonymous”
# Press “Update”

h1. Fixing
Ideally, we would fix whatever causes the {{CollectionItem}} to linger even after its work is deleted.

However, since the cause of that may be difficult to track down, we can settle for making it so unrevealing or de-anoning a collection doesn't error when it encounters a {{CollectionItem}} without a {{Work}}.

Here, have a convenient link to the methods related to revealing works/creators: [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/d049ce6a46933d56ec9e5fff93c62c437c5493d8/app/models/collection.rb#L447-L472]

h1. Notes
Note that [AO3-5544|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5544] can also lead to some works in a collection remaining unrevealed, but in that case, no error occurs when updating the collection settings.

h1. Testing
Because this is not something we can currently reproduce on demand to test manually, we will likely need to create an automated test for this scenario and trust that if it passes, the issue is fixed.

Summary: Collections: Works occasionally not marked unrevealed and anonymous upon posting directly to an unrevealed or anonymous collection
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Overview and steps to reproduce
If you have an anonymous, unrevealed collection (or, quite likely, a collection that is only one of those) and someone posts a work to said collection, the work and its creator may still be visible to all who encounter said work.

These steps will not always reproduce the bug, but here is the process:

# Log in
# Browse > Collections > New Collection
# Fill in required information
# Check both “This collection is unrevealed” and “This collection is anonymous”
# Press “Submit”
# Follow the “Post to Collection” link
# Fill in required information (the collection info will already be filled in because you used the “Post to Collection” link)
# Post Without Preview

h1. Details
This is a fascinating situation where the Work is incorrect ({{in_anon_collection: false, in_unrevealed_collection: false}}), but the CollectionItem is correct ({{anonymous: true, unrevealed: true}}):

{code}2.3.0 :001 > w = Work.find(000)
=> #<Work id: 000, expected_number_of_chapters: 1, created_at: "2017-11-17 20:20:18", updated_at: "2017-11-17 20:40:41", major_version: 1, minor_version: 1, posted: true, language_id: 1, restricted: false, word_count: 7498, hidden_by_admin: false, delta: false, revised_at: "2017-11-17 20:20:58", backdate: false, endnotes: "", imported_from_url: nil, hit_count_old: 0, last_visitor_old: nil, complete: true, summary_sanitizer_version: 1, notes_sanitizer_version: 1, endnotes_sanitizer_version: 1, work_skin_id: nil, in_anon_collection: false, in_unrevealed_collection: false, anon_commenting_disabled: false, spam: false, spam_checked_at: "2017-11-17 20:40:41", moderated_commenting_enabled: false>

2.3.0 :002 > c_i = CollectionItem.where(item_type: "Work", item_id: 000)
=> #<ActiveRecord::Relation [#<CollectionItem id: 000, collection_id: 105699, item_id: 000, item_type: "Work", user_approval_status: 1, collection_approval_status: 0, created_at: "2017-11-17 20:20:28", updated_at: "2017-11-17 20:20:28", anonymous: true, unrevealed: true>]>{code}
Please note that the {{Work}} and {{CollectionItem}} IDs have been changed to {{000}} and some work fields ({{title}}, {{summary}}, {{notes}}, {{authors_to_sort_on}}, {{title_to_sort_on}}, {{ip_address}}) removed for privacy, as they are not relevant.

We confirmed that this work \-\- and at least one other work affected by this issue \-\- belonged only to one anonymous, unrevealed collection.

We note that the {{Work}} and {{CollectionItem}} were created at the exact same time ({{created_at: "2017-11-17 20:20:28"}}), although this is not in itself unusual \-\- it happens on works that are properly marked unrevealed and anonymous as well.

We suspect a race condition. 😭

{{CollectionItem.update_work}} is one of the few {{after_commit}} callbacks we have that tries to read data that was just written in the previous commit. Because it's an {{after_commit}} callback, not an {{after_save}}, the database queries to look up {{user_approved_collection_items}} (in {{update_anon_unrevealed}}, which is called by {{CollectionItem.update_work}}) occur _outside_ of the transaction, which in theory would allow them them be routed to the read-only SQL servers, which have some chance of lagging behind the master SQL server by a transaction or two. (h/t ticking instant for the discovery and explanation.)

h1. Testing

Summary: Can't show hidden tags on external works or challenge prompts
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Reproducing

Set your preferences to *"Hide additional tags (you can still choose to show them)"* and/or *"Hide warnings (you can still choose to show them)"*.

Go to one of the following: 

* a *bookmark listing* that includes an external works with additional tags (please refer to the “Testing” section for notes on this)
* the *Prompts (#)* page for a prompt meme that allows participants to include warnings or additional tags in their prompts
* the *Requests Summary* page for a gift exchange that allows participants to include warnings or additional tags in their requests

Click the *“Show warnings”* or *"Show additional tags"* link in the blurb.

You’d expect to see tags appear, but nothing seems to happen.

*Note:* The preference only applies to items owned/created by other users. If it’s your prompt, for example the tags will always be visible.

h1. Diagnosing

Luckily for us, an error is logged!

Here is [an error for ExternalWorks|https://rpm.newrelic.com/accounts/115892/applications/190034/traced_errors/abd29730-c637-11e8-b397-0242ac110009_0_14784?original_error_id=abd29730-c637-11e8-b397-0242ac110009_0_14784]:

{quote}Error message
RuntimeError: Redshirt: Attempted to constantize invalid class initialize show_hidden ExternalWork
Sample stack trace (show Rails)
…ases/20180929162204/app/controllers/tags_controller.rb: 136:in `show_hidden'{quote}

And [an error for Requests|https://rpm.newrelic.com/accounts/115892/applications/190034/traced_errors/2a4ecb78-c69d-11e8-b397-0242ac110009_93727_108484/similar_errors?original_error_id=2a4ecb78-c69d-11e8-b397-0242ac110009_93727_108484]:

{quote}Error message

Sample stack trace (show Rails)
…ases/20180929162204/app/controllers/tags_controller.rb: 136:in `show_hidden'{quote}

h1. Fixing

ExternalWork and Request need to be allowed in the [show_hidden action of the tags controller|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/db06765a8cfa5d300efabcbc33f4e39302aaf1a3/app/controllers/tags_controller.rb#L136].

h1. Testing

Summary: Draft deletion task sometimes deletes chapters but leaves work itself behind
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
Sometimes, if a user has a draft that is more than 30 days old, the draft deletion task will delete the chapter(s) but leave the Work object behind. 

Not only does this leave the draft blurb visible on the user's drafts page, causing confusion (the user gets a 500 error when attempting to open or edit the draft), but if the work was in a collection, it can also cause 500 errors for moderators attempting to reveal or de-anon works (or, I believe, access the Manage Items page).

It's possible this is also related to tags used solely on drafts still showing up in the wrangling bins even when they are more than a month old.

Unfortunately, this is not something we can reproduce on demand, but it appears to be happening with increasing frequency. 

We will add more details when/if we get them.
Comment:
24/Nov/18 7:48 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;Currently, the draft deletion task deletes all the chapters first, and then deletes the works. This has a couple of effects:

(a) If the task encounters an error partway through deleting the works, this means that all of the works that it failed to delete will have no chapters. If it's an intermittent error, then the issue should be cleaned up the next time the draft deletion task is run. But if it's a persistent error, then every single draft could linger without chapters until someone intervenes.

(b) Even if it runs without a single error, if the draft deletion task takes a long time, then each of the works will spend some amount of time with missing chapters, potentially resulting in temporary issues like the one described in the bug report.

The solution is to stop deleting the chapters first, and instead allow the work's callbacks to handle chapter deletion. Using callbacks ensures that the chapter deletion and the work deletion occur in the same transaction, so that there's much less danger of running into works without chapters.

It's hard to test for this issue specifically, but the PR that I wrote rewrites the draft deletion task. So for manual testing, it'd be good to do the following:
# Make a draft (preferably with a bunch of interesting associations, like series and collections).
# Use the rails console to update the draft's {{created_at}} date to over a month ago.
# Run the draft deletion task.

If that results in the draft being deleted, the code should be good to go.

Summary: Collections: Some works occasionally not revealed (may also happen with anonymous setting)
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Steps to Reproduce
These steps will not always reproduce the bug, but here is the process:

# Log in
# Browse > Collections > New Collection
# Fill in required information
# Check “This collection is unrevealed”
# Press “Submit”
# Follow the “Post to Collection” link
# Fill in required information (the collection info will already be filled in because you used the “Post to Collection” link)
# Post Without Preview
# Repeat previous 3 steps until you have your desired number of works
# Return to the collection, e.g. by following the link in the work meta
# Follow the “Collection Settings” link
# Uncheck "This collection is unrevealed"
# Press "Update"

h1. What happens
Most of the works are revealed, but not all of them.

h1. What should happen
All of the works should be revealed.

h1. Notes
The {{CollectionItem}} for the work correctly has its {{unrevealed}} column updated to {{false}}. However, the corresponding {{Work}} does not get its {{in_unrevealed_collection}} column updated to {{false}}. It's _not_ a case of the work belonging to multiple unrevealed collections, as you can see from the following example (identifying data removed):

{quote}2.3.0 :007 > work = Work.find(000)
=> \#<Work id: 000, expected_number_of_chapters: 1, created_at: "2018-10-01 18:06:16", updated_at: "2018-10-19 01:59:30", major_version: 1, minor_version: 2, posted: true, language_id: 1, restricted: false, word_count: 0, hidden_by_admin: false, delta: false, revised_at: "2018-10-01 18:07:07", backdate: false, imported_from_url: nil, hit_count_old: 0, last_visitor_old: nil, complete: true, summary_sanitizer_version: 1, notes_sanitizer_version: 1, endnotes_sanitizer_version: 1, work_skin_id: nil, in_anon_collection: false, in_unrevealed_collection: true, anon_commenting_disabled: false, spam: false, spam_checked_at: "2018-10-01 18:10:38", moderated_commenting_enabled: false>

2.3.0 :008 > work.collection_items
=> \#<ActiveRecord::Associations::CollectionProxy \[\#<CollectionItem id: 000, collection_id: 000, item_id: 000, item_type: "Work", user_approval_status: 1, collection_approval_status: 1, created_at: "2018-10-01 18:06:17", updated_at: "2018-10-01 22:40:14", anonymous: false, unrevealed: false>\]>

{quote}
Quite possibly a race condition and quite possibly related to [AO3-5533|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5533].

{{CollectionItem.update_work}} is one of the few {{after_commit}} callbacks we have that tries to read data that was just written in the previous commit. Because it's an {{after_commit}} callback, not an {{after_save}}, the database queries to look up {{user_approved_collection_items}} (in {{update_anon_unrevealed}}, which is called by {{CollectionItem.update_work}}) occur _outside_ of the transaction, which in theory would allow them them be routed to the read-only SQL servers, which have some chance of lagging behind the master SQL server by a transaction or two. (h/t ticking instant for the discovery and explanation.)

[AO3-5532|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5532] can also cause some works in a collection to stay unrevealed, but the major difference is _that_ involves a 500 error when updating the collection settings. This does not have an error.

This can probably happen with anonymous works, too, but we’re not sure.

h1. Testing
Because this cannot be reproduced at will, it is unlikely the fix can be tested. All we can do is take several shots at posting to and then revealing an unrevealed collection to confirm the correct behavior still happens and watch for any new reports of this bug after the fix is deployed.

Summary: Automate gem updates with Dependabot
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: redsummernight
Description:
Right now we get notified of vulnerabilities by gem_security.sh, which fails builds. This makes it difficult to see other test failures.

If we use [Dependabot|https://dependabot.com/], we will get notified of gem vulnerabilities by pull requests that modified Gemfile/Gemfile.lock. The new workflow would be like:

- The bot open pull requests for gem updates. The bot can be configured to use the necessary labels: "Gem Updates" and "Awaiting Reviews".
- We create JIRA issues and edit the issue IDs into the bot's PR titles. After that, the workflow goes on as normal. As long as the issue is in JIRA and the PR is open, we won't forget about the update.

To switch to the bot, we need to:

- Modify gem_security.sh to stop "exit 1".
- Modify the Gemfile to use the Ruby version explicitly: the bot cannot resolve File.read.
- Sign up for an account on the bot site (any staffer can do it).
- Set the bot to run daily, and only include security updates.
- On the first PR by the bot, set the default labels for future PRs.

rake After:migrate_pseud_icons

Once it is done, we can run the deploy as normal (and then as soon as possible afterwards apply the Ansible to push out the required configs).

Finally, re-run the After task to catch any icons uploaded on old servers during the deploy.

{code:java}2.3.4 :004 > Work.find(5).approved_collections
  Work Load (1.0ms)  SELECT  `works`.* FROM `works` WHERE `works`.`id` = 5 LIMIT 1
  ↳ (irb):4:in `irb_binding'
  Collection Load (0.5ms)  SELECT  `collections`.* FROM `collections` INNER JOIN `collection_items` ON `collections`.`id` = `collection_items`.`collection_id` WHERE `collection_items`.`item_id` = 5 AND `collection_items`.`item_type` = 'Work' AND `collection_items`.`user_approval_status` = 1 AND `collection_items`.`collection_approval_status` = 1 LIMIT 11
  CollectionItem Load (0.4ms)  SELECT `collection_items`.* FROM `collection_items` WHERE `collection_items`.`collection_id` IN (1, 3){code}

The first query, of course, is the work being loaded from {{Work.find(5)}}. The second query loads the {{approved_collections}}, just as desired. But the third query loads every single CollectionItem in one of the work's approved collections (not just the work's CollectionItems). This means that if you have a single work {{w}} in a collection with thousands of collection items, calling {{w.approved_collections}} will load every one of those thousands of CollectionItems.

This shouldn't happen. The third query is the result of a mistake in the definition of {{approved_collections}}, and should disappear when the definition is fixed.

Note that this also affects {{user_approved_collections}} and {{rejected_collections}}.

Summary: Unwrangled tag count doesn't decrease when tag is wrangled to a different fandom
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce
# Log in as a tag wrangler.
# Post a work in one of your assigned fandoms, and on that work, include at least two brand new tags. We'll assume they are freeforms called Tag A and Tag B.
# Go to your wrangling page ([https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglers/USERS]) and follow the appropriate link to see these unwrangled tags. In the case of our example, you'd be going to the unwrangled freeform page for your fandom ([https://archiveofourown.org/tags/FANDOM/wrangle?show=freeforms&status=unwrangled]).
# In the Tag Name column of the table, check the box next to Tag A.
# In the "Wrangle to Fandom(s)" field, enter the name of your fandom (or choose it from the autocomplete).
# Press one of the "Wrangle" buttons.
# Return to your wrangling page and note that the number of unwrangled tags for your fandom has decreased.
# Again, follow the appropriate link to see the remaining unwrangled tag you created.
# In the Tag Name column of the table, check the box next to Tag B.
# In the "Wrangle to Fandom(s)" field, enter the name of some other fandom, e.g. No Fandom.
# Press one of the "Wrangle" buttons.
# Return to your wrangling page.

h1. What should happen
The number of unwrangled tags for your fandom should decrease.

h1. What happens instead
The number of unwrangled tags for your fandom is the same.

h1. Notes
Wrangling a tag to a fandom currently updates the unwrangled tag count for the fandom the tag was wrangled _to_. This happens because the fandom tag's updated_at date is changed, which [changes the cache key|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/5c29fc05e5f56019855970763b50f2efff928f4c/app/models/tag.rb#L1252].

Instead, it should update the unwrangled tag count of the tag's _suggested fandoms_ (pre_fandom_ids in Elasticsearch), since those are the counts that are actually affected when the tag is wrangled. It would probably make sense to do this with a callback in CommonTagging.

In AO3-4056, we [converted the database to UTF8MB4 encoding|https://railsmachine.com/articles/2017/05/19/converting-a-rails-database-to-utf8mb4.html].

The second stage conversion script does this:
{code:ruby}
default = (column.default.blank?) ? '' : "DEFAULT \"#{column.default}\""
{code}

This means columns with {{DEFAULT ''}} lose that attribute. Let's add them back:

- archive_faqs: slug
- collections: icon_alt_text, icon_comment_text
- invite_requests: simplified_email
- languages: sortable_name
- pseuds: icon_alt_text, icon_comment_text
- skins: icon_alt_text
- taggings: tagger_type, taggable_type
- tags: name, sortable_name

Note that the conversion script would work correctly if we replaced instances of {{column.default.blank?}} with {{column.default.nil?}}.

Summary: Rename Warning class
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
Our current code uses a class named Warning for Archive warning [+tags+|https://archiveofourown.org/faq/tags?language_id=en#whatisatag]. This class will need to be renamed ArchiveWarning to avoid conflicts with newer versions of Ruby. We would like this change to be made in a separate pull request prior to upgrading Ruby.
 
 Unfortunately, there are numerous places in our code where we use the tag class names to create user-facing text. For example, we call tag_type.classify.pluralize to create [headings in this tag set partial|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/46e9d9b713ba54dc6e6beb14e50255196c2465cc/app/views/tag_set_nominations/_show_by_tag_type.html.erb#L3]. In this case, renaming the Warning class would have the unwanted side effect of changing the user-facing text from "Warnings" to "ArchiveWarnings". 
 
 Fortunately, [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5123#icft=AO3-5123|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5123#icft=AO3-5123|smart-link] ([pull request|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/3013/files]) has a solution for dealing with situations where the preferred display text does _not_ match the class name. Much like [the label_name for the Freeform class|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/3013/files#diff-eb166e301667da04821038f1e54effc5R5] was set to "Additional Tags", we'd like to set the label_name for the ArchiveWarning class to "Warnings". Then we'd like to use this method in our views as much as possible.
 
 It's also important to ensure that class names used in the HTML don't get changed from warning/warnings to archivewarning/archivewarnings/archive_warning/archive_warnings/etc. The existing class names get used a lot by Archive users who create site skins (e.g. some people want to hide things related to warnings, whereas other users want to highlight warnings).
 
 *Reference*
 
 A [+branch+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/compare/master...sarken:AO3-5037_ruby_rename_warning?expand=1] containing an initial pass at this is available on GitHub. 
 
 There is also an [earlier pull request|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/3526] that predates the introduction of the label_name method.
 
 *Testing notes*
 
 This affects the CSS classes used on warning-related areas, so please create a site skin with the following CSS and use it while testing:
 
 {code}.Warning,
 .Warnings,
 .Archive_Warning,
 .Archive_Warnings,
 .ArchiveWarning,
 .ArchiveWarnings,
 .Archive,
 .Archives,
 .archive_warning,
 .archive_warnings,
 .archivewarning,
 .archivewarnings,
 .archive,
 .archives {
 background: hotpink !important;
 font-size: 1.5em;
 outline: 5px solid hotpink !important;
 }{code}
 
 If you see anything highlighted or outlined in pink, please comment with a screenshot. (Feel free to change it to some other color that is more noticeable to you, but make sure to leave the \!important.)
 
 *Testing notes II*
 
While wearing the hotpink site skin:
 
- Viewing works
-- Links to Warnings on work metas and work blurbs work.
-- Work blurbs show the correct symbols for Warnings.
-- Share a work: embed code should have warnings.
-- Tag RSS feed: links to Warnings show up and work.
-- Download a work (any format): links to Warnings show up and work.

Summary: Tag connections are lost when canonical tags are synned, aka the Tag Drop bug
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: briar_pipe
Description:
*Steps to reproduce*

Log in as an admin. On the edit page of a canonical tag, use the "Synonym of" field to syn that canonical tag to another tag, existing or not. This bug is intermittent, so it may take several tries to trigger it.

*What happens*

Periodically, all the connections from the old canonical tag are not transferred to the new tag. This includes metatags, subtags, synonyms, and other child tags. It's most obvious with fandom and character tags, which tend to have a lot of child tags. With fandom tags, this results in all the child tags and synonyms appearing in the mass bins again, as they have lost their fandom connection.

*What should happen*

All tag connections from the canonical should be transferred to the tag it is synned to, whether that tag is newly created or existed before.

Because this bug does not always happen, testing should be conducted on many tags.
Comment:
08/Feb/19 6:37 AM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;Setting {{syn_string=}} to a valid merger results in an async call to transfer the associations:

{code}        if new_merger && self.errors.empty?
          self.canonical = false
          self.merger_id = new_merger.id
          async(:add_merger_associations){code}
([Source|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/96935fb4a4bd73575e4ddcaee96b8b31d9e8ad2b/app/models/tag.rb#L1174-L1177])

However, that action also triggers another async call in a {{before_update}} hook in the Tag class:

{code}    if self.canonical_changed? && !self.canonical?
      self.async(:remove_canonical_associations){code}
([Source|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/96935fb4a4bd73575e4ddcaee96b8b31d9e8ad2b/app/models/tag.rb#L1082-L1083])

Since setting the synonym also sets canonical to false at the same time, as soon as the tag is saved this callback will queue up a call to {{remove_canonical_associations}} (which does exactly what you’d think).

So effectively you have dueling asynchronous function calls. If {{add_merger_associations}} acts first, the associations are transferred properly. If {{remove_canonical_associations}} acts first, the associations are deleted instead of transferring.

(The call to {{add_merger_associations}} is enqueued first, so technically it should be run first, if only by a narrow margin. But it also takes more time to run, so if both functions start at roughly same time, {{remove_canonical_associations}} is more likely to finish first.)

08/Feb/19 11:17 AM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;This can also result from stale data. The call to {{add_merger_associations}} only works if the merger can be read from the database at the beginning of {{add_merger_associations}}, but it’s added to the Resque queue before anything is even written to the database.

Summary: Edit Work page doesn't offer options for interacting with draft chapters if the work has only one posted chapter
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
*Steps to reproduce*

# Log in
# Post > New Work
# Fill in required information
# Press "Post Without Preview"
# Follow "Add Chapter"
# Fill in required information
# Press "Preview"
# Press "Save Without Posting" to save draft chapter
# Follow "Edit Work"

*What should happen*

To make sure users know they have multiple chapters and can access them, it should behave like editing a work with multiple posted chapters:

* Next to the "Add Chapter" button at the top of the form should be options to edit chapters, e.g. {{Edit Chapter: \[1\] \[2 (Draft)\] \[3 (Draft)\]}}, where the brackets indicate button-style text.
* Next to that should be a Manage Chapters link
** [AO3-4313|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-4313] exists for resolving the issue of things not working properly if a user reorders their work so the first chapter is a draft.
** [AO3-3846|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3846] exists for making draft chapters visible on the reordering page.
* The Work Text section should not be displayed. Instead, the user should have to go to the relevant Edit Chapter page to edit a chapter’s text.

*What happens instead*

The options aren't there, making it easy to forget you have draft chapters and hard to get to them if you remember.

*Notes*

It appears this is related to caching.

* In the edit page navigation, we [only display the edit and manage links if @chapters|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/80c950525269715a85ebe63a58c234a2822fdac9/app/views/works/edit.html.erb#L10-L20].
