Summary: Limit referrer information sent to other sites
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
When you follow a link from the Archive to another site or go to a page with the Twitter widget (e.g. a work), a header like the following is sent to that site:

{code:java}Provisional headers are shown
DNT: 1
Referer: https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/0000/chapters/000?view_adult=true
Upgrade-Insecure-Requests: 1
User-Agent: Mozilla/5.0 (Windows NT 10.0; Win64; x64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/72.0.3626.109 Safari/537.36{code}

The header contains the URL of the page you're coming from (or, in the case of Twitter, the page the widget is being loaded on – in other words, Twitter can tell what work you're accessing, and if you're logged in, that information is likely associated with your Twitter account).

To prevent this, we'd like to update [config/application.rb|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/config/application.rb] to set the {{Referrer-Policy}} to {{same-origin}}, as described in [Setting HTTP security headers in Rails|https://www.marksayson.com/blog/setting_http_security_headers_in_rails/].

To test, open your browser’s developer tools and check the response headers after navigating from one Archive page to another. The {{Referrer-Policy}} should say {{same-origin}}. (You may need to consult Google for instructions specific to your browser.)

When testing, we should also make sure the Twitter share widget on works is still functional, and we should also check that New Relic still contains referrer information.

Summary: Caching on work index pages doesn't check for include_work_search or exclude_work_search
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
*Steps to Reproduce:*
# Log in (to avoid nginx's cache, since it may complicate the results).
# Visit the following URL for all Marvel works tagged with "Hurt/Comfort":
https://test.archiveofourown.org/works?include_work_search%5Bfreeform_ids%5D%5B%5D=2379&tag_id=Marvel
# Visit the main Marvel listing:
https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Marvel/works

*What Should Happen:* Visiting the first URL should show the first page of a search with a total of around 3,000 works, and should only display works that are tagged with a synonym or subtag of "Hurt/Comfort." Visiting the second URL should show the first page of a search with a total of around 50,000 works, and should include works that aren't tagged with "Hurt/Comfort."

*What Actually Happens:* Both pages show exactly the same search results. If the {{include_work_search}} version is cached, then the second URL will have the wrong number of results. If the plain version is cached, then the first URL will have the wrong number of results.

(I think in theory it might be possible to get the right results if the second page view is perfectly timed to match the 20 minute expiration for the search results cache, but otherwise both results will be the same -- and one of them will be wrong.)

*Explanation:* Currently, {{WorksController#index}} decides whether to cache the search results by checking {{params\[:work_search\]}} to ensure that the user hasn't refined their search in any way. But since the Elasticsearch upgrade, search parameters are split between {{params\[:work_search\]}}, {{params\[:include_work_search\]}}, and {{params\[:exclude_work_search\]}}.

In normal use, any query that sets {{params\[:include_work_search\]}} or {{params\[:exclude_work_search\]}} will also set {{params\[:work_search\]}}, so this isn't an issue.

However, if someone tries to edit the URL to eliminate blank parameters, they may end up with a search that sets only {{params\[:include_work_search\]}} and/or {{params\[:exclude_work_search\]}}, without also setting {{params\[:work_search\]}}. That kind of search is cached using the same cache key as a blank search. As a result, if one person visits the page with extra search params and one person doesn't, the results that both receive will depend on who visits the page first.

Either {{WorksController#index}} should also check both {{params\[:include_work_search\]}} and {{params\[:exclude_work_search\]}}, or the work search parameters should be refactored so that they all fall under {{params\[:work_search\]}}.

Summary: Tag Set nominations aren't updated when the nominating pseud is deleted
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
Tag Set nominations are tied to pseuds, but when the pseud in question is deleted (not the user as a whole, just the pseud), the nominations are untouched (meaning that they still exist in the database, and still point to a pseud that no longer exists).

This doesn't appear to cause any 500 errors, but it does remove all association between the user and their previous nominations, allowing the user to nominate tags to the same tag set multiple times.

*Steps to reproduce:*

# Log in as User A.
# Go to Browse > Tags > Tag Sets > New Tag Set.
# Check the "Currently taking nominations?" box.
# Make sure that at least one of the numbers in the "Nomination Limits" section is non-zero.
# Fill in the rest of the fields as desired and press "Submit" to create the tagset.
# Log in as User B.
# Go to My Preferences > Manage My Pseuds > New Pseud.
# Fill in the fields as desired and press "Create" to create a new pseud.
# View the tag set created by User A and click "Nominate."
# Select the pseud that you just created.
# Nominate tags as desired, and then press "Submit."
# Go to My Preferences > Manage My Pseuds.
# Find the pseud that you just created/nominated for, and press the "Delete" button.
# View the tag set again and click "Nominate."
# Nominate different tags from before and press "Submit."
# Log in as User A.
# View nominations for the tag set, and note that both of User B's nominations are visible.

*What should happen:* When User B views the tag set the second time, they should see the "My Nominations" button, not the "Nominate" button. (Note that the button in the list of tag sets always has the label "Nominate," regardless of whether you've nominated before. But if you click on it it should redirect to the nominations that you previously submitted, not to a page that allows you to enter new nominations.)

*How to fix it:* Either tag set nominations should be associated with the user instead of the pseud (since it's not like anyone other than the nominating user can see which pseud they used), or the pseud_id on tag nominations should be updated to the default pseud whenever a pseud is deleted.

Not sure if that’s normal behavior.*{quote}

I’m pretty sure that’s the pre-existing behavior (though it might be worth a bug report). The {{owner_changes}} parameter is processed before the {{moderator_changes}} parameter (because it’s first in the call to permit). The call to {{owner_changes=}} causes the user to be completely removed as both owner and moderator. So when {{moderator_changes=}} is called, it treats it as adding a new moderator, since the user no longer has any relationship with the OwnedTagSet.

(The reason I wanted to test tagset ownerships is because at one point the PR included some more serious changes to {{parse_bylines}}, which is used in both {{owner_changes=}} and {{moderator_changes=}}. The changes have been reverted for the most part, so it pretty much just needs a quick check to make sure nothing unexpected occurs when parsing bylines.)

Summary: Rewrite FilterTagging and MetaTagging code
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
There are a number of bugs with the current MetaTagging and FilterTagging code. Rather than making the current code more complex to try to fix these bugs, it would be good to rewrite the code to make the MetaTagging and FilterTagging calculations more straightforward. It would also be good to introduce more tools to handle these types of issues in the future.

There are a couple of general issues that need to be addressed in any rewrite, and a few other changes that would also be good to make:

h3. Calling asynchronous functions before the data is committed

Most of the functions that update FilterTaggings access information about tags from the database – such as checking the current merger and whether it's canonical. But most of those asynchronous functions are called in {{before_save}} or {{before_update}} callbacks, which means that if the transaction takes a while to commit, the data won't be available at the time that the asynchronous function runs.

(The worst example of this is {{syn_string=}}, which calls {{async(:add_merger_associations)}}. Thanks to the way that the TagsController is set up, this means that when the asynchronous job is enqueued, the transaction hasn't even *started* yet, much less been committed.)

Unfortunately, the fix for this is more tricky than just making all of the callbacks occur {{after_commit}}, because the asynchronous function calls are based on which fields have changed. If a single tag object is saved more than once in the same transaction, any {{after_commit}} callback will only be able to check the most recent changes. (And if you have multiple copies of the same Tag object floating around, you're not even guaranteed to see the most recent changes, or any changes at all.) You can see an example of this type of issue if you run the following in the console:

{code:ruby}Fandom.last.update(canonical: false)
Tag.after_commit do |record|
  raise "BROKEN" unless record.saved_change_to_canonical?
end
Tag.transaction do
  Fandom.last.touch
  Fandom.last.update(canonical: true)
end{code}

I'm not sure if there are any transactions that result in the same tag being saved and/or touched more than once, but it would be good to prevent that sort of bug from occurring in the future, given how difficult it can be to diagnose.

So instead of changing to {{after_commit}}, a better way to handle this is to use the {{after_commit_everywhere}} gem to ensure that each async call occurs after the data is committed.

h3. Computing changes instead of calculating from scratch

Currently, the computations for FilterTaggings and MetaTaggings are split up into multiple functions. When updating FilterTaggings, there's one function for when a new synonym is added, one for when a synonym is deleted, one for when a meta tag is added, and one for when a meta tag is deleted. There's a similar set up for inherited MetaTaggings: one function for when a direct MetaTagging is added, and one function for when a direct MetaTagging is deleted. Effectively, the current code is all about trying to figure out how the change in the tag should be mapped to a change in the filters and inherited meta tags.

The issue with this occurs when there are multiple changes to the tag in quick succession. When a synonym is unhooked from a canonical, the {{remove_filter_taggings}} function looks up the list of meta tags of the former canonical and checks whether the filters for those meta tags should still be listed on the works tagged with the synonym. However, if one of the meta tags of the former canonical is removed in the time after {{remove_filter_taggings}} is enqueued but before it runs, then it won't delete filters for that meta tag. (This is the cause of AO3-5432.)

In some ways, this the opposite of the first issue. The function {{remove_filter_taggings}} is accessing data that's too new – if it had the list of meta tags at the time that the function was originally enqueued, it would be able to correctly figure out which meta tags to remove. 

In general, in order to make these sorts of sequential changes work properly, you'd need all of the asynchronous functions to run in exactly the right order, and each function would need to store a bunch of information about the state of the tags at the time that it was enqueued. Unfortunately, Resque isn't really built around the idea of having jobs occur in the right order – the whole point of having multiple workers for the same queue is so that more jobs can be run in parallel. And when a job fails, Resque assumes that it can be rerun later, regardless of what that might do to the order. As far as I can tell, these sorts of incremental changes make concurrency issues almost inevitable when using Resque.

A cleaner way to address this is to recompute which MetaTaggings/FilterTaggings should exist from scratch each time. (This is the way that {{ExternalWork#check_filter_taggings}} works, though it's currently a little buggy.) Inherited MetaTaggings can be computed from direct MetaTaggings using a simple breadth-first search. FilterTaggings can be computed from Taggings, Tags, and MetaTaggings. This approach means that there's no danger of breaking the MetaTaggings/FilterTaggings by performing operations in the wrong order. As long as the information retrieved from the database is correct, the MetaTaggings/FilterTaggings will be correct.

This also has the benefit of making it very easy to add tools to help fix issues in the event that something does go wrong. The same code can be used in a rake task to fix all MetaTaggings/FilterTaggings, or in a troubleshooting feature available to admins/tag wranglers.

h3. Other issues to address

*Tools for fixing existing problems.* There are several meta tag trees and a large number of works that have already been affected by these issues. There should be some rake tasks for fixing filters.

*Tools for fixing future problems.* There still could be future issues if the database suffers from replication delays or if the servers crash at an inconvenient time. It would be good to add tools in the admin/tag wrangling interface – like the "Reindex Work" and "Reindex Tag" buttons – to fix the filters for just one tag or just one work, instead of having to run an entire rake task.

*Unify the Work and ExternalWork code.* Currently, Works and ExternalWorks each have their own version of the code for calculating filters. This results in inconsistencies (such as [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5433#icft=AO3-5433|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5433#icft=AO3-5433|smart-link]) and duplicated code. The filter code in those classes should be refactored to DRY it up and reduce inconsistencies.

*Don't reindex bookmarks when wrangling.* The Elasticsearch upgrade moved all filter information into the BookmarkedWorkIndexer. This means that bookmarks don't have any information that would change after wrangling, so there's no need to reindex them when a tag becomes canonical/non-canonical. This results in the current wrangling code doing more work than it needs to.

*Reindex everything when changing the tag name or type.* There is, however, a case where the bookmarks do need to be reindexed: when the name of the tag has changed. That kind of change actually requires a lot of reindexing that's currently not performed.

----

h2. Testing Instructions

This is supposed to be an extensive rewrite of the underpinnings of tag wrangling, so it would be good to have a tag wrangler or two put it through its paces and see whether there's any unexpected behavior.

In addition, there are some specific tests that should probably be run:

h3. Troubleshooting Tests

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in

Summary: Drop filterable_type column for common_taggings
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
When running {{consistency_fail}} to check for uniqueness constraints enforced in the codebase but not backed by the database, one of the results shows a missing index for CommonTaggings:
{code}
CommonTagging        common_taggings (common_tag_id, filterable_id)
{code}
There is, however, a very similar uniqueness constraint that is enforced by the database:
{code}
  add_index "common_taggings", ["common_tag_id", "filterable_type", "filterable_id"], :name => "index_common_tags", :unique => true
{code}
The difference is the {{filterable_type}} column, which is used to allow {{CommonTagging#filterable}} to be polymorphic. However, in practice, {{CommonTagging#filterable}} is always a Tag, so the {{filterable_type}} column serves no practical purpose. It would be nice to get rid of the column entirely, to reflect the fact that the {{CommonTagging}} class is used to define relationships between tags.

Any PR for this issue should handle these things:
# A migration to drop the {{filterable_type}} column for {{common_taggings}}, and if necessary adjust the unique index.
# Updating the {{CommonTagging}} class so that the {{filterable}} association has {{class_name: "Tag"}} instead of {{polymorphic: true}}.
# Updating any associations that are {{through: :common_taggings}}, since switching away from polymorphic means that {{source_type: 'Tag'}} is no longer needed.
# Modifying all other classes so that there are no more references to {{common_taggings.filterable_type}}.

Summary: Allow users to search for works and bookmarks by language short name
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.

Description:

* "Work Search" in the header
* "Search within results" in the work filters
* "Any Field" on the work search page
* "Any field on work" on the bookmark search page
* "Search within results" in the bookmark filters

Summary: Tag Sets: When adding a non-canonical character/relationship and its canonical fandom to the same tag set, don't automatically associate them
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
When added to a tag set alongside their (canonical) fandom, non-canonical characters and relationships appear to be nested inside the canonical fandom, not in the "Unassociated Characters & Relationships" section.

But when the tag set is used in a challenge and the “Fandom only?” option is selected, the non-canonical characters and relationships are not actually associated with the fandom:

* The non-canonical characters and relationships do not appear in the autocomplete when the user selects their canonical fandom, which contributes to [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3511|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3511|smart-link].
* The non-canonical characters and relationships cannot be used on prompts even if they’re entered by hand (except in cases of [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5712|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5712|smart-link]). 

We want to make the display of tag sets consistent with the way that that the challenges handle these non-canonical character and relationship tags – that is, tag sets that contain both a non-canonical character/relationship and its canonical parent fandom should not automatically consider that character/relationship to be associated with the fandom.

In order to prevent older tag sets from suddenly having a lot of missing associations, we’d also like to have a rake task for recreating all of the relevant {{CommonTagging}}s as {{TagSetAssociation}}s.

h1. Testing Instructions

# Pick a non-canonical character/relationship tag that has a canonical fandom associated with this. (You might try looking at synonyms of canonical tags.)
# Pick a canonical character/relationship tag in the same fandom.
# Adding tags to a tag set, and manually associating them:
## Create a new tag set.
## Add all three tags to the tag set: the canonical fandom, the canonical character/relationship, and the non-canonical character/relationship. Save changes.
## View the tag set, and make sure that the canonical character/relationship is nested under the canonical fandom, while the non-canonical character/relationship is under the “Unassociated Characters & Relationships” section.
## Edit the tag set, and under the “Tag Associations” section, add an association between the non-canonical character/relationship and the canonical fandom.
## View the tag set, and make sure that both characters/relationships are now nested under the canonical fandom.
# Nominating tags for a tag set in the canonical fandom:
## Create a tag set, and set the nomination numbers to 1 fandoms, 2 characters/relationships.
## Nominate the canonical character/relationship and the non-canonical character/relationship under the canonical fandom.
## Go to “Review Nominations” for the tag set and approve all three nominations.
## Check that canonical character is nested under the canonical fandom, but the non-canonical character/relationship is listed under “Unassociated Characters & Relationships.”
## Go to “Review Associations” for the tag set and make sure that the association between the non-canonical character/relationship and the canonical fandom is listed there.
# Nominating tags for a tag set in a different fandom:
## Create a tag set, and set the nomination numbers to 2 fandoms, 1 character/relationship.
## Nominate the canonical character/relationship under the canonical fandom.
## Nominate the non-canonical character/relationship under a different fandom (canonical or not).
## Go to “Review Nominations” for the tag set and approve all four nominations.
## Check that the canonical character is nested under the canonical fandom, but the non-canonical character/relationship is listed under “Unassociated Characters & Relationships.”
## Go to “Review Associations” for the tag set and make sure that the association between the non-canonical character/relationship and the new fandom you picked is listed there.
# Checking the rake task: (Already tested ✅)
## Create a tag set.
## Add all three tags to the tag set: the canonical fandom, the canonical character/relationship, and the non-canonical character/relationship. Save changes.
## View the tag set, and make sure that the non-canonical character/relationship is listed in the “Unassociated Characters & Relationships” section, while the canonical character/relationship is listed under the fandom.
## Run the rake task.
## View the tag set again, and make sure that the character/relationship is no longer listed in the “Unassociated Characters & Relationships” section, but is instead listed under the canonical fandom.
## Edit the tag set and scroll down to the “Tag Associations” section to make sure that there is exactly one association there: the one connecting the non-canonical character/relationship to the fandom.

Summary: Gift Exchange: Simultaneously updating the Giver and Write-in Giver for a Potential Assignment breaks anonymity by causing the Giver's name to appear on the Write-In Giver's My Assignments page
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
*Steps to reproduce*

# Log in
# Create a collection with a gift exchange challenge
## Browse > Collections > New Collection
## Fill in required information and choose "Gift Exchange" for "Type of challenge, if any"
## Submit
## On the exchange settings form, check "Sign-up open?"
## Submit
# Sign up for the exchange as three different users (it’s easiest if one of them is the collection owner)
## Follow the "Sign-up Form" link in the collection sidebar
## Since we accepted the default settings, we don't even need to fill anything in – just press "Submit"
# If you're not already logged in as the collection owner, log back in with that account
# Run matching
## On your collection's sidebar, follow  the "Challenge Settings" link
## Uncheck "Sign-up open?"
## Press "Update"
## From the sidebar, follow the "Matching" link
## Press "Generate Potential Matches"
## You'll get a pop-up warning you matches will be random; choose "OK"
## Wait briefly for matching to finish and refresh the page to see potential matches
# Copy each name from the Giver field into the Write-In Giver field in the next column
# Use the red *×* to clear each Giver
# Replace the original Giver with the _other_ collection participant who is neither the Write-In Giver nor the Recipient
# Press “Save Assignment Changes”
# Press “Send Assignments”

*What happens*

When a participant follows the "My Assignments" link on the collection dashboard, they will find two assignments: theirs and someone else's. 

The someone else's is actually their pinch-hit, but it displays the actual assignee's name.

*What should happen*

It should display "their_name* (pinch hitter)".

*Notes*

While just fixing the name that displays is an okay fix for now, the problem is deeper.

When the challenge moderator fills in both the Giver and Write-In Giver fields as described, the ChallengeAssignment objects all end up with both an offer_signup_id and a pinch_hitter_id. 

This means that if the Write-In Giver (pinch-hitter) goes to fill the assignment, the assignment does not get marked as fulfilled on their assignments page (or, indeed, on the moderator’s view of assignments).

Usually, when a mod assigns a pinch-hitter through other means, a brand new ChallengeAssignment is created with a pinch_hitter_id (rather than adding a pinch_hitter_id to the existing ChallengeAssignment).

Ideally, we should fix this issue with the ChallengeAssignment, but in the meantime, we should at least make sure the write-in giver (pinch-hitter) doesn’t see the actual assignee’s name (and email due to AO3-5733).

Description:
This issue is limited to the latest version of Desktop Chrome (v77, as of writing), it's not a change on our part, we think it's a change to Chrome's layout rendering engine.

*Steps to replicate*

# Log in and go to your inbox
# Make sure you have some comments in your Inbox
# Click the "Reply" button to a comment
# The floating comment box appears, click into the textarea

*What happens*

* The box disappears from view, and will reappear depending on where you move your cursor, but trying to interact with any of the form fields will make it disappear again.
* You will find the comment box when you scroll all the way to the bottom of the page, that's where it will stay even if you interact with it.
* When you click "Reply" to make the box first show up, and click into the textarea, the box disappears, but you have put focus on the textarea. If you start typing, even though you don't see the box, the browser will jump to the bottom of the page to the textarea so that you can see what you're typing.
* When you click "Reply" to make the box first show up, then drag the box, that will ensure it stays put.

*What should happen*
The box should stay at the position where it was first initiated, even when focusing form elements inside of it.

*Notes*
One current theory is that this jumping happens because the box is created inside a container that is absolute positioned but doesn't have a top/right/bottom/left value applied. Once you set a top/left value by dragging the box, it will stay positioned there.

The floating box is used in two other places, the issue doesn't occur there. For the bookmarks form, because the top/left value is overwritten. For the comment box on the "Unread Messages" section on the homepage, because it gets rendered at the bottom of the container anyway (aka the place where it would jump to).

* [CVE-2020-8164|https://groups.google.com/forum/#!topic/rubyonrails-security/f6ioe4sdpbY]: Possible Strong Parameters Bypass in ActionPack

Summary: Restrict user-inserted images to the width of their container element to avoid overflow
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.

Description:

# Log in

h1. What happens
The image is too wide to fit on the screen. It scrolls sideways. Meh.

The image should have a maximum width of 100% of the container size. (Note that the container isn't the same width as the screen.

This needs an announcement first, which is in progress.

Test on images that have width and height attributes set, just width, and just height.

Summary: Update Sanitize gem to resolve issue with invalid closing tags on track and source elements
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
When using the {{<track>}} and {{<source>}} elements inside an {{<audio>}} or {{<video>}} element, closing {{</track>}} and {{</source>}} tags are automatically added. Furthermore, the closing tag {{</embed>}} for {{<embed>}} is also automatically added. Updating the Sanitize gem appears to fix this, so let's do that!

h2. What happens

Example input into the Work Text field in HTML mode:

{code:html}<video>
<source src="some url" type="video/mp4">
<track label="English" kind="subtitles" srclang="en" src="url">
</video>

<audio>
<source src="some url" type="audio/mp3">
<track label="English" kind="subtitles" srclang="en" src="url">
</audio>

<embed type="application/x-shockwave-flash" src="http://www.google.com/reader/ui/123-audio-player.swf">{code}

Example output:

{code:html}<video>
<source src="some url" type="video/mp4"></source>
<track label="English" kind="subtitles" srclang="en" src="url"></track>
</video>

<audio>
<source src="some url" type="audio/mp3"></source>
<track label="English" kind="subtitles" srclang="en" src="url"></track>
</audio>

<embed type="application/x-shockwave-flash" src="http://www.google.com/reader/ui/123-audio-player.swf"></embed>{code}

However, if you run the resultant code through the W3 Validator, it gives a "Stray end tags" error about {{</track>}}, {{</source>}} and {{</embed>}}.

h2. What should happen

So the desired output would be:

{code:html}<video>
<source src="some url" type="video/mp4">
<track label="English" kind="subtitles" srclang="en" src="url">
</video>

<audio>
<source src="some url" type="audio/mp3">
<track label="English" kind="subtitles" srclang="en" src="url">
</audio>

<embed type="application/x-shockwave-flash" src="http://www.google.com/reader/ui/123-audio-player.swf">{code}



In addition to testing the above, please also do all tests on [https://wiki.transformativeworks.org/mediawiki/HTML_Tag_Regression|https://wiki.transformativeworks.org/mediawiki/HTML_Tag_Regression]. The file attached to this issue does not have to be tested.

sarken Oct 7th at 19:58
I'm doing a smoke test of gift exchanges following the Ruby update and I wanted to double check that this is normal. I ran matching (set to random) on an exchange, and the generated assignments included two for the same giver/recipient combo.

ticking instant (AO3 Contributor) 23:26
That definitely shouldn't happen. There are a whole bunch of checks to try to make sure that no one has more than one assignment (either as a recipient or a giver). (edited) 

The ChallengeSignup fields assigned_as_request and assigned_as_offer are supposed to be set whenever an assignment is created, and there are a lot of lines of the form next if request_signup.assigned_as_request and similar.

(That said, there's a chance that it might not be caused by the Ruby update, since I think stale data could also produce behavior like that. ticking instant (AO3 Contributor) 17:13
It might be a matter of degree, if it is stale data. There were issues before where the assigned_as_request value was available when the assignment was not, because they were committed in different transactions. This issue would arise if the new value of assigned_as_request and the new assignment were unavailable. So if wsrep_local_recv_queue_avg has been trending upwards, this might be the next stage of it: accidentally double-assigning users.

(In theory, it could manifest as two different assignments for the same user, as well.)

A couple years back, I was playing around with rewriting the assignment generation code to (a) try to reduce the number of database queries, and (b) return a maximum matching instead of a maximal matching. Description:
Working with Translation to get Phrase (formerly PhraseApp) ready for them to start on translating the emails. Issue will be updated to reflect reality and what needs testing as we get farther along, but for now:

* Create a new project on Phrase, which will mean updating the .phraseapp.yml config.
* Restore all of the locale files Translation intends to use to their original, pre-messing-about-on-Phrase state by [manually replacing them with the files from rails-i18n|https://github.com/svenfuchs/rails-i18n#manual-installation].
** Remove any locale files not on Translation's list so they won't get loaded into Phrase and clutter things up. If Translation wants to add a new locale at a later date, the appropriate locale file from rails-i18n can be manually copied and added to the config/locales/defaults folder in our repo.
* [Organize the locale files into folders|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/i18n.html#organization-of-locale-files], and update config/application.rb so we can handle said structure.
* Also update {{available_locales}} in config/application.rb to match Translation’s requested locales.

*Translation’s requested locales:* af, ar, bg, bn, ca, cs, cy, da, de, el, es, fa, fi, fr, he, hi, hr, hu, id, it, ja, ka, ko, lt, lv, mk, mr-IN, ms, nb, pl, pt-BR, pt-PT, ro, ru, sk, sl, sr, sv, th, tl, tr, uk, vi, zh-CN

This will primarily affect Translation and their use of Phrase, but because we’re moving locales to nested folders, let’s do a smoke test to make sure the locale files are getting loaded.

* Make an unsuccessful attempt to log in as an admin, e.g. by entering the wrong username. You should get a blue flash error message and not, say, a 500 page or some text saying “translation missing.”

Summary: Drop approved column on Feedbacks table
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
For support tickets, we currently have an "approved" column that saves whether the ticket has been marked as ham (true) or spam (false). We don't do this for abuse reports, and there's no real reason to do it here. We can just run the report through the spam checker and send or reject it based on the results without saving said results to the database.

*How to test the Support form*: make sure you can still send a Support ticket. Also try sending one with the email field set to akismet-guaranteed-spam@example.com, and make sure that ticket still gets rejected as spam.

8. Double-check to make sure that the approved column has been dropped.

The "Series Updated" date ({{series.revised_at}}, used on series blurbs and for the "Date Updated" sort option on bookmark searches) is defined as:

* Adding a new work to a series will bump the series to the top of the list (either logged in or not).
* Adding a new restricted work to a series will make the series restricted and also bump it to the top of the list.
* Editing the title of an old series will not bump it to the top of the list (either logged in or not).
* Editing the title of an old series with all works restricted will not bump it to the top of the list.

22/Jan/20 3:55 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;The reason that {{redirect_back_or_default}} doesn’t work here is because there’s no {{skip_before_action :store_location}} in the skins controller. That means that any calls to {{redirect_back_or_default}} will redirect back to the current URL (which is the one most recently stored with {{store_location}}), instead of to the referrer.

This means that the {{#set}} and {{#unset}} actions are actually visited twice any time you use the skin chooser. The first time stores its own path in {{session[:return_to]}}, then redirects “back” to that same path and sets {{session[:return_to] = "redirected"}}. The second time sees that it was redirected from the value of {{session[:return_to]}}, so it clears {{session[:return_to]}} in {{store_location}} instead of setting it, resulting in {{redirect_back_or_default}} falling back on the default.

Summary: GDPR script get_user_data.rb doesn't include some changes from the Devise upgrade
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
When the sign-in system was moved to Devise, there were [five fields added to the users|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/7d30bf818a7ab3de6a259acfbc481c68ac3325ff/db/migrate/20181017032400_moves_users_to_devise.rb#L25-L29] table that are updated whenever the user signs in:

* {{sign_in_count}}
* {{current_sign_in_at}}
* {{last_sign_in_at}}
* {{current_sign_in_ip}}
* {{last_sign_in_ip}}

The IP addresses recorded in the audits table whenever one of those five values is updated (as well as the IPs in two of those fields) are not included in the script used to export the user's data.

There are a few more changes resulting from the Devise upgrade that aren't accounted for in the {{script/get_user_data.rb}} script:

# The field {{failed_login_count}} was renamed to {{failed_attempts}}. (But it may not be necessary to check {{failed_attempts}}, because Devise almost exclusively uses {{increment_counter}} to change {{failed_attempts}}, which doesn't call the {{before_update}} hook that the audited gem uses. Still, it might be good to double-check what gets added to the audits table when a failed login attempt occurs, when an account is locked, and when it's unlocked.)
# The field {{recently_reset}} is no longer used. Instead, Devise changes {{reset_password_token}}, {{reset_password_sent_at}}, and {{encrypted_password}} over the course of a password reset. (It may be necessary to leave in the code relating to {{recently_reset}} to account for older entries in the audits table, but I believe there needs to be new code for the new Devise fields regardless.)

The Devise upgrade also renamed various fields related to account activation (which is another activity that probably has the user's IP address associated with it).

----

After reviewing the above information, here are the changes needed:

* Add {{encrypted_password}} case to handle IPs recorded when someone changes their password.
* Add {{failed_attempts}} case to handle recorded IPs from failed login attempts, which are currently only logged in certain cases due to the way Devise updates the count of failed attempts.
* Add {{locked_at}} case to handle recorded IPs from the last failed login attempt before an account is locked due to too many login attempts.
* Clarify that the {{recently_reset}} case is from before the Devise change, and add a {{reset_password_sent_at}} case to handle IPs recorded for password reset requests now that we're using Devise.
* Add {{sign_in_count}} case to handle IPs recorded when someone successfully signs in to an account.

Ideally, to test this, someone would do each of the following with different IP addresses, and then we’d ensure each of those IP address appeared when a database admin ran the script:

* log in and change their account password
* log out and request a password reset
* attempt to log in to their account so many times they get locked out (50 tries, quickly)
* wait five minutes after being locked out and then log in successfully

Failing that, we should make sure the script works.

So wrong, apparently, that [The Old Reader|https://theoldreader.com/home] doesn’t even try to make the entry’s author names into hyperlinks, so YMMV when it comes to the bug’s exact behavior. {code:ruby} @works.each do |work| unless work.unrevealed? feed.entry work do |entry| entry.title work.title entry.summary feed_summary(work), :type => 'html' entry.author do |author| author.name text_byline(work, :visibility => 'public') end end end end{code} That is our current code, which is stuffing HTML for all of the authors into a single {{author}} element’s {{name}} element, like so: {code:xml} testy, testy2 {code} (Why is {{text_byline}} giving us HTML? When it’s fixed, this bug will change slightly: rather than a broken relative link for the author, there will be no link at all. However, the links in the summary portion should continue to work. Summary: Remove %{type} from the co-creator emails and standardize OD/Support link placeholders in invitation to claim emails (OD)
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Natalia Gruber
Description:
h3. Issue 1

*What happens:*
On the co-creator notification emails ({color:#ff0000}user_mailer.creatorship_invitation{color} and {color:#ff0000}user_mailer.creatorship_notification_archivist{color}), there's a {color:#ff0000}%\{type}{color} variable. This variable can be replaced by different things (work, series, chapter) which have different grammatical genders for several languages, making it impossible to translate this string accurately.

*What should happen:*
Instead of a variable, there should be different versions of the affected paragraphs for each type of creation, making translation easier.

h3. Issue 2

*What happens:*

There’s some inconsistency in the strings used to refer to Open Doors and Support in the user_mailer.invitation_to_claim email:

* “by %\{open_doors_link}” (= “Open Doors”)
* “imported by Open Doors (%\{open_doors_link})” (= actual URL)
* “please %\{support_link}.” (= “contact Support”)
* “please contact Support at %\{support_link}.” (= actual URL)

This can be confusing for translators working on this email.

*What should happen:*

It would be easier if these links were named more consistently.

Summary: Change kudo uniqueness validation to use users instead of pseuds
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: redsummernight
Description:
Update the Rails uniqueness validator on kudos to use user_id instead of pseud_id.

We won't clean up the duplicates in the database just yet, and as before people will still be able to get past this check on a dodgy connection, but it will be harder to leave duplicates from the same user (even when changing default pseuds).

When we do add the uniqueness constraint at the database level, we'll have the error handling ready at the application level (people will see "left kudos here :)" as usual).

For the rare cases where users can get past the Rails validation and run into the (future) database constraint, we should catch {{ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique}} exceptions, similar to what we do on user creations: https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/57e7cab589abc7cc666ddf4d3abe768d801b3493/app/controllers/users_controller.rb#L9-L24.

*How to test*:
- Check that leaving logged in kudos still works.
- Check that leaving logged in kudos a second time on the same work will get you the "left kudos here :)" message.
- Check that you can no longer leave logged in kudos after changing default pseuds.

Summary: Add migration to update the primary key and unique constraints on the kudos table
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: redsummernight
Description:
This is the one prophesied to take down the site. Migration:

- Change the primary key type from INT to BIGINT.
- Add unique index for commentable_id + commentable_type + user_id. This will remove duplicate kudos for the same work from the same user.
- Add unique index for commentable_id + commentable_type + ip_address. This will remove duplicate kudos for the same work from the same guest IP.

The migration will be different depending on the environment:

- Add a usual Rails migration, to be used in dev and CI environments.
- Add a comment with the pt-online-schema-change command to be run on staging and beta (similar to AO3-5844).

*How to test*:
- (/) (Anyone) Test AO3-5868 first.
- (/) (Server admin) Test the migration:
-# Run the migration.
-# Copy the commands that it prints to a file.
-# Run the pt-online-schema-change command, but not any of the SQL commands that follow it.
-# Create a brand new kudos, and note the ID in the database.
-# Create another kudos on the same work, from the same user (by using the Rails console and skipping validation, {{.save(validate: false)}}). This is a duplicate of the kudos from the previous step.
-# Run the SQL commands. (RENAME TABLE, DROP TRIGGER, and DROP TABLE)
-# Check whether the kudos that you created is still there. Check that it has no duplicates (the duplicates should have been eaten by the pt-online-schema-change migration).
-# From the Rails console: try to insert a duplicate kudos, bypassing validations, and make sure that it generates an error.
- (/) (Server admin) Test that the migration can run up and down and up again.
- (/) (Anyone) Finally, in the post-migration world:
-- Check that leaving logged in kudos still works.
-- Check that leaving logged in kudos a second time on the same work will get you the "left kudos here :)" message.
-- Check that you can no longer leave logged in kudos after changing default pseuds.

4. Leave a new logged in kudos. This kudos should have the user_id of your current user, but the pseud_id should be nil because we removed that code.
5. Run the SQL commands. (RENAME TABLE, DROP TRIGGER, and DROP TABLE)
6. Check whether the kudos that you created is still there. It should have no pseud_id at this point.

After the migration, sanity check that you leave logged in and guest kudos as usual.

Summary: Allow linking to each sign-up and each request on the Requests Summary page
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: redsummernight
Description:
Background:

- The Requests Summary page of a gift exchange is visible to all users, logged in or not, provided the option "Requests visible?" in the challenge settings is checked. Example: https://archiveofourown.org/collections/smut4smut2020/requests.
- The Prompts page of a prompt meme is visible to all users, logged in or not. Example: https://archiveofourown.org/collections/GenAndAroPrompts/requests.
- Note that when the Requests Summary/Prompts pages are visible, they don't show up on the challenge sidebar for logged out users ([gift exchange sidebar|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/6f987a7665d309c6f4e749a34787bcab632d864b/app/views/challenge/gift_exchange/_challenge_sidebar.html.erb#L1], [prompt meme sidebar|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/6f987a7665d309c6f4e749a34787bcab632d864b/app/views/challenge/prompt_meme/_challenge_sidebar.html.erb#L11]).

If the /requests page is visible as described above:

- The sign-up pages should be similarly visible, e.g. https://archiveofourown.org/collections/smut4smut2020/signups/220408. The sign-up page currently denies permission unless you own the sign-up or are a challenge mod.
-- A sign-up page should only show requests/prompts, _not offers_, unless you own the sign-up or are a challenge mod.
-- A sign-up page should not include anonymous requests/prompts.
-- A sign-up page should not be visible if there are no non-anonymous requests/prompts.
- The individual request/prompt pages within sign-ups should be similarly visible, e.g. https://archiveofourown.org/collections/smut4smut2020/prompts/1538164. In prompt meme's case, this issue overlaps AO3-3828.
- On the /requests page:
-- Each request/prompt should have a "All Requests in Sign-up" button at the bottom (next to the "Edit" button, if you own the request/prompt), allowing you to see other requests by that user and/or easily get the link to your own sign-up.
--- Exception: if the prompt is anonymous.
-- Each request/prompt's title (usually just "Request," unless the mod has enabled the "Title" field for sign-ups) should link to that request/prompt's page (e.g. https://archiveofourown.org/collections/smut4smut2020/prompts/1538164). Related: AO3-3828.
-- Each request/prompt's [byline|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/6f987a7665d309c6f4e749a34787bcab632d864b/app/views/prompts/_prompt_blurb.html.erb#L10-L14] should link to the prompter's dashboard, just like on work blurbs, but only if the prompter isn't anonymous.

* The page showing all of the user’s requests in a gift exchange cannot show their offers to other people.
* If a prompt is anonymous, it definitely shouldn’t link to the sign-up.
* If a user has a mix of of anonymous and non-anonymous prompts, the non-anonymous prompts can (and probably should) link to the sign-up, but the sign-up view cannot include any of the user’s anonymous prompts.
* If a user has all anonymous prompts, the sign-up probably shouldn’t be visible. (They should probably also be excluded from the list of people who are signed up, but that’s a different issue.)

Summary: Challenges: Possible to sign up for the same challenge more than once using multiple pseuds
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
When creating a new {{ChallengeSignup}}, the validations [check whether the same pseud has already created a sign-up for the same collection|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/6f987a7665d309c6f4e749a34787bcab632d864b/app/models/challenge_signup.rb#L72], but not whether a different pseud owned by the same user has already created a sign-up for the same collection. The only thing preventing a user with multiple pseuds from signing up with multiple pseuds is the code in {{ChallengeSignupsController#new}} that [redirects the user to the edit action if they already have a sign-up in the collection|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/6f987a7665d309c6f4e749a34787bcab632d864b/app/controllers/challenge_signups_controller.rb#L200-L202]. However, this check only prevents displaying the form -- if you load multiple copies of the form before the first sign-up is created, you can submit as many sign-ups as you have pseuds.

*Steps to Reproduce:*
# Create a new challenge (either a gift exchange or a prompt meme) with open sign-ups.
# Log in as a user with multiple pseuds, or create several pseuds for this purpose.
# Visit the challenge profile.
# Open multiple copies of the challenge sign-up form in different tabs, one for each pseud.
# In the first tab, select your first pseud from the dropdown, fill out the rest of the form, and submit it.

Summary: Rewrite hit counting to work with nginx caching
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h2. Background

We're going to start caching works for logged out users, which means whenever we serve up a cached work, we'll be skipping the code that triggers an increase in the work's hit count. That's not good!

To get around this, we will use JS to count hits, whether or not the page is cached, and whether or not the user is logged in. And since we are already here, we might as well rewrite how we count hits, to address AO3-4751.

How hits should work:
{quote}
You go to any chapter of a work. One hit is added. From there, you navigate to a different chapter of the work. No hits are added. You close the browser. Later or tomorrow, you come back to the work. One hit is added. You move through the work and again no hits are added.
{quote}

h2. Implementation

- Add JS on individual work/chapter pages to make an AJAX request to a new endpoint for logging hits. This JS code will be the same for logged out and logged in users. Hit counts will no longer be incremented as part of the work/chapter rendering.

- Log hits into Redis, then have background tasks periodically move new hit data into the database (the stat_counters table). This approach for database updates hasn't changed.

- De-duplicate hits on the same work (regardless of chapters), from the same visitor, within the same period of time (e.g. 24h). When logging a hit, save to Redis: the work ID, the visitor IP, and the time.

- Use Redis sets (tentative plan, see also the [actual implementation|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/3796] which combines some of these sets).
-- Sets (A) with (work ID + timestamp) key, containing IPs of all visitors on that work within the time period identified by the timestamp. 
-- Sets (B) with (work ID) key, containing the names of all the existing (A) sets. We use them to clean up outdated (A) sets.
-- Sets (C) with (work ID) key, containing the count of IPs added since the last time we move hits to the database. When moving hits to the database, take only the unique count of IPs. The actual IPs remain ephemeral in Redis.
-- A single set (D) of all work IDs with changed hits.

- For the timestamp in the key of (A), use a configurable value that stays the same for 24h. For example, if we use "the most recent 3am", 3am is the fixed rollover time. After 3am, the same visitor on the same work can generate a new hit.

- Move hit counts to the database more frequently than the de-duplicating time period (24h). Whenever a new, unseen IP is added to (A) by SADD, we increment the counter in (C) by SADD's return value. This way users don't have to wait 24h before seeing hits change.
-- If (A) is a new set, we need to add it to (B). The work ID should also be added to (D). We should use Redis transactions to make sure all writes succeed.

- Have the background task (run more frequently than 24h) do 2 things:
-- Get works with changed hits from (D), add their counts from (C) to the database. Updating StatCounter models will automatically trigger reindexing on works. Empty (D) and reset (C) to 0.
-- Iterate through (B) and delete outdated (A) sets (e.g. more than 24h old).

h2. Notes

h3. Things we can remove

- The unused LogfileReader module for parsing nginx logs, and the module's tests.
- The last_visitor column on the stat_counters table.
- The last_visitor_old and hit_count_old columns on the works table.

h3. Cons of JS-based hit counters

- We will not count hits from users who disable JS.
- We will not count hits from users who have privacy blockers. For example, FanFiction.Net has [its hit counter URL blocked by EasyPrivacy|https://github.com/easylist/easylist/blob/9101fc9c8b3ba2f156d4a15b012619da6a11312a/easyprivacy/easyprivacy_specific.txt#L686].

h3. Counting hits from nginx (alternative)

We considered looking at the nginx logs to determine how many hits to add to the work. We would increase the hit count by one every time we serve the actual work (not the adult content warning) to a particular remote address, provided the previous hit was not also from that address.

Reference: [Keeping Hitcounts accurate when using an NGinx Caching Proxy|https://www.bentasker.co.uk/documentation/linux/253-keeping-hitcounts-accurate-when-using-an-nginx-caching-proxy].

We decided against this because making our application code and our nginx setup highly dependent on each other will be difficult to maintain in the long term, especially as the nginx configuration is not currently tracked in the public repository.

h2. Testing

1. Make sure that the owner's hits don't count:
- Find a work that you created, but haven't visited recently.
- View it multiple times logged-in as the creator. Note the hit count in the header.

Summary: Adult content warning always appears when guests access adult works
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
We currently use the session cookie to determine if we should show guests the adult content warning.

Unfortunately, now that we’ve implemented caching, this approach no longer works: even if you view an adult (Mature, Explicit, or Not Rated) work and press “Proceed” on the content warning, the next adult work you access will show you the warning as well.

We need to more this information out of the session cookie and into a separate one so we can use it with [cookie-aware nginx caching|https://dev.to/ale_ukr/how-to-make-nginx-cache-cookie-aware-2ffl]:

Summary: Simplify Elasticsearch query to sort bookmarkables by "Date Bookmarked"
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: redsummernight
Description:
Initial write-up: [Bookmark sorting in Elasticsearch|https://docs.google.com/document/d/1i8ModbjUFKum2i4KOix3WwTs_BTgfOcQUiY4lQHblqU/preview].

When sorting bookmarkables (instead of bookmarks, e.g. on a page like {{tags/X/bookmarks}} instead of {{users/X/bookmarks}}) by "Date Bookmarked", we have to calculate on the fly the value for sorting, which is the maximum {{created_at}} time of all "child" bookmarks for each "parent" bookmarkable. This value is [stored in the result score|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/4579eacc4145a325cf89cf28a01037430e3b3e1e/app/models/search/bookmarkable_query.rb#L96-L106]. Queries like this are complicated and show up in the [slow query log|https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/6.8/index-modules-slowlog.html].

We should keep the query simple, by sorting on a new field last_bookmarked_at of the indexed parent bookmarkable. Every time a new bookmark is made, reindex its bookmarkable. To avoid reindexing the bookmarkable too much (e.g. on popular works), we can batch updates, similar to the StatCounterIndexer.

We basically move the calculation from query time (happens for every search) to index time (happens only when new bookmarks are created).

*How to test*:
For tag listings:
# On a {{tags/X/bookmarks}} page, sort by "Date Bookmarked". Find an older bookmarked work in the listing, note its position, then bookmark it. After reindexing, the work should show up at the top of the listing.
# Delete the bookmark you just made. Wait for reindexing. Then on the same page, sorted by "Date Bookmarked", the work should return to its former place in the listing.

For bookmark searches:
# On https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search, select Sort by option "Date Bookmarked", and search for whatever you want. Find an older bookmarked work in the search results, note its position, then bookmark it. After reindexing, the work should show up at the top of the search results.
# Delete the bookmark you just made. Wait for reindexing, then rerun the search. The work should return to its former place in the search results.

*Note*: We will need to reindex all bookmarkables (not bookmarks though).

Summary: Parent skin names are case insensitive, potentially leading to users having access to others' skins
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: GoldenFalls
Description:
What should happen:
When a user saves a skin after having added a parent skin, the skin assigned as the parent skin should belong to the user (or be public) and should match the case of what the user entered.

What happens instead:
When a user enters the name of a skin to be used as a parent skin, regardless of what capitalization they use, when the save the child skin the parent skin actually assigned will be whatever skin was first created with that name disregarding capitalization/cases. This will happen even if that skin does not belong to the user who is trying to add a parent skin.


To replicate:

1) make a site skin with a unique name using one account
2) switch to a different account
3) make another site skin with the same name, but different cases/capitalization
3) make a third skin and try to add the second skin as its parent

The child skin will have the first skin listed as a parent skin instead of the second skin, and if you use that child skin and inspect what css is being applied, you will see the css from the first skin being applied but not any from the second skin.

Summary: Modify batch kudos notification code to avoid the Redis KEYS command
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
Currently, the batch kudos notification code calls the Redis {{KEYS}} command once for each author who received kudos in the past day:
{code}
      keys = REDIS_KUDOS.keys("kudos_#{author_id}_*")
{code}
[(source)|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/030fa4607d3c59fba2cacbe4e9c99b3c49fbc1cb/app/models/redis_mail_queue.rb#L19]

However, the Redis docs discourage the use of {{KEYS}} in production code:
{quote}
Warning: consider KEYS as a command that should only be used in production environments with extreme care. It may ruin performance when it is executed against large databases. This command is intended for debugging and special operations, such as changing your keyspace layout. Don't use KEYS in your regular application code.
{quote}
[(source)|https://redis.io/commands/keys]

The batch kudos notification code should be rewritten to avoid the use of {{KEYS}}.

h3. Notes

The deploy for this may be a bit tricky. Ideally, all users should be notified about all kudos they receive, even those that were recorded by the old kudos notification code right before the new kudos notification code goes live. There are several different possible approaches to take, including the following:

# Deploy the new code, then run {{rake notifications:deliver_kudos}} one last time on an old copy of the code (like AO3-5905). This would result in an extra kudos email.
# Split this issue over two deploys: one to add extra sets for bookkeeping purposes (that aren't immediately used, because the data added just before the deploy wouldn't be tracked properly), and one to get rid of the call to {{KEYS}} (deployed at least a day later).
# Write an After task, to be run immediately after deploy, to make sure that all of the information added prior to the deploy is updated to match the new code.

h3. Testing Instructions

The instructions for how to test the change from the old kudos notification code to the new kudos notification code will depend on the approach taken. However, the instructions for testing the new code should be the same in all cases:
# Find (or create) a work by an account whose email you have access to.
# Leave a logged-in kudos on the work.
# Leave a logged-out kudos on the work.
# Wait until the kudos notification emails are sent.
# Make sure that the email includes both of the kudos that you left.

Summary: Fix some flaky tests related to login with JS and tag wrangling with Elasticsearch
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
There are a number of automated tests that fail intermittently. The goal of this issue is to make some of those tests pass more consistently. (Hopefully.)

h3. features/works/work_create.feature:52

For this test, the HTML snapshot from cucumber seems to indicate that the user isn't logged-in, even though there's a step immediately beforehand which is supposed to make the user log in:

{code:ruby}
Given /^(?:I have )?(?:a|an|the) (hidden)?(?: )?(anonymous)?(?: )?(moderated)?(?: )?(closed)?(?: )?collection "([^\"]*)"(?: with name "([^\"]*)")?$/ do |hidden, anon, moderated, closed, title, name|
  step %{I am logged in as "moderator"}
  step %{I set up the collection "#{title}" with name "#{name}"}
{code}

It seems like something about the log-in step may be causing it to fail:

{code:ruby}
Given /^I am logged in as "([^"]*)" with password "([^"]*)"$/ do |login, password|
  user = find_or_create_new_user(login, password)
  step("I am logged out")
  step %{I am on the homepage}
  find_link('login-dropdown').click

  fill_in "User name or email:", with: login
  fill_in "Password:", with: password
  check "Remember Me"
  click_button "Log In"
  step %{confirmation emails have been delivered}
end
{code}
It may be that after the "Log In" button is clicked, cucumber moves onto the next step and loads the next page before the request to log in has finished processing. If that's the case, it would result in the user sometimes failing to be treated as logged-in. It would be possible to fix this just by adding an extra step to the log-in step that checks whether the user sees the appropriate page after login (because this only occurs in tests tagged with {{@javascript}}, which means that if the browser doesn't immediately see the appropriate page, it will wait for the page to finish loading before declaring defeat).

This is a common issue that may also contribute to these intermittent failures:
{code}
features/tag_sets/tag_set.feature:141
features/tags_and_wrangling/tag_wrangling_freeforms.feature:6
features/tags_and_wrangling/tag_wrangling_characters.feature:6
features/tags_and_wrangling/tag_wrangling_relationships.feature:6
{code}

h3. features/tags_and_wrangling/tag_wrangling.feature:25

The line the failure typically occurs on is 235, the last line in this block of code:
{code}
    When I follow "Unwrangled"
    Then I should see "Showing Unwrangled Character Tags"
      And I should see "Samantha Carter"
      And I should not see "Jack O'Neill"
      And I should not see "Daniel Jackson"
      And I should not see "Anubis Arc"
{code}
If you look at the snapshot of HTML that cucumber prints out when this failure occurs, you can see that "Anubis Arc" is correctly listed as "Unwrangleable," which ought to mean that it doesn't show up on the "Unwrangled" page. But the "Unwrangleable" mark is determined from the SQL database; the choice of which tags to include is an Elasticsearch query. So it must be that Elasticsearch isn't up to date.

Tags automatically reindex themselves when the value of {{unwrangleable}} changes:
{code}
    if tag.saved_change_to_unwrangleable?
      tag.reindex_document
    end
{code}
However, tags can't refresh Elasticsearch automatically. And because the tag automatically reindexes itself, the test doesn't currently include the joint reindex/refresh test step. So Elasticsearch isn't guaranteed to perform a refresh in between the change to unwrangleable and the page that performs the query. It may be that refreshing is all that's needed to fix this test.

h3. Testing Instructions

This should be tested during the review phase by running the Travis builds enough times to see if the tests are less flaky than they used to be. Doesn't require any QA once it's deployed to staging.

Summary: Add a unique constraint for name and user ID on the pseuds table
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: redsummernight
Description:
We are enforcing uniqueness on pseud names per user in Rails but not at the database level. Users who somehow end up with duplicate pseuds will be unable to change their passwords, because their duplicate pseuds are not valid (this symptom is similar to [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3589#icft=AO3-3589|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3589#icft=AO3-3589|smart-link]).

We need:

* A rake task to rename existing duplicates (e.g. "pseud" to "pseud_2") so they don't prevent the creation of a unique index.
* A migration to add said unique index. The table has more than 500k rows, so we probably want to use pt-online-schema-change here. [There’s an example of how to write such a migration here.|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/3805/files]

*How to test*:

* You need to have duplicate pseuds on staging. Database admins can force them into existence if necessary. Check that you cannot change your password ("Invalid pseud error").
* (Server admin) Run the rake task and make sure the duplicate pseuds get renamed.
* (Server admin) Run the migration.
* Check that you can change your password.

Summary: Use Codecov Bash uploader for coverage
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: redsummernight
Description:
Our code coverage tend to fluctuate (when it should be sitting pretty at 89% in April 2020). That's partly because our tests themselves are flaky (but we're not talking about that here), and partly, possibly because the gem codecov-ruby attempts to upload coverage data just once and [does not retry|https://github.com/codecov/codecov-ruby/issues/50].

The gem is updated infrequently. We can switch to the [Codecov Bash uploader|https://docs.codecov.io/docs/about-the-codecov-bash-uploader], which is more actively maintained and does have retrying behavior. Summary: Concurrency issue with comment threading
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
When creating a new comment, {{threaded_left}} and {{threaded_right}} are supposed to be adjusted to accommodate the new comments. However, if two replies are being added to the same comment at exactly the same time, both new comments will end up with the same {{threaded_left}} and {{threaded_right}} values. This is because {{CommentsController#create}} loads the commentable (i.e. the parent comment) outside of the transaction, and it's not reloaded inside the transaction, so its {{threaded_left}} and {{threaded_right}} values (which are used to compute the new comments' {{threaded_left}} and {{threaded_right}} values) are out-of-date when the second comment is saved.

Currently, {{threaded_left}} and {{threaded_right}} are only used to compute the number of descendants that a given comment had ({{children_count}}), which is only displayed when the max depth has been reached and the comments are hidden. So on top of being tricky to replicate thanks to concurrency, it's almost impossible to notice.

*Testing Instructions:* This is basically impossible to replicate, so I'm not sure it can be tested manually. But it would be good to try replying to some comments and make sure that it still works as expected.

Summary: Enqueue for reindexing after commit
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: redsummernight
Description:
Now that the PR for AO3-5667 has added the gem {{after_commit_everywhere}}, we can reduce the number of stale data issues in Resque by having IndexQueue always queue items for reindexing after commit, to ensure that Resque won't be trying to look up information from the database before it's been committed.

In cases where the existing reindex callbacks don't need to check what changes were made to a record (e.g. via {{saved_change_to_x?}} and {{previous_changes}}, etc.) we can also change the callbacks from {{after_update}} to {{after_commit}}.

Similar to AO3-5940, which addresses the same issue for mailers.

*How to test*: TBD.

Summary: Remove cookie-based redirection to the last visited page
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: redsummernight
Description:
On most page loads, we save the current path in the session cookie (as {{session[:return_to]}}) so in the future, we can redirect the user back to this page if necessary. This feature behaves unpredictably at best, and any brokenness is exacerbated for guest users by [nginx-level full page caching|https://archiveofourown.org/admin_posts/15379], which ignores cookies.

We are removing this feature entirely. A non-exhaustive list of things to remove:

* Any references to {{session[:return_to]}}.
* The {{store_location}} callback.
* The unused method {{set_flash_cookie}}.
* The method {{redirect_back_or_default}}. Most of the time, this method can be replaced with a simple {{redirect_to}} targeting whatever we used to have as the {{default}} argument. In some cases, however, we do want to preserve the user's last visited location (e.g. when logging in, when logging in after viewing a restricted work as a guest). If we need to remember the last visited location, we should add the URL to redirect back to into the login form.

Summary: Allow guest users to choose site skin
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: redsummernight
Description:
*How to test*:

For guests:

* A guest user should see the "Choose Skin" section in the footer.
* A guest user should be able to pick one of the 4 options in the chooser (Default, Low Vision Default, Reversi, and Snow Blue). The chosen site skin should stick around while the guest user browses different pages, and after the guest closes and opens a new browser session (unless the old session was private/incognito).
* Multiple guest users can browse the site at the same time with different site skins (a guest should not see another guest's cached version of a page).

Site skin set by "Choose Skin" should still take precedence over site skin set in a user's preference:

* If a guest chooses site skin A from the footer, then logs in as a user with no default site skin set in their preferences, they should keep using A.
* If a guest chooses site skin A from the footer, then logs in as a user with a default site skin B set in their preferences, they should keep using A. If they then pick Default from "Choose Skin", they should start using B (not necessarily the Archive's default).

*Notes*: for guest site skins to work with full page caching by nginx, we need to:

* Change skin actions (set/unset) to not use GET requests ([https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5953#icft=AO3-5953|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5953#icft=AO3-5953|smart-link]).
* Fix redirection after the set/unset skin actions ([https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5949#icft=AO3-5949|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5949#icft=AO3-5949|smart-link]), to reduce confusion.
* Move the session skin for guests and users into a separate cookie instead of keeping it in the session cookie, for nginx's cookie-aware caching (similar to what we did with the adult warning preference in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5906#icft=AO3-5906|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5906#icft=AO3-5906|smart-link]).

Our code for sending invitations appears to be struggling at least some of the time, so ideally we can determine why and optimize the process.

h1. "Send invite codes to people in our invitations queue" option

Full details, although I am certain not all are relevant:

* We started with these settings: Account creation enabled, Account creation requires invitation, and Invite from queue enabled. The "Number of people to invite from the queue at once" was set to 15,000, "How often (in days) should we invite people from the queue" was set to 1, and "How many weeks you have to activate your account before we purge it" was set to 2.
* The [Manage Queue page|https://archiveofourown.org/invite_requests/manage] showed 4,053 as the position of the last user in the queue.
* On the [admin invitations/Invite New Users page|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/invitations], the text in the "Send invite codes to people in our invitations queue" section said, "There are 4037 requests in the queue."
* Eight more people joined the queue.
* At about 06:00 UTC, an admin entered 4061 (4053 + 8) in the "Number of people to invite" field.
* The admin then went to the settings page and unchecked "Invite from queue enabled" and set "Number of people to invite from the queue at once" to 1.

The invitations began to slowly go out. No, I mean _slowly_: about one invitation was sent every half hour. As of 23:10 UTC later that day, "Send invite codes to people in our invitations queue" said, "There are 3933 requests in the queue" and the Manage Queue page showed the last user with a position of 3947.

That's 114 invitations sent in 17 hours, or an average of about 7 an hour.

This option only sees occasional use, so we're not sure if this is always a problem.

h1. The automated queue

This is with the same invitation-related admin settings.

PAC chair Matty reports that the invitations can be slow to send with this option as well and notes, "there have been a few days when they didn't go out at all, but those have been very sporadic. and some days when only some of them went out, but again, that's very sporadic. Has a migration to drop a column: {{bundle exec rake db:migrate:up VERSION=20220622075958}}. This should be run after the code has been deployed.

In addition, this replaces the {{rake invitations:check_queue}} task with a job in the Resque scheduler, so that task should be removed from the crontab.

Summary: Updating a user's email address does not delete any invitation requests that exist for that address, leaving the request lingering in the queue
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce:

# Follow the "Get Invited!" link on the homepage
# Submit an email address
# Log in to an account
# Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Profile > Edit My Profile > Change Email
# Change the email to the one you put in the queue
# Have a database admin run the task for sending invitations
# Log in as an admin
# Invitations > Manage Queue

h1. What happens:

The address is still there, at the top of the queue, and an admin has to delete it.

h1. What should happen:

The address should not be lingering in the queue, requiring manual cleanup.

h1. Notes:

When the task to send out invitations runs, [invitations are not created for/sent to any addresses that match existing accounts|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/df7cac7f4103b8fa1a42cfe509097ad4cb71e9e2/app/models/invitation.rb#L10]. However, presumably because [the same method that creates the invitation also deletes the invitation request|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/df7cac7f4103b8fa1a42cfe509097ad4cb71e9e2/app/models/invite_request.rb#L57-L65], when we can't make the invitation, we also fail to delete the request.

You [cannot join the queue with an email address that is already used on an account|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/df7cac7f4103b8fa1a42cfe509097ad4cb71e9e2/app/models/invite_request.rb#L6].

If you create an account that uses an address that currently has a request in the queue, [the request is deleted|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/df7cac7f4103b8fa1a42cfe509097ad4cb71e9e2/app/models/user.rb#L35].

Summary: Add task to fix tags with leading or trailing spaces
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: redsummernight
Description:
If a tag has surrounding spaces (e.g. "   Shinji   ") and there exists a version of that tag with no spaces (e.g. "Shinji"), then you can (not) edit the first tag, because of a Rails validation that squishes the tag, removing the spaces, resulting in an unsaveable duplicate tag (e.g. [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2349#icft=AO3-2349|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2349#icft=AO3-2349|smart-link]).

Rails 4 might have exacerbated the problem. From [~accountid:557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6]:

{quote}[https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/b5245da94a7c7667b57bb2184fa9aa7beb998da6|https://github.com/rails/rails/commit/b5245da94a7c7667b57bb2184fa9aa7beb998da6]

So any tags created before that update with non-breaking spaces can't be saved/updated except by admins because the name automatically gets squished (and the nbsp removed), which means that name doesn't match the previous name.{quote}

We should have a one-time After task to:

* Loop through all existing tags (in batches and sensibly printing its progress, of course).
* If running {{squish}} on a tag's name returns a different name, then save the tag with its spaces replaced with underscores. See Rails' implementation of {{squish}} for how to detect spaces.
* At the end of the task, print to stdout in CSV format for each updated tag: its ID, its old name, its updated name. Tag wranglers can use this list to check and further edit the tags if necessary.

*How to test*:
Run the task on staging. If the task updates no tags, then get database admins to manually screw up some tags.

Check that you (as a wrangler) can edit the changed tags on the site.
