Summary: Limit the number of tags that can be used on works
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
It should not be possible to use more than 75 total [user-defined tags|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/f6e1b98aa472c0777cf2140064218c1d5a8c87c5/app/models/tag.rb#L23] (fandom, character, relationship, or additional tags) on a work. Category, rating, and warning tags should not count toward this total.

The limit should be configurable.

*Work form changes*

The limit should be explained on the top of the tag section, which currently says, "Tags are comma separated, 100 characters per tag." 

The new text should be: "Tags are comma separated, 100 characters per tag. Fandom, relationship, character, and additional tags must not add up to more than 75. Archive warning, category, and rating tags do not count toward this limit."

*Error message*

If your work has more than the total number of tags permitted, previewing, saving, or posting should fail until the excess tags are removed. 

This should be done with backend validation, and the error message should say, "Fandom, relationship, character, and additional tags must not add up to more than 75. Your work has \[x] of these tags, so you must remove \[y] of them."

*Existing works*

Existing works with over 75 tags will continue to exist, but the creator must remove tags if they wish to edit the work or add chapters to it. 

It should be possible to delete works that have over 75 tags without needing to remove any tags. 

It should be possible to bookmark works that have over 75 tags. (We currently use [@bookmarkable.save when creating a bookmark|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/b63fce67a3975ec0614bb535c75d76c8dafbda71/app/controllers/bookmarks_controller.rb#L196], which prevents creating bookmarks of invalid works.)

If a work with over 75 tags is in an unrevealed or anonymous collection, it should be possible to reveal or deanonymize the work.

If someone have gifted you a work with over 75 tags, it should possible to accept or reject that gift.

If a series contains a work with over 75 tags, it should be possible to add other works to the series or edit the series.

*Admin*

When you are logged in as an admin, the [work meta|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/views/works/_meta.html.erb] should indicate "Over Tag Limit: Yes" or "Over Tag Limit: No". This should be in the {{<dl>}}, beneath "Akismet Reported As Spam:"

*External works*

On the Bookmark External Work page ({{https://test.archiveofourown.org/external_works/new}}), the limit should be explained on the top of the tag section, which currently says, "Creator's Tags (comma separated, 100 characters per tag). Only a fandom is required." 

The new text should be: "Creator's Tags (comma separated, 100 characters per tag). Only a fandom is required. Fandom, relationship, and character tags must not add up to more than 75. Category and rating tags do not count toward this limit."

Attempting to save a bookmark of an external work with over 75 tags should fail. This should be done with backend validation, and the error message should say, "Fandom, relationship, and character tags must not add up to more than 75. You have entered \[x] of these tags, so you must remove \[y] of them."

When posting a work, it should still be possible to cite a work not on the Archive using the “This work is a remix, a translation, a podfic, or was inspired by another work.” (Citing a work creates an external work, hence including this in this section.) 

*Stats*

To get data on the frequency of tag counts on works:

{{results = ActiveRecord::Base.connection.exec_query "SELECT tag_count, COUNT(*) AS frequency FROM (SELECT taggable_id, COUNT(*) AS tag_count FROM taggings WHERE taggable_type = 'Work' GROUP BY taggable_id) tc GROUP BY tag_count"}}

{{puts "Tag count,\tfrequency"; results.rows.each { |r| puts "#{r[0]},\t#{r[1]}" }; nil}}

Note: This needs to be updated to only look at user defined tags.

*Blocking*

This needs an announcement first.

We also have a number of linked issues whose fixes will require us to update tags on works. These should be resolved first, since this change will make it more difficult to update a work’s tags.

Summary: Series blurbs display wrong rating icon when a work in the series is not rated, and a bookmarked series appears in search results and filters for all ratings used on its works
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
*Steps to reproduce wrong rating icon*

# Log in 
# Post > New Work
# For "Rating," select "Not Rated"
# Fill in other required fields
# Check "This work is part of a series"
# In the "Or create an use a new one" field, fill in a title for your series
# Press "Post"
# Post > New Work
# For "Rating," select "General Audiences"
# Fill in other required fields
# Check "This work is part of a series"
# Use the "Select one of your existing series" option to select the series you created when posting the previous work
# Press "Post"
# Hi, username! > My Dashboard

*What happens* 
The rating icon displayed on the series blurb is for the General Audiences rating, but it should be the icon for the Not Rated rating. 

*What should happen*
The rating icon that displays on the blurb is meant to be that of the series' highest-rated work. After consulting with Content Policy, we have determined the ratings are, from lowest to highest:

General Audiences
Teen And Up Audiences
Mature
Explicit 
Not Rated

The rating icon should not change based on whether or not the highest-rated work is restricted, hidden, or unrevealed. That is, if a series has 3 public General Audiences works and 1 restricted, hidden, or unrevealed work that is rated Explicit, the series icon should still be Explicit for everyone.

*Steps to reproduce bookmarked series appearing in search results and filters for all ratings used on its works*

# Complete all the steps for reproducing the wrong rating icon
# Follow the link in the blurb to access the series
# Press "Bookmark Series"
# Press "Create"
# Wait a moment or two
# Hi, username! > My Bookmarks
# In the "Include" section of the filters, expand the "Ratings" section
# Choose "General Audiences"

*What happens*
The series you just bookmarked appears. The "Ratings" section of the filter also contains "Not Rated"

*What should happen*
The series should only appear in the results for the highest rating (the one that is used for the icon). In the case of our example case, this is "Not Rated."

Again, the rating should not change based on whether or not the highest-rated work is restricted, hidden, or unrevealed. That is, if a series has 3 public General Audiences works and 1 restricted, hidden, or unrevealed work that is rated Explicit, the series should still filter as Explicit for everyone.

Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
{code:ruby}> Chapter.where(work_id: nil).size
=> 42066 
> chapter_ids = Chapter.where(work_id: nil).pluck(:id) ; nil
=> nil 
> Creatorship.where(creation_id: chapter_ids, creation_type: "Chapter").size
=> 34139 {code}

There are roughly 42k chapters in the database without works, probably due to work deletion choking. (We want to make work deletion asynchronous so it doesn't happen as much: AO3-5517.)

There are about 34k creatorships for these chapters.

If one of those chapters belongs to you and you try to delete your account, nothing happens. No error page, it just does nothing when you press the button to delete your account.

We should make it so any work-less chapters you own are deleted and account deletion proceeds as expected. 

If there are co-creators on your work-less chapter, it shouldn't delete the chapter outright, but it should delete your creatorship. As long as the chapter has a creator, we'll just let the chapter hang out for now.

*Testing*

A database admin will need to:

# Create an account you're cool with deleting
# Post a work
# Add another chapter to the work 
# Add a co-created chapter to the work
# Set the {{work_id}} columns of the chapters from steps 3 & 4 to {{nil}}, probably using {{update_column}} to avoid callbacks and validations
# Attempt to delete the account

This is fixed if:

* the account is deleted

Summary: Story Parser copies story meta to imported chapter 2+
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Ariana
Description:
When a multi-chapter work is imported, the StoryParser scrapes work meta from the HTML page and copies the work title, summary and notes to the chapters after chapter 1 if they don't already have values for these fields. This leads to repetition and may affect readability if the summary is long. 

See https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1073383 for a manually-imported example, whose chapter list looks like this:
 !Screenshot 2021-06-27 at 15.13.51.png|thumbnail! 
(Chapter 7 happened to have a title, so it only got the duplicate summary)

h2. Steps to reproduce
This behaviour is also visible when importing works manually:
1. Import multiple pages that contain work title and summary meta fields (ie separate lines starting with `Title:` and `Summary:` respectively) but no chapter titles (identified by `Chapter title:`). 
1. Note that once the work is imported, chapter 2 and subsequent have the title set to the title of the work, and a copy of the work summary is displayed at the top of the chapter.
Open Doors can make a temp site available with this type of data if needed for testing.

h2. Details
The problem is due to code in the [get_chapter_from_work_params method in the StoryParser|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/models/story_parser.rb#L435-L443] which copies meta scraped from the chapter page into the work as well as the chapter. Probably the only fields that need to be copied into chapters from the work are the date fields.

Note that this is low priority for Open Doors imports as they can work around the issue by synthesising missing chapter titles and removing the summary from chapter pages so that meta doesn't get scraped from the HTML, but it isn't desirable behaviour.

Summary: Index tag_set_nominations on owned_tag_set_id, and index tag_nominations on tag_set_nomination_id
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
{{TagSetNominationsController#index}} takes 10 seconds, on average. We should add some indices to help with that.

All of the queries in that action depend on the {{owned_tag_set_id}} from the {{tag_set_nominations}} table, but (a) there are no indices on the {{tag_set_nominations}} table, and (b) the only index on the {{tag_nominations}} table that references {{tag_set_nominations_id}} (which is used by the join) is on {{(type, tag_set_nominations_id)}}, which only covers those queries that specify a type. This means that a line like {{if @tag_set.tag_nominations.unreviewed.empty?}} could require a full-table scan.

*Testing Instructions:* This adds some indices, so there shouldn't be any visible changes. Migrate up, migrate down, migrate up again.

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as a tag wrangler. We'll assume you're using testy, who is assigned the Testing fandom.

If a tag does not have a posted work, it should not be there, nor should it be included in the count.

h1. Notes

Summary: Add an index to the tag_set_associations table
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
The {{tag_set_associations}} table has no indices, so some queries involving it have to search through all 600,000+ rows. We should add an index starting with {{owned_tag_set_id}}, since most queries involving tag set IDs should specify the {{OwnedTagSet}}. (The {{Prompt#restricted_tags}} method is [one of the only places|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/63ed5aa8387b7593831811e66a2f2c2654bdea15/app/models/prompt.rb#L166] where the {{OwnedTagSet}} isn't specified, but that's because of [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5712|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5712|smart-link] .)

It might also be good to add an index starting with {{tag_id}} and another starting with {{parent_tag_id}}, particularly if this is addressed before [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5712|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5712|smart-link] . And a unique index on all three fields would be nice. But the index on {{owned_tag_set_id}} is probably the most important part.

*Notes:* The table is large enough that we probably want to use {{pt-online-schema-change}} on staging/production for this one.

*Testing Instructions:* Run the migration, revert it, and then run it again to make sure it works both ways.

Summary: Remove activerecord-mysql-reconnect gem and set reconnect: false in database.yml
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
Automatic reconnect and transactions don't play well together. Specifically, if a disconnect/reconnect occurs in the middle of a transaction, the first half of the transaction is rolled back (because it wasn't committed before the disconnect), and the second half of the transaction isn't wrapped in a transaction (because the transaction isn't reopened after the reconnect).

Let's get rid of automatic reconnect, to prevent these half-transactions.

*Note:* {{config/database.yml}} isn't under version control, so the PR part of this should just be the removal of the {{activerecord-mysql-reconnect}} gem.

Summary: Include IP address, referrer URL, and title of public site skin in support tickets
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
We're going to do some fun site skin things! To make handling any skin issues (seriously, theme or style would've killed us?) easier, we want to make sure tickets sent to Support automatically include information about which skin a user is using.

* Support will need to set up a custom field in the ticket tracker. The name will probably be something like {{cf_site_skin}}, but you'll need to check in with them.
* This should not be user-facing, and it should ideally not even be a hidden field on the Support and Feedback page, since that would be editable. You can look at how we handle the Rollout version ({{cf_rollout}}) for inspiration.
* If the user is using a public site skin (including Default), the field should reference it by title. If the user is using a non-public site skin, the field should say "Custom skin."
** Note: If the user has set a skin using the skin chooser in the footer or the Set for Session option on the skin page, this will override the skin they have set in their preferences/by using the Use button on the skin page. Ergo, the field should list the skin set via the session cookie ({{session[:site_skin]}}) if present. If none is present, then it’s safe to use the preference skin.
* It does not need to be recorded in the database.

Additionally, Support sometimes needs to pass tickets to Policy & Abuse. Policy & Abuse sometimes needs IP address and often needs URLs so they can action the tickets. Therefore, Support would like the tickets they get to also include IP addresses and referrers.

* Support will need to set up custom fields for these as well; probably something like {{cf_ip}} and {{cf_referer}}, but you'll need to check with them.
* These should also be neither user-facing nor hidden fields.
* These do not need to be recorded in the database.
* If the referrer is not an AO3 URL (e.g., if the person is coming from the pinned tweet or the link in an email footer), it can be left blank. If it _is_ an AO3 URL, it should be presented as-is (i.e., without any of the URL clean-up used by the abuse form) and should not have any restrictions applied.
* The “Our spam filter does collect IP addresses, but we never see them” message should be removed from the form.

*Testing*

To test the skin field, you'll want to submit a support ticket while using 

* the Default skin,
* a public skin from the chooser in the footer
* a public skin from the skins page, and 
* a custom skin.

To test the referrer, you will also need to submit a support ticket from

* the link in an email
* a page on the site

You should also make sure the message about IP addresses is no longer on the support form.

Someone from support will need to confirm the ticket contains the right info.

NB: We’re not changing the admin feedback mailer because it’s being removed in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6443|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6443|smart-link].

Summary: Non-admin wranglers can syn a canonical tag to another canonical
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce

tl;dr if you're logged in as a non-admin wrangler, you can syn Canonical A to Canonical B *if* you still have a tab open to Canonical A's pre-canonization edit page. This sometimes happens accidentally because wranglers often have multiple tabs open.

# Log in as a user with the tag wrangler role
# Create some new character and relationship tags\! The easiest way to do this en masse is by creating a new work:
## Post > New Work
## Fill in required information
## In "Characters" field, enter three new character tags, e.g. {{AO3-6239 Canonical Char 1}}, AO3-6239 Syn Char 1, {{AO3-6239 Char 1}}
## In relationships field, enter two new relationships, e.g. {{AO3-6239 & Ship 1}}, {{AO3-6239 / Ship}} 1 
## Press "Post"
# We're going to need to edit two of these tags, so 
## Find the link to {{AO3-6239 Canonical Char 1}} in the work meta, open it in a new tab/window, follow its "Edit" link
## Find the link to {{AO3-6239 Char 1}} in the work meta, open it in *two* new tabs/windows, and in each of these windows, follow its "Edit" link
# On the edit page for {{AO3-6239 Canonical Char 1}}, check "Canonical" and press "Save changes"
# On one of the edit pages for {{AO3-6239 Char 1}}, check "Canonical" and press "Save changes"
# Still in the same tab, add some associations to {{AO3-6239 Char 1}}
## Fill in the "Relationships" section with {{AO3-6239 & Ship 1}}, {{AO3-6239 / Ship 1}}
## Fill in the "Synonyms" section with {{AO3-6239 Syn Char 1}}
## Press "Save changes"
# Wait a minute or two
# Now switch to the other tab where you have {{AO3-6239 Char 1}}'s edit page open
# Fill in the "Synonym of" field with {{AO3-6239 Canonical Char 1}}
# Press "Save changes"

h1. What happens

{{AO3-6239 Char 1}} becomes a synonym of {{AO3-6239 Canonical Char 1}}. 

{{AO3-6239 Canonical Char 1}} now has all the associations that were attached to {{AO3-6239 Char 1}}. 

h1. What should happen

The changes should not be save and you should get an error message that says, "Only an admin can make a canonical tag into a synonym of another tag."

Description:
Once we have

*  exported from Phrase ([AO3-6109|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6109])
*  set up the i18n-tasks gem ([AO3-6003|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6003])
*  run the initial i18n-tasks normalization task and merged the result (also AO3-6003)

and before we

* merge any other i18n work
* add any other translations to Phrase

we need to rename some keys we use in the mailers. They're currently named things like "part5" or "para1," which is not great if we want to add or remove paragraphs.

To do this, we’ll

* use [i18n-tasks mv|https://github.com/glebm/i18n-tasks#move--rename--merge-keys] to update the keys for all locales at once (commands below)
* update the view files to actually use those keys
* merge those changes
* import all of the locales – not just the English – back into Phrase

Summary: Changing fandom name while approving tag set nominations can split the fandom
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Nary
Description:
Steps to reproduce the bug:

1. Create a new tag set: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_sets/new|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_sets/new]
2. Select "Currently taking nominations?"
3. Enter some limits for Fandom and Character nominations (for instance, 2 and 5).
4. Select "Submit" so the tag set will be open for submissions.
5. Have at least 2 different accounts nominate tags for the tag set, as follows:
a.  Both accounts should select the same fandom (it can be anything, but for this purpose, let's say "Wrong Fandom".
b.  Both accounts should enter, under "Wrong Fandom", the character "Right Character".  They should also enter several other random characters of their choice.
6. As the tag set maintainer, go back to your tag set and select "Review Nominations".
7. See "Wrong Fandom" with the character "Right Character x2" (or however many multiple nominations this character has.)
7. Using the text box next to "Wrong Fandom," enter "Right Fandom" as if you want to manually change the fandom name when you approve it.    Do not approve or change the characters.
8.  Select "Submit".

What should happen: 

The fandom "Right Fandom" should appear at the top of the page under "Already Approved Fandoms", with the full list of nominated characters underneath it.  "Wrong Fandom" should not be approved or appear anywhere.

What actually happens:

Two fandoms appear at the top of the page under "Already Approved Fandoms" - Right Fandom, containing all characters who were nominated 1 time, and Wrong Fandom, containing any characters that were nominated 2 or more times.  The fandom is now "split", and various further problems/errors can occur from here as the confused mod tries to sort out the problem:

* If you try to change the multiple-nominated character name under the Wrong Fandom, such as to "Right Character (Books)", you receive an error: "Oh no\! We ran into a problem partway through saving your updates, changing Right Character to Right Character (Books) – please check over your tag set closely\!" Both "Right Character" and "Right Character (Books)" will now show in the fandom box.
* If you try to change the multiple-nominated character name to a name already approved (such as in the Right Fandom version of the nomination), you receive the same error as above, plus the additional error "Someone else has already nominated the tag \[TAGNAME] for this set but in fandom \[FANDOMNAME].  (All nominations have to be unique for the approval process to work.) Try making your nomination more specific, for instance tacking on FANDOMNAME2."
* You can reject the multiple-nominated character under the Wrong Fandom and then edit it manually back into the correct fandom using batch loading.
* You can approve the multiple-nominated character under the Wrong Fandom and it should go through, but this is nonintuitive.

See attached images of this happening in a real tag set under review.

Summary: Incorrect pluralization in kudos emails
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. A brief language lesson.

In English, the number of people who've left kudos on your work does not change the verb we use in the email:

* Singular: username *left* kudos on Work Title.
* Plural: username1 and username2 *left* kudos on Work Title.

In French, for example, the verb must change based on the number of people:

* Singular: username *a félicité* votre œuvre Work Title.
* Plural: username1 et username2 *ont félicité* votre œuvre Work Title.

Other languages get even more complex, e.g., you might need a different verb if 5 people have left kudos than if 50 have left kudos.

h1. The bug

Note: It doesn't matter if the people leaving kudos are logged in users, guests, or a combination of both. 

If...

* 3 people leave kudos on Work A and Work C, and 
* 1 person leaves kudos on Work B, 

Then you might get an email that incorrectly uses the plural verb for Work B:

{quote}username1, username2 et username3 *ont félicité* votre œuvre Work A.

username *ont félicité* votre œuvre Work B.

username1, username2 et username3 *ont félicité* votre œuvre Work C.{quote}

Or that incorrectly uses the singular for Work A and Work C:

{quote}username1, username2 et username3 *a félicité* votre œuvre Work A.

username1, username2 et username3 *a félicité* votre œuvre Work C.

username *a félicité* votre œuvre Work B.{quote}

If...

* 1 person leaves kudos on Work A and Work C, and 
* 2 people leave kudos on Work B, 

Then you might get an email that incorrectly uses the singular verb for Work B: 

{quote}username *a félicité* votre œuvre Work A.

username1 et username2 *a félicité* votre œuvre Work B.

username *a félicité* votre œuvre Work C.{quote}

Or that incorrectly uses the plural for Work A and Work C:

{quote}username *ont félicité* votre œuvre Work A.

username *ont félicité* votre œuvre Work C.

username1 et username2 *ont félicité* votre œuvre Work B.{quote}

h1. Whyyyyy

If you read over the examples again, you might notice a pattern: when there are kudos for multiple works, the pluralization for every work is determined by the last work in the email.

The problem appears to be that the {{@kudos_count}} we use to determine pluralization ({{count: @kudos_count}}) is not set for each work ({{commentable}}):

[kudo_mailer.rb|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/4085de66e21dde41a9e6730b0f746e205b6da3a5/app/mailers/kudo_mailer.rb#L18-L40]:

{code:ruby}  kudos_hash.each_pair do |commentable_info, kudo_givers_hash|
    # Parse the key to extract the type and id of the commentable - skip if no commentable
    commentable_type, commentable_id = commentable_info.split('_')
    commentable = commentable_type.constantize.find_by(id: commentable_id)
    next unless commentable


    # If we have a commentable, extract names and process guest kudos text - skip if no kudos givers
    names = kudo_givers_hash['names']
    guest_count = kudo_givers_hash['guest_count']
    kudo_givers = []


    if !names.nil? && names.size > 0
      kudo_givers = names
      kudo_givers << guest_kudos(guest_count) unless guest_count == 0
      @kudos_count = names.size + guest_count
    else
      kudo_givers << guest_kudos(guest_count).capitalize unless guest_count == 0
      @kudos_count = guest_count
    end
    next if kudo_givers.empty?


    @commentables << commentable
    @kudo_givers[commentable_info] = kudo_givers{code}

[batch_kudo_notification.text.erb|https://github.com/sarken/otwarchive/blob/6b99402ac54eba0b220e85163408c777322c2251/app/views/kudo_mailer/batch_kudo_notification.text.erb#L2-L8]

{code:ruby}<% @commentables.each_with_index do |commentable, index| %>
    <% givers_list = @kudo_givers["#{commentable.class.name}_#{commentable.id}"].to_sentence
       commentable_link = "\"#{commentable.commentable_name.html_safe}\" (#{polymorphic_url(commentable)})".html_safe %>
    
    <%= t 'mailer.kudos.text.left_kudos', givers_list: givers_list, commentable_link: commentable_link, count: @kudos_count.to_i %>{code}


Additionally, if you check the count supplied by {{@kudos_count}}, it's off by one if there are any guests involved. 

That appears to be because {{names}} ultimately includes not just the usernames, but also the string that represents guests, e.g., {{"a guest"}} or {{"5 guests"}}. 

So {{kudos_count = names.size + guest_count}} is actually doing {{["username1", "username2", "a guest"].size + guest_count}}

Summary: Allow SSL for SMTP to be configurable
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: james_
Description:
On Debian 11, we get an error when sending mails:

{noformat}OpenSSL::SSL::SSLError (hostname "localhost" does not match the server certificate){noformat}

The easiest solution seems to be to disable SSL support for [SMTP in Rails|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/action_mailer_basics.html#action-mailer-configuration], specifically by setting {{enable_starttls_auto}} to {{false}} and {{openssl_verify_mode}} to {{none}}.

{quote}{{:enable_starttls_auto}} - Detects if STARTTLS is enabled in your SMTP server and starts to use it. Defaults to {{true}}.

{{:openssl_verify_mode}} - When using TLS, you can set how OpenSSL checks the certificate. This is really useful if you need to validate a self-signed and/or a wildcard certificate. You can use the name of an OpenSSL verify constant ('none' or 'peer') or directly the constant ({{OpenSSL::SSL::VERIFY_NONE}} or {{OpenSSL::SSL::VERIFY_PEER}}).{quote}

On our current Debian 10 systems, check that email notifications still work:

# Strip non-printing characters like the zero-width joiner.

Summary: Same work appears on multiple pages of search results due to ties in Elasticsearch
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: korrien
Description:
h2. Problem description

Our sorting recipes (for example [WorkQuery|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/e60e8226f193eed1daf13f6ab2ea45b49b58e7a9/app/models/search/work_query.rb#L273] one) include only primary search criteria and don't tell ES what should happen if elements are equal. This may result in inconsistent sorting.

We want to unambiguously break ties and return predictable results.

h2. Background

It's possible that this change will in some degree solve the intermittent issue "work appears on multiple pages".

If works A and B are are considered equal as per sorting criteria, their order is not guaranteed to be persistent between searches. Actions such as updating works, adding comments, changing stats, wrangling tags should cause reindexing and thus change the default ES sorting order.

Lets say works A and B are suppose to end up as as last work on page 1/first work on page 2. It might happen that on navigation to page 1 works order is (A, B), so work A is shown on page 1, and on navigation to page 2 order would become (B, A), so again work A would be shown on page 2, instead of expected work B.

In production this behavior might be observed for a period of time (at least couple of minutes) and can be reproduced in different browser sessions. It's unclear what causes it/how much caching or elasticsearch internals are involved.



Note that the issue is valid not just for works, but for bookmarks (and possibly tags) as well.

h2. Testing instructions

Reproducing search instability is a bit difficult in real environments with many Elasticsearch shards as problem depends in which shard the work ends up in.

(After identifying the works in the same shard it should also be possible to reproduce "work appears on multiple pages" by changing setup such a way that these works appear on different pages. It would be possible to observe behavior at least once, but maybe not for a couple of minutes as in production.)

# Create at least 13 works by author Writer (there are currently 12 work shards by default, so with 13 works we assure there are at least two in the same shard)
# Navigate to works by Writer and sort works by Author.
# Notice works order (before the fix it would seem random).
# For the first work from the bottom:
## Update summary to "Updated 1"
## Assure/wait for reindexing to complete
## Refresh the page with works from step 2
# Check if the order changed (summary number is out of order).
# Keep repeating steps 4 and 5 for all other works updating summary to "Updated n".

Current behavior: 
At least two works switch places at least once.

Expected behavior:
Works order keeps being stable

Summary: Try to reduce frequency of RecordNotFound errors when calling flush_work_cache
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
There are a lot of Resque errors along the lines of this one:
{code}
Tag
Arguments
--- perform_on_instance

--- 71249578

--- flush_work_cache
Exception
ActiveRecord::RecordNotFound
Error
Couldn't find Tag with 'id'=71249578
{code}
When a brand new tag is created, the {{flush_work_cache}} job is enqueued after the tag is committed to the database. However, the Resque workers sometimes process jobs so quickly that when the worker tries to read the tag from one of the read-only database copies, that copy hasn't processed the commit that created the tag yet, causing the job to fail due to a {{RecordNotFound}} error.

We'd like to switch the {{queue_flush_work_cache}} callback so that it no longer runs when a tag is first created, since when a tag is first created there are no other works that need their cache flushed.

h1. Testing Instructions

To make sure that changing the callback from {{after_save}} to {{after_update}} didn't break anything, it would be good to make sure that the cache expiration still works when a tag is renamed:
# Pick a tag.
# Open a work that uses that tag.
# Rename the tag.
# Wait five minutes to make sure that the cache expiration runs.

Summary: User suspension message provides incorrect time for the end of a user's suspension
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
# Log in as admin with the role superadmin or policy_and_abuse 
# Mange Users > Find Users
# In "Name" field, enter the login of a user whose account you have access to
# Press "Find"
# Follow the "Details" link in the correct row of the results table
# Under "Warnings and Suspensions," choose "Suspend: enter a whole number of days"
# Enter a number of days, e.g. 2
# In "Notes," supply some text explaining why you're suspending the user
# Press "Update"
# Log out as admin
# Log in as the suspended user
# Post > New Work

*What happens*

You are redirected to your user page with the flash error: "Your account has been suspended until Sun, 27 Feb 2022 23:55:39 +0000. You may not add or edit content until your suspension has been resolved. Please contact Abuse for more information."

The time in the error message is exactly 48 hours from the time the admin created the suspension, but that's not the time the suspension will be lifted – suspensions are lifted en masse once per day by the [unsuspend_users rake task|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/b63fce67a3975ec0614bb535c75d76c8dafbda71/lib/tasks/admin_tasks.rake#L2-L6 ], which lifts the suspensions of any user whose {{suspended_until}} time is no more than 12 hours after the task is run.

{{User.where(["suspended_until <= ?", 12.hours.from_now]).update_all("suspended_until = NULL, suspended = false")}}

The [task is run at 06:51 UTC|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/b63fce67a3975ec0614bb535c75d76c8dafbda71/config/schedule.rb#L37-L40] so the user above would not be unsuspended until Monday, February 28 2022, 06:51 UTC.

*What should happen*

The message should reflect the actual date the user will be unsuspended. Ideally, this information should be provided in the user's preferred timezone, but it should not include the time itself.

*Notes*

The draft work deletion message has similar issues.

Full list:

0 - ०
1 - १
2 - २
3 - ३
4 - ४
5 - ५
6 - ६
7 - ७
8 - ८
9 - ९
10 - १०
1,000 - १,०००
10,000 - १०,०००
100,000 - १,००,०००
1,000,000 - १०,००,०००
10,000,000 - १,००,००,०००

*Steps to reproduce*

1. Set your locale in Preferences to receive emails in Hindi or Marathi
2. Go to your Dashboard -> Invitations -> Request invitations
3. Request any number of invitations
4. Using an admin account with the PAC role (or a superadmin account), authorise or deny the request

*What happens*

You'll receive an email that mentions the number of invitations using an Arabic numeral (e.g. "4") amid the Marathi or Hindi text.

*What should happen*

The number of invitations should be mentioned only in Devanagari script, as per the list above.

then

This happens because staging and production use the same S3 path; staging should be given its own that includes "staging" in the name, while production's should be unchanged to avoid wiping out any icons. 

-We will also need to temporarily stop validating icon type on staging so we can upload some invalid icons.- We can test the rake by uploading a valid icon and changing the {{icon_content_type}} column to something invalid.

Summary: Add user ID to bookmarks
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
We have three kinds of bookmark blurbs:

* bookmark blurbs, which contain the bookmarkable and a single user's bookmark. These are used for
** the Recent Bookmarks page, i.e., [https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks|https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks]
** bookmark search results
** user and pseud dashboards, e.g., [https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/NAME|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/NAME] and [https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/NAME/pseuds/NAME|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/NAME/pseuds/NAME]
** user and pseud bookmark listings, e.g., [https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/NAME/bookmarks|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/NAME/bookmarks] and [https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/NAME/pseuds/NAME/bookmarks|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/NAME/pseuds/NAME/bookmarks]
** collection dashboards, e.g., [https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/NAME]
* bookmarkable blurbs, which contain the bookmarkable and multiple users' bookmarks. These are used for
** tag bookmark listings, e.g., [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/NAME/bookmarks|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/NAME/bookmarks]
** collection bookmark listings, e.g., [https://test.archiveofourown.org/collection/NAME/bookmarks|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collection/NAME/bookmarks]
* short bookmark blurbs, which contain a single user's bookmark. These are used for
** the bookmarkable blurb, to list the individual bookmarks
** a bookmarkable's bookmark page, e.g., [https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/###/bookmarks|https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/###/bookmarks]

Bookmark blurbs should have the user ID of both the bookmarker and the bookmarkable's creator(s). They should also have the bookmarkable’s ID (i.e., work-123, series-123, external-work-123).

Bookmarkable blurbs for series and works should have the user ID of only the bookmarkable's creator(s). They should also have the bookmarkable’s ID (i.e., work-123, series-123, external-work-123).

Short bookmark blurbs should have the user ID of the bookmarker.

h1. Testing using a skin to hide a given user’s bookmarks

h2. Testing setup steps

We're going to assume you have User A, User B, User C, and User D, and that the Testing fandom is canonical. (We need a canonical tag so we can see its bookmark listings.)

# Post a work

## Fill in Fandoms with Testing
## Fill in Title with AO3-6325 My Epic
## Fill in the other required fields
## Post
# Log out
# Log in as User B

## Fill in Title with AO3-6325 Test Work
## Check "This work is part of a series"
## Fill in "Or create and use a new one" with AO3-6325 Test Series
## Fill in the other required fields
## Post
# Locate and bookmark the work AO3-6325 My Epic
# Log out
# Log in as User C
# Locate and bookmark the works AO3-6325 My Epic and AO3-6325 Test Work and the series AO3-6325 Test Series
# Log out
# Log in as User D
# Visit the profiles for User B note their ID. We'll assume it's 123.
# Create and use a site skin to hide anything by User B
## Hi, username\! > My Dashboard > Skins > Create Site Skin
## Fill in CSS with {{.user-123 { display: none !important }}}
## Fill in the other required fields
## Submit
## Use

Summary: Allow users to block other users from commenting
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. What it should do

Blocking should apply to users and stick around if the user changes their name. (Only the blocked user's current name should be displayed.) 

Blocking a user should prevent them from:

* commenting on your works
* replying to comments on your works (i.e., they cannot reply to you, themselves, or a third person)
* directly replying to your comments on news posts, their works, or anyone else's works
* editing comments they have previously left on your works or comments 

It should not prevent them from:

* commenting on tags you wrangle
* replying to comments on tags you wrangle (i.e., they can reply to you, themselves, or a third person)
* replying to your comments on tags you do not wrangle
* deleting comments they have previously left on your works or comments

If you’ve co-created a work (or works) with them:

* they should be able to comment on the work or works you’ve co-created
* they should not be able to reply to  you on the work or works you’ve co-created

"Preventing" should involve back end checks in addition to hiding the relevant forms and buttons. 

"Your works" includes your anonymous works and works you have co-created.

h1. Who you can block

You should not be able to block:

* official accounts ([+AO3-5986+|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5986] should be implemented before comment blocking); you should receive an error.
** Text: Sorry, you can't block an official account.
* yourself. There shouldn’t even be a button for this.

h1. How you can block

* Wherever the button appears, it should say “Block” when the user is not currently blocked and “Unblock” when the user is currently blocked. (We’re calling it “the block button” below for simplicity.) 
* The block button should only be shown to logged in users.
* Checks for whether a particular user can be blocked (i.e., did the blocker co-create a work with the potential blockee) should occur after pressing the block button, not before displaying it.

Summary: Allow tags to be sorted by number of uses
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
We’d like to modify the tag search form introduced in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5830|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5830|smart-link] to allow tags to be sorted by the number of uses.

h2. Implementation Notes

In Elasticsearch, the {{uses}} field for tags is based on the {{taggings_count_cache}} column. However, the {{taggings_count_cache}} is only updated in {{Tag.write_redis_to_database}} ([source|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/22394a36d4a93ac9f0e3d703871c42ca0483ee4e/app/models/tag.rb#L38-L51]), which uses {{update_all}} to skip callbacks. So Elasticsearch is only informed of the new {{taggings_count_cache}} value when the tag is manually edited by a wrangler. This means that sorting on {{uses}} produces very buggy-looking results.

The reason {{Tag.write_redis_to_database}} skips callbacks is because (a) it's a scheduled task that runs every 2 minutes, and (b) any tag with fewer than 1000 uses will be added to the list of tags processed by {{Tag.write_redis_to_database}} every time the tag’s taggings count is viewed. (i.e. When a tag is listed in tag search results, when a tag is listed in the wrangling bins, when a tag is edited.)

We’d like to add some kind of indexing (or partial indexing) whenever the taggings count changes to keep the {{uses}} field up-to-date. To avoid overwhelming Elasticsearch with updates, we'd also like to avoid doing extra work when the taggings count doesn't change. 

h2. Deploy Instructions

To account for older updates to the {{taggings_count_cache}} that didn’t make it into Elasticsearch, we need to reindex all tags with {{rake search:index_tags}}.

h2. Testing Instructions

*Note:* The {{uses}} field is the number shown beside the tag when searching, not the number of works shown on the fandom index page or the tag works page.

# To test updates of small tags:
## Create a work using two brand new tags with very similar names, similar enough that you can easily create a tag search that will return both of those tags and very few other tags.
## Remove Tag A from the work.
## Wait 5-10 minutes for the search to update.
## Perform a tag search that will return both tags, and sort by uses in descending order. Tag B should be listed first, and Tag A should be listed second.
## Change the order from descending to ascending. Now Tag A should be first, and Tag B should be second.
## Go back to the work and replace Tag B with Tag A.
## Wait 5-10 minutes for the search to update.
## Perform another tag search sorted by uses in descending order. Tag A should now be listed first.
# To test updates of larger tags:
## Find two tags with over 1000 uses that have very similar taggings counts. You should be able to do this by doing a tag search with no query, but sorted by number of uses.
## Perform a search sorted by uses, and figure out what page the two tags are on and what order they appear in.
## Add enough works to the smaller tag to make it slightly larger than the other tag.
## Wait somewhere between 3 minutes and 40 minutes, depending on how large the tags you’ve chosen are.
## Perform the search again, and return to the page that the two tags were on. Depending on how this issue was tackled, they may be in the same order that they were before – this isn’t a bug, it’s just the way that the code works.
## Wait 5-10 minutes for the search to update.
## Perform a search sorted by uses, and return to the page that the two tags were on. Verify that they have switched order.

There are 3 steps to this:

# Make sure writes from Redis to DB are from actual changed count values.
# Use callback function to reindex Elasticsearch document when writes to DB happen.
# Ensure that callback function is triggered when writes to DB happen.

Here’s what I’m planning to use for the three steps:

For the first step, it’s possible to approach this by ether checking to see if the counts have actually changed before adding to redis update or by preventing calls to {{write_taggings_to_redis}} unless the counts have changed. Since there's no way to determine this within {{taggings_count=(value)}}, I've decided to go with the first approach. If {{taggings_count=(value)}} is never called except from {{taggings_count}} or {{update_cache_count(id)}}, I could try the second approach, but I don't believe that is the case. It would also be feasible to make this change if, outside of the previous two methods, {{taggings_count=(value)}} is only called when there is an actual change to the count.

I will use the code ticking instant wrote out in a previous pull request that was trashed for other reasons.

{code:ruby}  def write_taggings_to_redis(value)
    # Atomically set the value while extracting the old value.
    old_redis_value = REDIS_GENERAL.getset("tag_update_#{id}_value", value)

    # If the value hasn't changed from the saved version or the REDIS version,
    # there's no need to write an update to the database, so let's just bail
    # out.
    return value if value == old_redis_value && value == taggings_count_cache

    # If we've reached here, then the value has changed, and we need to make
    # sure that the new value is written to the database.
    REDIS_GENERAL.sadd("tag_update", id)
    value
  end{code}

For the second step, I will add a statement to the {{after_update}} method:

{code:ruby}    # Reindex immediately to update the unwrangled bin.
    if tag.saved_change_to_unwrangleable? ||
      tag.saved_change_to_taggings_count_cache?
      tag.reindex_document
    end{code}

For the third step, I will change the code of {{Tag.write_redis_to_database}} using some code written by ticking instant from the previously mentioned pull request to make the method more readable and changing the method from {{update_all}} to {{update}} so the callback is triggered:

{code:ruby}  def self.write_redis_to_database
    batch_size = ArchiveConfig.TAG_UPDATE_BATCH_SIZE
    REDIS_GENERAL.smembers("tag_update").each_slice(batch_size) do |batch|
      Tag.transaction do
        batch.each do |id|
          value = REDIS_GENERAL.get("tag_update_#{id}_value")
          next if value.blank?
          Tag.where(id: id).update(taggings_count_cache: value.to_i)
        end
        REDIS_GENERAL.srem("tag_update", batch)
      end
    end
  end{code}

    write_taggings_to_redis(value)
  end{noformat}

But for a big tag, we’re bailing out once {{update_tag_cache}} finds something in the cache, and {{taggings_count=(value)}} / {{write_taggings_to_redis(value)}} is indeed never being called for tags with cached counts. So it seems like the newly added tag callback isn’t fixing it because it only deletes the cached count if {{tag.saved_change_to_taggings_count_cache?}} , but the number in the database only changes if we successfully invoke {{write_taggings_to_redis(value)}}? 

A big downside to the tagging callback change I’m suggesting is it’s a _lot_ of counting, because we check the real tagging count for a tag every single time we create or destroy a tagging. :| For things like Ratings, Warnings, and Categories, which are huge tags that are on almost every work, that’s gonna be kind of ridiculous.

Summary: N+1 queries when displaying comments
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
When displaying a collection of comments, the following queries are performed once per comment displayed:

# [The number of reviewed replies is counted.|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/59bb5ebc3ca4fa86056b410d922152905b8cc179/app/views/comments/_comment_thread.html.erb#L9]
# [The reviewed replies are loaded, if there are any.|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/59bb5ebc3ca4fa86056b410d922152905b8cc179/app/views/comments/_comment_thread.html.erb#L15]
# [The pseud is loaded to check whether the comment can be marked as spam.|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/59bb5ebc3ca4fa86056b410d922152905b8cc179/app/helpers/comments_helper.rb#L129]

The comment’s parent also must be loaded (along with the work and its pseuds, in the case of comments on chapters), though when displaying multiple comments they usually share a parent, so the N+1 queries often end up hitting the query cache instead of the database.

That makes for 2-3 queries per comment when cached. When uncached, the user is loaded alongside the pseud, for 3-4 queries per comment.

The issues [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5986|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5986|smart-link], [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6323|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6323|smart-link], and [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6327|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6327|smart-link] also involve loading the user even when cached, as well as contributing other queries.

We’d like to be able to display a single page of comments more efficiently, without performing database queries for each comment. Ideally, the number of database queries should be independent of the number of comments displayed.

h1. Testing Instructions

In staging and production, there’s not enough information in the logs to determine whether there are n+1 queries. (Bullet can catch some, but only those that involve loading associations.) So verifying that there aren’t n+1 queries is going to have to be a process that occurs in review/automated testing.

In order to apply different rate limits to the 2 request types (at nginx level), we need them to use different paths, by [setting up an alias for the second request type|https://github.com/heartcombo/devise/#configuring-routes].

* The {{WorkIndexer}} class produces roughly 24N+1 queries for a batch of size N.
* The {{WorkCreatorIndexer}} class produces 2N+1 queries for a batch of size N.

Summary: Add a rake task to fix thread column for comments from 2009

Description:

Any replies to these comments will have “Parent Thread” links that point to the wrong comment (or no comment at all). Plus, with the changes introduced by [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6333|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6333|smart-link], these comments now trigger 500 errors when viewing the work with {{show_comments=true}}. # Add a rake task to fix any top-level (i.e. depth 0) comments that have {{thread != id}}, and update all replies (and replies to replies, etc.) to match. Something like the following should work, though it might be good to add more progress messages:
{code:ruby}def fix_comment(comment)
  comment.with_lock do
    if comment.reply_comment?
      comment.update_column(:thread, comment.commentable.thread)
    else
      comment.update_column(:thread, comment.id)
    end
    comment.comments.each { |reply| fix_comment(reply) }
  end
end

Summary: Handle or prevent RecordNotUnique errors for tag wrangling operations
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
These three {{Tag}} functions can cause {{RecordNotUnique}} errors to appear in Resque:

* {{update_filters_for_filterables}}
* {{transfer_or_remove_associations}}
* {{update_inherited_meta_tags}}

We’d like to address these errors, either by modifying the code to use {{upsert}} to prevent errors when multiple processes are inserting duplicate records at around the same time, or by using the {{ActiveJob}} system to retry jobs that encounter {{RecordNotUnique}} errors.

h1. Testing Instructions

Because the {{RecordNotUnique}} errors are caused by having two similar tasks run at the same time, it’s difficult to reproduce the error on demand. For staging, it should be sufficient to check that the following still work:

* Testing {{update_filters_for_filterables}}:
** Pick two tags of the same type, A and B.
** Make A canonical.
** Make B a synonym of A.
** Wait 10+ minutes for the filters to update.
** Make sure that when you view the tag A, it also includes works tagged only with B.
** Remove the synonym relationship between A and B.
** Wait 10+ minutes for the filters to update.
** Make sure that when you view the tag A, it no longer includes works tagged only with B.
* Testing {{transfer_or_remove_associations}}:
** Pick two canonical fandoms A and B.
** Pick a character C and add A as its parent.
** As an admin, edit the tag A and syn A to B.
** Wait a few minutes for the job to run.
** Check the tag page for C to make sure that it has B listed as a parent tag.
* Testing {{update_inherited_meta_tags}}:
** Pick three canonical tags of the same type, A, B, and C.
** Subtag C to B, and B to A.
** Wait 10+ minutes for the filters to update.
** Make sure that when you view the tag A, it also includes works tagged only with C.
** Remove the metatag relationship between B and C, and between A and B.
** Wait 10+ minutes for the filters to update.
** Make sure that when you view the tag A, it no longer includes works tagged only with C.

h1. Deploy Steps

# Turn off wrangling in the admin settings.
# Run these lines in the console to restart all of the previous failed tag jobs. 
{code:ruby}Resque::Failure.each do |id, job|
  next unless job.dig("payload", "class") == "Tag"
  next unless job.dig("exception") == "ActiveRecord::RecordNotUnique"
  next if %w[transfer_or_remove_associations transfer_or_remove_favorite_tags].include?(job.dig("payload", "args", 2))
  Resque::Failure.requeue(id)
  Resque::Failure.remove(id)
end{code}
(It might be good to run this twice, once during the deploy and one a day or two before the deploy, so that this step finishes quickly during the deploy.)
# Wait for all tag tasks to finish running. Go back to Step 2 if any of them fail.
# Do the deploy.
# Wait until all unicorns and resque workers have finished restarting.
# Re-enable wrangling in the admin settings.
# Start a {{screen}} session.
# Run {{rake Tag:destroy_invalid_common_taggings}}.
# Run {{rake Tag:destroy_invalid_meta_taggings}}.

Once this has been deployed, it should be marked as Pending Attention on Beta, and someone should check to see if it helps prevent new {{RecordNotUnique}} errors from appearing in the Resque failures queue.

Summary: Emoji entered in tags behave erratically
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Nary
Description:
Entering emoji in tags fields can turn certain emoji into other emoji, or make them disappear entirely, or generally behave unexpectedly.

Steps to reproduce:

# Create a new work or bookmark.
# Add an emoji like 💕 (two hearts) as a tag on the work/bookmarker’s tags.
# Save the work/bookmark.

What should happen: Your emoji should stay what you entered it as.

What actually happens: Your lovely two hearts emoji is now 💩 (poop emoji).  Ack, bad\!

This one is a consistent error so it’s good for testing, but not the only example of this problem.  This issue happens with various emoji, although some remain correct (smilies seem to be largely ok for instance).  If there’s a pattern to which ones work and which don’t, I don’t know it.

Further testing on this: entering a cat, a whale, and a train turned into three curling stones (???).  Any further emoji entered in that field on the same work ([https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1077202|https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1077202]) simply vanished upon saving.  (The smile with hearts and the cat face remained the same when entered in the rel and character fields respectively.)
Comment:
12/Jul/22 11:17 PM;557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6;This is caused by the database collation. The {{utf8mb4_unicode_ci}} collation apparently [thinks of all 4-byte emoji as equal|https://stackoverflow.com/questions/41147829/how-can-i-search-by-emoji-in-mysql-using-utf8mb4]. So whichever of those single-emoji tags was created first will always be the one retrieved from the database on a lookup, and all of the other tags cannot be created (for emojis with 4 bytes, at least). In production, it looks like the single 4-byte emoji tag is 🤣. On staging, the single 4-byte emoji tag is 💩. There are similar issues with tags of any length – as long as a tag has a 4-byte emoji, it’ll be treated as a wildcard for all other 4-byte emojis.

The fix would be to switch collations. Apparently {{utf8mb4_unicode_ci}} is an old collation, and {{utf8mb4_unicode_520_ci}} is the newer version that correctly separates emoji and still allows for case-insensitive comparison. (There are apparently even newer collations, but they might require a newer version of MySQL, too. What version are you using currently?)

Unfortunately, [it appears that|http://mysql.rjweb.org/utf8mb4_collations.html] {{utf8mb4_unicode_520_ci}} also considers {{Æ}} equivalent to {{ae}}, while {{utf8mb4_unicode_ci}} considers them to be separate characters, so any migration to fix this is going to have to have extra code to avoid deleting tags, as happened during the original transition to {{utf8mb4}}. There also may be other characters with that issue that aren’t listed on the linked website, so the solution for detecting these tags needs to be fairly general.

(Another alternative might be to switch to a binary collation, but that’s a can of worms in a different way.)

EDIT: This applies to all 4-byte characters, not just emoji, which means that it affects pseuds as well. (Pseud names are required to match {{/\A[\p{Word} -]+\Z/u}}, so they can’t include emoji, but there are a number of {{\p{Word}}} characters among the set of 4-byte characters, all of which will be treated as interchangeable by the database.) So it might be good to change more than just the tag name collation.

Since we’re still on 5.7, we can only get to {{utf8mb4_unicode_520_ci}}. But MySQL will eventually use {{utf8mb4_0900_ai_ci}} as the default collation for utf8mb4, available from 8.0.

Systems also have plans to switch to MariaDB (we’re only using it in Docker/development right now), as another possible scheduling factor.

ETA: Just to clarify the problem a bit more, here’s our [user factory|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/factories/users.rb]:

    # devise :confirmable.
    confirmed_at { Faker::Time.backward }

    trait :unconfirmed do
      confirmed_at { nil }
    end{noformat}

The email is made up of a first name ({{Faker::Name.first_name}}) with a number appended ({{#{n}}}). The name will be in whatever locale you select when previewing the email. So, e.g., if you select zh-CN, it will be one of the [first names for zh-CN|https://github.com/faker-ruby/faker/blob/2f06350da484de1fbc3f2e8ef3f1c755502a7a45/lib/locales/zh-CN.yml#L21], and thus it will contain characters that [our email format validator|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/317e3e840ce28f1d66e2ede43fdbd3e6bf0218bd/app/validators/email_format_validator.rb#L10] doesn’t allow.

The easiest way around that is to specify account emails for any users we create for the mailer previews, but that’s probably going to get old. We might want to change the factory itself, maybe to something like a nice alphanumeric ({{Faker::Alphanumeric.alphanumeric(number: 10, min_alpha: 3, min_numeric: 3)}})?

ETA 2: Oh! I know why we see the error in different places. In locales like {{pt-BR}}, only some first names have characters that are invalid in AO3 email addresses. So it’s possible for the first creator to be valid, but the second creator to be invalid:

{noformat}  def creatorship_notification_data
    first_creator = create(:user, login: "JayceHexmaster")
    second_creator = create(:user, login: "viktor_the_machine")
    work = create(:work, authors: [first_creator.default_pseud, second_creator.default_pseud])
    second_creatorship = Creatorship.find_by(creation: work, pseud: second_creator.default_pseud)
    [second_creatorship, first_creator]
  end{noformat}

Whichever user has the invalid-to-us email is determines how the page errors. So if you set the email in both places (or fix the factory), then yeah, both types of 422 errors will clear up.

Summary: Creating a non-canonical tag with the same name as an existing canonical via new tag page decanonizes existing tag
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Dre
Description:
# Log in as a tag wrangler (testy has wrangling privileges on staging)
# Browse > Tags > New Tag ([https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/new|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/new])
# input name of existing canonical tag. 
# DO NOT check the canonical box. 
# DO check the box for the type of tag the current canonical is. 
# Click Create Tag button. 

Doing so will overwrite current canonical tag by decanonizing it. If the name of the tag was typed into the field with any case changes, those will carry over to the decanonized tag as well. 

This can be done by any tag wrangler. Does not require admin role to do.

Summary: Add confirmation page and email when a user changes the email on their account
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Nary
Description:
Currently, if a user changes the email address on their account, there is no method to confirm that they actually own the email address they're changing to. This can lead to situations where a user changes to an email address they do not own, and that person starts getting their emails from the site. We would like to add a separate confirmation page and email as part of the email change process. After submitting their new email, there should be a new page created (like the muting confirmation page) where they are presented with the email they entered and asked whether this is the correct email. Upon agreeing, an email is sent to the new address and they need to confirm it by clicking on a link in the email before their account's email is actually updated. If they do not confirm within a certain length of time, the email address should not be changed. We'll most likely want to use Devise's[ |https://www.rubydoc.info/github/heartcombo/devise/main/Devise/Models/Confirmable][+Confirmable module+|https://www.rubydoc.info/github/heartcombo/devise/main/Devise/Models/Confirmable] for this, which has the following option: {noformat}+reconfirmable+: requires any email changes to be confirmed (exactly the same way as initial account confirmation) to be applied. Requires additional unconfirmed_email db field to be set up (t.reconfirmable in migrations). Until confirmed, new email is stored in unconfirmed email column, and copied to email column on successful confirmation. Also, when used in conjunction with send_email_changed_notification, the notification is sent to the original email when the change is requested, not when the unconfirmed email is confirmed.{noformat} h2. Summary: Editing a character or relationship that has been nominated in a tag set removes it from the "Review Associations" page of the tag set
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
h1. Steps to Reproduce

# Find or create a character tag “Char X” that has been wrangled into a canonical fandom “Fandom 1.”
# Create a tag set with open nominations.
# Nominate “Char X” with a different fandom “Fandom 2.” (Make sure that “Char X” is not wrangled into “Fandom 2,” because otherwise it’ll never appear on the “Review Associations” tag, edited or not.)
# Review nominations for the tag set.
# Accept both nominations (the fandom and the character).
# Note that “Char X” is listed among the unassociated tags.
# Look at (but don’t modify) the “Review Associations” tab.
# Note that it suggests adding the “Char X → Fandom 2” association.
# Log in as a wrangler.
# Go to the Edit page for “Char X.”
# Press “Save changes” without making any changes.
# Log back in as the tag set owner.
# Note that “Char X” is still listed among the unassociated tags.
# Look at the “Review Associations” tab.

h1. What Should Happen

It should still contain the suggested “Char X → Fandom 2” association.

h1. What Actually Happens

The suggested association is gone.

h1. Notes

[https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3757|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-3757|smart-link] is specifically related to wrangling & tag sets, but the “Review Associations” page isn’t cached, so this isn’t a caching issue.

Once [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6328|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6328|smart-link] is in, it won’t be necessary to have tag wrangler access to trigger this bug, because tags will be saved more frequently to keep the count up-to-date. So you’ll be able to trigger the bug by nominating a character, and then writing a work with that character tag.

The cause of this is the difference between [the code for setting the value of parented|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/26603cf9510587afa4ebd911a399de6a8b84a6c9/app/models/tagset_models/tag_nomination.rb#L74-L89] in the {{TagNomination}} class, and [the code for fixing parented when the tag is updated|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/26603cf9510587afa4ebd911a399de6a8b84a6c9/app/models/tag.rb#L1142-L1156]. The former sets {{parented}} to true only if the tag was nominated in one of its canonical fandoms; the latter sets {{parented}} to true for all tag nominations as long as the tag has any canonical fandoms at all. So whichever callback fired more recently will determine whether the tag appears on the “Review Associations” page.

(Practically speaking, the {{TagNomination}} callback will only fire when the tag is first being nominated, because [nominations are approved in bulk without callbacks|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/26603cf9510587afa4ebd911a399de6a8b84a6c9/app/models/tagset_models/owned_tag_set.rb#L77-L78]. So this bug occurs even if the tag is edited before the nomination is approved.)

Summary: Recipient with multiple givers order not stable in Assignments page
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Nary
Description:
How to produce this issue:

# Set up a challenge and have over 20 participants sign up (the assignments page displays 20 results at a time, so over 20 is needed to observe this problem.)
# Close signups and run matching (recommended to set matching parameters so that anyone can match with anyone, for simplicity).
# Go to the the Assignments page ([https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME/potential_matches|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME/potential_matches]) 
# Make the last recipient on page 1 of the results the same as the first recipient on page 2 (e.g. If testy is signed up, make testy the recipient in both of those assignments).
# Page back and forth between page 1 and page 2.

What you would expect: the order of assignments should remain stable despite paging back and forth.

What actually happens: the order of those assignments with the same recipient can flip around unpredictably.  This causes confusion and problems for exchange mods.

I think what is currently determining the order of the list is the recipient’s username.  So in cases where this is identical, there should be a second ordering factor of some sort to make sure the order remains stable.  I would suggest using Assignment ID (the number in the left column) to determine which assignment out of several for the same recipient should come first, but I’d be happy with anything that keeps things in the same order from page to page.

Summary: Reorganize My Assignments page

Description:
Currently, a user’s My Assignments page [lists all undefaulted assignments from oldest to newest, and then all undefaulted pinch hits from oldest to newest|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/de0fa361add04f0be7fed8a91d2651373eeb48d4/app/controllers/challenge_assignments_controller.rb#L80]. All are listed on a single page, without pagination.

To make it easier to find the most pressing information – assignments waiting to be filled – we would like to make some changes:

* Split assignments across two pages like we do with the My Claims page: the default URL ({{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/testy/assignments}}) should list unposted assignments, and {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/testy/assignments?posted=true }}should list complete assignments.

* Each page should list all appropriate assignments from oldest to newest regardless of whether they're pinch hits or not.
** When there are multiple assignments that were sent at the same time (which can happen if the user has multiple assignments in one challenge), they should then be sorted by ascending ID to ensure stable pagination.
* When necessary, pages should be paginated at top and bottom, using the default number of items for pagination.
* The "Assignments (#)" count in dashboard sidebar should only include unposted assignments, like "Claims (#)" only includes unfulfilled.
* The note about checking for claims prompts should have the class {{notes}} instead of {{note}} – bonus points if you change the Claims page as well. (And maybe add a period to the “Try X” sentences.)

The bookmark should be removed.

Description:
h1. Steps to Reproduce # Open the “Post > New Work” form. # Fill out all required fields. # Enter the following HTML: {noformat}Cause I'm having a good time{noformat} # Press Preview or Post. h1. What Happens If you hover over the text of the work, the title attribute says “Don”, not “Don’t stop me now.” If you view the source of the work, the parser appears to have outputted the following: {noformat}

Cause I'm having a good time

{noformat} h1. Notes This doesn’t happen if the title attribute is set on a paragraph, or on a tag that’s already been placed inside a paragraph when the parser first runs. But it happens on {{
}}s, {{}}s, {{}}s, {{}}s, {{}}s, {{
}}s, etc. – any tag that isn’t in [the list of tags in dont_touch_content_tag?|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/d74d404f052b4e60e223c712fff619844695806d/lib/html_cleaner.rb#L224-L228] The reason this occurs is because when {{add_paragraphs_to_text}} is rewriting the document, it reformats most tags by calling {{open_tag}}, which [regenerates the list of tag attributes using single quotes to enclose all attributes|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/d74d404f052b4e60e223c712fff619844695806d/lib/html_cleaner.rb#L4-L19]. This, of course, breaks when the attribute contains a single quote. The only unaffected tags are those listed in {{dont_touch_content_tag?}}, or any tag contained inside one of the {{dont_touch_content_tag?}} tags, because those are reformatted by [calling Nokogiri’s native node.to_s|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/d74d404f052b4e60e223c712fff619844695806d/lib/html_cleaner.rb#L279-L290], which handles attributes containing {{'}} correctly. h1. Summary: Users sometimes report chapter URLs that do not contain the work IDs
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
Sometimes, users will supply chapter show URLs (e.g., [https://test.archiveofourown.org/chapters/123|https://test.archiveofourown.org/chapters/123] or [https://test.archiveofourown.org/chapters/123?some_params=something|https://test.archiveofourown.org/chapters/123?some_params=something]) in the abuse form’s “Link to the page you are reporting” field. 

It’s annoying for Policy & Abuse not to have the work IDs handy.

So when a user does this, before we run {{before_validation :clean_url, on: :create}} and {{validate :url_is_not_over_reported}}, we'd like to:

* look up which work the chapter belongs to
* add the work information to the URL
* assuming the chapter and work can be found, run the usual before_validation and validation checks
* if the chapter or work cannot be found, don’t modify the URL and don’t error, just send the report on through with the URL as entered

Having the “complementary” role means that chapters in Reader View never contain their chapter titles as the titles. Currently the chapter in Reader View starts with the fixed string "Chapter Text". It should instead be the same as the normal text: "Chapter : ".

The role should be removed to make sure the following sometimes appears in Reader View:

* Work: title, summary, notes, endnotes
* Chapter: title, summary, notes, endnotes

On a multichapter work with end notes and a summary, and a final chapter with end notes, access the final chapter. View the page source and search for {{role="complementary"}}. It should not appear.

Summary: Work in anonymous collection does not generate subscription notifications to someone also subscribed to the creator

Creator: Nary
Description:
Users can subscribe to a work in an anonymous collection and should receive notifications when it updates.  However, if any of those users are also subscribed to the creator of the anonymous work, they won’t get a notification when that work updates.

To replicate:

# While logged in as User A, subscribe to User B’s entire profile (by going to their dashboard and selecting ‘Subscribe’ there)
# While logged in as User B, post a new work in an anonymous collection.  (User A should not receive a notification at this point, since that could de-anon your work.)
# While logged in as User A, subscribe to that anonymous work (by going to the work itself and selecting ‘Subscribe’ there).
# While logged in as User B, post a new chapter to your anonymous work.  

What should happen: User A should receive a subscription notification like anyone else subscribed to the anonymous work.  The subscription notification should inform them that Anonymous has posted a new chapter of Work Title (not de-anoning the author).

Summary: Set User.current_user in an around_action hook, so that it's cleared more consistently in tests
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
When a request by a logged-in user is processed, {{User.current_user}} is set at the beginning of the request, but never cleared afterwards. This is fine in most cases, because when the next request comes in, {{User.current_user}} will be set again, overwriting the previous value.

However, in features and in request specs, where requests are sometimes interleaved with e.g. calls to {{FactoryBot.create(:work)}}, this can cause errors, because all of the actions performed after the end of the request are treated as though they were being performed by the user who made the previous request. This can result in errors like, “x does not allow others to invite them to be a co-creator,” when trying to create a work with a single creator.

To prevent these errors from affecting the tests, most of the feature steps that call {{FactoryBot.create(:work)}} also include an {{I start a new session}} step to make sure that {{User.current_user}} is cleared, and the N+1 comments request spec explicitly calls {{User.current_user = nil}}.

Let’s set {{User.current_user}} in an {{around_action}} hook, setting it before the request and clearing it after the request is complete, so that calling {{User.current_user}} is more accurate in tests.

h1. Testing Instructions

This shouldn’t change the functionality at all, but we should make sure that the following things still work:
