Summary: Try to fix deadlock issues with the readings:to_database task
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
The rake task {{readings:to_database}} is currently broken. The original cause of the issue appears to be the {{ActiveRecord::Deadlocked}} error, which may have been caused either by (a) conflicts between two machines running the task at the same time, or (b) conflicts between a single copy of the task, and a user deleting their account (and thus all of the readings associated with that account).

As a result of this recurring error, the task was unable to finish processing the {{Reading:new}} Redis set, which ended up growing more and more until it became so large that calling {{smembers}} to retrieve the set and process its contents produces a timeout error. (This also means that while the {{smembers}} query is running, no other processes can access {{REDIS_GENERAL}}, leading to 500 errors from Redis timeouts.)

We’d like to do the following to try to address this:

# Use {{sscan}} instead of {{smembers}} to access the {{Reading:new}} set, so that we can actually process all 27+ million (and growing) readings currently stored on Redis.
# Move most of the code in {{readings:to_database}} into an {{ActiveJob}} with {{retry_on ActiveRecord::Deadlocked}}, so that it can automatically retry on deadlock.
# Try sorting the batches in the readings code so that they’re processed in a consistent order, avoiding deadlocks when the task is being run on multiple machines at once.
# Try to tweak the {{readings}} association on users so that it doesn’t conflict with the readings code. (Maybe {{dependent: :delete_all}} instead of {{dependent: :destroy}}, to try to make deletion faster and leave less time for conflicts? Or maybe a custom callback that changes the order they’re destroyed in?)

h1. Testing Instructions

These bugs only occur at _very_ large scales, so there’s no real way to replicate them on staging. It’s enough to make sure that the history code still works:

# Log in as a user with history enabled.
# View a work that you’ve never viewed before.
# Wait until it’s 55 minutes after the hour, then wait another few minutes to let the task run.
# Make sure that the work you viewed is listed in your history.

h1. Deploy

The cron job that runs {{rake readings:to_database}} is temporarily disabled on production to avoid timing out other processes relying on the same Redis instance handling readings. It should be re-enabled once the fix is deployed.

Summary: Address LockWaitTimeouts in the readings code
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
The readings code is experiencing occasional lock wait timeout errors (which is particularly a problem now that the readings are so backed up – the jobs tend to overlap a lot). We’d like to switch readings to use a similar system to [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6457|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6457|smart-link] for the batch updates, so that they can be run in parallel, in their own queue so that they can be throttled as needed, and with a retry on {{ActiveRecord::LockWaitTimeout}} and {{ActiveRecord::Deadlocked}} so that if the parallelism becomes a problem they can (try to) recover.

(In the current system, we have a single job that’s trying to process 50+ million readings, to try to catch up to the present. We could retry on {{ActiveRecord::LockWaitTimeout}} in that job, but it’ll be running for days, and with that many transactions, we might run out of retries before the job finishes. If we split it into smaller jobs, we can finish faster, and the number of retries permitted will be proportional to the number of transactions.)

h1. Testing Instructions

As is the case with a lot of issues recently, we can’t really test this at scale, but we should make sure that we haven’t broken things worse.

# Log in as a user with history enabled.
# Visit a work that you’ve never viewed before.
# Wait until a little after :55 to let the readings job run.
# Make sure that the work now appears in your history.

h1. Deploy Notes

This needs a new {{readings}} Resque queue (and workers for said queue).

Since the existing rake will be removed, we need to remove the crontab entry:

{noformat}55 * * * * /bin/bash -l -c 'cd /home/ao3app/app/current && RAILS_ENV=production bundle exec rake readings:to_database  >> /home/ao3app/log/readings:to_database.log 2>&1' > /dev/null 2>&1{noformat}

Once we’re satisfied with the new code and want to catch up on the backlog of readings, we can run the following:

{code:ruby}(1..(REDIS_GENERAL.get("Reading:job_id").to_i + 1)).each do |i|
  RedisSetJobSpawner.perform_later("ReadingsJob", key: "Reading:new:#{i}")
end{code}

This should iterate through all of the various sets of readings that were split off by the previous code, and create a bunch of jobs for each of them.

Summary: Record Fannish Next of Kin changes in user history
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
*Steps to reproduce*

# Log in as an admin with the policy_and_abuse, support, or superadmin role
# Manage Users > Find User
# Search for a user
# Follow the “Details” link for the user
# Enter another user’s username and email in the Fannish Next of Kin fields
# Save
# Change the username and email in the Fannish Next of Kin fields
# Save
# Remove the username and email in the Fannish Next of Kin fields
# Save
# Again in the FNOK fields, enter the username and email of another user, but this time make it one you have access to and don’t mind deleting
# Save
# Leave this tab/window open and in another browser or private window, log in as the user you just entered as the FNOK
# Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Profile > Delete My Account
# Confirm you want to delete your account
# In the tab where you’re logged in as admin, refresh the page and notice that the FNOK field is now blank

*What happens*

Nothing is recorded in the User History table for any of these changes, so we don’t have any records when things get confusing. Instead, we have to spend time puzzling things out.

*What should happen*

We want to log these changes in the User History table, not just for the user who is getting (or losing) a FNOK, but also for the user who is becoming (or ceasing to be) the FNOK. 

We’ll use user IDs so we don’t keep unnecessary records of deleted usernames, and so we don’t get confused in the event someone’s username changes.

Date - Fannish Next of Kin Added: [user ID] - Change made by [admin login]

Date - Added as Fannish Next of Kin for: [user ID] - Change made by [admin login]

Date - Fannish Next of Kin Removed: [user ID] - Change made by [admin login]

Date - Removed as Fannish Next of Kin for: [user ID] - Change made by [admin login]

Date - Fannish Next of Kin Removed: [user ID] - System Generated

If the form is submitted without making changes, nothing should be added to the activities log.

Summary: Allow tag wrangling admins to download CSV of wranglers' last wrangled tags
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
# Log in as an admin with the tag_wrangling or superadmin role
# Go to a user’s wrangling page (https://test.ao3.org/tag_wranglers/USERNAME/)

There should be a button-style “Tags Wrangled (CSV)” link under the “username’s Wrangling Page” heading that allows you to download a CSV of tags that were last wrangled by the user. (You can check the Profile, Subscribe, etc navigation on user show pages to see how the markup should be handled on pages with icons and underlined headings.)

The CSV should be tab-separated and include Tag Name, Date Updated, Tag Type, Merger, Fandoms, Canonical, Unwrangleable. (“Merger” is the tag it is synned to, if any, and “Canonical” and “Unwrangleable” have true or false values.)

You can adapt what we usually do from the console:

{code:ruby}user = User.find_by(login: "username")
wrangled_tags = Tag.where(last_wrangler: user) ; nil
wrangled_tags.each do |tag|
  merger = tag.merger_id? ? tag.merger.name : ''
  fandoms = tag.respond_to?(:fandoms) ? tag.fandoms.map(&:name).join(" + ") : ''
  puts "#{tag.name},#{tag.updated_at},#{tag.type},#{merger},#{fandoms},#{tag.unwrangleable}"
end ; nil{code}

The CSV should _not_ be treated liked downloads and cached on the front ends; it should be generated on demand and only available to authorized admins, like challenge CSVs are only available to the challenge moderators.

The “Tags Wrangled (CSV)” link should not be present if you are not logged in as an authorized admin.

Note: This information is already indexed for [works|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/fcb6a8e6eeec7f5001d31da07d72219d82ee5ded/app/models/work.rb#L1177] and [series|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/fcb6a8e6eeec7f5001d31da07d72219d82ee5ded/app/models/series.rb#L229].

The filters for bookmarks should allow searching, sorting, and filtering by word count:

* The Sort by select menu in the filters (found on pages like https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/TAG_NAME/bookmarks) should have a Word Count option under the two date options.

* The Sort by select menu on the Bookmark Search page (https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search) should also have a Word Count option added under the two date options.
* Above the Work language field on the Bookmark Search page, a Word count field should be added. 

We will not be adding support for the {{words: 100}}, {{words:<1000}}, etc syntax in "Search within results" due to [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5104|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5104|smart-link].

Because some but not all works in a series can be restricted, we need to index two separate word counts, one for logged in users (including restricted works) and one for guests (excluding restricted works), similar to how we would tackle [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6304|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6304|smart-link].

Summary: Remove ApplicationController#set_media, and load the media for the menu only when necessary
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
The {{ApplicationController#set_media}} method performs three database queries, and assigns the results to the variable {{@menu_media}}. The only place the {{@menu_media}} variable is used is here: {code:ruby} <% cache "menu-fandoms-version3", skip_digest: true do %> <% for medium in @menu_media %> <% unless medium.id.nil? %>

(For tidiness, it’d be nice to keep the code out of the view file, but placing it in a helper or in the media model would make sense.) h1. Summary: Add code to allow ES search results to load records with includes()
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:

Both controllers call {{includes()}} in some cases, but they still perform n+1 queries in others, in part because the search code doesn’t have any easy way to call {{includes()}} on the records being returned by the search. Summary: In a challenge where relationships are checkboxes, editing a prompt for A/B/C will automatically check the A/B and B/C checkboxes
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
h1. Steps to Reproduce

# Create a tag set with three relationships: {{A/B/C}}, {{A/B}}, and {{B/C}}.
# Create a prompt meme or gift exchange using that tag set. Set the number of allowed relationships in requests to at least 1, but make sure you don’t check the “Fandom only?” or “Tag set fandom only?” box for relationships — you want them to show up as checkboxes.
# Sign up for the prompt meme/gift exchange requesting only {{A/B/C}}.
# Edit your sign-up.

[This gift exchange|https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/ti_overlapping_tags] is already set up with the required settings, so if you want to see it in action on staging you can skip steps 1 and 2.

h1. What Should Happen

The edit form should have the {{A/B/C}} relationship checked, but not the {{A/B}} or {{B/C}} relationships.

h1. What Actually Happens

In addition to {{A/B/C}}, the {{A/B}} and {{B/C}} boxes are also checked.

h1. Notes

This occurs because the code for checkboxes in tag sets is a little imprecise — basically, to check whether a tag should be checked on the edit form, it looks at the comma-separated list of tags (in this case, just {{A/B/C}}), and checks whether the value of the checkbox is included in that string. Because {{A/B/C}} contains {{A/B/C}}, {{A/B}}, and {{B/C}}, all three checkboxes will be automatically checked whenever {{A/B/C}} is checked.

Note that it doesn’t actually add the tags {{A/B}} and {{B/C}} to the prompt unless you save the prompt without unchecking the checkboxes. But it does mean that every time you want to edit your prompt, you have to remember to uncheck the {{A/B}} and {{B/C}} tags.

You can reproduce this with other tags, as long as the tags are the same type, and at least one of the tags is a substring of the other. For obvious reasons, that’s easiest to do with relationships, but this would also work for fandoms, characters, and freeforms if you pick the right tag names.

Summary: Merge the Bookmarkable module and the BookmarkCountCaching module
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
We have two different systems for caching the number of public bookmarks associated with a work.

The {{Bookmarkable}} module defines {{public_bookmark_count}} for all types of bookmarkable. This cache expires every 2 hours, and whenever the bookmarkable is touched. It’s used in bookmark blurbs (the number in the upper right corner). 

The {{BookmarkCountCaching}} module defines {{public_bookmarks_count}} (note the plural) for just works. This cache never automatically expires, but is manually deleted whenever a bookmark is created, edited, or deleted. It’s used in work blurbs and headers.

We don’t need two different methods of caching the same number. Let’s pick one of the two names, rename all references to the other, and merge the {{BookmarkCountCaching}} module into the {{Bookmarkable}} module. I’m not sure which expiration scheme we want to keep, but combining the two schemes seems doable.

Summary: Try bypassing the cache for CSS classes when the pseuds are already loaded
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
The code for generating the CSS classes for a work uses a cache, resulting in 20 separate memcached gets for all work index pages.

Once pseuds are loaded on all work indexes ([https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6475|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6475|smart-link]), it might be faster to rewrite the {{css_classes_for_creation_blurb}} function to use {{pseuds.pluck(:user_id).uniq}} instead of {{users.pluck(:id).uniq}}, and bypass the cache when the pseuds are loaded (or just skip the cache altogether). Let's try it, preferably in a release without any other performance changes, so that it’s easier to check if it’s an improvement.

h2. Notes

The first pull request for this only changed the database query, without touching the caching. We will decide whether to change the caching based on the performance on production.

Summary: Character & Relationship Tags No Longer Register Properly in Works Autocomplete Post-Fandom Rename
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Dre
Description:
Generally all fandom renames are done via admin these days by synning the old fandom tag to the newly created fandom tag. 

When doing so, sometimes the character & relationship tags do not register properly with the new fandom tag which results in those tags which were moved to the new fandom tag via synning the old fandom tag to the new NOT showing up in the works autocomplete unless we either:

a.) Use the Troubleshooting Options to Fix the Tag Count associated with each individual tag.
b.) Remove and re-add the fandom tag to each tag.

Unfortunately, when this happens, it seems to be an all or nothing deal where if it happens, it happens to every tag in the fandom and it’s recently happened on several very large fandoms which results many Support tickets since big fandoms are often very visible and popular fandoms, it’s also a lot of work to put right from the Tag Wrangler side of things. 

With this bug, we’d be very content with either a fix so that this didn’t happen or a way to handle it reasonably quickly if it does.

* Create New Fandom Canonical Tag
* Syn Old Fandom Canonical Tag to New Fandom Canonical Tag
* Check Work Posting Form to see if Character and/or Relationship tags populate.

    • *

Summary: Notify wrangling supervisors via email when a wrangler changes their username

Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce # If you don’t already have tag wrangling permissions, give them to yourself: ## Log in as an admin with the tag_wrangling or superadmin role ## Manage Users > Find Users ## Use the search options to find an account you have access to (e.g., your account or a testy) ## Check the checkbox in the Tag Wrangler column ## Press Update ## Log out of admin # Log in as the tag wrangler # Change your username ## Hi, username! > My Preferences > Change My User Name ## Fill in and submit the form h1. The wrangler <%= style_bold(old_username) %> has changed their name to <%= style_bold(new_username) %>.

Best,
AO3

Summary: Can't click label to select checkbox on admin skin actions for skins with certain punctuation
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.

Description:
*Setup*

You’ll need an approved site skin with a name containing an exclamation point. You might already have one  like “The Screeny Exposure!” – if you do, you can skip right to steps to reproduce.

# Log in as a user
# Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Skins > Create Site Skin
# Fill in form, using an exclamation point in your skin title, and making sure to check “Apply to make public”
# Submit
# Log in as an admin with the superadmin role
# Skins > Approval Queue
# Locate the skin in the table
# Check the corresponding “Approve” checkbox
# Press “Update”

*Steps to reproduce*

# Log in as an admin with the superadmin role
# Skins > Approved Skins
# Locate the skin in the table
# For one of the actions, e.g., Unapprove, click the word rather than the checkbox

*What should happen*

The checkbox should be selected. (You can try on another skin like Reversi to see the desired behavior.

*What happens*

Nothing, because the label element’s {{for}} attribute (which doesn’t have the exclamation point) doesn't match the checkbox's {{id}} attribute (which does have it):

{noformat}<label class="action" for="make_uncached_the_screeny_exposure_">
Uncache  
  <input type="checkbox" name="make_uncached[]" id="make_uncached_the_screeny_exposure!" value="882">
</label>{noformat}

The exclamation point may not be valid in {{id}} attributes, so it’s probably best to remove it there rather than add it to the {{for}}.

Summary: Store ID of user who creates collection item on the collection item, as well as the time the item's anonymous or unrevealed setting was updated
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Changes

h2. Store ID of user who creates collection item

When a collection item is created, e.g., by a creator adding a work or bookmark to a collection or a maintainer inviting a work, we should store the ID of the user who prompted the item’s creation on the collection item for our own edification.

It should stay as long as the collection item exists (i.e., don’t nil it out if the work creator removes themselves from the work, the collection moderator removes themselves from the collection, or the user deletes their account). 

We can call it {{collector_id}} or {{collection_item_creator_id}} or some such.

h2. Store datetime of the latest change to the collection item’s anonymous and unrevealed setting

Additionally, whenever a collection item’s unrevealed or anonymous setting is changed (e.g., by a mod revealing the entire collection or individual works), the date and time of the change should be recorded in a corresponding {{unrevealed_updated_at}} or {{anonymous_updated_at}} column.

h1. Testing

This information shouldn’t be displayed anywhere for now. Database admins will need to test.

h2. Store ID of user who creates collection item

You’ll need

* an account (User1) that
** you don’t mind deleting
** has a co-owned collection
* a second account (User2) with 
** at least one work and 
** the “Allow others to invite my works to collections” preference enabled

The {{collector_id}} or {{collection_item_creator_id}} on each collection item should list User1’s ID when User1

#  posts a work to their collection
#  edits an existing work to add it to their collection
#  adds a bookmark to their collection when creating the bookmark
#  edits an existing bookmark to add it to their collection
#  uses the “Invite to Collection” option on User2’s work to add it to their collection

The information should remain on those collection items when User1

# removes themselves as a co-owner of their collection
# deletes their account

h2. Store datetime of the latest change to the collection item’s anonymous and unrevealed setting

You’ll need 

* a collection that’s set to both anonymous and unrevealed
* at least one anonymous and unrevealed work in that collection. 

The{{unrevealed_updated_at}} or {{anonymous_updated_at}} column should change when

# the unrevealed box is unchecked on the Manage Items page
# the anonymous box is unchecked on the Manage Items page
# the unrevealed box is checked on the Manage Items page
# the unrevealed box is checked on the Manage Items page
# the “This collection is unrevealed” box is unchecked on the Collection Settings page
# the “This collection is anonymous” box is unchecked on the Collection Settings page

The columns should not change when

# the “This collection is unrevealed” box is checked on the Collection Settings page
# the “This collection is anonymous” box is checked on the Collection Settings page

(these actions do not change a collection item’s unrevealed or anonymous setting)

The “pseud (username) does not accepts gifts” error message should also be shown if User C, who is not blocked, attempts to gift User A a work they co-created with User B.

For now, this should have the same exceptions as having gifts disabled: gifts that are filling a challenge claim or assignment should be allowed (AO3-6257).

* When User A has User B blocked and “Allow anyone to gift me works” enabled
** User B is posting a new work to gift to User A
** User B is editing an existing work to gift to User A
** User B is filling an assignment in a gift exchange for User A
** User B is filling a claim in a prompt meme for User A
** User B is posting or editing a work co-created with User C, who is not blocked, and attempts to gift it to User A
** User C, who is not blocked, is posting or editing a work co-created with User B and attempts to gift it to User A
* When User A has User B blocked and “Allow anyone to gift me works” disabled
** User B is posting a new work to gift to User A

Summary: Use parent aggregations for bookmarks instead of a separate query for aggregations
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
Back when the {{BookmarkQuery}} class was created, there were no parent aggregations in Elasticsearch, so the parent aggregations are filled in by adding an [extra Elasticsearch query|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/ccd24c3697144cc303f17c0e19cc65ff24915a5b/app/models/search/bookmark_query.rb#L24-L34]:

{noformat}# After the initial search, run an additional query to get work/series tag filters
# Elasticsearch doesn't support parent aggregations, and doing the main query on the parents
# limits searching and sorting on the bookmarks themselves
# Hopefully someday they'll fix this and we can get the data from a single query
def search_results
  response = search
  if response['aggregations']
    response['aggregations'].merge!(bookmarkable_query.aggregation_results)
  end
  QueryResult.new(klass, response, options.slice(:page, :per_page))
end{noformat}

But Elasticsearch now has [parent aggregations|https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/8.7/search-aggregations-bucket-parent-aggregation.html]. We should modify the {{BookmarkQuery}} class to use them, so that we can perform a single query instead of two to get the info we need. This may help reduce some of the load on Elasticsearch caused by bookmark queries (though definitely not all of it).

We have already done this for several tasks using the {{RedisSetJob}} class and the {{RedisSetJobSpawner}} class, but the hit counter uses Redis hashes, not Redis sets. So we'd like to modify the {{RedisSetJob}} system to allow it to be adapted for use with Redis hashes.

Summary: Use standard analyzer for creators and bookmarker on bookmark search
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
On work search, the {{creators}} field uses Elasticsearch's [standard analyzer|https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/analysis-standard-analyzer.html], while on bookmark search, we use the [simple analyzer|https://www.elastic.co/guide/en/elasticsearch/reference/current/analysis-simple-analyzer.html] for both the {{bookmarker}} and {{creators}} fields.

This means that in the bookmark search form, no matter if one

* searches "bookmarker: testy" in the "Any field on bookmark",
* or searches "testy" in the "Bookmarker" field

the results are essentially for {{*testy*}}, [returning also bookmarks from testy5, testy7, etc|https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search?bookmark_search%5Bbookmarkable_query%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bother_tag_names%5D=Testing&bookmark_search%5Bbookmarkable_type%5D=&bookmark_search%5Blanguage_id%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bbookmarkable_date%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bbookmark_query%5D=bookmarker%3Atesty&bookmark_search%5Bother_bookmark_tag_names%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bbookmarker%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bbookmark_notes%5D=&bookmark_search%5Brec%5D=0&bookmark_search%5Bwith_notes%5D=0&bookmark_search%5Bdate%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bsort_column%5D=&commit=Search+Bookmarks]. The same thing happens when [searching "creators: testy" on the Bookmark Search|https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search?bookmark_search%5Bbookmarkable_query%5D=creators%3Atesty&bookmark_search%5Bother_tag_names%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bbookmarkable_type%5D=&bookmark_search%5Blanguage_id%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bbookmarkable_date%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bbookmark_query%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bother_bookmark_tag_names%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bbookmarker%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bbookmark_notes%5D=&bookmark_search%5Brec%5D=0&bookmark_search%5Bwith_notes%5D=0&bookmark_search%5Bdate%5D=&bookmark_search%5Bsort_column%5D=&commit=Search+Bookmarks] (but [not in the Work Search|https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/search?commit=Search&work_search%5Bquery%5D=creators%3Atesty&work_search%5Btitle%5D=&work_search%5Bcreators%5D=&work_search%5Brevised_at%5D=&work_search%5Bcomplete%5D=&work_search%5Bcrossover%5D=&work_search%5Bsingle_chapter%5D=0&work_search%5Bword_count%5D=&work_search%5Blanguage_id%5D=&work_search%5Bfandom_names%5D=&work_search%5Brating_ids%5D=&work_search%5Bcharacter_names%5D=&work_search%5Brelationship_names%5D=&work_search%5Bfreeform_names%5D=&work_search%5Bhits%5D=&work_search%5Bkudos_count%5D=&work_search%5Bcomments_count%5D=&work_search%5Bbookmarks_count%5D=&work_search%5Bsort_column%5D=_score&work_search%5Bsort_direction%5D=desc]).

To make the behavior more consistent between the two forms, we’d like to use the standard analyzer for bookmark search’s {{bookmarker}} and {{creators}} fields.

We need to reindex before we move to Elasticsearch 8 (AO3-6259), so this should be done in the same release.

Summary: Co-creator error message reveals when users are banned or suspended
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.

Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce

You’ll need two accounts and and an admin account with the policy_and_abuse or superadmin role. On staging, you can test using testy_suspended and testy_banned. 

# Ban or suspend a user
## Log in as admin
## Manage Users > Find Users 
## In “Name,” enter the name of the user you want to ban or suspend
## Find
## Follow the “Details” link
## Under “Warnings and suspensions,” choose the desired option to ban or suspend
## Fill in “Notes”
## Update
## Log out
# Post a co-created work as the user who is not banned/suspended
## Log in
## Post > New Work
## Fill in required info
## Check “Add co-creators?”
## Enter the name of the banned/suspended user
## Post

h1. What happens

You get an error:

{quote}Invalid creator: testy_banned is currently banned and cannot be listed as a co-creator. {quote}

If they don’t have their preferences set to allow co-creators, it has two messages

{quote}Invalid creator: testy_suspended does not allow others to invite them to be a co-creator.
Invalid creator: testy_suspended is currently banned and cannot be listed as a co-creator.{quote}

h1. What should happen

I've pushed a fix for the staging error. The issue was that some orphaned comments have {{nil}} values for{{threaded_left}}/{{threaded_right}}, which causes two problems:

# {{sort_by!}} crash — comparing {{nil}} with an integer raises {{ArgumentError: comparison of NilClass with 2 failed}} (the error you saw on staging).

# The thread value is clearly bogus. The commentable and the parent (the chapter) is deleted. ## My conclusion for what happened there: The comments weren’t deleted when the work they were on was deleted. ## My fix for these comments: Delete them. The parent they were meant to be on is gone anyway, ergo they should be gone (deleting a parent deletes its comments). There would be no correct place to put them because the comment the thread value points to was always clearly the wrong place.
# The thread value is not clearly bogus (the comment it points to is deleted, so I don’t know enough to come to a conclusion). The commentable and the parent is deleted. These don’t cause issues with unrelated works, they only error on CommentsController#show.

## My fix for these comments: Do nothing. They could be deleted since there is no reason for them to exist when the parent is gone, but it didn’t seem worth my time to fix these when they only affect comments on works that are already gone, so you’re less likely to come across them naturally.

* follow the Delete Work link to delete your work
* follow the Orphan Work link to orphan your work
* if the work is co-created, follow the Remove Me As Co-Creator link to remove yourself from the work

Or for your chapter, you should be able to access the edit page and then:

* follow the Delete Chapter link to delete your chapter
* if the chapter is co-created, follow the Remove Me As Chapter Co-Creator link to remove yourself from the chapter

* Post or Preview changes to your work or chapter

Summary: Include user_role and comment_type in data sent to Akismet
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
We don’t include {{comment_type: "contact-form"}} in the support ticket data we send to the spam checker, which means it gets mixed in with comment data.

Let’s add it to the [akismet_attributes|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/754e816d0e1730d51dada5c6650cdc4db00717f2/app/models/feedback.rb#L25-L34] for support tickets, like we have it [in abuse reports|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/754e816d0e1730d51dada5c6650cdc4db00717f2/app/models/abuse_report.rb#L30].

redsummernight also suggested adding a {{comment_type}} to the comments we check. Let’s use {{comment}} for admin post comments (because Akismet assumes {{comment}} means “blog post comment,” and an admin post is pretty similar to a blog post) and {{fanwork-comment}} for comments on works.

The Akismet team also wouldn’t mind having {{user_role}} data:

* works should have {{user_role: "user"}}
* comments should have {{user_role: "guest"}} 
* abuse and support tickets should have {{user_role: "guest"}} for guest and {{user_role: "user-with-nonmatching-email"}} for logged-in users with emails that don't match their account emails.

*Testing*

Make sure you can submit both support and abuse ticket as a guest and a logged-in user with an email that doesn’t match the one associated with your account, post a work, and leave comments on both works and admin posts as a guest.

Summary: Error 500 for long CSS entries in skin editor
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Former user
Description:
*Steps to reproduce* 

# Log in
# Go to the skin editor, creating a site or work skin. 
# Enter CSS in the CSS field that is more than 65 000 characters
# Enter a name
# Submit the form
# Get an Error 500

*What should happen*

* I should be redirected to the page with an error message saying that the CSS is too long. 
* It would be helpful to have JavaScript validation to stop the user from hitting beyond 60 000 characters (This is to account for created spaces from sanitization)

*Notes from AD&T*

* There actually is a a limit to how many characters skins can have in the code (500k, or ArchiveConfig.CONTENT_MAX) that should give an error when your skin hits that length... but I guess the 500 error is probably happening because the CSS sanitizer just can't handle something that long?
* We'll need a buffer between the displayed limit and the real limit, because the sanitizer can add spaces (maybe make the displayed limit 60k and the real one 65k?) so if you're taking them out to make room because you're almost at the limit... yeah, it's just going to add them back and you'll hit the limit anyway
* We might need a news post or something to make sure people whose skins are too long (i.e., because the sanitizer didn't always error at this specific length, or because they're in the no man's land between the new limit we set to keep people from running into the 500 error and the number that actually causes the 500 error) don't lose part of their skin the next time they try to save
* The ideal fix would be to find the cause of the 500 error, keep the ArchiveConfig.CONTENT_MAX limit instead of lowering it, and add a display counter (with a buffer, like we do works, so actually CONTENT_MAX: 510000 and CONTENT_MAX_DISPLAYED: 500000)

Summary: "Log In" link in header doesn't have required ARIA role
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: alien
Description:
The  {{p}} with the Log In link has an ARIA role of {{menu}}. This role requires that its children have the role {{menuitem}}, so screen readers know how to interpret the structure of the HTML. ([https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.1/#menu|https://www.w3.org/TR/wai-aria-1.1/#menu|smart-link] )

However, the link that is the direct child of the paragraph doesn’t have any roles.

Suggested solution: add the role {{menuitem}} to the Log In link.

How to test:

* Manually: use a screen reader to visit the Archive while not logged in. Check that the Log In menu is announced correctly.
* Automatically: I use the axe tools plugin (free). Install the plugin, open Developer Tools, use axe tools to scan the page for issues. There should be no issue affecting the login link element.

Summary: The list of media on the homepage doesn't have required ARIA role
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: alien
Description:
Visit the home page while logged out, or logged in if you don’t have any favorite tags, so you get the list of media under the “Find your favorites” heading.

Scan the page with an automated accessibility tool like axe DevTools.

axe DevTools reports a “critical” issue, which is that the list with the role {{menu}} doesn’t have required children.

Elements with the role {{menu}} must have direct children with the role {{menuitem}}. (Or a few other roles like {{menuitemcheckbox}}, but I’m only giving the one relevant to this menu.)

The {{li}} elements don’t have a role.

However, Sarken rightly pointed out that the list shouldn’t be a menu in the first place, but a navigation.

Let’s change it into a navigation - but if we just replace the role on the {{ul}}, we’ll have a similar ARIA role mismatch issue, where it will complain that the {{li}}s don’t have an appropriate parent.

The solution seems to be to have a container {{div}} around the {{ul}}, and apply the navigation role to the container. The {{ul}} and its children shouldn’t have a role declaration.

How to test:

* with a screenreader, presumably that the navigation is announced properly and it makes sense
* with an a11y tool checker, that it doesn’t report any brokenness

Other concerns:

* does this change impact any site skins?

Has CSS changes.

Summary: Remove the fetch_admin_settings hook, and change code that uses @admin_settings to use AdminSetting.current instead
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
The {{fetch_admin_settings}} hook is [skipped|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/ba94c04580de2bac4c7a932e33a11fad4de7e06d/app/controllers/application_controller.rb#L523-L528] for JS and JSON requests. However, occasionally there are JS or JSON requests for pages that don’t have a JS or JSON view, like the homepage. This results in an error where the views are expecting the admin {{@admin_settings}} variable to set, when it’s not. This produces a 500 error.

This can be addressed by switching over to using {{AdminSetting.current}} instead of {{@admin_settings}} everywhere. This won’t actually prevent the mismatches, in cases where e.g. a JS action should be returning an error instead of redirecting to an HTML version of the homepage, but it’s nice to reduce 500 errors.

Note that, in cases where {{@admin_settings}} is accessed multiple times in quick succession, this won’t result in multiple memcached reads, because Rails' {{MemCacheStore}} maintains a [local cache|https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActiveSupport/Cache/Strategy/LocalCache.html] when performing a single request.

Summary: Define the translate_string function using % instead of I18n.translate
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
Currently, the {{translate_string}} function is defined as follows:

{code:ruby}    def translate_string(str, **options)
      translate(str, **options.merge(default: str))

Summary: Enable Admins to Mark Canonical Tags So They Appear in the Filtering Autocomplete but NOT the Work Form Autocomplete
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Dre
Description:
While some metatags are useful for filtering in tag search, their usefulness is limited specifically because their appearance in the work form autocomplete causes an increase in ambiguity issues. As such, we were wondering whether it would be possible to create a field on the tag edit page which allowed tag wrangling admins to mark a tag so it would not appear in the work form autocomplete whilst still appearing in the filtering autocomplete?

Summary: Give admins options when hiding works
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. *Overview* This issue is the first in a series of updates designed to streamline the Policy & Abuse team's processes, link admin records with Zoho tickets, declutter the user admin page, and remove access to user account status options from admin roles that don't need them. To lay the groundwork for these updates, a separate "Policy & Abuse: Action Users" form should be created that allows PAC admins to take action against a user's account and hide any works that need to be hidden simultaneously. This is complicated by three factors:  # Users may have multiple works that need to be hidden; 10+ is not unusual, and some users may need dozens hidden # Some of the works may have co-creators, who may also have additional violating works separate from the first creator # When there are multiple users being actioned, those users may have differing histories and so receive differing penalties  To accommodate this, a two-page action process is needed to allow the actioning of multiple works and users at once: # The "Policy & Abuse: Mass Action Setup" page (henceforth in this issue referred to as just the "Mass Action Setup" page), which is a form where the admin enters a list of works to be hidden and/or a list of account names that they are actioning # The "Policy & Abuse: Action Users" page (henceforth in this issue referred to as just the "Action Users" page), which is a form (created by the input into the Mass Action Setup form) where the admin specifies the individual actions applied to each account, the individual reasons for each user to be actioned, and confirms the list of all works to be hidden. The accounts displayed on this form are determined by what was entered on the Mass Action Setup form.  The Mass Action Setup form should be accessible from the admin navigation bar, as a new option on the "Manage Users" menu. This navigation option, the Mass Action Setup page, and the Action Users page should only be accessible to admins with the {{policy_and_abuse}} or {{superadmin}} roles.  h1. Mass Action Setup page Example mockup of the Mass Action Setup page:  !AD_4nXc9ReZWhz7eFCDSUxhUNXW-z7WUTncbtgjLGy5UommfTo1s9HyoVU70Wk7uey8dFI2eXtxFw9CBnmGyGPIqSBqlFj_OnaHCE6C0iys-YYQ0GRKp-HSWD08E1LhlcSy3iDL4-YcvxQ_key=XPh-Ir_561mY6U5syTSOv5wb|width=875,height=661! The Mass Action Setup form should have two entry fields:  # Works to hide: allows the admin to enter the work URLs for those works to be hidden, as a text list separated by line breaks. Locating the work ID on each line should key off of {{/works/00000}}, where 00000 is the work ID. Lines may include extraneous other text on the same line (such as whitespace, title or author), which should be ignored –  the important info is the work ID. E.g.: [+https://archiveofourown.org/works/1234567+|https://archiveofourown.org/works/1234567] [+https://archiveofourown.org/works/9876543/+|https://archiveofourown.org/works/9876543/]  "Example work title", located at [+https://archiveofourown.org/works/1234567+ |https://archiveofourown.org/works/1234567/] "Example work title", located at [+https://archiveofourown.org/works/1234567/chapters/987654321/+|https://archiveofourown.org/works/1234567/chapters/987654321/]  # Users to action: allows the admin to enter usernames of users to action, as a text list separated by line breaks. Whitespace on either side of an entered username should be ignored. When the admin clicks the "Proceed to Action Users form" button, the form should:  # Validate works:  #* For each line, locate the work ID on the line, ignoring any irrelevant text #* Ignore any empty lines  #* Verify that each work in the "Works to hide" field is an existing work or draft on AO3  #* Check that each work is not already hidden #* Remove any duplicate entries #* If there is an invalid URL, the submission should fail and an error message should be provided stating that there is an invalid work entry and what it is # Validate additional users:  #* For each line, remove any whitespace around the username  #* Ignore any empty lines #* Verify that each username listed is a user on AO3 #* If there is an invalid username, the submission should fail and an error message should be provided stating that there is an invalid username and what it is # Generate a list of "users to action", consisting of:  #* Each user who is a creator on one or more of the works in the validated "Works to Hide" list (excluding the orphan_account), AND #* Any accounts listed in the validated "Users without works to hide" list, even if they're not a creator on one of the listed works  # Remove any duplicate entries from the "users to action" list (whether from being listed twice in the "Additional users" list, or appearing in both the "works to hide" and "additional users" lists, etc)  # Remove the orphan_account from the "users to action" list, if present # Create the "Action Users" form with the validated "Works to hide" list as the works list, and a user subsection for each user on the "user to action" list  If both the "Works to hide" and "Users to action" fields are blank, then the submission should fail with an error message saying that at least one valid work or user must be listed to proceed.  Please consider- In future issues, this tool may be expanded from hiding works only to also being able to hide series and bookmarks. However, for now the scope is works only.  Rough HTML for the Mass Action Setup page for ease of reference; please note that labels and inputs are not properly associated here: {noformat}

Policy & Abuse: Mass Action Setup

All works and users being actioned must belong to the same ticket.

Works to hide

List the full URLs of all works you wish to hide, separated by line breaks.

Users to action

List the current usernames (not pseuds) of users you wish to action, separated by line breaks. You don't need to list the creators of the works you are hiding, as they will be included automatically.

{noformat} h1. Action Users page An example of the page when multiple works, one of which has multiple creators, have been added to the form to be hidden: !AD_4nXccxSthK24iH1-z-szQ7kDx-IaLo6SrsIfVyEhpZIXuS2LnJX1rnOj-szP5aeCbXYgCIeHp2tErkmd5lYqaSkmbXfW4wPMyNGq2YWSv56yagWoCAAmdc5D5CpSznNIXk_7pKyQa_key=XPh-Ir_561mY6U5syTSOv5wb|width=952,height=1207! On this page the admin can perform a variety of actions: # Enter the ID of a ticket with the initial complaint to confirm hiding the work(s) or taking action against the account(s), the same way admins enter ticket IDs to confirm profile edits # For each account, record a note, warning, or suspension on the user's account, along with a reason.  The Ticket ID (of the original complaint), action (for each user), and reason (for each user) are required fields. If any of these is empty, then it should not be possible to submit the form with the "Preview emails" or "Take action and hide work(s)" buttons; instead, attempting to do so should fail and a red error message should pop up beside each unfilled field reminding the admin that it is a required field. The Ticket ID should be validated upon form submission (by either the "Preview emails" button or the "Take action and hide work(s)" button), in the same manner that ticket IDs are validated for profile edits. If it fails, then the submission should fail and an error message should appear at the top of the form, using the same set of error messages as for failed ticket IDs for profile edits. Each work on the "Work(s) to be hidden" list should display on its own line as: {quote}*TITLE* by UserA, UserB, UserC{quote} where *TITLE* is a link to the work. Creators should be listed with usernames only, not in the "pseud (username)" format. No method is provided (in this stage) to add or remove a work from the form; if that is necessary the admin would need to start over with the Mass Action Setup form. The order of the works listed should match to the order the works were entered on the Mass Action Setup page. If the orphan_account is listed as a creator on the work then they should be listed in this byline, even though they should not have their own user subsection below on the form.  If all of the works to be hidden are orphaned, then only the Hide Works section will display and there will be no User sections below it. Each user subsection should be titled "User: Username (userID)" where the username is a link leading to that user's admin page (that is, [+https://archiveofourown.org/admin/users/username+|https://archiveofourown.org/admin/users/username]).  The "Action on User" options should be present with the same logic that the current User Admin page has for "Warnings and Suspensions": * If a user is temporarily suspended, then the option to temporarily suspend becomes "Lift temporary suspension, effective immediately." * If a user is permanently suspended, then the option to suspend the user permanently becomes "Lift permanent suspension, effective immediately." and the option to temporarily suspend them is disabled * If a user is first temporarily suspended and then permanently suspended, then it should be possible to lift either suspension state without affecting the other  * Unlike the current User Admin page, there should _not_ be a spamban option Unlike the "Notes" box on the User Admin page, the "Reason for actioning user" should be a text input, one line high, not a textarea.  Form validation upon submitting via either the "Preview emails" or "Take action and hide work(s)" buttons should include:  * Re-validating the works list:  ** If a work URL is no longer for a valid work or draft (because it has been deleted or expired in the time since the list was generated), then the submission should fail with an error message identifying that "Work 000 does not exist" (where 000 is the work ID). The admin will need to manually return to the Mass Action Setup page to change the work list – they should not be automatically redirected from the Action Users page. ** If a work URL is for a work that is already hidden, then the submission should fail with an error message identifying that "Work 000 is already hidden". The admin will need to return to the Mass Action Setup page to change the work list. * Re-validating the users list:  ** If a user has deleted their account, then the submission should fail with an error message that "User ID USERID no longer exists". The admin will need to return to the Mass Action Setup page to recreate the users list.  ** If a user has changed their username, then the submission should fail with an error message that "User OLDNAME (USERID) has updated their username to NEWNAME. The form has been updated." The user subsection for that user should update and change the username to match the new name. All of the information the admin has entered on the Action Users form should be retained on the updated form. ** Because users can rename or delete their accounts between the submission of the Mass Action Setup form and the Action Users form, the Action Users form's setup should track users by (and validation should occur based on) their userID, not their username or a pseud. The "Preview emails" page should validate the form information and then provide a single-page preview with the works list at the top (formatted in the same way it is on the Action Users form), and then the actions, reasons, and emails for each user.  This is a "dumb" previews page only – there should not be any way to edit anything from here; the user only has the option to submit. However, if the admin back-buttons in their browser then they should be taken back to the filled-out Action Users form, and once there they should be able to edit if needed and then resubmit, rather than starting over entirely from the beginning.  Each user subsection on the Preview Emails page should be titled the same way it is on the Action Users form, as "User: Username (userID)". The username should be a hyperlink to the user's admin page.  Example:  {quote}*User:* [+*Testy*+|https://archiveofourown.org/admin/users/testy] *(6477)* 30-day suspension NFW (discord ad) [Email preview]{quote} The email preview should be for the body of the email only. It should not include any header information, subject line, to/from, etc.  The descriptions for each type of action available on the form should be:  Noted Warned X-day suspension Temporary suspension lifted Permanent suspension Permanent suspension lifted At the bottom of the preview page, there should be the option to return to the Action Users page to edit, or to "Take action and hide work(s)". When the emails are generated, they will include the list of works specific to that user. For example, if the "Works being hidden" list is as follows:  {quote}*TITLE1* by UserA *TITLE2* by UserA, UserB{quote} then UserA's email notification will list both TITLE1 and TITLE2, but UserB's email notification will only list TITLE2.  The order of the works listed in the email should match to the order the works were entered on the Mass Action Setup page. If a user does not have any works to be hidden, then they will not receive an email. They should still have a section on the preview page, which should contain a note saying they will not receive an email. For example:  {quote}*User:* [+*Testy*+|https://archiveofourown.org/admin/users/testy] *(6477)* 30-day suspension NFW (discord ad), user orphaned No email {quote} If all of the works to be hidden are orphaned, then there should be no emails or user sections on the Preview Emails page, but it should still display the works list. All of the validations performed if the "Take action and hide work(s)" button was used on the "Action Users" page should also be performed if "Take action and hide work(s)" is used from the Preview Emails page. If the validations fail, then the admin should be returned to the "Action Users" form, with the form still filled-out, and with appropriate error messages displaying to indicate what failed. Successfully submitting with the "Take action and hide work(s)" button (whether from the Preview Emails page or directly from the Action Users form) will:  # apply the appropriate action(s) to the user account(s),  # record the note(s), warning(s), and suspension(s) in the user history, # hide the work(s),  # log the admin activities,  # send the appropriate email(s), and # take the admin to the Mass Action Setup page, with the form cleared, and a blue success banner at the top saying "Policy & Abuse enforcement action successfully taken". If the process fails midway, then it should not proceed with the remaining actions. Instead, it should go to the Action Users page (with all of the fields still filled out) and put up an error banner at the top stating that the process failed midway. The admin will then need to investigate to see what failed before trying again.  If the admin closes the Mass Action Setup form, the Action Users form, or the Preview Emails page without submitting (e.g. by closing the tab), then it should act the same as if there was a "Cancel" button on these pages – nothing should be changed on any user accounts or works, nothing logged, and the data entered should be discarded. Future updates in this series of issues will allow PAC to use the Action Users page to update the works to hide list, specify different types of pre-generated emails, as well as send custom messages (similar to comment notification emails). Please ensure that the design for this issue will not cause difficulties for this future expansion.  Rough HTML for the Action Users page for ease of reference; please note that labels and inputs are not properly associated here: {noformat}

Summary: Optimize the database query for the series count in the user sidebar
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: ticking instant
Description:
Currently, there are a couple of problems with [the series count in the user sidebar|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/0f30207d6dfe9050d38398522339f1a0d754c58c/app/helpers/users_helper.rb#L82-L100]:

# It calls {{length}} to compute the number of series. This results in all series owned by that user being loaded, which can take a long time for users like the {{orphan_account}}. The reason it does this is because the {{exclude_anonymous}} scope is rather complex, with a join on the works table and a group, so calling {{count}} returns a hash instead of a number. But you can call {{count.size}} instead of {{length}} to get the true number.
# The scope that it uses, {{for_pseuds(user.pseuds)}}, means that the SQL query includes a list of all of the user’s pseud IDs. This is fine for most users, but not great for {{orphan_account}}, with its 10,000+ pseuds. It would probably be better to do a join on the pseuds table.

Let’s try to fix this, so that viewing {{orphan_account}}’s various pages is a little easier on the database.

Summary: Switch to reviewdog for running rubocop
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Brian Austin
Description:
Hound, our current tool, is several versions of rubocop out-of-date, and also does not support custom cops (which would be useful for catching common issues like needing to use {{departure}} for large tables). We already use reviewdog for running ERB lint, so let’s use that for running rubocop as well.

Here’s a draft of what the new Github action workflow could look like:

{code:yaml}  rubocop:
    name: Rubocop
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - name: Check out code
        uses: actions/checkout@v3

      - name: Set up Ruby and run bundle install
        uses: ruby/setup-ruby@v1
        with:
          bundler-cache: true

      - name: rubocop
        uses: reviewdog/action-rubocop@e70b014b8062c447d6b515ee0209f834ea93e696
        with:
          use_bundler: true
          reporter: github-pr-check
          rubocop_version: gemfile
          rubocop_extensions: rubocop-rails:gemfile rubocop-rspec:gemfile{code}

h1. Testing Instructions

After this is merged, update an existing PR (or create a new one). Ideally this would be one that has known Rubocop violations, but that shouldn’t be required.

h1. Post-Merge Actions

A senior AD&T member will need to do the following once this is merged:

# -Go into the Hound console and disable/remove the otwarchive project. This will avoid duplicate checks, and errors when we upgrade rubocop or introduce custom cops.- (This won’t be done until we migrate JS linting away also.)
# Authorize the {{reviewdog/action-rubocop@e70b014b8062c447d6b515ee0209f834ea93e696}} action via the Github repo’s settings. (Refer to the linked issue for details.)

Summary: Allow users to resend invitations
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description: h1. Description Users frequently submit support requests because they have accidentally deleted or not received their invitations. Therefore, we’d like to allow users to resend their invitations without submitting a support ticket. (In the case of missing emails, it’s fairly likely the resent email will continue to be eaten by spam filters, but it’s possible some will get through.) Summary: Upgrade to Rails 7
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Brian Austin
Description:
Let’s upgrade to Rails 7! (It feels like we just did a Rails upgrade 😆 ). From the release notes, some significant changes are:

* {{ActionView::Helpers::UrlHelper#button_to}} has been changed to use {{PATCH}} by default when passed an already-persisted object
* [Spring|https://github.com/rails/spring] is off by default
* Sprockets is now an _optional_ dependency (so if we need it, the gem needs to be specified explicitly in the Gemfile)
* Applications can now only run in {{zeitwerk}} mode (this should be fine since we switched as part of the Rails 6 upgrade)
* {{config.autoloader=}} has been deleted
* {{ActiveSupport::Dependencies}} private API has been deleted
* Autoloading during initialization is now an error, in contrast to being a deprecation warning in Rails 6.1
* {{ActionDispatch::Request#content_type}} now returns Content-Type header as it is.
* Key generator digest class changing to use SHA256
* Digest class for ActiveSupport::Digest changing to SHA256
* There is a new ActiveSupport::Cache serialization format
* Active Storage video preview image generation (requires ffmpeg v3.4+)
* Active Storage default variant processor changed to :vips

Of the above, the autoloading change definitely needs action before the upgrade. And as part of the upgrade, we should add code to convert legacy SHA1 things to SHA256 (there is an example in the upgrade guide). Requirements to upgrade, in broad strokes, are described in [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/upgrading_ruby_on_rails.html#upgrading-from-rails-6-1-to-rails-7-0|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/upgrading_ruby_on_rails.html#upgrading-from-rails-6-1-to-rails-7-0|smart-link] .

We also get some new features, which are described in [https://rubyonrails.org/2021/12/15/Rails-7-fulfilling-a-vision|https://rubyonrails.org/2021/12/15/Rails-7-fulfilling-a-vision|smart-link] .

Summary: Avoid autoloading constants deprecation warning

Description:
In Rails 6, autoloading constants during initialization outside configuration blocks is deprecated and logs a warning at application boot. This will become an error in Rails 7 ([https://guides.rubyonrails.org/upgrading_ruby_on_rails.html#autoloading-during-initialization|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/upgrading_ruby_on_rails.html#autoloading-during-initialization|smart-link] ), so we need to fix the warning before we can upgrade.

Summary: Kindle EPUB Table of Contents sometimes greyed out
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Find and access a multi-chapter work
# Download the EPUB
# Send it to your Kindle device via email (it’s unclear if this issue occurs on the app)
# Open it

h1. What happens

The built-in ToC only shows the preface and a greyed out Table of Contents, but not the actual list of chapters.

h1. What should happen

The built-in ToC should work!

h1. Notes

Some folks suggested that downloading the mobi and converting it to EPUB with Zamzar works just fine, so I took a look at the resulting file and did some thinking out loud in a Slack channel with Support chairs: 

----

The file from that site that reportedly works: {{<meta content="calibre (4.13.0)" name="dtb:generator"/>}}

The file from us: {{<meta name="dtb:generator" content="calibre (5.12.0)"/>}}

So if we're optimistic, _maybe_ it's a bug with our version. If we're pessimistic, newer versions of Calibre might just produce incompatible tables of content

I'm comparing the guts of the two files and the most notable differences to me are -- actually, let me back up and give some background. EPUBs are basically containers. Each chapter is a separate file inside the container, and you have a file for the TOC, and any images and stysheets and stuff. They're not special files, really -- the image is a JPG or whatever, the stylesheets are CSS, etc.

Now, the two big things I'm noticing are Zamzar's EPUB, converted from our MOBI files using calibre 4.13, uses .html extensions for the chapters, and the chapter names are like {{index_split_001.html}}.

_But_ the EPUB file straight from the Archive has .xhtml chapters, and the chapter names match the download file name. So my chapters are {{The Devils Right There_split_001.xhtml}} .

I wonder if Kindle chokes when it encounters the encoded spaces in the TOC

{noformat}    <navPoint id="uR7o4lGb4J2CSJToHLQAhNF" playOrder="2">
      <navLabel>
        <text>truth is like blood underneath your fingernails</text>
      </navLabel>
      <content src="The%20Devils%20Right%20There_split_002.xhtml"/>
    </navPoint>{noformat}

We could test that theory by having someone with a Kindle download the epub of a multichapter work with a one-word title and see if it worked

Looking a little more and the manifest seems to use actual spaces, e.g., {{<item id="html4" href="The Devils Right There_split_029.xhtml" media-type="application/xhtml+xml"/>}}, while the TOC uses the encoded {{%20}}, so I'm increasingly willing to bet that's the issue

----

Brian tested my theory and confirmed: epubs with one-word titles work, while those with multi-word titles produce the broken ToC.

So we should be able to fix this by stripping spaces from the file names.

However! That makes them hard to read, especially when each word doesn’t start with a capital letter and result in lovely camel casing. So let’s replace the spaces with underscores instead, since we know it can handle them as well.

h1. Testing instructions

Please try downloading EPUBs of works with and without spaces in their titles and making sure they work when sent to Kindle! 

It wouldn’t hurt to try the Kindle app as well.

With any device, and in any download format, please also try downloading works with:

* titles in non-Latin scripts, and confirming they are transliterated and the words are separated with underscores in the filename (note that we do not have control over _how_ they are transliterated)
* titles containing only emoji, and confirming the filename is {{Work_##.extension}}, where {{##}} represents the work's ID
* titles that are only 1-2 characters long (e.g., {{Me}}), and confirming the filename has {{_Work_##}} added to it (e.g., {{Me_Work_##}}).

# Create a new tag with a Chinese ({{，}} ) or Japanese ({{、}}) comma
## Browse > Tags > New Tag
## In the Name field, enter a tag name that contains one of the commas

## Fill in required fields

h1. What happens

For example, I entered both  {{Tag With 、Japanese Comma}} and {{Tag With ，  Chinese Comma}} when creating [this work|https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/1083964], but the actual tags on the work are [Tag With|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Tag%20With/works], [Japanese Comma|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Japanese%20Comma/works], and [Chinese Comma|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Chinese%20Comma/works] instead of the expected [Tag With 、Japanese Comma|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Tag%20With%20%E3%80%81Japanese%20Comma/edit] and [Tag With ，Chinese Comma|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Tag%20With%20%EF%BC%8CChinese%20Comma/edit].

Summary: If a user has roles the admin is not authorized to add, that role is removed when updating attributes

Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce

## Repeat steps 1b-1e

## Repeat steps 1b-1e
## In the search results row for testy, enter a new email address

The archivist role is added, but the wrangling role is removed.



The email is successfully updated, but the role is removed.

Any existing roles should remain as-is; updates to authorized roles should be edited accordingly. 

Email updates should succeed/fail without affecting the user’s existing roles.



Role authorization should only prevent you from changing roles you are not authorized to add; it should not remove them if they are already there.

Summary: Usernames that have numbers aren't searched correctly
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Dalton
Description:
We use Elasticsearch’s simple analyzer in the bookmark index’s [bookmarker field|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/bba3552e90254ea003cd8e67191a0c207fc1ea40/app/models/search/bookmark_indexer.rb#L46-L49] and [+creators field+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/bba3552e90254ea003cd8e67191a0c207fc1ea40/app/models/search/bookmark_indexer.rb#L36-L39], which means searching for bookmarks by bookmarkers or creators whose usernames or pseuds contain numbers produces either:

* no results if the username/pseud only contains numbers, or
* unwanted results if two users have names or pseuds that differ only by numbers (e.g., if you have users named testy2 and testy5, results for testy5 will appear when searching for testy2)

To reproduce:

* create an account with a username that's all numbers
* bookmark something
* go to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search|https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search], enter the whole numerical username in either "Any field on bookmark" or "Bookmarker," press Search Bookmarks
* notice there are no results

Another way to reproduce:

* go to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search|https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search]
* enter “testy2” in “Bookmarker” and press Search Bookmarks
* notice you’ll get results for testy5 and other testy accounts

This was discovered by a user in zoho ticket #653212

*Deploy notes*

We may need to give users a warning before reindexing things.

Summary: PDF files containing Japanese characters are very large
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in
# Post a work that only uses characters in the Latin alphabet (Aa-Zz)
# Download the work in PDF format
# Edit the work to include Japanese characters either in the actual content or the metadata, e.g., add a fandom tag like “ハートキャッチプリキュア! | Heartcatch Precure!”
# Download the updated work in PDF format
# Compare the size of the two files

h1. What happens

The second PDF is enormous because it includes a font that’s about 8 megabytes in size (WenQuanYi Zen Hei) in order to display the Japanese. 

It’s very likely this problem also occurs with Chinese and Korean, since WenQuanYi Zen Hei contains Chinese, Japanese, and Korean and is probably used in PDFs for all three languages.

h1. What should happen

The two PDFs should be much closer in size.

We can use Calibre’s {{--subset-embedded-fonts}} option for PDFs to only include the necessary characters.

h1. Testing notes

* Make sure to use a new work for this so you’re not getting a cached download file.
* Please test a second time using different characters – we want to be sure the second file contains the new characters.
* It wouldn’t hurt to check other languages like Arabic or Thai.

Summary: Redirect loop when accessing a posted work with no posted chapters in chapter by chapter mode
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Dalton
Description:
h1. *Steps to reproduce*

Since [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5627|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5627|smart-link] is fixed, it’s no longer possible to reproduce this without console access.

# Log in as User A
# Post a work 
## Post > New Work
## Fill in required fields
## Press Post
# Add a draft chapter
## Follow Add Chapter link on work
## Fill in required fields
## Press Preview
# From the console, delete the first posted chapter
# Log out
# Log in as User B
# Set your preferences to show works in chapter by chapter mode
## Hi, username! > My Preferences
## Under Display, uncheck “Show the whole work by default.”
## Press Update
# Go to User A’s works page ({{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/UserA/works}}) and follow the link to the work you posted earlier

h1. What happens

You get stuck in a redirect loop and likely encounter an error from your browser. 

However, if you either change your preferences to enable “Show the whole work by default” or go directly to the full work URL ({{https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/####?view_full_work=true}}), you see the work meta/header, title, and byline, with a blank space where the work text would normally be.

h1. What should happen

Rather than get stuck in a redirect loop, you should see the work header/meta, title, and byline, with a blank space where the work text would normally be. 

The way to accomplish this _might_ be to redirect to the work URL with the {{view_full_work}} parameters rather than attempting to show something at the chapter URL ({{https://test.archiveofourown.org/works/####/chapters/####}}). 

If we went that route, the redirect would need to only apply to people who are not an admin and not a creator (or invited creator) of the work. It would also need to apply _only_ if the chapter belonged to a posted work. (The behavior for attempting to access a draft chapter on a draft work should not change.)

Summary: Option to ban a user and delete all their creations includes collections the user doesn't own
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as a user
# Create a collection
## Browse > Collections > New Collection
## Fill in required information
## Press “Submit”
# Join a collection
## Browse > Collections
## In the filters, choose “No” under “Closed”
## And choose “Yes” under “Moderated”
## Press “Sort and Filter”
## Use the “Join” button on the first collection that appears in the list and which you do not own/are not a moderator of
# Log out
# Log in as an admin with the superadmin or policy_and_abuse role
# Ban the user from Step 1 for spam
## Manage Users > Find Users
## In “Name,” enter the user’s name
## Check “Exact match only” for “Search settings”
## Press “Find”
## Follow the appropriate “Details” link in the results table
## Under “Record Warnings, Suspensions, or Notes,” choose “Spammer: ban and delete all creations”
## Fill in some text under “Notes”
## Press “Update”

h1. What happens

On the Delete Spammer Creations page, the yellow banner says something like, “Are you sure you want to *_delete_* all the works and comments created by this user, along with their 0 bookmarks, 0 series, and 2 collections? This *cannot be undone*.”

Wait. *2* collections? But if I look at the user’s dashboard or collections page, they only have one!

Yeeeeah. Here’s what I said to PAC:

{quote}The [spam ban actions define a user's collections as @user.collections|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/e211c6bb9ad792e344aacb629020c3bc92576b0a/app/controllers/admin/admin_users_controller.rb#L131-L150], but all that does is get you [a list of collections the user is a participant in|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/e211c6bb9ad792e344aacb629020c3bc92576b0a/app/models/user.rb#L97-L98]. What it should do is get a list of collections the user is an owner or maintainer of, which would be [@user.maintained_collections|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/e211c6bb9ad792e344aacb629020c3bc92576b0a/app/models/user.rb#L101], or maybe even [sole-owned collections, like when you're deleting your account|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/e211c6bb9ad792e344aacb629020c3bc92576b0a/app/controllers/users_controller.rb#L180].{quote}

h1. What should happen

It should only count and delete collections the user is the sole owner of.

h1. Testing notes

In addition to Steps 1-3, you should also make a second collection and add a co-owner before testing the spam ban. To do so:

#  While logged in as the user from Step 1, repeat Step 2 to create a second collection you own
# Access the collection
# From the collection’s Dashboard, follow the “Membership” link under the collection title
# Under “Add new members,” enter the name of another user
# Press “Submit”
# Choose “Owner” from the select/dropdown menu that corresponds with the user you just added
# Press “Update” to save

Summary: Reduce load on mysql from searching for imported works.
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: james_
Description:
The fallback query in [Work.find_by_url_uncached|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/9ce7f82a0e0eaca675a7899222b805eed421b57c/app/models/work.rb#L383] resorts to a LIKE with a leading {{%}} which means that the entire {{works}} table will be scanned for non-matching queries. 

Some external links to previously imported urls are hitting this and periodically tying up MariaDB with unnecessarily slow queries (additionally compounded by a bug for urls that don’t start with {{www}})

The following changes therefore need to be made:

* modify {{with_www}} and {{no_www}} to preserve the protocol
* add {{with_http}} to change the protocol from HTTPS to HTTP
* add {{with_https}} to change the protocol from HTTP to HTTPS
* change {{Work.where(imported_from_url: [url.minimal, url.no_www, url.with_www, url.encoded, url.decoded]).first}} to now include {{url.with_http}} and {{url.with_https}}
* remove {{Work.where("imported_from_url LIKE ?", "%#{url.minimal_no_http}%")}}

Summary: Languages page caching
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Brian Austin
Description:
Going to [https://archiveofourown.org/languages|https://archiveofourown.org/languages|smart-link]  is _painfully_ slow, especially when logged in. We should cache it for everybody (including logged in users) since the counts definitely don’t need to be real-time, and even adding new languages doesn’t need to be reflected there instantaneously. Let’s try caching for 1 day to begin with.

Another improvement we can make is to use [https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActionView/Helpers/NumberHelper.html#method-i-number_to_human|https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActionView/Helpers/NumberHelper.html#method-i-number_to_human|smart-link]  to display the values, which will better indicate (at least for larger counts) that the numbers are now effectively approximations.

*Testing*

Go to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/languages|https://test.archiveofourown.org/languages] and check the counts there. Most languages in stage will be unaffected, but 

* numbers bigger than 999 should now have delimiters (i.e. “1,000” versus “1000”) and 
* the largest numbers should have similar rounding to the homepage (i.e., “863,300” instead of “863,301”)

Next, try posting a work *and a restricted work* (in a smaller language that has a precise number) and return to the languages page. The counts should _not_ update. When you come back in 24 hours, then they should have updated. *Check the count for a registered user is updated by 2 but the guest count is only updated by 1.*

The page heading should also say “Work Languages” now instead of “The Archive supports these languages.”
