Summary: Allow certain admins access to an index of orphaned works by a given original creator
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in
# Post a few works you don’t mind orphaning
## Post > New
## Fill in required information
## Press “Post”
## Repeat as desired (Note: When testing, we’ll want to put some of the works in anonymous and unrevealed collections, plus have an admin hide one of the works.)
# Orphan the works you posted in Step 2
## Hi, username! > My Works > Edit Works
## Check the checkboxes for the works you want to orphan
## Press the “Orphan” button
## Press “Yes, I’m sure” to confirm
# Log out
# Log in as an admin with the superadmin, legal, or policy_and_abuse role
# Access one of the works you orphaned in Step 3

h1. What happens

In the meta box at the top of the work, it will say “Original Creator ID: 123 (username)".  (Note: If the user is deleted, the text that appears is only the ID.) 

Refer to [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5521|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5521|smart-link] for more details on Original Creator IDs.

h1. What should happen

In the meta box, the text “123 (username)” should link the username to the user’s admin page ({{/admin/users/username}}). The user ID should be a link to {{/work_original_creators/123}}, and that page should use an {{<ol>}} to list the blurbs for all works orphaned by that user, including anonymous, unrevealed, and hidden works. 

The unrevealed blurb should not by the mystery work placeholder, but rather the full blurb, allowing the admin to actually access the work.

Blurbs should tell you when the original creator orphaned the work, e.g. “Orphaned at: [date time],” similar to the way your History page shows you when you last visited the work.

The page heading should be “Orphaned Works by 123 (username)” and the browser page title can be the same. If the user still exists, the text “123 (username)” in the heading should link the ID number to the user admin page ({{/admin/users/username}}) and the username to the user's works page ({{/users/username/works}}). 

The list should be paginated, as any other work listing would be. 

There should not be filters or a sidebar.

Like the data on the orphaned works themselves, the page should only be accessible to admins with the superadmin, legal, or policy_and_abuse role.

Going to {{/work_original_creators/123}} should give a 404 if there’s no data in the {{work_original_creators}} table for the given ID.

Summary: Switch our imageset partially to SVG
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: bingeling
Description:
We want to switch many of the pixel images used on the Archive to SVG. And then as a next step we want to create variations of these in our skins, namely reversi. But they should also be skinnable by users for their own skins. This goal dictates a specific way this needs to be implemented:

# it needs to be inline SVG
# with css classes for individual parts
# copied from SVG file to inline in a way that ensures no duplicate IDs either on the SVG itself or the elements inside the SVG (blurb icons are rendered many times in a works listing, for example)
# i18n-able aria-titles and/or other text (so not part of the source SVG file, but added while inlining)
# We need to allow some SVG-specific attributes in our CSS parser. A full list needs to be compiled, but {{fill}} and {{stroke}} are needed for certain.

Not part of this switch to SVG are the user icons (default, anon, guest, etc). Everything else can be switched to SVG but it's not necessary to switch all of them at once. The high priority and the main reason for this switch is the work blurb icons. The kudos icon is also used in emails, where we want to keep using the pixel version. So this specific one will have both a SVG version and a pixel version.

The look of our icons creates some complications. It's possible to create gradients and drop shadows in SVG, but these are defined in a {{defs}} block at the start of the file and are then used by elements by referencing their IDs. That means the same drop-shadow would be inlined for every icon on the page. So we have to ensure that each one gets a unique ID. The same is the case for the gradients. These two things have different possible solutions.

h2. Gradients

This is the easy one. Since we want these icons to be CSS-stylable anyway, we will get rid of the gradients in the graphic, render the SVG with a flat color background and then add the gradient via CSS.

One thing to note here is that you can't set a CSS background for SVG elements, only {{fill}} works. So the way to do this is to set {{fill: none;}} on the element (in the CSS) and then set the background gradient on the SVG element itself (in the CSS).

If somebody comes up with a reason for why we don't want to do it that way, the other possible solutions are the same as for the shadows.

h2. Shadows

We can't go the CSS-only route here, since the {{box-shadow}} CSS attribute has no effect on SVG elements, and would also render a rectangle box, instead of following the shape of the element. And while the {{drop-shadow}} CSS filter works, it can't help us, since we need inline shadows.

# The radical approach is to get rid of the shadows. Web design has changed a lot in the ~15 years since the work blurbs were added, maybe we use this project as a reason to give the blurb icons a new look.
# Least favorite option, only if everything else doesn't work out: We accept the bloat in the HTML file and add the shadow every time, our SVG renderer has to consider this and apply unique IDs to the shadow definitions when creating the inline SVG.
# We use {{use}} to build our icons. This means we have one big inline SVG element at the top of every page (visually hidden). This SVG contains all individual elements that we use on the site. The actual SVG icons that are visible on the page then are made up of {{use}} elements that reference the components from the sprite SVG at the top of the page.
## This is basically the imageset solution we have now, except SVG
## This would mean we don't have to deal with duplicate IDs
## No bloat, because even aside from the shadow and gradient issues, we wouldn't have to render the "Gen" (for example) icon N times either, only ever once.
## Here is a guide on how to do this from 2014: [https://24ways.org/2014/an-overview-of-svg-sprite-creation-techniques/|https://24ways.org/2014/an-overview-of-svg-sprite-creation-techniques/|smart-link]  with one very important change though: shadow DOM has come a long way in the last ten years and now it _is_ possible to reference these elements in CSS, so they are skinnable for us. The solution noted in the article, to externally reference the SVGs, however, _isn't_ suitable for us, since SVG hasn't come that far and filters (aka what we use to create the shadows in SVG) aren't externally referencable ([Open bug on Chromium|https://bugs.chromium.org/p/chromium/issues/detail?id=109212).]). This was the big stumbling block when we first worked on this, so it's really great that we have a viable solution now.
## browser support: [https://caniuse.com/mdn-svg_elements_use|https://caniuse.com/mdn-svg_elements_use|smart-link] 

h2. TL;DR, the individual steps that need to be done:

* Rebuild the pixel icons in SVG, this is mostly done, but needs to be adjusted to work with whatever solution that inlines it into the HTML.
* In case of the sprite solution:
** Make a partial with an SVG element that is visually hidden (width 0, height 0, etc) but not display: none (this differs from the article I linked above but is needed for the {{defs}} block to work).
** Define a single {{defs}} block at the top for all the gradients (if we use them) and the shadow, etc.
** Make a {{symbol}} for every icon with its own viewBox.
** Add the partial to all necessary layout files.
* In case of the "bloat" solution:
** add the SVGs as individual files to our Rails project
** Write a view helper (or whatever would be best suited for this task) that takes a path to an SVG, plus additional options we might need (string to use to build unique IDs, any text, etc), reads and copies the contents of that file and outputs the inlined SVG markup. Obviously should only work for files in our own project, can't pass external URLs. Take a look at [https://github.com/jamesmartin/inline_svg|https://github.com/jamesmartin/inline_svg|smart-link]  to see if there is a way for us to use it. Right now, to display the icons 1:1 the answer is no. Because 1. can't set IDs for elements inside the SVG, 2. we use neither sprocket nor webpack (and webpacker is deprecated). But forking it or using parts of the code might speed this task up.
* Change CSS parser to allow {{fill}} and {{stroke}} and other attributes TBD.
* Change HTML and CSS for every place the pixel version of an icon is currently used and redo it with the SVG version.
* This can be a next step in a separate issue: Redo the imageset to only contain the remaining pixel graphics. Update all instances where the imageset is used to the new x and y positions of the remaining graphics.

Description:
* Admins with the {{policy_and_abuse}} or {{superadmin}} roles should be able to access a user’s Change Username page ({{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/username/change_username}}) by
** following the “Change Username” link on {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/username/edit}}
** following the “Change My Username” link on {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/username/preferences}} if [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6542|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6542|smart-link] has been completed
** following a new “Rename” link on {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/users/username}} , located between “Activate” and “Manage Roles” 
* For these admins, the Change My Username page should look and behave differently from the user version:
** The page heading should be “Change Username”
** The yellow caution box should not appear
** Where the page says, “If that is not what you want, you can create a new Pseud instead,” it should instead say, “Change the name of this user to a generic name in the format user + their account ID.”
** Where the existing navigation is, there should instead be a button-style navigation link to “Manage User,” which should point to {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/users/username}}
** The “New username” field should be disabled and prefilled with “user123,” where “123” is the user’s ID
*** There should be backend validation to ensure the prefilled username is not altered
*** The footnote associated with this field should say, “This username cannot be edited. If you need to change it to a different name, contact your chair.”
** In place of the “Password” field, there should be a "Ticket ID" field that is used to validate the ticket exists in the ticket tracker, a la [AO3-6156|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6156].
*** If [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6587|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6587|smart-link] is not completed, the field should have a footnote that says, “Numbers only.”
** Assuming validations pass, submitting the form should rename the user and log it in the User History as "Old Username: whatever, New Username: whaterever, Changed by: admin-whoever, Ticket ID: #123"
*** Ideally, this would rename the user even if it had not been 7 days since their last rename
* Other admins attempting to access {{/users/username/change_username}} should redirected

If [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6717|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6717|smart-link] is implemented first, admins should be able to change the usernames of banned or suspended users.

Summary: All Join buttons on a collection listing switch to Leave when you press Join on one collection blurb
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.

# Log in
# Access a collection listing with multiple open, moderated collections on one page, e.g. by:

## And choose “Yes” under “Moderated”
## Press “Sort and Filter”

The page reloads, and all the “Join” buttons for collections following the collection you’ve just joined now say “Leave,” leading you to believe it just made you join all of them. (Don’t worry; you haven’t.)

Only the collection you joined should have its button updated to “Leave.”

Summary: Bump nokogiri from 1.14.3 to 1.16.2
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Brian Austin
Description:
This resolves a medium-severity CVE reported by dependabot: [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/security/dependabot/69|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/security/dependabot/69].

There are a number of changes, so I’ve pulled the list of deprecated features so we can double check them. Also of note, we can now opt in to native (not Ruby) memory management for libxml2 for improved speed performance but with the potential for issues that come with C memory management.

h3. Deprecated

* Passing a {{Nokogiri::XML::Node}} as the first parameter to {{CDATA.new}} is deprecated and will generate a warning. This parameter should be a kind of {{Nokogiri::XML::Document}}. This will become an error in a future version of Nokogiri.
* Passing a {{Nokogiri::XML::Node}} as the first parameter to {{Schema.from_document}} is deprecated and will generate a warning. This parameter should be a kind of {{Nokogiri::XML::Document}}. This will become an error in a future version of Nokogiri.
* Passing a {{Nokogiri::XML::Node}} as the second parameter to {{Text.new}} is deprecated and will generate a warning. This parameter should be a kind of {{Nokogiri::XML::Document}}. This will become an error in a future version of Nokogiri.
* [CRuby] Calling a custom XPath function without the {{nokogiri}} namespace is deprecated and will generate a warning. Support for non-namespaced functions will be removed in a future version of Nokogiri. (Note that JRuby has never supported non-namespaced custom XPath functions.)

h3. Removed

* Removed {{Nokogiri::HTML5.get}} which was deprecated in v1.12.0. [[#2278|https://github.com/sparklemotion/nokogiri/pull/2278]] ([@flavorjones|https://github.com/flavorjones])
* Removed the CSS-to-XPath utility modules {{XPathVisitorAlwaysUseBuiltins}} and {{XPathVisitorOptimallyUseBuiltins}}, which were deprecated in v1.13.0 in favor of {{XPathVisitor}} constructor args. [[#2403|https://github.com/sparklemotion/nokogiri/pull/2403]] ([@flavorjones|https://github.com/flavorjones])
* Removed {{XML::Reader#attribute_nodes}} which was deprecated in v1.13.8 in favor of {{#attribute_hash}}. [[#2598|https://github.com/sparklemotion/nokogiri/issues/2598], [#2599|https://github.com/sparklemotion/nokogiri/pull/2599]] ([@flavorjones|https://github.com/flavorjones])
* [CRuby] Removed the {{libxml/libxml2_path}} key from {{VersionInfo}}, used in the past for third-party library integration, in favor of the {{nokogiri/cppflags}} and {{nokogiri/ldflags}} keys. Please note that third-party library integration is not fully supported and may be deprecated soon, see [#2746|https://github.com/sparklemotion/nokogiri/discussions/2746] for more context. [[#2143|https://github.com/sparklemotion/nokogiri/pull/2143]] ([@flavorjones|https://github.com/flavorjones])

Summary: Remove session cookie migration logic
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Albert Pedersen
Description:
I wrote a piece of code to migrate session cookies from encrypted to signed format as part of [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6629|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6629|smart-link]. This was done to ensure users would not be logged out.

[https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/4e56a347944a6fb831414d9cccdfc866ddfacce5/app/controllers/application_controller.rb#L99-L108|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/4e56a347944a6fb831414d9cccdfc866ddfacce5/app/controllers/application_controller.rb#L99-L108]

The AO3 session cookie has an expiry of two weeks, after which browsers delete the cookie automatically. Each page load causes AO3 to issue a new session cookie, so a user who visits at least once every two weeks can stay signed in indefinitely.

Here’s how removing the migration logic will (not) impact users:

* Users who visited the site since the upgrade have already had their session cookie migrated to the new format. Removing the migration logic will not impact these users.
* Users who have not visited since the upgrade will have to sign in again on their next visit regardless, since their browser will have already deleted the session cookie (change was made more than two weeks ago). Removing the migration logic should have no impact here either.
** Users who selected “remember me” at sign in have another cookie named {{remember_user_token}}. This cookie has a longer expiry, but the format of this cookie did not change, so it does not depend on the migration logic and will still work.
* The impact to bots depends on how they’re written.
** Bots with a proper cookie jar will stay signed in, since their session cookie will have been migrated automatically if they made a request since the change was deployed. Standard HTTP libraries usually have cookie jars.
** Bots with a hard-coded session cookie will be logged out. The session cookie itself does not have an expiry date (it’s only enforced by the browser), so it is possible some developers have done this.

The function has a slight impact on server load since it runs on every request. There’s also little reason to keep unused logic in the codebase. Those are the main reasons for removing it.

Summary: Parts of header navigation inaccessible to screen readers
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
# Log in on an iOS device (ideally 17.3.1)
# Use VoiceOver to access the navigation in the site header

A user reports that the items in the “Hi, username!” menu are read only as “menu item” instead of the text, e.g. My Dashboard.

The ARIA roles {{menu}} and {{menuitem}} are not meant to be used for navigation. Instead, they are meant to be used for application-style menus and menu items, like in the Rich Text Editor.

So let’s fix some of the accessibility issues in the header. That means:

* The {{menu}} and {{menuitem}} roles should be removed.
* The {{<div>}} around the header should now be a {{<header>}} element instead.
** This gives the section the {{banner}} role, which might seem weird if you’re not used to screen readers, but it's the normal behavior. (Refer to mdn’s [ARIA: banner role|https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/Accessibility/ARIA/Roles/banner_role] and [header element|https://developer.mozilla.org/en-US/docs/Web/HTML/Element/header] documentation for more info.)
* The navigation lists should now be wrapped inside {{<nav>}} elements, with {{aria-label}} attributes to distinguish the user nav (the one containing "Hi, name!" and so on) from the site nav and the admin nav.
** The names should not include the word “navigation,” because screen readers will say “navigation” shortly thereafter due to the presence of the nav element. (More [info on screen reader behavior with aria-labels on nav elements|https://russmaxdesign.github.io/accessible-forms/landmarks-nav04.html].) 
* The search form in the site navigation was missing the {{search}} role. The role appears to have better support than the {{<search>}} element, so we want to use that, and we should give it an {{aria-label}} because it appears on all pages, including those with other search fields (although I don’t think any of them have the {{search}} role yet.)

Summary: Automatically return unwrangleable tags with no fandom to unwrangled bin
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Brian Austin
Description:
h1. Overview

Wranglers can mark tags as unwrangleable without attaching a fandom tag which leads to these tags becoming lost and no longer easily accessible. Right now, we (sometimes) run manual updates to get the tags back. To reduce manual work, we’d like to create a Resque job to do this for us. Once every week for now should be fine.

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as a user with wrangling privileges
# Access your wrangling page: Hi, username! > Tag Wrangling
# Mark a tag as unwrangleable without assigning it a fandom
## If you have tags in your unwrangled bins…
### Access one of the unwrangled bins by clicking on the tag count
### Follow the Edit link for one of the tags
### Check “Unwrangleable”
### Do not fill in the “Fandoms” field
### Press “Save changes”
## If you don’t have tags in your unwrangled bins…
### Access one of your unfilterable bins by clicking on the tag count
### Follow the Edit link for one of the tags
### Check “Unwrangleable”
### In the Fandoms listbox, check the boxes for all of the fandoms to select them for removal
### Press “Save changes”

h1. *Testing*

Follow the steps to reproduce. After the configured time, the job will run and the tag should be returned to the unwrangled bins for all of its suggested fandoms.

The first time the task is run, you may end up with a lot of tags in your unwrangled bins, not just the tags you personally marked unwrangleable. This is expected, since it will be returning any existing fandom-less, unwrangleable tags to the bins as well.

Summary: Allow certain admins to choose FAQ categories for inclusion in main navigation
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
Once [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6698|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6698|smart-link] is implemented, admins with the docs or superadmin role should be allowed to choose FAQs for inclusion in the main navigation.

* “FAQ” should be removed from the “About” menu
* An “FAQ” menu should be added after “About,” and when JavaScript is disabled, clicking it should link to {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/faq}} 
* The first item in the “FAQ” menu should be “All FAQ Categories”
* Admins with the docs or superadmin roles should be able to choose up to X FAQ categories to appear in the menu, where X represents a configurable number (we can set it to 10)
* The admins should be able to set the text used to represent the category in the FAQ menu, but if none is provided, it should fall back to using the category name
* The menu should be cached

When an authorized admin goes to a category’s edit page (e.g., {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/faq/category_name/edit?language_id=en}}), the topmost fieldset should contain

* a checkbox for including the category in the menu, labeled “Included in FAQ dropdown menu” and with the explanatory paragraph “If this box is checked, the category will be included in the FAQs dropdown menu in the main navigation. Up to [configured value] categories can be included.”
* a text field labeled “Display name for FAQ dropdown menu,” with the explanatory paragraph, “Alternate name for dropdown menu; if left blank, uses category name.”

The paragraphs can be plain paragraphs without classes, as on tag edit pages, rather than footnotes.

Summary: Enhance the Redis initializers to allow sentinel
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Brian Austin
Description:
Right now, if the one Redis instance the Archive points to goes down, the whole application is inaccessible. Failing over requires updating (either manually or via Ansible) the config to point at a new Redis server – if one is even available. We can use Redis replication along with [https://redis.io/docs/management/sentinel|https://redis.io/docs/management/sentinel|smart-link] to enable automatic failovers.

The following initializers will need to be updated:

* [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/17b131fa4df492ec7576e7642e4d4844797766e8/config/initializers/gem-plugin_config/redis.rb|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/17b131fa4df492ec7576e7642e4d4844797766e8/config/initializers/gem-plugin_config/redis.rb|smart-link]

Updating them must maintain backwards compatibility with the existing string-based configuration.

Summary: Allow certain admins to access inboxes

Description:

* should be able to follow the link to access that page
* should be able to use the inbox filters to filter comments
* should *not* be able to approve or delete comments, or mark them as read (but they can still see the buttons, and it’s okay if the Select All/Select None/Select buttons still work)

Admins with other roles should be redirected to the homepage with an error saying, "Sorry, only an authorized admin can access the page you were trying to reach."

[AO3-6427|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/issues/AO3-6427] will need to be updated to remove inboxes from the list of URLs that can’t be reported.

Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.

Description:
Sometimes for various reasons users want to stop getting any subscription emails, or want to clear out all their subscriptions and start fresh. Summary: Allow users to resend invitations, this time with index
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description: h1. Description Users frequently submit support requests because they have accidentally deleted or not received their invitations. Therefore, we’d like to allow users to resend their invitations without submitting a support ticket. (In the case of missing emails, it’s fairly likely the resent email will continue to be eaten by spam filters, but it’s possible some will get through.) To prevent spam, there should be a configurable limit on how soon you can resend an invitation ({{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}). It should start off at 24 hours. Resending an invitation should not alter the invitation’s {{sent_at}}, because we sometimes need this information. It should be tracked separately as {{resent_at}}. This information should be available to admins on pages where the [invitation partial|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/views/invitations/_invitation.html.erb] is used, e.g., {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/USERNAME/invitations/###}}, where it can be added below the existing “Sent at” info as “Last resent at.” Users can currently check the status of their invitations by entering their email address on [https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests/status|https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests/status]. We’d like to add the resend option to this page. *If the user checks the status of their invitation less than 24 hours (*{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}*) after the invitation is initially sent*, the resend option should not be present. The text should say: {quote}Your invitation was emailed to this address on [sent at date]. If you can't find it, please check your email spam folder as your spam filters may have placed it there. If it has been more than [{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}] hours since you should have received your invitation, but you have not received it after checking your spam folder, you can visit this page to resend the invitation.{quote} *If the user checks the status of their invitation more than 24 hours (*{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}*) after the invitation is initially sent*, the resend option should be present. The text should say: {quote}Your invitation was emailed to this address on [sent at date]. If you can't find it, please check your email spam folder as your spam filters may have placed it there. Because your invitation was sent more than 24 hours ago, you can have your invitation resent. [button reading: Resend Invitation]{quote} *If the user checks the status of their invitation less than 24 hours (*{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}*) after the invitation is resent*, the resend option should not be present. The text should say: {quote}Your invitation was emailed to this address on [sent at date] and resent on [resent at date]. If you can't find it, please check your email spam folder as your spam filters may have placed it there. If it has been more than [{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}] hours since you should have received your invitation, but you have not received it after checking your spam folder, you can visit this page to resend the invitation.{quote} *If the user checks the status of their invitation more than 24 hours (*{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}*) after the invitation is resent*, the resend option should be present, and there should be a suggestion to contact Support. The text should say: {quote}Your invitation was emailed to this address on [sent at date] and resent on [resent at date]. If you can't find it, please check your email spam folder as your spam filters may have placed it there. Because your invitation was resent more than 24 hours ago, you can have your invitation resent again, or you may want to contact Support. [button reading: Resend Invitation]{quote} h1. Notes If you could fix it so the “Invitation status for email@example.com” heading is an {{h3}} when loaded on [https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests/status|https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests/status], that would be appreciated! (It should remain an {{h2}} when you have JavaScript disabled and it takes you to a separate page.) Example: !javascript_resend.png|width=83%,alt="The Invitation Request Status page with the invitation status loaded below the email field using JavaScript."! !no_javascript_resend.png|width=83%,alt="The separate Invitation Status page for users who have JavaScript disabled."! This was deployed in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6609|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6609|smart-link] and reverted with [this pull request|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4710] due to the performance issues described in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6666|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6666|smart-link]. We can probably revert the revert to get the code back, and then add the necessary indexes. Regarding what to index, Brian notes: {quote}It looks like we don't even have an index on {{invitee_email}} (at least according to the [latest schema dump|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/bd57a26224017d4b871fb70a9787d7fe3c29d249/db/schema.rb#L377]) which is quite surprising to me. Adding those 2 indexes sounds like a reasonable approach to me, we can try running an {{EXPLAIN}} on staging before the deploy to make sure the DB is doing the right things with them{quote} And Bilka notes: {quote}I tried locally running the explain for the current table/index situation, it was very unhelpful. I think an index on {{redeemed_at}} by itself might not make much sense, because all the queries are looking for (not) null, not a specific value. {{invitee_email}} would be a very good target, agreed with Brian there.{quote} h1. Summary: Allow comment moderation on news posts
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
We’d like to have comment moderation for news posts, just like comment moderation for works.

# Log in as an admin who can create news posts (board, board_assistants_team, communications, support, translation, superadmin)
# Admin Posts > Post AO3 News

There should be a check box for “Enable comment moderation” above the section for “Who can comment on this news post” 

Checking this box and pressing post should create a news post with a comment section. 

The comment form should have a blue notice on it that says, “Comments on this news post are moderated. Your comment will not appear until it has been approved.”

# Log out of your admin account
# Access the news post
# Leave a comment (or two or three)

You should get a success message that says, "Your comment was received! It will appear publicly after it has been approved."

# Log in as an admin with any role, because for the initial roll out we’re treating this like hiding comments on admin posts (which any admin can do)
# Access the news post

There should be a link at the top of the news post that says, “Unreviewed Comments (#)” near “Delete Post.”  

Following the link will take you to a page with the heading “Unreviewed Comments on [News Post Title].” 

The page should say under the heading, “Please note that comments cannot be unapproved once you have approved them. After you delete any comments you do not wish to appear on the news post, you can approve all that remain.”

You should be able to approve the comment by using either:

*  the “Approve” button on the comment, which will take you back to the Unreviewed Comments page and give you the success message, “Comment approved,” or
* the “Approve All Unreviewed Comments” button, which will take you to the admin post with the success message, “All moderated comments approved.”

The approved comments should appear on the news post (please allow for possible delay due to caching). 

If there are no unreviewed comments, the “Unreviewed Comments (#)” link will go away.

Some other things you can test, if you’d like:

# using other buttons on the unreviewed comments, e.g., hiding, deleting, or spamming a comment – there’s no new behavior here, but if there are existing bugs, it wouldn’t hurt to log them
# combining the moderated comment functionality with limiting who can comment on the news post to no one or logged-in users only – again, this can already be done on works and there’s no new behavior here, but if there are existing bugs, it wouldn’t hurt to log them
# on a *work* with moderated comments enabled, an admin should not be able to approve comments (AO3-5977 exists for getting rid of the big “Approve All Unreviewed Comments” button)

Summary: Don't allow images in comments
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
We’d like to extend [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6564|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6564|smart-link] to all comments and comment emails.

h1. Testing

You can test with comments on works or tags (to comment on a tag, you’ll need to be logged in as a tag wrangler, e.g., testy). 

*Because you’ll need to check emails and inboxes*, it’s easiest to use works created by another account you own, or tags wrangled by another account you own.

# *Before anything else*, go to your preferences (Hi, username! > My Preferences) and make sure you have the following settings
## “Turn off emails about comments” should be *unchecked* 
## “Turn off messages to your inbox about comments” should be *unchecked*
## “Turn off copies of your own comments” should be *unchecked*
# *Before this is deployed to staging*, leave a comment containing an image. Bookmark this comment or otherwise remember where it is (if you have emailed copies of your own comments enabled as instructed above, that’s a good way to find it).

*This will not be ready for testing until someone with server access has restarted the workers (perhaps multiple times) to make sure the emails are updated.* Please comment to say you have done so before this is set to QA.

Now for the testing that happens once this is set to *QA*! 

You’ll probably get more emails than we tell you to check for a given step. That’s fine! The important thing is to *check the subject lines* and make sure you’re checking the contents for the specified. All in all, there are 6 different comment emails and you only need to check each one once.

# Check the comment you left in “Before this is deployed to staging.” The image should not be visible:
## on the comment
## in the inbox of the comment recipient
## in the homepage inbox of the comment recipient
# While logged in, leave a comment with an image. The image should not be visible
## on the comment
## in the copy of the copy emailed to you, which will have a subject like “Comment you left on [thing]”
## in the comment emailed to the comment recipient (i.e., the work creator/tag wrangler), which will have a subject like “Comment on [thing]”
## in the inbox of the comment recipient
## in the homepage inbox of the comment recipient
# Edit the comment you just left in Step 2 (you can change anything, but don’t remove the image, since that’s what we’re looking for). The image should not be visible
## in the edited comment emailed to the comment recipient, which will have a subject like “Edited comment on [thing]”
# As a logged in user, comment on a work. Then as a *different* logged in user, reply to that user with a comment that includes an image. The image should not be visible
## in the copy of the comment emailed to you, which will have a subject like “Reply you left to a comment on [thing]”
## in the comment emailed to the comment recipient (i.e., the person you’re replying to), which will have a subject like “Reply to your comment on [thing]”
# Edit the comment you left in Step 4 (you can change anything, but don’t remove the image, since that’s what we’re looking for). The image should not be visible
## in the edited comment emailed to the comment recipient, which will have a subject like “Edited reply to your comment on [thing]”

Summary: Synned Relationship Tags Not Carrying Over Fandoms + Character Tags to Newly Created Canonicals
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Dre
Description:
Since about July of 2023, we've had an issue where tags were significantly delayed in carrying over parents and children when synned. This issue seemed to begin to occur with increasing regularity from about :30 past the hour until about :50 past the hour whenever the archive was moderately to extremely busy. It was an inconvenience, but it didn’t directly impact our workflow beyond being a little annoying. This issue impacts all tags, but is most noticable and impactful in the creation of relationship tags.

Recently this issue has gotten significantly worse, to the point where it is occuring more and more frequently outside of that time frame and tags which would normally transfer to the canonical during synning are not transferring at all if they are not left attached to the syn until they have done so (which, can take a long, long time depending on how bad the delay currently is). 

For example, if I attach character tags *Alastor* and *Angel Dust* to a relationship tag and then use that tag to create the canonical for *Alastor & Angel Dust (Hazbin Hotel)*, the fandom and the character tags would not immediately transfer to the new canonical. If I leave them on the syn, eventually they will transfer over, typically after the delay window has passed, but if I remove them at any point prior to them transferring, it will never add them at all and those tags will instead need to be added manually. 

Delays relating to tags being assigned to fandoms and works from synned tags to be aggregated into the works on the canonical tag have also significantly increased. 

Additionally, if the character tags are removed prior to fandom & character tags transfering to the syn, though the syn is still assigned to the fandom, the fandom will never transfer to the canonical. It will only eventually transfer _if_ the character tags are still attached when the delay has resolved.

This is all having a significant impact on workflow.


*To Reproduce Issue:*

# Create a work
# Assign a fandom to this work and create a new relationship tag and add it to this work
# Publish work
# Go to unwrangled bin of the fandom assigned to the work and find the newly created relationship tag
# Assign character tags to the relationship tag
# Wait until between :31-:49 past the hour. While this error occurs other times, it occurs most frequently within this time frame
# Use this relationship to create a canonical tag via the Synonym of field on the tag edit page
# Click through to the canonical tag’s edit page
# Refresh and observe whether the fandom + character tags are added to the canonical tag
## If they have not been added you can check whether they will be added as designed (i.e. regardless of whether the syn has the character tags attached when the delay resolves) by taking the following steps:
### Remove the character tags from the synned relationship tag
### Navigate back to the canonical tag edit page
### Refresh and wait to see if the character and fandom tags show up on the canonical tag
### If functioning properly, the fandom & character tags should be showing up eventually on the canonical whether the character tags are currently attached to a syn or not
## If they have not been added, you can verify that they will be added if the character tags are left attached to the synned tag by taking the following steps: 
### Remain on the canonical edit page
### Refresh periodically until character & fandom tags show up on the canonical tag (typically this happens when the delay resolves, usually between :50-:00 of the hour

Description:
Right now, we have to use a magic {{i18n-tasks-use}} comment to get the i18n-tasks gem to recognize the locale used by email subjects translated with the {{default_i18n_subject}} method, e.g. [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/c2354df0800637c1e9a0ddd9a3651cc59a17597a/app/mailers/user_mailer.rb#L219-L220|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/c2354df0800637c1e9a0ddd9a3651cc59a17597a/app/mailers/user_mailer.rb#L219-L220|smart-link] . Together with the upgrade we should remove all existing magic comments for mailer subject locales.

The matcher needs to be enabled in the i18n-tasks configuration file. Let’s take the opportunity to also use the [simplified configuration syntax|https://github.com/glebm/i18n-tasks/blob/9e765a40308ecd9674453d70a9177d74a2596c61/templates/config/i18n-tasks.yml#L99-L101] for the RailsModelMatcher, so we don’t need to manually require it.

Summary: Separate languages used for works from other uses of languages

The {{languages}} table currently serves multiple purposes:

* allow users to identify the language their works are in
* allow admins to 
** identify which languages we can provide support or abuse assistance in
** identify languages of FAQs and admin posts
** associate languages with locales

Using one table to serve user-facing and admin-facing purposes sometimes creates problems, as the needs of these two groups can be conflicting.

Ergo, we’d like to separate the admin-based uses and the user-based uses. 

# Create a new table called {{locale_languages}} that is a duplicate of the existing language table in terms of both structure _and_ existing data. The goal here is to keep everything associated with the language it is currently associated with.

(You can leave the columns in the database for the time being; we will probably rename the table to {{work_languages}} for clarity and we can drop them in that migration.)

Summary: Custom cop for calling html_safe on translated strings
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Bilka
Description:
Let’s add another custom Rubocop cop for a common nitpick: Uses of {{t().html_safe}}.

[html_safe|https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/String.html#method-i-html_safe] does _not_ escape HTML in strings, instead it marks strings as safe so they are inserted into the HTML with no escaping. This is often used if there is some HTML in the translation, such as links. However, due to the lack of escaping, {{html_safe}} should not be called on potentially unsafe user-generated text, like interpolation variables in translations.

The {{t()}} method provides another way to [use translations with HTML|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/i18n.html#using-safe-html-translations]: Keys ending with {{_html}} or {{.html}} are considered html safe so they can contain HTML tags. But their interpolations are still escaped. Combined with using Rails helpers like [link_to|https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActionView/Helpers/UrlHelper.html#method-i-link_to] and the [tag helpers|https://api.rubyonrails.org/classes/ActionView/Helpers/TagHelper.html#method-i-tag] that automatically handle marking their output as html safe, interpolations and translations can still contain all needed HTML without any calls to {{html_safe}}.

So, let’s recommend using translations keys ending with {{_html}} or {{.html}} when code calls {{html_safe}} on the {{t()}} or {{translate()}} methods.

The [PR for AO3-6691|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4763] has an example of adding a custom cops and tests that may be helpful. Furthermore, here is some initial code for the custom cop from ticking instant, but it will need some adjustments:

{code:ruby}module CustomCops
  class TranslateHtmlSafe < RuboCop::Cop::Base
    MSG = 'Instead of calling t(key).html_safe in views, try renaming the key so that it ends in _html or .html, and remove the .html_safe call'.freeze

    def_node_matcher :html_safe_translate?, <<~PATTERN
      (send (send nil? :t ...) :html_safe)
    PATTERN

    # optimization: don't call `on_send` unless
    # the method name is in this list
    RESTRICT_ON_SEND = [:html_safe].freeze

    def on_send(node)
      return unless html_safe_translate?(node)

      add_offense(node)
    end
  end
end{code}



This cop will complain about the [commonly used greetings|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/47cc03880769f4256456598e94eed99a8d6e0faf/config/locales/mailers/en.yml#L72-L74] in the mailers, {{mailer.general.greeting.formal}} and {{mailer.general.greeting.informal.addressed}}. Let's rename these locale keys to {{mailer.general.greeting.formal_html}} and {{mailer.general.greeting.informal.addressed_html}} and remove the {{html_safe}} calls on their translations in the mailer view files.

*Testing*

No manual tests required, automated testing is sufficient.

To improve these tasks, we want to do a couple things:

# Update the {{index_*}} tasks to include a warning like we added in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6624|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6624|smart-link]. Summary: Low Vision Default: On narrow screens, expanded navigation menus hide behind top-level options and overflow onto main content
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in on a smallish mobile device in portrait mode, or in a browser window narrowed to resemble mobile
# In the Customize section of the footer, choose the Low Vision Default Skin
# Once the skin is applied, select one of the items in the main navigation that usually has a dropdown menu in the default skin, e.g., “Hi, username!” or “Fandoms” 

h1. What happens

The expanded options are underneath the main options, making it hard to see and use them, and then they overflow the header and spill onto the main content, making _that_ difficult to see and use as well. Furthermore, you can’t tell which menu you have open because the selected item has a solid grey background that is almost indistinguishable from the grey gradient on the unselected items.

Note that if you’re on a device with a large screen, the menus function correctly. 

!Screenshot 2024-07-05 at 7.59.05 PM.png|width=665,height=771,alt="Broken mobile screenshot. 'Fandoms' is selected, prompting a vertical list of black buttons to appear under the top-level navigation items and on top of the main content area, albeit with some aspects of the main content (the icon and subnavigation) overlapping them."!



h1. What should happen

They expanded items should appear between the selected menu item and the next one. The selected menu item (e.g., “Hi, username!”) should take on a red background instead of a grey that is so difficult to distinguish from the button styles.

Basically, it should work the same on narrow screens as on big screens.



!Screenshot 2024-07-05 at 7.59.41 PM.png|width=1177,height=767,alt="Correctly functioning header navigation. The selected 'Hi, sarken2' option has a red background instead of a grey gradient that looks like a button. Below the 'Hi, sarken2' item, the My Dashboard, My Subscription, My Works, My Bookmarks, My Sign-ups, My Assignments, My History, My Preferences, and Tag Wrangling options are clearly visible, listed vertically with black backgrounds. After those options, the button-style top-level menu options (Post, Log Out, Fandoms, Browse, Search) resume."!

h1. Deploy notes

An admin with the superadmin role will need to copy the updated CSS into Low Vision Default _before_ merging (to ensure it gets recached on deploying):

# Log in as admin
# Skins > Approved Skins
# Locate Low Vision Default in the table and click the title to open the skin show page
# Follow the Edit link at the bottom to access the skin edit page
# Copy the entire contents of public/stylesheets/masters/low_vision_default/low_vision_default_site_screen_.css from the pull request
# Paste into the CSS field on the skin edit page
# Press Update to save
# Merge the pull request

h1. Testing

Then testers should check the behavior of Low Vision Default on multiple screen sizes and browsers. The correct colors for the navigation:

# Top-level items should be button-style with black border and dark text by default.
# Top-level items that are being hovered over with the mouse, have keyboard focus, or are the parent of an open dropdown menu, should have red backgrounds with light grey text and border.
# Dropdown menu items should have black background with -light grey- white text and border.
# Dropdown menu items that are being hovered over with the mouse or that have keyboard focus should have light grey backgrounds with dark grey/black text.

Summary: Admin Roles: Restrict admin access to wrangling-related areas
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Overview

As part of the admin roles epic (AO3-5518), we need to restrict admin access to wrangling-related areas. 

These areas are spread across a number of controllers, but should be governed by one policy: {{WranglingPolicy}}. The affected controllers and pages (actions):

# {{TagWranglersController}}
## Wrangler pages, e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglers/testy|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglers/testy] ({{show}})
## Wrangling assignments, i.e. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglers|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglers] ({{index}}, {{create}}, {{destroy}})
## Wrangler activity report ({{report_csv}})
# {{TagWranglingsController}}
## Mass bins, e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings?show=fandoms|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings?show=fandoms] ({{index}}, {{wrangle}})
## Wrangling Tools, i.e. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_wranglings] ({{index}})
# {{UnsortedTagsController}}
## Unsorted bin, i.e. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/unsorted_tags|https://test.archiveofourown.org/unsorted_tags] ({{index}}, {{mass_update}})
# {{TagsController}}
## Tag edit pages, e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Testing/edit|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Testing/edit] ({{edit}}, {{update}})
## New tag page, i.e. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/new|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/new] ({{new}}, {{create}})
## Tag bins, e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Testing/wrangle?show=characters|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Testing/wrangle?show=characters] ({{wrangle}}, {{mass_update}})
# {{WranglingGuidelinesController}}
## Manage wrangling guidelines, e.g., [https://test.archiveofourown.org/wrangling_guidelines/manage|https://test.archiveofourown.org/wrangling_guidelines/manage] ({{manage}}, {{update_positions}})
## New wrangling guidelines, e.g., [+https://test.archiveofourown.org/wrangling_guidelines/new+|https://test.archiveofourown.org/wrangling_guidelines/new] ({{new}}, {{create}})
## Edit wrangling guidelines, e.g., [https://test.archiveofourown.org/wrangling_guidelines/2/edit|https://test.archiveofourown.org/wrangling_guidelines/2/edit] ({{edit}}, {{update}})
## Delete wrangling guidelines ({{destroy}})

Admins with the {{tag_wrangling}} or {{superadmin}} roles should have access to all of these actions. 

Admins with the {{policy_and_abuse}} role should have read-only access to:

* the mass bins ({{TagWranglingsController#index}}, but not {{TagWranglingsController#wrangle}})
* unsorted bin ({{UnsortedTagsController#index}}, but not {{UnsortedTagsController#mass_update}})
* tag bins ({{TagsController#wrangle}}, but not {{TagsController#mass_update}})
* tag edit pages ({{TagsController#edit}}, but not {{TagsController#update}} )

To make coding, reviewing, and testing manageable, each controller will have a separate issue. 

The issues can be worked on in any order. 

The final pull request will need to hide the major navigational elements: 

* the “Tag Wrangling” item in the admin navigation from all admin roles except {{superadmin}}, {{policy_and_abuse}}, and {{tag_wrangling}} 
* the sidebar on [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/search|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/search] and [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/testing|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/testing] from all admin roles except {{superadmin}} and {{tag_wrangling}}

Creator: Bilka
Description:
There should be a mailer preview for the {{batch_kudo_notification}} email.

The amount of guest and user kudos should be flexible and controlled with [url parameters|https://www.bigbinary.com/blog/rails-5-2-allows-passing-request-params-to-action-mailer-previews], e.g. {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/rails/mailers/kudo_mailer/batch_kudo_notification?user_count=5&guest_count=10}}.

To make the previews' locale selector work, the {{I18n.with_locale}} block should be moved outside the mailer method, into [RedisMailQueue#deliver_kudos|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/93f8571483aa496265f8fa165edb52c4940fa478/app/models/redis_mail_queue.rb#L40]. There should be a cucumber test for sending a translated kudos email to a user.

This is also a good opportunity to update the locale keys used in the mail to the [current I18n standards|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/wiki/Internationalization-%28i18n%29-Standards]. Particularly, the keys used in the HTML mail should end in {{.html}} and the {{html_safe}} calls should be removed. The keys used in the text mail should be updated to match.

*Testing*

All of the following previews should be valid mails with no translation errors and no exposed HTML, for both the HTML and text version. Selecting a locale from the dropdown that has translations for at least the footer (e.g. cs, hr, ja, ko, de, sv) should result in a translated footer, but other text may remain in English, depending on whether translations are available.

Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# First, we need to follow the steps in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6777|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6777|smart-link] to create a blank tag.

## Press “Submit”

## Follow the “Edit” link from your Nomination’s page
## Use the remove option (×) to remove one of the tags – I’m removing “Spock”
## Press “Submit”

h1. What happens

The tag you removed is no longer in your nominations, but instead, it’s replaced with the blank space tag.

I’d love to put images here, but Jira doesn’t recognize any file type I try to upload.

There should be no tag present at all.

I’m not sure if the autocomplete JavaScript is to blame or something else – please do update the Components if this turns out to be either just front end or just back end.

* characters that already exist on the archive and are associated with a fandom
* characters that already exist on the archive but are not associated with a fandom (e.g., character tags hanging out in the unwrangled character bin)

Summary: Make it easier to pause sending invitations while letting users add themselves to the queue
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
Note: Holding onto this issue while we finalize the text.

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as a superadmin, policy_and_abuse, or support admin
# Go to Settings
# Check the boxes for the following settings:
##  “Account creation enabled”
## “Account creation requires invitation”
## “Invite from queue enabled (People can add themselves to the queue and invitations are sent out automatically)”
# Press Update to Save
# Return to the Settings page
# Enter 0 in “Number of people to invite from the queue at once” 
# Press Update to save

h1. What happens

You get an error telling you 

h4. Sorry! We couldn't save this admin setting because:

* Invite from queue number must be greater than 0. To *disable* invites, uncheck the appropriate setting.

Except doing that also disables people’s ability to _add_ themselves to the queue. You have to work around it by setting “How often (in days) should we invite people from the queue” to a high number (this field will accept 0, but 0 currently behaves the same as 1).

h1. What should happen

You should be able to set either “Number of people to invite from the queue at once” or “How often (in days) should we invite people from the queue” (or both of them) to 0 if you want to pause sending invitations while still allowing people to join the queue.

When either/both of these are set to 0:

# [https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests|https://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests] should say: If you have already requested an invitation, you can [check your position on the waiting list|http://localhost:3000/invite_requests/status]. There are currently X people on the waiting list. We aren’t sending invitations right now, but they’ll be back soon. For now, you can still join the waiting list.”
# [http://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests/status|http://test.archiveofourown.org/invite_requests/status] should say: There are currently X people on the waiting list. We are not sending invitations, but you can still check your position on the waiting list.”
## Once you submit your email address, if your invitation has not been sent, the resulting text should say: You are currently number *X* on our waiting list! We aren’t sending invitations right now, but they’ll be back soon. When we start sending them again, this page will tell you when to expect yours.”

When [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6712|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6712|smart-link] is done, only the first paragraph provided for each scenario should appear, and it should not be possible to resend invitations. For ease of reference, the text that should appear:

# *If the user checks the status of their invitation less than 24 hours (*{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}*) after the invitation is initially sent*, the text should say: Your invitation was emailed to this address on [sent at date]. If you can't find it, please check your email spam folder as your spam filters may have placed it there.
# *If the user checks the status of their invitation more than 24 hours (*{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}*) after the invitation is initially sent*, the text should say: Your invitation was emailed to this address on [sent at date]. If you can't find it, please check your email spam folder as your spam filters may have placed it there.
# *If the user checks the status of their invitation less than 24 hours (*{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}*) after the invitation is resent*, the text should say: Your invitation was emailed to this address on [sent at date] and resent on [resent at date]. If you can't find it, please check your email spam folder as your spam filters may have placed it there.
# *If the user checks the status of their invitation more than 24 hours (*{{ArchiveConfig.HOURS_BEFORE_RESEND_INVITATION}}*) after the invitation is resent*, the text should say: Your invitation was emailed to this address on [sent at date] and resent on [resent at date]. If you can't find it, please check your email spam folder as your spam filters may have placed it there.

h1. Notes

A problem for future us: if we _are_ sending invitations, the text says, “We are sending out 1 invitations per day” even when “How often (in days) should we invite people from the queue” is set to 2 or more days.

Summary: Add task to reset word count on works created before prior word count fix task was run
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
If you have a work that

* was written in a script that doesn’t use spaces to indicate words (for our purposes, those are {{CHARACTER_COUNT_SCRIPTS: ["Han", "Hiragana", "Katakana", "Thai"]}})
* *and* was posted before [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2046|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2046|smart-link] 
* *and* was not labeled with one of the languages mentioned in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2378|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2378|smart-link] (Chinese (zh), Japanese (ja), Russian (ru), Thai (th)) when the task was run on December 23, 2018

*then* the word count for the work is still incorrect _unless_ the work creator has edited the work text since December 23, 2018.

To fix this once and for all, we want a version of the rake task in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2378|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-2378|smart-link] that will run on *all works* created before December 25, 2018 (let’s give it a little buffer to allow for the possibility it may have taken some time for the original task to complete), regardless of language. 

h1. Testing

A database admin should break the word count on two works: one created before December 25, 2018, and one created after. They should be works that use the {{CHARACTER_COUNT_SCRIPTS}} .

Word counts can be broken like so:

{noformat}chapter.update_column(:word_count, 9001)
work.update_column(:word_count, 9001){noformat}

Check the staging site to make sure the blurb and meta for the works now display the broken word counts.

Then run the task and check the blurbs and meta again to confirm that:

Summary: Skins that are not approved for public use can be listed in the chooser
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Create a skin and apply to make it public
## Log in as a user
## Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Skins > Create Site Skin
## Fill in required fields
## Check “Apply to make public”
## Save
## Log out
# Approve the skin and add it to the chooser
## Log in as a superadmin
## Skins > Approval Queue
## Locate the skin from Step 1
## Check “Approve”
## Press “Update” to save
## Skins > Approved Skins
## Locate the skin from Step 1
## Check “Cache” and “Chooser”
## Press “Update” to save
# Unapprove the skin and remove it from the chooser
## Skins > Approved Skins
## Locate the skin from Step 1
## Check “Unapprove,” “Uncache,” and “Not in chooser”
## Press “Update” to save

h1. What happens

The skin is unapproved and uncached, but stays in the chooser in the footer.

(Bonus fun, the update message will list the skin name once for each of its attributes that you update. In this case, the skin gets unapproved and uncached, so it says “The following skins were updated: Skin Title, Skin Title”)

h1. What should happen

Skins should absolutely not be in the chooser if they are not approved for public use. 

Either you should get an error telling you to remove it from the chooser before you unapprove it, or unapproving a skin should also remove it from the chooser. 

(We _could_ make it so skins included in the chooser also have to be {{official: true}}, but it’s better to get the {{in_chooser}} column set to {{false}} so re-approving the skin in the future doesn’t put it right back into the chooser.)

h1. Notes

{{official}} is the name of the column controlled by approving/unapproving skins.

The database column {{in_chooser}} is not getting updated; it's not a simple case of caching.

Featuring/unfeaturing has the same bug: if you try to unapproved it and unfeature it at the same time, it only unapproves. The {{featured}} column remains set to {{true}}.

Summary: Work original creator timestamp gets reset
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Brian Austin
Description:
In testing [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6798|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6798|smart-link], I noticed that the updated_at timestamp for {{WorkOriginalCreator}} is getting reset sometimes to a too-recent date. Steps to reproduce seem to be

# Orphan a work as its creator
# Some time later, view that work as an admin
# Check the original creator record in the database, and see that the timestamp is now later than it should be

In my opinion, we should just update to use a non-Rails controlled field to avoid the pitfalls of using {{updated_at}}, which can be changed unexpectedly.

Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.

Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce

This issue appears to happen when:

* the length of the admin post is shorter than the length of the side bar *and*

## About > News

The grey byline section of the first comment gets very tall and the icon is displayed much lower than it should be.

The first comment should be normal.

Happens way more often on staging than production, since real admin posts tend to be longer.

Summary: "Automatically flagged as spam" email gets sent when hiding works manually
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: lydia-theda
Description:
When the “Automatically hide spam works” setting is turned off, works flagged as spam are marked “Akismet Reported As Spam: true”, but not hidden and no email is sent. If that work is later manually hidden by an admin using the “Hide Work” button, the user receives the “flagged as spam” email instead of the “hidden by admin” email. This is misleading because the spam email tells the user their work was “flagged by our automated system as spam and hidden until it can be reviewed by our Policy & Abuse team” when this is not the case.

The “hide work” button should only ever send the “hidden by admin” email regardless of whether the work was flagged by Akismet or not. The “flagged as spam” email should only be sent when the work is automatically hidden (when the setting is on) or when the admin uses the “Mark as spam” button (on the work or from the spam queue).

Summary: Editing a canonical fandom tag that has been nominated in a tag set incorrectly marks the fandom nomination as not parented

Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Create a tag set

## Press “Save changes” – no need to actually make any changes
# Review the nominations
## Follow the “Back to [tag set title”] link from your tag nomination page (the page you’ll be on immediately after submitting your nominations)
## Follow “Review Nominations”

h1. What happens

The name of the nominated fandom will appear in regular (not bold) text, and the tool tip that appears when you hover over it will say, "This is a canonical tag but not associated with the specified fandom” (not “This is a canonical tag“).

Checking the {{TagNomination}} in the database will show {{parented: false}}, e.g.

  id: 6996529,

h1. What should happen

The name of the nominated fandom will appear in bold text, and the tool tip that appears when you hover over it will say, “This is a canonical tag.”

Checking the {{TagNomination}} in the database will show {{parented: true}}, e.g.

{noformat}#<FandomNomination:0x00007f06b6a169b8

*Note: Just leaving this here for posterity. We figured out how to reliably reproduce the bug.*

It _seems_ like the {{set_parented}} callback might not always be running. We recently (AO3-6783, deployed August 13, about a month ago) started skipping it {{if blank_tagname?}}, but as you can see from the examples, the tag name doesn’t appear to be blank, nor do the nominations appear to have been edited. (The tags also appear to have had their parents before the nominations were created. So it’s not a case of someone nominating the fandom before it had a media.) 

But the timing is suspicious, and I checked the code inside the {{set_parented}} callback, and confirmed it _should_ be running [the code|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/f607097eacad333ee18fc92d3578026802f801e0/app/models/tagset_models/tag_nomination.rb#L74-L78] that sets {{parented = true}}

get_parent_tagname)

* it only happens if the nominated {{tagname}} has parentheses
* it only happens if the tag has a different {{sortable_name}} than the nominated {{tagname}}
* it only happens if the tag has syns
* it matters how many times the tag is nominated (e.g., it only happens if there is 1 nomination or >1 nomination)

DMCA Policy

The Digital Millennium Copyright Act (DMCA) establishes the procedure the Organization for Transformative Works (OTW) must follow when users of our sites, including the Archive of Our Own (AO3), reproduce copyrighted material without authorization. Specifically, 17 U.S.C. § 512 protects the OTW from potential liability when infringing content is present on our sites.

The OTW will respond promptly to notices of alleged copyright infringement that substantially comply with all legal requirements. However, we believe that transformative fanworks are legal, and we reserve the right to review the allegedly infringing content and independently determine whether it is infringing. If you have any questions about our DMCA Policy, please contact the OTW Legal committee.

Table of Contents

  1. My work was posted on AO3 without my permission. What can I do?
    • Filing a DMCA takedown notice
    • Requirements of a DMCA takedown notice
    • DMCA takedown process
  2. I was notified that my work was removed from AO3 due to a DMCA takedown notice. What can I do?

    • Requirements of a DMCA counternotice
    • DMCA counter-notification process
  3. Repeat offenses

My work was posted on AO3 without my permission. What can I do?

If you encounter content on AO3 that you believe infringes on your copyright, you have the following options:

  • Submit an Abuse report: Abuse reports are evaluated by the Policy & Abuse committee for violations of the AO3 Terms of Service, and held to a very high standard of confidentiality. When submitting an Abuse report about copyright infringement, you must provide a link to the violating content on AO3 and clearly identify the original source in your report description. For more information, please refer to the Terms of Service FAQ.
  • File a DMCA takedown notice: DMCA takedown notices can only be filed by the copyright owner or someone legally authorized to act on their behalf. DMCA notices must be sent to the OTW's designated agent and comply with all legal requirements. DMCA notices are not subject to confidentiality. The OTW reserves the right to make public all DMCA notices that we receive, though some information may be redacted for privacy.

Please do not submit an Abuse report if you intend to file a DMCA notice. Submitting both an Abuse report and a DMCA notice about the same content may delay the processing of both requests.

Filing a DMCA takedown notice

To initiate a formal DMCA takedown request, contact the OTW's designated agent using the Legal committee's contact form, via email to legal@transformativeworks.org, or by mailing a letter to:

Organization for Transformative Works
228 Park Ave S #18156
New York, NY 10003-1502
Attention: Legal

We prefer to receive DMCA requests through the contact form or by email.

Requirements of a DMCA takedown notice

The takedown notice must substantially comply with the requirements of 17 U.S.C. § 512(c)(3)(A). You are also required to consent to the jurisdiction of a United States court. The legal requirements of a valid DMCA takedown notice include:

  1. your physical or electronic signature;
  2. your contact information;
  3. identification of the copyrighted work being infringed upon (for example, a URL or publication listing);
  4. the URL(s) of the specific content on our site that you believe to be infringing;
  5. a statement that you have a good-faith belief that the use of the content is not authorized by the copyright owner(s), their agent, or the law;
    1. a statement, made under penalty of perjury, that you are authorized to act on behalf of the copyright owner; and
    2. a statement that the information you have provided is accurate.

Per 17 U.S.C. § 512(f), you may be subject to liability if you knowingly and materially misrepresent your claim that the content infringes on your copyright.

DMCA takedown process

If the OTW receives a DMCA takedown notice that fulfills all legal requirements, we will remove the content once we review the validity of the infringement claim.

When the content is removed from AO3, the information you provided in the DMCA takedown notice will be forwarded to the owner of the account responsible for posting the content. We may also send a redacted version of the DMCA takedown notice to Lumen and other third parties at our discretion.

If the account owner believes that their content does not infringe upon your copyright, they may file a DMCA counternotice disputing the takedown. The account owner can file a DMCA counternotice at any point after the content has been removed; there is no time limit.

If the OTW receives a valid DMCA counternotice, we will make reasonable efforts to notify you. You will have 10 business days to file a lawsuit to prevent the restoration of the content. If you do not notify us within 10 business days that you have filed a lawsuit, we will allow the content to be restored in accordance with 17 U.S.C. § 512(g)(2)(B)-(C).

I was notified that my work was removed from AO3 due to a DMCA takedown notice. What can I do?

Copyright infringement and plagiarism are violations of Sections II.D and II.E of our Terms of Service, respectively. For more information, please refer to our Terms of Service FAQ.

If the OTW receives a valid DMCA takedown notice for content you uploaded to AO3, we will remove the content and notify you by email. We may also send a redacted version of the DMCA takedown notice to Lumen and other third parties at our discretion.

If your content was removed due to a DMCA takedown notice, you cannot reupload or repost the content unless you have filed a DMCA counternotice to dispute the takedown. If you reupload or repost the content without filing a DMCA counternotice, we may suspend your account.

Filing a DMCA counternotice

If you believe that your content does not infringe on the copyright owner's rights, you can file a DMCA counternotice to dispute the takedown. By filing a counternotice, you are indicating that you are willing to defend your use of the original copyrighted material in court if the party who submitted the original takedown notice chooses to pursue legal action against you.

If you are considering whether to file a DMCA counternotice, we recommend that you contact an intellectual property lawyer licensed to practice in your jurisdiction, so that you are aware of your legal rights and obligations. You can also review the Lumen DMCA Explanation and FAQ.

To initiate a formal DMCA counter-notification request, contact the OTW's designated agent using the Legal committee's contact form, via email to legal@transformativeworks.org, or by mailing a letter to:

228 Park Ave S #18156
New York, NY 10003-1502
Attention: Legal

We prefer to receive DMCA requests through the contact form or by email.

You can file a DMCA counternotice at any point after your content has been removed; there is no time limit.

Requirements of a DMCA counternotice

The counternotice must substantially comply with the requirements of 17 U.S.C. § 512(g)(3). You are also required to consent to the jurisdiction of a United States court. The legal requirements of a valid DMCA counternotice include:

  1. your physical or electronic signature;
  2. your name, address, and phone number;
  3. the URL(s) of the content that was removed;
  4. a statement, made under penalty of perjury, that the content was removed due to a mistake or misidentification;
  5. a statement that you consent to the jurisdiction of a U.S. federal court in either:
    1. the district where you live, if you are in the U.S.; or
    2. the district where the OTW is located (Manhattan, New York), if you are not in the U.S.; and
  6. a statement that you will accept service of process from the party who submitted the original takedown notice.

Per 17 U.S.C. § 512(f), you may be subject to liability if you knowingly and materially misrepresent your claim that the content was removed due to a mistake or misidentification.

DMCA counter-notification process

If the OTW receives a valid DMCA counternotice, we will make reasonable efforts to notify the party who submitted the original takedown notice.

The original submitter will have 10 business days to prevent the restoration of your content by filing a lawsuit against you. If the original submitter does not file a lawsuit within 10 business days, the OTW will restore your content (or, if your content has already been deleted, allow you to reupload it) between 10 and 14 business days after we receive the counternotice. We may also send a redacted version of the DMCA counternotice to Lumen and other third parties at our discretion.

Repeat offenses

As required by 17 U.S.C. § 512(i)(1)(A), we may suspend users who repeatedly violate others' copyright. The OTW has the discretion to decide what qualifies as a repeated offense.

When an abuse report is submitted for a work, it should include the user IDs of the work creators in the field {{cf_user_id}}:

* multiple IDs should be separated by a comma *and* listed in ascending numerical order
* a given ID should be listed only once, regardless of how many pseuds the user has on the work

* the IDs of users merely _invited_ to be co-creators should not be included

If the work is an orphaned work, in addition to the above, it should also:

* replace orphan_account’s ID with the placeholder *orphanedwork* (it should come before any other user IDs)

If the work does not exist, the field should include the placeholder text: *deletedwork*

Please note that this should not be transmitted via a hidden field on the abuse report form, but rather handled in the controller/model as appropriate.
