Summary: Rename the Underage warning tag
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
In order to clarify the tag's meaning, the Underage warning should be renamed to Underage Sex. This means first adding a suffix to the existing Underage Sex freeform tag (Tag Wrangling has approved this change).

h2. Renaming the tag

Renaming a tag -- typically done by wranglers in the context of changing diacritics or by admins in the context of suffix swaps -- is already set up to handle any cache expiration or reindexing via Resque.

# The existing tag [+"Underage Sex"+|https://archiveofourown.org/tags/Underage%20Sex] first needs to be renamed "Underage Sex - Freeform.".
# The "Underage" warning tag needs to be renamed "Underage Sex."

We will create rake tasks to handle these steps. While we know "Underage Sex" is a freeform on production, the task for renaming it should be able to handle it regardless of type (e.g., if it's a relationship tag, it should rename it to "Underage Sex - Relationship" instead).

h2. Code changes

These changes appear to relate to tests and new archives.

# The [+WARNING_CHAN_TAG_NAME config variable+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/config/config.yml#L227] needs to be changed from "Underage" to "Underage Sex."
# Tests need to be updated. After making the following changes, run the test suite and fix any failures.
## The [+warning created in the tag fixtures+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/test/fixtures/tags.yml#L5631-L5643] needs to be renamed Underage Sex.
## The [+warning created in the tag_seed.json file+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/script/gift_exchange/tag_seed.json#L79] needs to be renamed Underage Sex.
## The [+content used by the work import steps+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/features/step_definitions/work_import_steps.rb#L5] needs to use the new Underage Sex warning.
## The [+content used by the API helper tests+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/spec/controllers/api/api_helper.rb#L18] needs to use the new Underage Sex warning.

h2. Text changes

Text needs to be updated in several places.

# [+https://ao3.org/help/work-search-text-help.html+|https://ao3.org/help/work-search-text-help.html] ([+https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/public/help/work-search-text-help.html#L34-L35+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/public/help/work-search-text-help.html#L34])
## ""Character A/Character B" Underage Mature OR Explicit" should be ""Character A/Character B" "Underage Sex" (Mature OR Explicit)"
## "an Underage warning" should be "an Underage Sex warning"
# [+https://ao3.org/help/warning-help.html+|https://ao3.org/help/warning-help.html]
## "and Underage" should be "and Underage Sex" ([+https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/public/help/warning-help.html#L7+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/public/help/warning-help.html#L7])
## "Underage:" should be "Underage Sex:" ([+https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/public/help/warning-help.html#L53+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/public/help/warning-help.html#L53]) 
# [+https://ao3.org/first_login_help+|https://ao3.org/first_login_help]   ([+https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/app/views/home/first_login_help.html.erb#L125-L126+|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/1bdb4441e193ca269bb31f8c4a78ab5db7d1b663/app/views/home/first_login_help.html.erb#L125-L126]) 
## "and "Underage"" should be "and "Underage Sex"" 

h2. Testing notes

In addition to ensuring the text changes mentioned above are present...

h3. *Before* the warning is renamed:

# Bookmark a work that has the Underage warning.
# Bookmark a series that has the Underage warning.
# Bookmark a work and add the Underage tag as a bookmarker's tag.
# Create a tag set using the Underage warning.
# Create a gift exchange that uses the tag set you made. It should be set to match on warnings.
# Get at least two people to sign up for the gift exchange and use Underage in their sign-ups. Leave sign-ups open.

h3. After the warning is renamed:

# Access the sign-up you created for the gift exchange and make sure it says Underage Sex.
# Using another account that hasn't already signed up for the exchange, access the sign-up form and ensure that it says Underage Sex and that you can create a sign-up using the tag.
# Make sure matching for the gift exchange works as expected.

The rake tasks should be run in the following order: 

* {{bundle exec rake After:add_suffix_to_underage_sex_tag }}
* {{bundle exec rake After:rename_underage_warning}}

Summary: Front end issues aplenty when viewing tags in tag sets
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce

We’re going to need to make two tag sets that will cover all of the possible display variations. The first steps to making either tag set are the same:

# Log in
# Browse > Tags > Tag Sets > New Tag Set
# Fill in a title
# Check “Visible tag list?” in case you need to look at it with a different account or show it to someone else

Note that for most of these steps, it doesn’t actually have to be a canonical tag, just one with the proper associations – so canonical is easier.

h2. Tag Set #1

Example: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_sets/745|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_sets/745] 

Most tag sets group fandoms under their media categories, but this one will cover a special case where fandoms are their own top-level sections. This happens when we extrapolate the fandoms from character and/or relationship tags rather than explicitly entering a fandom. If we have tags that don’t belong to any fandom at all, a “(No linked fandom - might need association)” section is added.

We’re also going to create an Additional Tags section with multiple sections inside it.

# Under Add Fandoms, *do not enter anything*. 
# Under Add Characters, enter 1 canonical character and 1 brand new character tag
# Under Add Additional Tags, enter at least 31 additional tags. You can paste this list: 
Action/Adventure, Alternate Universe, Alternate Universe - Battlestar Galactica Fusion, Alternate Universe - Canon, Alternate Universe - Canon Divergence, Alternate Universe - Gate is Broken, Alternate Universe - Gender Changes, Alternate Universe - Historical, Alternate Universe - Modern Setting, Alternate Universe - Pirate, Childhood, Episode: s07e16 Election Day Part I, Fluff, Fluff and Angst, Friends to Lovers, Friendship, Missing Scene, Pillow Talk, Pirates, Podfic, Podfic & Podficced Works, Podfic Available, Podfic Length: 0-10 Minutes, Podfic Length: 10-20 Minutes, Podfic Length: 20-30 Minutes, Podfic Length: 30-45 Minutes, Politics, Romance, Romantic Comedy, Science Fiction, Smut, Taco Bell
# Press Submit

h2. Tag Set #2

Example: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_sets/751|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_sets/751]

This tag set will have fandoms listed under media categories; rating, warning, and category sections, an unassociated characters and relationships section, and a small section of additional tags.

# Under Add Fandoms, enter some canonical fandoms from different media. It doesn’t have to be a lot, but make sure at least one medium has multiple fandoms, e.g. 3 TV Shows and 1 Video Game.
# Under Add Characters, enter 
## multiple canonical characters from some of the fandoms 
## no characters from other fandoms
## at least one character that doesn’t belong to a fandom you listed in Step 1
# Under Add Additional Tags, enter at least one additional tag (but fewer than 31)
# For the Categories, Ratings, and Warnings sections, press the “All” button on each one to select all the tags
# Press Submit

h2. Combined Tag Sets

Example: [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_sets/show_options?restriction=3103&tag_type=freeform|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tag_sets/show_options?restriction=3103&tag_type=freeform]

There’s another page that uses the same view partials that we should test. You’ll need to make a challenge that uses your tag sets to see it.

# Log in
# Browse > Collections > New Collection
# Fill in required information
# For “Type of challenge, if any,” choose “Prompt Meme” (either option will work)
# Press Submit
# Make sure “Sign-up open?” is checked
# Under “Request Settings,” enter 1 in the Allowed field for each type (for ease)
# Under “Tag Options,” enter the names of both tag sets in “Tag Sets To Use”
# Press Submit
# Follow the “Prompt Form” link in the sidebar
# Follow the “List X Additional Tags” link

h1. What happens

In general,

*  the buttons on the listboxes are misaligned, both with the headings and with each other 
* in fact, they aren’t even buttons – they’re links with a lot of invalid custom attributes, and they should be made into buttons with HTML5 {{data-*}} attributes)
* the heading levels are quite wrong
* the tags should be listed vertically, rather than in comma-separated lists

*Associated updates that will required are as follows:*
Text on work form ([https://archiveofourown.org/works/new|https://archiveofourown.org/works/new]) will need to be updated to:

Tags are comma separated, 150 characters per tag. Fandom, relationship, character, and additional tags must not add up to more than 75. Archive warning, category, and rating tags do not count toward this limit.

*Error messages for too long tag length will also need to be updated to 150:*

h4.

We (Tag Wrangling) are currently consulting with Docs about this change.

22/Dec/24 3:04 AM;557058:baa5f297-c116-4036-bbf1-109f8a7e50a7;Both tag noms as well as tags use the varchar type for the column. Based on the [mysql docs on storage size|https://dev.mysql.com/doc/refman/8.4/en/storage-requirements.html#data-types-storage-reqs-strings], changing the limit from 255 to 150 does not affect the overhead of storing the length of the string: It’s 2 bytes in both cases because the db uses {{utf8mb4}} which means each character needs up to 4 bytes. So 150 chars would be 600 bytes, which already larger than the largest length that can be stored in one byte.

I found some info that runtime performance is impacted by the limit of the varchar type but it’s not much info: [https://stackoverflow.com/questions/1962310/importance-of-varchar-length-in-mysql-table/1962329#1962329|https://stackoverflow.com/questions/1962310/importance-of-varchar-length-in-mysql-table/1962329#1962329|smart-link], [https://mariadb.com/kb/en/varchar/#for-storage-engine-developers|https://mariadb.com/kb/en/varchar/#for-storage-engine-developers|smart-link] So we could potentially gain some performance by limiting the length of {{tagnames}} and then also {{parent_tagnames}} and {{synonym}} for nominations.

However, similar to the down migration for tag names, we’d need to be sure that we do not have more characters than the new limit in the columns. Considering this migration would be a risk (making the type smaller is always harder than making it larger), would have no impact on storage size and may only have a small impact on performance, I don’t think it is worth the hassle. If we want to do migrations to improve database performance, adding (unique) indexes for slow queries is lower risk and already proven to help a lot.

Description:
Traffic grows enough that recently we’ve had issues where the application starved memcached of memory.

{quote}Rack::Timeout is not a solution to the problem of long-running requests, it's a debug and remediation tool. App developers should track rack-timeout's data and address recurring instances of particular timeouts, for example by refactoring code so it runs faster or offsetting lengthy work to happen asynchronously.{quote}

The gem can be configured by setting {{RACK_TIMEOUT_SERVICE_TIMEOUT}} environment variable, so no extra code is required beyond adding the dependency.

Summary: Add puma_worker_killer gem
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Brian Austin
Description:
To temporarily address performance issues with puma (while we are waiting on new hardware), we want to do rolling restarts of puma appservers. This can be accomplished with [https://github.com/zombocom/puma_worker_killer|https://github.com/zombocom/puma_worker_killer|smart-link] .

* PUMA_ROLLING_RESTART_SPLAY = 720

Details about configuring the library [https://github.com/zombocom/puma_worker_killer?tab=readme-ov-file#configure|https://github.com/zombocom/puma_worker_killer?tab=readme-ov-file#configure|smart-link]

Summary: Upgrade to Rails 7.1
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Bilka
Description:
Rails 7 drops out of security support in April, so let's upgrade to Rails 7.1! From the release notes, some significant changes are:

* Generate Dockerfiles for new Rails applications
* Add ActiveRecord::Base.normalizes
* Add ActiveRecord::Base.generates_token_for
* Add perform_all_later to enqueue multiple jobs at once
* Composite primary keys
* Introduce adapter for Trilogy
* Add ActiveSupport::MessagePack
* Introducing config.autoload_lib and config.autoload_lib_once for Enhanced Autoloading
* Active Record API for general async queries
* Allow templates to set strict locals
* Add Rails.application.deprecators
* Support pattern matching for JSON response.parsed_body
* Extend response.parsed_body to parse HTML with Nokogiri
* Introduce ActionView::TestCase.register_parser

Requirements to upgrade, in broad strokes, are described in [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/upgrading_ruby_on_rails.html#upgrading-from-rails-7-0-to-rails-7-1|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/upgrading_ruby_on_rails.html#upgrading-from-rails-7-0-to-rails-7-1|smart-link] .  Furthermore, there are several config changes that can only be done after the initial upgrade.

We also get some new features, which are described in [https://rubyonrails.org/2023/10/5/Rails-7-1-0-has-been-released|https://rubyonrails.org/2023/10/5/Rails-7-1-0-has-been-released|smart-link] .

This is the bulk of the upgrade! Refer to [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/upgrading_ruby_on_rails.html#upgrading-from-rails-7-0-to-rails-7-1|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/upgrading_ruby_on_rails.html#upgrading-from-rails-7-0-to-rails-7-1|smart-link]  for details about this.

*Testing*

Nokogiri had a new version with some breaking changes, so we need to test importing:

* Confirm that posting and importing works with some formatting functions normally. You can compare to what was observed on [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6511|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6511|smart-link]  .
* Tips: For importing, you can use a text post from Tumblr with /mobile at the end of the URL, e.g., [https://sarking.tumblr.com/post/704571626519429120/curds-and-wheyface-i-think-a-fundamental-part/mobile|https://sarking.tumblr.com/post/704571626519429120/curds-and-wheyface-i-think-a-fundamental-part/mobile|smart-link]  . Note that a given URL can only be imported once, so if you use the URL here, it would be kind to delete the work when you’re done, which will let someone else use it.
* For posting, you can use the RTE to apply formatting or paste already formatted text (like the same Tumblr post).

Bookmark search had some issues as well, so we need to test that it functions normally when searching for bookmarkers:

* On [https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search|https://test.archiveofourown.org/bookmarks/search], search for a Bookmarker, both by pseud and by username. The search should return only bookmarks bookmarked by that pseud/user.

The file where the session secret is set for Rails changed so we should do a smoke test to make sure it’s still getting read. See the deploy section for this.

*Deploy*

There are migrations and production config changes.

Ansible needs to be run to upgrade the version of {{rubygems}} installed. Example from staging:

{noformat}ANSIBLE_CONFIG=env/production/ansible.cfg ansible ao3app_staging --become-user ao3app -m shell -a "~/.rvm/bin/rvm rubygems 3.6.0" -u brianaustin -i env/production/inventory -kK --vault-password-file group_vars/vault_pass {noformat}

Migrations should be run pre-deploy. Because of a bug in Departure ([https://github.com/departurerb/departure/issues/110|https://github.com/departurerb/departure/issues/110|smart-link]), they need to run with [advisory locks disabled|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/configuring.html#configuring-a-mysql-or-mariadb-database].

Summary: Reduce the amount of unclean disconnections from the Resque workers to the database
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: james_
Description:
We can see a large number of closed database connections from Resque workers. MaxScale can not save us as they are not calling {{mysql_close()}}. It’s possible that Resque is not correctly wrapping jobs (with [the Rails Executor|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/threading_and_code_execution.html]), meaning Rails' connection pooling management does not happen.

We need to reduce the amount of connections to the database as the connection thundering is causing issues with database stability. This is likely more of an issue now than in the past because ActiveStorage uses more database connections (for example, [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6878|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6878|smart-link]).

Summary: Upgrade to latest version of jQuery and jQuery UI
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
We're currently using jQuery 1.9.0 and jQuery UI 1.10.0, so we very badly need to update to the current versions. (Generally speaking, you don't need jQuery these days, but upgrading is much easier than finding replacement plugins and rewriting our existing code to use vanilla Javascript.)

Because there are [many breaking changes|https://jquery.com/upgrade-guide/3.0/] along the way, the usual course of action would be to use the [migrate plugin|https://github.com/jquery/jquery-migrate], which would require us to first update to jQuery 1.12 or 2.2, and then use the plugin to migrate to 3.x. 

Fortunately, we don't use a lot of complex jQuery, so it turns out we can skip that process and go right to 3.7.1. The main change is we need to replace the [Live Query plugin|https://plugins.jquery.com/livequery/] with a {{MutationObserver}} to keep autocomplete working.

ticking instant has a [branch that upgrades to 3.6.4|https://github.com/tickinginstant/otwarchive/tree/noodling-javascript-barebones]; sarken has a [branch that resolves that branch’s merge conflicts, removes the unrelated changes, and upgrades to 3.7.1|https://github.com/sarken/otwarchive/tree/jquery_update]. 

It will probably need updating again by the time we're ready for it.

h1. Testing

It's not feasible to test every use of JavaScript on the site, so instead, we want to test a sample that should ensure most plugins and functions are tested at least once. 

Please test the following, which I’ve broken up into vaguely themed groups so no one needs to do everything.

Summary: Use ActiveJob for asynchronous indexing
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.

Description:
The Rails Executor can [return acquired db connections to the pool|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/threading_and_code_execution.html#default-callbacks], and asynchronous jobs using Active Job or Action Mailer wrap code in an executor by default.

Sidekiq is one example of a queue backend that [wraps code in an executor|https://github.com/sidekiq/sidekiq/pull/3221], but it looks like Resque (as of 2.6) does not.

We will attempt to address [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6895|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6895|smart-link] by moving one of the more common jobs, [AsyncIndexer|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/671cdb9273be76984a14957bfe7e44f0c7bfd841/app/models/search/async_indexer.rb#L56], to Active Job.

Summary: Remove PseudSweeper class and move callbacks to user and pseud models
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: redsummernight
Description:
When a pseud or a user gets renamed, there are callbacks to update the autocomplete cache, not in the pseud or user models themselves, but in [a cache sweeper|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/ec6c90fc44815a902e0bd738071292887b922b5a/app/sweepers/pseud_sweeper.rb]. While we never actually enabled the cache sweeper in [the Devise controller that creates users|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/ec6c90fc44815a902e0bd738071292887b922b5a/app/controllers/users/registrations_controller.rb], it rarely if ever becomes a noticeable issue. From [~accountid:557058:fa089759-8cd1-4db3-b506-5731a37fd5a6]:

{quote}There’s something a little odd going on with the {{PseudSweeper}}. As I understand it, sweepers are only supposed to add callbacks in those controllers that [explicitly specify|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/ec6c90fc44815a902e0bd738071292887b922b5a/app/controllers/pseuds_controller.rb#L2] {{cache_sweeper :pseud_sweeper}}. But a few days ago I noticed that there’s no line enabling the {{PseudSweeper}} for the {{Users::Registrations}} class, which is where users (and their initial pseud) are actually created. So in theory, no new user accounts will be added to the autocomplete.

In practice, it seems that there’s a bug in the way that the sweepers work: if the server has ever filled a request that involved the {{PseudSweeper}}, then all subsequent requests seem to have the {{PseudSweeper}} enabled as well, regardless of which controller is used. So because all of the unicorn workers have probably served at least one request for the {{PseudsController}} or the {{UsersController}}, that bug effectively cancels out the bug with {{PseudSweeper}} not being enabled for the {{Users::RegistrationsController}}.

But it still would be good to either move the autocomplete changes out of the sweeper and into the Pseud class, or add {{cache_sweeper :pseud_sweeper}} to the {{Users::RegistrationsController}}.{quote}

Let’s delete the sweeper and move the callbacks into the model classes. This way we can also remove the special code to run the cache sweeper in feature tests ([one|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/ec6c90fc44815a902e0bd738071292887b922b5a/features/support/user.rb#L13-L15], [two|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/ec6c90fc44815a902e0bd738071292887b922b5a/features/support/user.rb#L37]), since it’s not run by default.

# Change your user / pseud back to its original name. Make sure that the uncommon name no longer shows up in autocomplete.

Summary: Add TOTP with devise-two-factor
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Brian Austin
Description:
Follow [https://github.com/devise-two-factor/devise-two-factor?tab=readme-ov-file#getting-started|https://github.com/devise-two-factor/devise-two-factor?tab=readme-ov-file#getting-started|smart-link] and [https://www.jamesridgway.co.uk/implementing-a-two-step-otp-u2f-login-workflow-with-rails-and-devise/|https://www.jamesridgway.co.uk/implementing-a-two-step-otp-u2f-login-workflow-with-rails-and-devise/|smart-link] to enable TOTP and backups codes for Admin users. We’ll want to provide secrets via environment variable.

h1. Implementation

h2. 2fa activation

There should be a link to set up two-step verification (the friendlier name we’ll use for 2fa) on the landing page:

!image-20260124-164357.png|width=444,alt="image-20260124-164357.png"!

The text also needs some updating.

{quote}*With great power comes great responsibility.*{quote}

should be removed. The existing log out reminder should be bold instead: 

{quote}*Please remember to log out before resuming your normal site activity!*{quote}

After this, we want a horizontal line to separate the introduction from a new “Account Settings” section. Within a box (like the meta on a work), should appear the admin’s roles, the two-step verification status, and a link to set up two-step verification with an authenticator app.

Clicking on the link should bring the admin to a page to confirm their password:

!image-20260124-164833.png|width=444,alt="image-20260124-164833.png"!

Entering the correct password should bring the admin the page with instructions on setting up two-step verification:

!image-20260124-164939.png|width=444,alt="image-20260124-164939.png"!

After entering the correct 6-digit code, the admin should be presented with the backup codes, for use in case they lose the device that has been set up for two-step verification. Once they acknowledge the backup codes, they should be returned to the admin landing page. Now, the 2fa status should be enabled, and there should be two links: 1) to disable 2fa and 2) to regenerate the backup codes.

h2. Logging in with 2fa

If an admin has 2fa enabled, after entering their username/password, they should be prompted for a 2fa code:

!image-20260124-165355.png|width=444,alt="image-20260124-165355.png"!

_Entering either the code or a backup code should work here_.

h2. Disabling 2fa

Following the link on the admin landing page should prompt the admin for their password. Once entered, 2fa should be disabled and the admin returned to the admin landing page (with a flash message to let them know 2fa was disabled). _Right now, we are not going to require a 2fa code here._

h2. Password Resets

We are not going to require a 2fa code to reset passwords for now. There is a follow-up ticket to do this later: [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-7220|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-7220|smart-link]

Summary: Spam check comments from new users
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
Comments posted by logged in users are not currently checked for spam. 

We’d like to begin spam checking comments from new users on works and admin posts (but not tags).

When submitted to Akismet, these comments should have

* the {{user_role}} set to {{"user"}}, 
* the {{comment_author}} set to the user’s {{login}}, and 
* the {{comment_author_email}} set to the user’s {{email}}.

For now, there should *not* be a way for admins or users to mark individual comments by logged in users as spam. 

_However_, when an admin with the {{policy_and_abuse}} or {{superadmin}} role bans any user for spam, the user’s comments should be submitted to Akismet as spam before deletion. (Note that they should not be marked as spam in our database, partly for efficiency and partly due to [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5002|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5002|smart-link].) This will help train Akismet to recognize logged-in comment spam.

Admins with the {{policy_and_abuse}} or {{superadmin}} role should be able to set the threshold for newness by going to the Settings page. 

The option should be in a new “Content” fieldset, along with the existing options for “Automatically hide spam works” and “Turn off guest comments across the site.” The option should be an input labeled “How old (in days) accounts should be before we stop checking comments for spam.” (Note that the attached mockup does not reflect the desired wording.) It should accept any integer. Entering 0 should disable spam checking of logged in comments, and the field should have a (properly ARIA-associated) footnote that says, “Enter 0 to turn off comment spam checks for all logged in users.” It should initially be set to 0.

h1. Testing

The tl;dr: We’re going to make an account with an email that should always trigger a positive (spam) response from the spam checker. Then we’re going to make sure its comments don’t get marked as spam if the spam check is off, and do get marked as spam (on works and admin posts) when spam checking is on. We’ll also make sure we can spam ban the user.

## follow the “Create an Account!” link on the homepage
## fill in the required information, making sure to use an email address you have access to, and press “Create Account”
## follow the “follow this link to activate your account” link in the activation email
# ✅ Shortly after this is deployed (ie, before anyone might try to update the admin settings) an admin with the {{policy_and_abuse}} or {{superadmin}} role should make sure the initial newness threshold is set correctly.
## log in
## go to Settings
## make sure “How old (in days) accounts should be before we stop checking comments for spam” is set to 0 (don’t change it – you’re just checking the initial value; if it’s not already 0, there’s a problem) 
# An admin with the {{tag_wrangling}} or {{superadmin}} role should make sure our test account is a tag wrangler and can therefore comment on tags:
## log in
## go to Manage Users > Find Users
## search for the user you created in step 1
## check the “Tag Wrangler” checkbox in the appropriate row of the results table and press “Update” to make sure the user has the wrangling role
# ✅  An admin with the {{superadmin}}, {{board}}, {{board_assistants_team}}, {{communications}}, {{support}}, or {{translation}} role should make an admin post to comment on:
## log in
## go to Admin Posts > Post AO3 News
## fill in required fields, make sure logged-in users will be able to comment, and post 
# Log in as the user from Step 1 and ensure the spam check is disabled by commenting just “viagra-test-123” (without the quotation marks) on a tag, an admin post, and a work without getting an error. (You can also try replying to a comment on a work or admin post. This shouldn’t error, either.)
# Using an account that is *not* the user from Step 1, reply to one or all of the comments left in Step 5. Make note of the work, admin post, or tag where you left these replies – we’re going to use these later to make sure we’re not affected by [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5002|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5002|smart-link].)
# An admin with the {{policy_and_abuse}} or {{superadmin}} role should make sure the spam check will run when the user from Step 1 posts a comment:
## log in
## go to Settings
## change “How old (in days) accounts should be before we stop checking comments for spam” to “10” and save

Summary: Admin: Refine subnavigation options on admin posts, wrangling guidelines, FAQs, and known issues
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as an admin with the superadmin role
# Go to these pages under the Admin Posts menu and observe the subnavigation options: AO3 News ({{/admin_posts}}), Archive FAQ ({{/faq}}), Known Issues ({{/known_issues}}), Wrangling Guidelines ({{/wrangling_guidelines}})

h1. What happens

When you have access to all the admin areas, you quickly discover there are way too many items in the subnavigation that don’t relate to the page you’re on:

* {{/admin_posts}} has AO3 News, Post AO3 News, Archive FAQ, Known Issues, Wrangling Guidelines
* {{/faq}} has New FAQ Category, Reorder FAQs, AO3 News, Post AO3 News, Archive FAQ, Known Issues, Wrangling Guidelines
* {{/known_issues}} has AO3 News, Post AO3 News, Archive FAQ, Known Issues, Wrangling Guidelines
* {{/wrangling_guidelines}} has New Wrangling Guideline, Reorder Wrangling Guidelines, AO3 News, Post AO3 News, Archive FAQ, Known Issues, Wrangling Guidelines

When you go to the pages for editing and creating, the situation is similarly unpleasant.

h1. What should happen

The subnavigation should just be the items be relevant to the section (e.g., the FAQ should only have navigation related to the FAQ):

* {{/admin_posts}} and {{/admin_posts/new}} should have AO3 News and Post AO3 News
** {{/admin_posts/###/edit}} should also have Delete Post
* {{/faq}} (or {{/faq?language_id=en}}), {{/faq/new}} , and {{/faq/manage?language_id=en}} should have Archive FAQ, New FAQ Category, Reorder FAQs
** {{/faq/category-name/edit?language_id=en}} should have Reorder Questions in place of Reorder FAQs
** other languages should not have the Reorder items
* {{/known_issues}}, {{/known_issues/new}}, and {{/known_issues/###/edit}} should have Known Issues and New Known Issue Post (the link to {{/known_issues/new}} is currently missing, and while we won't use it, others using otwarchive might find it helpful)
* {{/wrangling_guidelines}} , {{/wrangling_guidelines/new}}, {{/wrangling_guidelines/manage}}, and {{/wrangling_guidelines/###/edit}} should have Wrangling Guidelines, New Wrangling Guideline, Reorder Wrangling Guidelines

This is in addition to any filters (i.e., the language dropdown for FAQs and the language and tag dropdowns for admin posts).

h1. Notes

If you see any {{ul}} elements with {{role="navigation"}}, please remove it and don’t add it to any new ones.

h1. Testing

*Update:* The desired links have been verified by the relevant committees, so as long as the reality matches the issue description, we should be good without requiring each committee to test their respective area. (The committees were actually promised they’d be excused from testing in exchange for verifying the issue, but Docs has volunteered to test anyway 😆 )

Ideally, we’d get one admin who frequently uses an area to check and make sure nothing they actually need has been forgotten by the person writing this issue (hi):

*  a {{communications}} admin would check AO3 News, `
* a {{docs}} admin would check Archive FAQ
* a {{support}} admin would check Known Issues
* a {{tag_wrangling}} admin would check Wrangling Guidelines

Summary: Update autocomplete to treat pipes (|) as delimiters
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Brian Austin
Description:
[~accountid:712020:bb568d1c-045f-4d41-b06d-825ace2cfa5b] noticed that adding pipes (without spaces in particular) to search messes with autocomplete results, as shown in the attached screenshot.

Additionally, folks have observed that adding more pipes (surrounded by other delimiter characters like spaces) can result in increased response times for the autocomplete popup, depending on how many pipes are in the inputted text. So “taylor hebert | skitter” takes longer than “taylor hebert skitter” or “taylor hebert|skitter”. Compared to requests without pipes, the response times are generally up from 3 times longer for fandoms, 5+ for characters and freeforms, 15+ for relationships, and 30+ for all-tag search, which is at least several seconds of delay and really noticeable.

We should be able to add the pipe character to the list of delimiters (characters used to split phrases) [here|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/82f4b30f3a0ba490207ce34edaef6bc97805ef5f/lib/autocomplete_source.rb#L243] to resolve these issues.

*Testing*

# Open the Post new work page, do the following in the “Relationship” field:
# Try inputting “|” (a single pipe) - the autocomplete should say “No suggestions found”
# Try inputting words only separated by a bar with no spaces, e.g. “Taylor|Skitter“ - it should result in some autocomplete suggestions
# Take a search query that has a pipe or multiple, e.g. a character tag like “Taylor Hebert | Skitter | Weaver“
## First try inputting it with the bars removed (“Taylor Hebert Skitter Weaver“), note how long it takes to show autocomplete suggestions (probably less than a second)
## Try inputting it with the bars present, it should take a similar time to search and not weirdly long. If “&;” shows up in the search results, you can ignore it, that’s [a different bug|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6348]

Summary: Manage Items page for collection may show unrelated work instead of bookmark
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.

# Create an open, unmoderated collection
# Add a bookmark to it
# View the approved items on the Manage Items page for the collection: {{https://test.archiveofourown.org/collections/COLLECTIONNAME/items?status=approved}}

*What happens*

The page lists a completely different work.

*What should happen*

The page lists the bookmark that you added.

*Explanation*

The page is showing the work that has the id of the bookmark. As a result, this is difficult to reproduce on production and staging, where new bookmarks have much higher ids than new works and so it can be difficult to get the bookmark id to also be a valid work id. However, this can be tested with an automated test that sets the id of objects so that there is a valid work with the id of the bookmark.

This is a bug with {{includes}} that we can work around by changing the {{:include_for_works}} scope on CollectionItem to be {{{ includes(item: :pseuds) }}}.

*Testing*

No manual QA, automated tests only.

Summary: Avoid unhiding admin-hidden works when un-spamming
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Brian Austin
Description:
Right now, marking a work as not spam (ham) will un-hide the work. This is the correct behavior only if the work was automatically hidden for being spam, not if it was manually hidden by an admin. We want to make it so that admin-hidden works stay hidden even when marked as not spam (either individually or in bulk). 

In addition, if an admin hides and then later unhides a spam-flagged work, the work should be marked as not spam upon being unhidden (because the admin has presumably reviewed the work and confirmed it is no longer in violation of TOS).

This came up when discussing the email fix implemented in [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4947|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/pull/4947|smart-link] , so that may be a good start for inspiration.

h3. *Testing*

# As a PAC admin or superadmin, go to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/settings|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/settings] and check the “Automatically hide spam works” box.
# As a user, post three works (A, B, C) that get flagged as spam (you can try setting the work body to akismet‑guaranteed‑spam per [https://akismet.com/support/getting-started/confirm/|https://akismet.com/support/getting-started/confirm/] ).
## You should receive an "Automatically flagged as spam" email for each work and all three works should be hidden from public view.
# As a PAC admin or superadmin, go to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/settings|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/settings] and uncheck the “Automatically hide spam works” box.
# Repeat step 2. You should not receive any emails and all three works (D, E, F) should be visible to all users.
# As a PAC admin or superadmin, use the "Hide Work" button to admin-hide all six works.
# Go to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/spam|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/spam] and check the "Not Spam" boxes for works A and D, then click "Update Works".
# Use the "Mark Not Spam" button to unspam works B and E.
# Use the "Unhide Work" button to unhide works C and F.

h3. Expected Results:

* After step 2, the user should receive an "Automatically flagged as spam" email for each work and works A-C should be hidden.
* After step 4, the user should not have received any new emails. All six works should be marked “Akismet Reported As Spam: true”, but only works A-C should be hidden.
* After step 5, the user should receive a "Your work has been hidden by the Policy & Abuse team" email for works D-F, but not works A-C (since those were already hidden as spam). All six works should be hidden and marked “Akismet Reported As Spam: true”.
* After step 8:
** All six works should be marked “Akismet Reported As Spam: false”.
** Works A, B, D, and E should be hidden (red-locked) and the buttons at the top should say "Unhide Work" and "Mark As Spam".
** Works C and F should not be hidden and the buttons at the top should say "Hide Work" and "Mark As Spam".

Summary: Incorrect error message when leaving duplicate comment
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as a tag wrangler
# Go to the comment page for a tag, e.g. [https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Testing/comments|https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/Testing/comments] 
# Enter some text in the comment field
# Copy the text to your clipboard – you’re going to need to reenter it exactly the same way
# Press “Comment” to submit the comment
# Scroll back up to the comment box and paste in the text (note: to trigger the error we’re testing with, you have to be commenting on the exact same item; you can’t be replying to a comment or commenting on a different chapter)
# Press “Comment” to submit the comment
# Look at the error page

h1. What happens

The error message says, “This comment has already been left on this work. (It may not appear right away for performance reasons.)”

It would also give this same error if you did this on an admin post or when replying to a comment, since we use the same validation regardless of what the comment is on. 

h1. What should happen

We _could_ make it specify the correct item type, but it would be easier to make it say, “You’ve already left this comment here. (It may not appear right away for performance reasons.)” 

This is also more accurate. [The validation|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/bab383a53b516f48112434bf48da47da73fefbe4/app/models/comment.rb#L71-L75] isn’t checking if anyone left the same comment; it’s checking if _you_ left the comment. And it’s not even checking if you left it on the work, but on the specific item you’re commenting on, e.g., you can reply “Thank you!” to multiple comments on the same work, but you can’t reply “Thank you!” to the same comment twice.

h1. Testing

It’s not necessary to verify the error message on tags, works, admin posts, and comments, since they all use the same validation.

Summary: Admin post drafts and previews
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Overview Admins with certain roles should be able to create and manage draft admin posts, similar to the way users can create draft works. This includes the ability to preview the admin post. It does not include automatic draft deletion. Users should not see any change to the way admin posts work. h2. Translations It should be possible to create drafts that are translations of either posted _or_ draft admin posts. Posting a draft should also post its draft translations.  Deleting a posted _or_ draft admin post with draft translations should delete the draft translations. h1. Database The {{admin_posts}} table will need two new columns: * a {{posted}} boolean column * a {{published_at}} datetime column h2. Existing Data Existing admin posts should have their {{posted}} column set to {{true}} and their {{published_at}} set to their {{created_at}} date. This is necessary to maintain the current behavior for published posts. h1. Roles (AdminPostPolicy) Admins with existing {{POSTING_ROLES}} ({{superadmin}}, {{board}}, {{board_assistants_team}}, {{communications}}, {{support}}, {{translation}}) should be able to create, edit, delete, and post drafts. Admins with {{DRAFTING_ROLES}} ({{policy_and_abuse}}) should be able to create, edit, and delete drafts, but not post them. h1. Public Pages The admin post index and show pages, as well as the news section on the homepage, should be updated to keep the current behavior: * The posts on the page and in the sidebar should only include admin posts where {{posted: true}}. They should be ordered by the {{published_at}} date. * The posts on the page and in the sidebar should be ordered by the {{published_at}} date. * The "Published" date for a post should use {{published_at}}, not {{created_at}}. * The list of translations for a post should only include posts where {{posted: true}}. * The "Preview Post" and "Next Post" links on individual posts should navigate according to the posts' {{published_at}}, not the posts' ID. h1. Admin Pages h2. Admin Navigation "Post AO3 News" should say "Draft AO3 News" for admins with {{DRAFTING_ROLES}}. "AO3 News" should continue to lead to the public index for admins without {{POSTING_ROLES}}. “AO3 News Drafts” should be added after “AO3 News” and it should link to the index of draft admin posts. It should be visible to any admin with a role listed in the {{AdminPostPolicy}} section. h2. Subnavigation The admin post pages share subnavigation, so these changes should apply across all pages. (If [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6940|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6940|smart-link] is done first, or if you’re not a {{superadmin}}, you may see slightly different subnavigation than in the mockups.) * "AO3 News" should continue to lead to the public index for admins without {{POSTING_ROLES}}. * "AO3 News Drafts" should be added between "AO3 News" and "Post AO3 News." It should be visible to any admin with a role listed in the {{AdminPostPolicy}} section. * Moving between "AO3 News" and "AO3 News Drafts" should not remember any language or tag filters you have currently selected. For example, if you have filtered for posts tagged "site changes," when you follow "AO3 News Drafts," you should see all drafts, not just those tagged "site changes." * "Post AO3 News" should say "Draft AO3 News" for admins with {{DRAFTING_ROLES}}. h2. Sidebar For simplicity, the sidebar should always link to the most recently published admin posts. h2. Index of Posted Admin Posts [+https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin_posts+|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin_posts] !news_drafts_posted_index.png|width=100%,alt="Admin index of published admin posts. Summary: Line breaks in page title and description meta tag lead to awkward link previews on other sites
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce

Paste a link from AO3, e.g. a news post, onto a site like Bluesky or Tumblr that generates automatic link previews.

h1. What happens

On some sites, the link preview has the page title broken across lines, e.g. the news post title will be on one line, the | character on the next, and then the site name after that. 

On other sites, it might have extra space between parts (Bitly is good at that), like {{Page Title           |          Archive of Our Own}}

Additionally, some sites display the content of the description meta tag, and break _that_ into two lines as well (as seen in the [bit.ly|http://bit.ly] screen shot below).

!Screenshot 2025-04-03 at 5.08.57 PM.png|width=535,height=166,alt="A link preview with the post title on one line, followed by I... on the second."!

h1. What should happen

It should be on one line that can be wrapped or truncated as needed by whoever is generating the link preview.

h1. Notes

This happens because it’s not stripping the line breaks from the page title or the description meta tag. If you view the page source (which is what you’ll have to do on staging to test this, since you won’t be able to link to it), you see they look like this:

    Organization for Transformative Works" />

<title>
          
          Admin Posts
        |
        Archive of Our Own
    </title>{noformat}

(Note: I do mean page source. Depending on the browser, using the inspector may strip the line breaks and display it as, e.g., {{<title>Admin Posts | Archive of Our Own</title>}} unless you edit the node.)

That happens because the code in application.html.erb is like this:

{noformat}    <meta name="description" content="An Archive of Our Own, a project of the
    Organization for Transformative Works" />
    
    <title>
      <% if defined?(@page_title) %>
        <%= @page_title %>
      <% else %>
        <% if defined?(@page_subtitle) %>
          <%= @page_subtitle %>
        <% else %>
          <%= controller.action_name == "index" ? "" : process_title(controller.action_name) %>
          <%= controller.action_name == "index" ? process_title(controller.controller_name) : process_title(controller.controller_name.singularize) %>
        <% end %>
        |
        <%= ArchiveConfig.APP_NAME  %>
      <% end %>
    </title>{noformat}

The best fix would probably involve putting the page title logic in a {{browser_page_title}} helper.

It would be a good idea to check that the browser page titles on the following pages display as usual in your browser:

* a work, logged in and out, ideally with and & or < in the title
* an admin post, ideally with an & or < in the title

Description:
A lot of feature tests need a work to post comments on, bookmark, edit or similar. Many times, that work has no requirements besides a specific title and author. Description:
h1. What happens

If you attempt to access the tag cloud ({{/tags}} or {{/tags?show=random}}) when the tag named in {{ArchiveConfig.FANDOM_NO_TAG_NAME}} doesn’t exist, you’ll get a 500 error.

h1. What should happen

Instead of a 500 error, it would be better if the page loaded but did not display any tags.

Because this is unlikely to be something you see in reality, we can keep this simple: there’s no need to change any text or navigation on the page. We can cope with it saying “These are some tags…” and then showing nothing.

h1. Reproducing in dev

To see this in action, use your {{local.yml}} to set {{FANDOM_NO_TAG_NAME}} to a tag that doesn’t exist in your dev environment, restart your server, and try to go to [https://localhost:3000/tags|https://localhost:3000/tags]. You’ll get a 500 error:

{noformat}NoMethodError in TagsController#index
undefined method `children' for nil:NilClass
Extracted source (around line #35):
33 else 
34   no_fandom = Fandom.find_by_name(ArchiveConfig.FANDOM_NO_TAG_NAME)
35   @tags = no_fandom.children.by_type('Freeform').first_class.limit(ArchiveConfig.TAGS_IN_CLOUD){noformat}

You could also update this test added in [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6963|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6963|smart-link] to remove the line that creates the tag:

h1. Testing notes

* log in as an admin with the {{tag_wrangling}} or {{superadmin}} role, go to the edit page for the No Fandom tag ({{https://test.archiveofourown.org/tags/No%20Fandom/edit}}), and rename it to something else (please don’t do this; it will probably cause a cascade of issues)

However, I’d say automated tests are enough for this.

However, it should use a different limit than the comment moderation threshold, configurable in the {{ArchiveConfig}}.

Furthermore, we'd like to exclude comments from spam checking if the user is commenting on/replying to comments/editing comments [on their own work|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/5fbbad0ca130cc382a9593fedf989f9e71ec18fb/app/models/comment.rb#L409-L412].

Summary: Support form notices
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Brian Austin
Description:
h1. Background

Support would like to have quickly editable text on the /support page that Support admins can quickly change in reaction to changing site events, without having to close the Support form entirely. These will be called “notices”, although the share some characteristics with the site-wide banners functionality.

h1. Implementation

There are two pieces: displaying the notices to users, and giving admins the ability to manage the notices.

h2. User-Facing

Banners should be displayed, with a configurable existing class (notice, caution, error), right under the information about what languages we can provide support in.

!support_notice.png|width=325,alt="support_notice.png"!

If there is no banner marked active, the banner would not display a placeholder.

h2. Admin-Facing

A new table will need to be created to store these notices. It should be called {{support_notices}}, with the model being called {{SupportNotice}}. This can be structured the same as the [existing admin_banners table|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/7da89d39ecc5aa70fb8281b54ab9dc6492ccae4a/db/schema.rb#L67].

We need to create new routes:

# {{/admin/notices/support}} that points to an index of all Support notices, similar to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/banners|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/banners]
# {{/admin/notices/support/new}} for a form to create new notices. This can be modeled on [https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/banners/new|https://test.archiveofourown.org/admin/banners/new], although the types should be Notice, Caution, Error. Notice should be the default.
# {{/admin/notices/support/:support_notice_id/edit}} to update the support notice. (This will also require the corresponding update route)
# A route to delete a notice

There needs to be a new item on the admin menu, next to banners, called “Support Notices”, which links to {{/admin/notices/support}}. This menu should only be visible to admins with the superadmin and support roles, and all of the new routes should display an error if an admin without one of those roles attempts to access them.

When an admin creates, updates, or deletes an support form notice, the action should be logged as an admin activity: the date, admin name, action (i.e., update support notice, create support notice, destroy support notice), and target (Support Notice ID) should be recorded, and the summary should contain the notice text (because notices can be deleted). For updates, the summary should contain the new notice text, not the old.

h1. Deploy notes

This has a migration {{rails db:migrate:up VERSION=20251215194643}} and needs a skin recache.

h1. Testing

# An admin with a superadmin or support role creates a notice for each of the types listed above and marks it active. Then, at least one guest and one registered user open the support form to make sure the notice is in the right place and styled properly.
# An admin with a superadmin or support role marks the notice(s) as inactive. Accessing the support form should not show any notice (it looks the same as on production AO3).

Summary: Add suggested fandoms to a tag via checkbox
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in as a tag wrangler (you can use testy on staging)
# Post a work with at least two fandom tags and a new character, relationship, or additional tag (it doesn’t _have_ to be new, but it’s a tiny bit easier for these directions)
# From the meta of your newly posted work, follow the link to your new tag’s landing page
# Follow the Edit link

h1. What happens

There is a list of Suggested Fandoms that is just a comma-separated list of tags.

!suggested_fandoms_current.png|width=91.66666666666667%,alt="The current Suggested Fandoms area, which is a list of links to tags."!

h1. What should happen

The list of Suggested Fandoms should be a listbox full of checkboxes, like the list of fandoms on the tag, but it should say “Check to add” instead of “Check to remove” and there should not be an autocomplete section.

Since noncanonical fandoms cannot be added as parents, the checkbox would ideally be disabled for them, and the grey gradient area around the checkbox would be flat grey ({{#ccc}}) .

If that’s not possible, when you check a noncanonical fandom, you should experience a similar error to the one you get when entering a noncanonical fandom manually: you are taken to {{/tags/TAG%20NAME}}, which has an error that says, “Cannot add association to ‘FANDOM': Parent tag is not canonical.” Ideally, any fandoms that errored will be unchecked and you’ll only have to press “Save changes” to actually finish adding the valid canonical fandoms.

Other than that, the behavior should generally be the same: 

* the name of the fandom tag should be a link to its edit page, 
* adding a fandom should remove it from the Suggested Fandoms section, and
* the Suggested Fandoms section should not be present if there are no suggested fandoms.

Summary: Add tag category to tag comment emails

Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce

This applies to multiple emails, so the instructions are a bit long. You’ll need to use two accounts with the tag_wrangler role, and you’ll need to be able to access the email for each.

# Log in as WranglerA
# Make sure you are assigned a fandom
## Hi, username! > Tag Wrangling
## If you have fandoms listed on the page, make a note of the fandom and skip to Step 3. If you _don’t_ have any fandoms listed on the page, follow the Wranglers link in the sidebar
## Under “Assign fandoms to yourself,” choose a canonical fandom tag from the dropdown
## Press “Assign”
## Return to your wrangling page (Hi, username! > Tag Wrangling)
# Leave a comment on the tag from Step 2 – you’re going to need to reply to this later
## In the Fandom column, follow the link to the fandom’s wrangle page
## Follow the comment link (text will vary depending on how many comments are on the tag) 
## Note the URL for future steps
## Fill in the comment form on the top of the page and press “Comment” to post the comment
# Log out
# Log in as WranglerB
# Make sure you’re set up to receive copies of your own comments via email
## Hi, username! > My Preferences
## Uncheck “Turn off copies of your own comments.”
## Press “Update” 
# Leave a comment on WranglerA’s fandom tag from Step 2
## Go to the tag comment page using the URL from Step 3c
## Fill in the comment form on the top of the page and press “Comment” to post the comment and send two emails: 
### “Comment you left on the tag [Tag Name]” to WranglerB (comment_sent_notification)
### “Comment on the tag [Tag Name]” to WranglerA (comment_notification)
## Use the “Edit” button to change your comment and trigger two emails:
### “Comment you left on the tag [Tag Name]” to WranglerB – this is the same comment_sent_notification email as in Step 7bi, so you won’t need to test anything in this step
### “Edited comment on the tag [Tag Name” to WranglerA (edited_comment_notification)
## Use the “Reply” button on WranglerA’s comment from Step 3 to leave a reply and trigger two more emails:
### “Reply you left to a comment on the tag [Tag Name]” to WranglerB (comment_reply_sent_notification)
### “Reply to your comment on the tag [Tag Name]” to WranglerA (comment_reply_notification)
## Use the “Edit” button to change your comment and trigger two emails
### “Reply you left to a comment on the tag [Tag Name]” to WranglerB – this is the same comment_reply_sent_notification email you got in Step 7di, so you don’t need to test it a second time
### “Edited reply to your comment on the tag [Tag Name]” to WranglerA (edited_comment_reply_notification)

h1. What happens 

At the top of each email is some text that includes the phrase “on the tag [Tag Name].” 

h1. What should happen

It should say “on the [Tag Category] tag [Tag Name].”

h1. Coding notes

In a total change of pace, please don’t i18n these emails as part of this. Let’s keep it straightforward to test/review.

h1. Testing notes

It would be a good idea to test multiple types of tags to make sure the category is correct.

Summary: Use CommentMailer when sending comment emails to admins

Description:
When we send comment notifications to the admin email address, we use {{AdminMailer.comment_notification}} and {{AdminMailer.edited_comment_notification}} and their corresponding templates. 

The templates are duplicates of the ones for {{CommentMailer}}.  

We’d like to consolidate the code for comment notifications and use {{CommentMailer}} and its templates instead.

# Be subscribed to the mailing list that gets notifications of comments on admin posts
# Log in as an admin with one of the following roles: superadmin, board, board_assistants_team, communications, support, translation
# Admin Posts > Post AO3 News
# Fill in required fields
# Check “Enable comment moderation”
# Set “Who can comment on this news post” to “Registered users and guests can comment” (you can also use “Registered users only” – the important thing is registered users can comment and therefore edit their comments)
# Press “Post”
# Make note of the URL of the news post
# In another browser or an incognito/private window, log in
# Go to  the news post URL from step 7
# Fill in some comment text
# Press “Comment”
# Follow the “Edit” link
# Make some changes
# Press “Update” to save

After steps 11 and 14, the admin email address should get emails. 

The individual admin who posted the admin post should _not_ get any emails.

The email for step 11:

username (Registered User) left the following comment on Admin Post Title:

Comment text.

Posted: 2025-05-14 06:23:57 UTC

Comments on this news post are moderated and will not appear until approved.

Review comments on Admin Post Title
Go to the thread starting from this comment
Read all comments on Admin Post Title{quote}

Last edited: 2025-05-14 06:24:11 UTC

Review comments on Admin Post Title

We just want to confirm that the email is still the same and we didn’t somehow completely eliminate the note about comment moderation.

Creator: Brian Austin
Description:
The old version of Reversi has a few problems:

* It’s disorganised
* It has more visual bugs compared to the default skin
* Updating it is annoying
* The name is confusing now that the rest of the web has standardised on terms like “dark mode”

Sarken has the code in [https://github.com/sarken/otwarchive/tree/rewrite_reversi|https://github.com/sarken/otwarchive/tree/rewrite_reversi|smart-link] , and since [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6232|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-6232|smart-link] is done, we should be ready to PR it.

h1. Deploy Notes

* This will require logging in as AO3_ADT and creating three skins as described in the README, and then logging in as an admin with the superadmin role and approving the skins before actually deploying the Archive code. *UPDATE:* Three skeleton skins (i.e., skins with placeholder CSS and nothing else) were created on June 23, since we needed the skin IDs for the news post.
** It will be necessary for a database admin to rename the existing skin with the title “Dark Mode,” which belongs to a user. Then AO3_ADT can be used to rename the skin currently titled “Dark Mode (Rename Me).”
** *For each skin*, you’ll have to provide a preview image and check “Apply to make public.” While everything will work if you only apply to make Dark Mode public, admins will not be able to edit Dark Mode - Site or Dark Mode - Midsize, which contain the actual CSS. Please use the first line of the README as the Description text for Dark Mode (you can skip description text for the other two. Because they’ll be set to “parent only,” their blurbs will not be listed anywhere except AO3_ADT’s user skin page.)
*** *UPDATE:* Preview images have been attached.
** Then you’ll need to log in as an admin with the superadmin role and approve all three skins from the Approval Queue page. From the Approved Skins page, you’ll need to check the “Chooser,” “Featured,” and “Cache” options. 
*** Should we check “Chooser” *after* the deploy to ensure the skin is cached before people see it in the footer and try to use it?
*** It’s very possible you won’t be able to load the Approval Queue. If you can, you might not be able to see the “Approve” checkbox in certain browsers without editing the page source to remove the fieldset around the table. Realistically, it will be easier to approve the three skins from the database.
*** Do we want to change the skin author from AO3_ADT to nil? (We use nil for Reversi, Snow Blue, and Low Vision Default because the skins were attached to a volunteer’s personal AO3 account, which resulted in people commenting on the volunteer’s works to ask them about the skins. Summary: Hidden inputs get keyboard focus in Safari
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce

Note: The kudos button is just a handy example here; this problem can also be seen in other places where we have hidden inputs, like the inbox on the homepage.

# In Safari on MacOS on a device with a keyboard, ensure that you have “Press Tab to highlight each item on a webpage” enabled in the [Safari settings|https://dequeuniversity.com/mac/keyboard-access-mac]
# Access a work you don’t own
# Use the Tab key to navigate through the focusable elements to the Kudos button (faster version: scroll down to the comment field, click in it to put your focus there, and use Tab + Shift to navigate backwards)

h1. What happens

If you’ve used Tab, your keyboard focus will vanish for three presses between the button right before Kudos (probably Top or Next Chapter) and the Kudos button.

If you’re going backwards and using Tab + Shift, it will vanish for three presses after landing on the Kudos button but before moving to the button before it (which might be Next Chapter or Top).

h1. What should happen

You should never lose focus! It should go straight to the Kudos button.

h1. Notes

This happens because we accidentally override user agents' {{display: none;}} style on {{input[type="hidden"]}} when we do things like {{.actions input { bunch of styles including display: inline-block; }}}.

Summary: ActiveStorage::FileNotFoundError for some icons uploaded pre-2025
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Brian Austin
Description:
In [https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5778|https://otwarchive.atlassian.net/browse/AO3-5778|smart-link], we switched to ActiveStorage. However, for some reason, the backfill script (in {{after_tasks.rake}}) resulted in some DB records being created even when S3 uploads didn’t succeed (or just didn’t happen – why is unclear).

h1. Steps to reproduce

# Find a user or collection whose icon was uploaded around 2024 or earlier.
# Ask Systems (AD&T doesn’t have access to the S3 bucket yet) to delete the icon manually via the AWS console (don’t worry, they’ll know what to do roughly even if you don’t know what that means 🙂 )
# Load a page that should display the icon

Note: this impacts skins too, but previews for them are more annoying so feel free to skip them – the code should be exactly the same.

h2. What happens

The image is not shown, and an [error is recorded in Sentry|https://organization-for-transformativ.sentry.io/issues/6308530931/?project=4507488737820672&query=is%3Aunresolved&referrer=issue-stream&stream_index=4].

h2. What should happen

# The image is not shown on initial page load
# On subsequent reloads (or other page loads), the icon should now be shown again.

h1. Implementation Notes

This takes 2 parts: rescuing the exception, and re-backfilling the icon. (Cleaning up the active storage data doesn’t need to happen now, but if you want {{purge}} ing the icon like we do on delete should work.)

h2. Exception rescue

The easiest (and probably best) way to do this would be to create an exception handler in {{ApplicationController}} like [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/controllers/application_controller.rb#L28|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/master/app/controllers/application_controller.rb#L28|smart-link] .

There is another option, though, if that ends up being too much code for that file: implement a custom subclass of the ActiveStorage controllers [as described in the Rails docs|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/active_storage_overview.html#authenticated-controllers].

h2. Re-backfill

AD&T has a script to do this ad-hoc for a list of users. You’ll need to figure out a way to get the right objects to update though, since we can’t just rely on {{User.current_user}} (because collections are also a thing to consider). _Note from Brian:_ collections may be much less likely to display this issue due to how the backfill for them worked (it used simpler code) – in a  pinch, I suppose we can just assume it’s a user.

{code:ruby}usernames = %w[...]
User.where(login: usernames).each do |user|
  user.pseuds.each do |pseud|
    next unless pseud.icon_file_name
    image = pseud.icon_file_name
    ext = File.extname(image)
    image_original = "original#{ext}"

    icon_url = "https://s3.amazonaws.com/otw-ao3-icons/icons/#{pseud.id}/#{image_original}"
    old_icon = URI.parse(icon_url).open
    pseud.icon.attach(io: URI.parse(icon_url).open,
                      filename: image_original,
                      content_type: pseud.icon_content_type)

    puts "Sleeping to avoid DB issues"
    sleep 2
  end
end{code}

Summary: Restrict the ability to apply to make skins public to official users
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in
# Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Skins > Create Site Skin

h1. What happens

There is an option called “Apply to make public,” but if you click on the help link, it says you can’t apply to make skins public. (This is also true for work skins.)

h1. What should happen

This option should only be there for official users, not for admins or for users with no or other roles (e.g., tag wranglers). (Note: Generally, we like to keep the forms the same for admins and users, in case admins need to screenshot something. In this case, most users will _not_ see the “Apply to make public” checkbox, so including it would have the opposite effect. Additionally, including it provides no information for admins: if the skin author doesn’t check this box, the admin cannot access its edit page.)

The help link and associated file can be removed.

After this is deployed, we should remove all skins from the Approval Queue and Rejected Skins pages. We can do this with a rake task included in this issue.

h1. Testing

Note: It would be a good idea for an admin who can access Manage Users > Find Users to confirm that testy_official has the “official” role before testing.

Summary: Upgrade to Rails 7.2
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Brian Austin
Description:
Rails keeps on releasing new versions, and our current (7.1) goes EOL October 2025. So time to upgrade again!

Highlights from the Rails team:

* Development containers configuration for applications.
* Add browser version guard by default.
* Make Ruby 3.1 the new minimum version.
* Default Progressive Web Application (PWA) files.
* Add omakase RuboCop rules by default.
* Add GitHub CI workflow by default to new applications.
* Add Brakeman by default to new applications.
* Set a new default for the Puma thread count.
* Prevent jobs from being scheduled within transactions.
* Per transaction commit and rollback callbacks.
* Enable YJIT by default if running Ruby 3.3+.
* New design for the Rails guides.
* Setup jemalloc in default Dockerfile to optimize memory allocation.
* Suggest puma-dev configuration in bin/setup.

Requirements to upgrade, in broad strokes, are described in [https://guides.rubyonrails.org/upgrading_ruby_on_rails.html#upgrading-from-rails-7-0-to-rails-7-1|https://guides.rubyonrails.org/upgrading_ruby_on_rails.html#upgrading-from-rails-7-0-to-rails-7-1|smart-link]. Summary: Warn on login if current password is insecure
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Brian Austin
Description:
When a user or admin logs in, they should [receive a warning message|https://github.com/michaelbanfield/devise-pwned_password?tab=readme-ov-file#how-to-warn-existing-users-when-they-sign-in] if their password can be found in [HaveIBeenPwned’s database|https://haveibeenpwned.com/Passwords]. 

Users should also be redirected to the change password page ({{/users/USERNAME/change_password}}) so they can more easily act on the warning. (Admins don't have this page so should not be redirected.) 

Both parties should see the following message: 

{quote}Your password has appeared in a data breach from another site and is no longer secure. For your protection, please select a new, unique password.{quote}

h2. Testing

# A database admin should create or modify a user account and an admin account to each have the password {{password}}. 
# Log in as the insecure user. Make sure that you are redirected to the change password form with the above message. 
# Try to log in with an incognito/private window. You should also be redirected with the warning message.
# Change your password to something stronger (you can use an online generator). 
# Log in again. You should not be redirected to the change password form or receive the warning message.
# Log in as the insecure admin. You should receive the warning message. 
# Reset your admin password. You should be logged in and receive no warning message.

Summary: Only permit email for password resets
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Brian Austin
Description:
h1. Background Since username is publicly visible, allowing someone to trigger a reset with that instead of email is a potential vector for harassment. Support and PAC have requested that we restrict resets to only be initiated by email. h1. Implementation We will need to update [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/c1d52a8b76b1b76da4879f009d1e5f703e13d97a/app/controllers/users/passwords_controller.rb#L10|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/c1d52a8b76b1b76da4879f009d1e5f703e13d97a/app/controllers/users/passwords_controller.rb#L10|smart-link] to only search by email, not email and username (AKA login). We should also update the checks for user existence and password resets over the configured limit to not allow email enumeration attacks (by not saying if a user is not found). To accomplish this, we will change all the status flash messages to a single message. The text for [https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/c1d52a8b76b1b76da4879f009d1e5f703e13d97a/app/views/users/passwords/new.html.erb#L10|https://github.com/otwcode/otwarchive/blob/c1d52a8b76b1b76da4879f009d1e5f703e13d97a/app/views/users/passwords/new.html.erb#L10|smart-link] should also be updated, and it would be nice to change the form parameter from {{login}} (what we used to call username) to email, since it’s just that now. h3. Password reset page: {quote}

Reset Password

If you've forgotten your password, we can send you an email with instructions to reset your password.

Please enter the email address associated with your AO3 account. You may only request a password reset a limited number of times per day.

Email address _________________ [Reset Password]{quote} (Right now it’s 2 per email per 24 hours, but even when we change the threshold that message is close enough.) The browser title of this page should also be changed to “Reset Password” (currently it’s “New Password”). h3. Flash messages If you enter something that isn’t an email: {quote}You must enter your email address.{quote} If you enter something that looks like an email: {quote}If the email address you entered is currently associated with an AO3 account, you should receive an email with instructions to reset your password.{quote} h1. Testing # Find/create an account with an email address you have access to. # Go to [https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/password/new|https://test.archiveofourown.org/users/password/new]. # Make sure it only mentions email address, not username. # Try to trigger a reset by your account’s username. After submitting the form you should be on the reset password page with a “You must enter your email address.“ flash message. Check that you do not receive an email within about 15 minutes. # Try to trigger a reset by your account’s email address. After submitting the form you should be on the reset password page with a “If the email address you entered is currently associated with an AO3 account, you should receive an email with instructions to reset your password.“ flash message. Check that you receive an email within about 15 minutes with instructions on how to reset. # Repeat step 5 after an hour, another 15 minutes that, and after a day. Make sure that submitting the form always keeps you on the same page with the “If the email…” flash message and does not redirect you to another page. You should receive one more email. After that you should not receive another email until it has been at least 24 hours after the latest email.

Summary: Radio buttons and checkboxes have unwanted shadows in desktop Chrome
Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.
Creator: Sarken
Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Using the Chrome browser on a computer, log in as a user with tag wrangling access (e.g. testy on Staging)
# If the Dark Mode skin is available, apply it – it’s easier to see the issue with Dark Mode applied, although it exists in the default skin as well
## Scroll down to the footer and choose “Dark Mode” from the “Customize” section
# To get a good look at the problem with radio buttons, go to Browse > Tag Search and look at the “Type” or “Wrangling status” section
# To get a good look at the problem with checkboxes, go to a wrangling bin (Hi, username! > Tag Wrangling > Fandoms by Media)

h1. What happens

On the radio buttons, there is a faint square shadow around the round buttons.

On the checkboxes, there is a shadow that partially obscures the top border of the checkboxes and makes it appear faded. There’s also a little bit of it visible beyond the corners of the checkboxes, since the checkboxes have rounded corners.

h1. What should happen

The shadow should only be used on inputs where you enter text, not on checkboxes or radio buttons.

h1. Notes

To illustrate the issue a little better, I’ve changed the shadow color to red for the attached screenshots.

h1. Deploy notes

Skins need to be recached.

Project description: This is the project to use for issues related to Archive of Our Own.

Description:
h1. Steps to reproduce

# Log in
# Hi, username! > My Dashboard > Skins > Create Site Skin
